menus.Name: hidradenitis-suppurativa
menus.Text:
## HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA
A chronic inflammatory condition that typically involves occlusion, rupture,
abscess formation and infection of hair follicles as well as secondary infection
of apocrine glands/surrounding tissues. Lesions most often occur in the
intertriginous areas (axillae, inguinal and anogenital) in is associated with
smoking and obesity. There is a 40% genetic predisposition for hidradenitis
suppurativa (HS) and is often accompanied by pain, malodor, and drainage.
Cultures are negative 50% of the time and often are polymicrobial with S.
epidermidis and S. aureus most isolated. The Hurley Staging System is often used
to determine severity of HS.
Therapy generally consists of treatment of comorbidities that can exacerbate HS,
avoidance of triggers, pain management, wound care, and topical/oral
antimicrobials. Hormonal agents, steroids, retinoids, and surgery can also be
used to treat certain patients. Biologics may be considered in Stage II-III HS.
## Consult Dermatology in all cases
## Hurley Staging System:
Stage I: recurrent nodules and abscesses with minimal scarring
Stage II: limited number of sinuses and/or scarring within a body region
Stage III: multiple or extensive sinuses and/or scarring
## Duration of Therapy:
Treatment is typically for 12 weeks but may require longer durations in certain
cases. Metronidazole should only be used for a maximum of 6 weeks to avoid
neurologic toxicity.
## Interventions for All Patients:
Smoking cessation, weight loss, avoidance of triggers, and pain management
should be part of all treatment plans. Consult Dermatology for use of hormonal
agents, steroids, retinoids, and surgery.
## Inpatient

## Optional Topical Treatment, May be Used in Addition to Oral Therapies Below:
Chlorhexidine gluconate 4% liquid topically wash affected area q24h ($) [M]
< OR >

< ADD ON THERAPY FOR FLARES - MUST USE IN ADDITION TO ONE OF THE AGENTS ABOVE>

## Stage I-II Initial Treatment:

< OR >

## HIV
## Inpatient/Outpatient

HIV infection and AIDS are associated with several host defense defects. Cell-
mediated immune defects render a patient more susceptible to opportunistic
infections with pathogens like Pneumocystis jirovecii (formerly Pneumocystis
carinii), Toxoplasma gondii, cytomegalovirus, mycobacterium-avium intracellulare
complex, and Candida spp.
Contact ID or HIV service for assistance.

menus.Name: hsv-encephalitis
menus.Text:
## HERPES SIMPLEX ENCEPHALITIS
Herpes simplex virus (HSV) type 1 is the leading cause of sporadic fatal
encephalitis worldwide and should be suspected in patients who have symptoms
unexplained by other causes. Typical symptoms include acute alteration of
consciousness for more than 24 hours, fever, new onset seizures and/or focal
neurologic deficits. Patients taking natalizumab are at increased risk of HSV
encephalitis. Early diagnosis and treatment are essential to achieve resolution
of infection and symptoms. If diagnosis is not certain and there is little
likelihood of herniation, obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) sample for HSV
polymerase chain reaction (PCR). MRI without contrast nearly always show
abnormal signs in patients with HSV encephalitis. Neurology and Infectious
disease consultations are strongly encouraged.
## Treatment, Initiate Immediately When HSV Encephalitis is Suspected
## Inpatient

Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h ($$) [R,DI] for 14 to 21 days
*If BMI > 35, use IBW to dose
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Outpatient

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS. References:
Rabinstein, Neurol Clin, 2017, 695-705

## IMMUNOGLOBULIN DEFICIENCY (HUMORAL IMMUNE SYSTEM)
Antibody deficiency typically leads to recurrent, severe respiratory tract
infections associated with encapsulated bacteria, especially Streptococcus
pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae, and to a lesser extent, Staphylococcus
aureus. Recurrent otitis media, sinusitis, and pneumonia are common syndromes.
Gastrointestinal disease associated with Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, or
rotavirus is also common in some patients.
## Preferred empirical treatment
## Inpatient

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($5.71/day) [M]
## Alternative for severe penicillin allergy
Chloramphenicol is not currently available. Contact Infectious Diseases for
advice.
## Outpatient
Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS
References
Rich RR, et al, eds. Clinical Immunology
Roitt I, et al, eds. Immunology

menus.Name: immunocom-altered-micro-flora
menus.Text:
## ALTERED MICROBIAL FLORA
A rich, diverse microbial flora lives on or in skin, mucosal surfaces, and
respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts of healthy people. This flora prevents
disease by inhibiting the growth of potential pathogens. Disruption of the
normal flora, usually by antimicrobial therapy, reduces this barrier and
increases the risk of infectious disease. Patients exposed to broad-spectrum
antimicrobials are at greater risk for colonization with resistant bacteria,
fungal infections, and Clostridium difficile colitis. During hospitalization,
many patients become colonized with more resistant organisms like methicillin-
resistant Staphylococcus aureus and resistant Gram-negative bacilli.
References
Rich RR, et al, eds. Clinical Immunology
Roitt I, et al, eds. Immunology

## COMPLEMENT DEFICIENCY
Complement deficiency can be inherited or acquired. Acquired defects are
usually a consequence of other diseases like systemic lupus erythematosus.
Complement deficiency leads to increased rates of infections, usually of the
upper respiratory tract, but also occasionally with bacteremia or meningitis.
Pathogens are usually Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and
Neisseria gonorrhea.
Patients presenting with fever or other symptoms suggesting systemic bacterial
infection should be treated immediately with antimicrobials active against these
pathogens.
## Preferred empirical treatment
## Inpatient

Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($5.71/day) [M]
## Alternative for severe penicillin allergy

advice.

menus.Name: immunocom-malignancy

## MALIGNANCY
## Inpatient/Outpatient/ER Malignancies affect host defenses in many ways. Hematogenous malignancies can
diminish the effectiveness of neutrophils and other cells involved in host
defense. Tumors often disrupt mucous membranes or blood vessels and allow
contaminating organisms into hollow cavities or the bloodstream. Chemotherapy
used to treat these malignancies often impairs mucus membranes and suppresses
neutrophil production and function.
Ordinarily, empirical antimicrobials are not indicated for patients with
malignancy and fever unless they have neutropenia or a specific infectious
disease.
Neutropenic fever
Prevention of bacterial infections in a patient with malignancy
Prevention of fungal infections in a patient with malignancy

menus.Name: immunocom-neurol-dysfunction
menus.Text:
## NEUROLOGICAL DYSFUNCTION
## Inpatient/Outpatient

Several types of neurological dysfunction predispose patients to infectious
diseases. Comatose patients are unable to keep weight off dependent tissues,
predisposing them to decubitus ulcers and pressure necrosis. Atelectasis is
common in obtunded patients who cannot cough or breathe deeply. When patients
require artificial ventilation, intubation compounds the risk of respiratory
infection.
Neurological dysfunction of the bladder can interfere with normal bladder
emptying and predisposes patients to bacteriuria. The risk of bacteruria
increases if patients are catheterized. Antimicrobial treatment is not
indicated for asymptomatic bacteriuria. It provides no benefit and increases
risk of colonization with resistant organisms.
Neurological dysfunction predisposes patients to aspiration of oropharyngeal or
gastric contents. Aspiration causes fever, inflammation, and/or pulmonary
infiltrate, but does not require antimicrobial treatment. Bacterial pneumonia
occurs in a minority of patients who experience significant aspiration,
typically about 3 days later. Typically, the patient improves for the first 2
days and then worsens as bacterial pneumonia develops with increased fever, new
or progressive infiltrates, leukocytosis, and newly purulent sputum.
Aspiration pneumonia
References
Rich RR, et al, eds. Clinical Immunology
Roitt I, et al, eds. Immunology

menus.Name: immunocom-neut-fever
menus.Text:
## NEUTROPENIC FEVER
## Inpatient/Outpatient/ER The risk of severe, rapidly progressive infections increases when the absolute
neutrophil count (ANC, segmented neutrophils plus bands) is less than 500
cells/microliter. The risk increases dramatically when the ANC is <100
cells/microliter. Because of these risks, patients with fever and neutropenia
to this degree should receive empirical antimicrobial therapy immediately.
Empirical therapy should also be given to patients with fever and ANC 500-1000
cells/microliter when the concentration is expected to be <500 cells/microliter
within the next 48 hours. For this purpose, fever is defined as a single
temperature greater than 38.3 degrees Celsius.
## Initial therapy
Since infection can be rapidly progressive and severe, broad-spectrum
antimicrobials are given urgently to patients with neutropenic fever as defined
above. Vancomycin should only be given when there are clear indications for its
use.
Candidates for empirical treatment with oral antimicrobials include those who
are febrile but who have no evidence of focal infection or signs or symptoms of
severe disease, like hypotension. Outpatient antimicrobials for neutropenic
fever must be ordered only in consultation with Hematology-Oncology or
Infectious Diseases.
## Treatment
If patient IS a candidate for oral therapy
If patient is NOT a candidate for oral therapy
[Link to a scoring tool that identifies low risk patients for oral therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-scoring-tool)
## Modifcation to therapy

menus.Name: impetigo
menus.Text:
Impetigo and Ecthyma
Impetigo is a superficial skin infection that rarely causes systemic
symptoms. Ecthyma is a skin infection characterized by crusted sores
beneath which ulcers form. It is a deep form of impetigo, as the same
bacteria causing the infection are involved. Ecthyma causes deeper
erosions of the skin into the dermis.
Gram stain and culture of the pus or exudates from skin lesions of
impetigo and ecthyma are recommended to help identify whether
Staphylococcus aureus and/or beta-hemolytic Streptococcus is the cause.
Bullous and non-bullous impetigo can be treated with oral or topical
antimicrobials, but oral therapy is recommended for patients with
numerous lesions or in outbreaks affecting several people to help
decrease transmission of infection. Treatment for ecthyma should be an
oral antimicrobial.
## Inpatient

## Treatment for impetigo with few lesions
Mupirocin ointment to affected area q8h for 5 days ($) [M]
## Treatment for ecthyma and for impetigo with numerous lesions or
## whose symptoms have not responded to topical treatment
Treat orally for 7 days
## Alternative for penicillin allergy
Doxycycline 100MG PO q12h ($) [DI]
## IF MRSA confirmed or suspected:
Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h ($) [R,DI]
Doxycycline 100MG PO q12h ($) [DI]
## Outpatient

## Treatment for impetigo with few lesions
Mupirocin ointment to affected area TID for 5 days ($) [M]
Non-VA order for above
## Treatment for ecthyma and for impetigo with numerous lesions or
## whose symptoms have not responded to topical treatment
Treat orally for 7 days
Non-VA order for above
## Alternative for penicillin allergy
[Assess Beta-lactam allergy prior to ordering alternative](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)
Doxycycline 100MG PO bid ($) [DI]
Non-VA order for above
## IF MRSA confirmed or suspected:
Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid ($) [R,DI]
Non-VA order for above
Doxycycline 100MG PO bid ($) [DI]
Non-VA order for above

## INITIAL EPISODE OF CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)
Discontinue implicated antibiotic(s). Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic
therapy is still needed. Avoid antiperistaltic agents (narcotics, loperamide,
etc.). Avoid antacid therapy without clear indication. If diarrhea has improved
or resolved prior to starting C. difficile treatment, consider re-assessing the
diagnosis before initiating therapy. C. difficile infection usually responds to
antimicrobial therapy. If symptoms do not respond to appropriate antimicrobial
therapy, re-consider the diagnosis.
## Inpatient

## Patient at increased risk of CDI recurrence:
(e.g., age >65 years old, concomitant antibiotic use during CDI treatment,
and/or immunosuppression)
Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days [M]

## INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED COAGULASE-NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCUS INFECTION
## (CNS)
Catheter removal is optional. However, treatment is more likely to be successful
with removal of catheter. The decision about whether to remove the catheter
depends on severity of illness, presence of resistant organisms, the need for
the catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Treatment if the catheter is removed
## Duration of therapy
## Inpatient

In cases where bacteremia is rapidly cleared, treat for 5-7 days. In cases where
rapid clearance of bacteremia does not occur, treat for up to 14 days.
Refer to [coagulase-negative staphylococcus bacteremia](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-coag-neg-staph) recommendations for
antimicrobial selection.

Consult infectious diseases in all cases. Treatment success rate is improved
when the infected catheter is filled with an antimicrobial solution during
periods when the catheter is not used. Consult Infectious Diseases or Pharmacy
for information.

14 days. If follow up blood cultures are persistently positive after 72 hours,
catheter should be removed promptly.

menus.Name: keratitis
menus.Text:
## KERATITIS
Keratitis is an emergency requiring prompt treatment to prevent vision loss.
Contact Ophthalmology immediately.
Keratitis is associated with viral or bacterial infection, trauma, foreign
bodies, or allergies. About half of cases of infectious keratitis are caused by
bacterial pathogens, most commonly Staphylococcus spp., Streptococcus spp., and
gram-negative bacilli. Viruses are the second leading cause. Fungi and parasites
have also been associated with corneal infection. Obtain corneal scrapings for
gram stain and bacterial and viral cultures and start empirical therapy
immediately.
Link to herpes keratitis page
Herpes keratitis
If bacterial keratitis is likely, contact ophthalmology to obtain a corneal
scraping and give empirical antibacterial drops immediately. Modify therapy
based on Ophthalmology and/or Infectious Diseases recommendations. Ophthalmic
corticosteroids are contraindicated in patients with keratitis.
## Duration of therapy
## Inpatient

Treatment should be continued until ulcer and other signs of infectious
keratitis have resolved. A minimum of two weeks and in rare cases, up to a month
of therapy may be required.
## Mild to moderate bacterial keratitis empirical treatment
Moxifloxacin 0.5% ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops in affected eye(s) q1h ($) [M]
## Severe (vision-threatening) bacterial keratitis empirical treatment
Cefazolin 50 mg/ml ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops q1h <AND> gentamicin 15 mg/ml
ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops q1h ($) [M] in affected eye(s)
## Suspected MRSA
Patient may require vancomycin 50mg/mL eye drops q1h in addition to gentamicin
eye drops. Vancomycin eye drops must be specially compounded and managed by
Ophthalmology.
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Outpatient

## Mild to moderate bacterial keratitis empirical treatment
Moxifloxacin 0.5% ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops in affected eye(s) q1h ($) [M]
Non-VA order for above

ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops q1h ($) [M] in affected eye(s)

menus.Text:
## LIVER ABSCESS
Oral step-down treatment
Liver abscess should be suspected in all patients with fever, leukocytosis, and
a space-occupying liver lesion. Liver abscesses fall broadly into two
categories: pyogenic and amebic. In the United States, pyogenic liver abscess is
much more common. Amebic liver abscess occurs almost exclusively in travelers
and immigrants.
Infectious Diseases consultation is recommended due to prolonged treatment and
need for follow-up.
## Duration of therapy
A typical course for pyogenic liver abscess is 4 to 6 weeks based on improvement
and follow-up imaging.
## Inpatient

## Treatment
Preferred:
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h [M] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
Critical illness or immunosuppression:
Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h [R]
Alternative for critical illness or suppression:
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h [R] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]
Alternative for severe beta lactam reaction:
Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h [R,DI] <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

## ACUTE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH LYME DISEASE
Neurological disease is a common manifestation of Lyme Disease that typically
occurs within weeks to months after the tick bite. Unilateral or bilateral
facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy) can be treated with oral antimicrobials. Other
neurological manifestations, including meningitis, require treatment with
intravenous antimicrobials.
## Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases
## Duration of therapy
Treat for at least 14 days. Longer durations, up to 21 days for facial nerve
palsy and 28 days for other neurologic disease, may be required in severe cases.
## Treatment of isolated facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy)
Preferred: ##Inpatient Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI]
For pregnant patients or those with contraindications to doxycycline: Amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h ($) [R]
## Treatment of neurological disease other than facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy)
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h ($) [M]

# # ER Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT ($) [M] ## Outpatient Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 14 days
For pregnant patients or those with contraindications to doxycycline: Non-VA order for above

## LYME DISEASE AND OTHER TICK-BORNE ILLNESSES
## Inpatient/Outpatient/ER Patients who display signs of illness or fever within 30 days of removing an
attached tick should be evaluated for tick-borne illness. In the upper Midwest
these are Lyme, anaplasmosis, babesiosis, ehrlichiosis, and Powassan virus
disease. Patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick (deer tick) but
who do not display signs or symptoms of infection should not be treated with
antimicrobials. Refer to recommendations below for pathogen specific
recommendations.
Anaplasmosis
Ehrlichioisis
Babesiosis
Powassan virus disease - contact Infectious Diseases for more Information.
## Lyme Disease
Lyme disease results from the transmission of Borrelia burgdorferi from an
Ixodes spp. tick bite. Refer to CDC for map of endemic areas.
CDC Lyme Disease Case Map
Prophylactic antimicrobial treatment may be beneficial in certain patients who
have been bitten while in endemic areas.
Lyme Disease Prophylaxis
Except for erythema migrans, Lyme disease is a complicated, difficult disease to
diagnose and treat. Infectious Diseases consultation is strongly encouraged.
Refer to recommendations below for
Erythema migrans
Acute neurological disease
Arthritis
Cardiac disease

menus.Name: lyme-disease-prophylaxis
menus.Text:
## LYME DISEASE PROPHYLAXIS
## Inpatient/Outpatient/ER Patients who have been bitten while in endemic areas of New England, Mid-
Atlantic States, Minnesota, and Wisconsin where local rate of Ixodes spp. tick
infection rate with Borrelia burgdorferi in an endemic area may be treated with
prophylactic antibiotics for prevention of Lyme disease. Using a wait and see
method by monitoring for signs and symptoms of Lyme disease is also an
acceptable approach in patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick.
## All following criteria must be met to be considered for prophylactic treatment
1. Doxycycline is not contraindicated (i.e. allergy, pregnant, lactating)
2. Attached tick is reliably identified as an adult or nymphal Ixodes spp.
Ixodes spp. identification
3. Tick is attached for greater than or equal to 36 hours based on degree of
tick engorgement with blood or likely time of exposure to tick infested area.
4. Prophylaxis must be started within 72 hours after time tick was removed.
5. Bite occurs in a highly endemic area.
CDC Lyme Disease Case Map
## Prophylactic treatment if all of the above criteria are met
Doxycycline PO 200mg once ($) [DI]

## ERYTHEMA MIGRANS ASSOCIATED WITH LYME DISEASE
Erythema migrans is the first manifestation of Lyme disease in 70-80% of cases.
It is typically an erythematous circular rash, 5cm or larger in diameter, with
induration and central clearing (although other patterns occur). It usually
develops at the site of the bite and/or in one or more distant locations. The
rash occurs 3 to 30 days after the bite. Rashes with onset less than 3 days
after a tick bite are not from Lyme disease.
If suspected erythema migrans is atypical, serology testing is recommended
with repeat in three weeks if negative.

## MILD TO MODERATE SINUSITIS
Community-acquired bacterial sinusitis is most often due to Streptococcus
pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae or Moraxella catarrhalis. Streptococci,
Staphylococcus aureus and anaerobes are isolated less frequently.
## Treatment for first 10 days of illness
Treat with decongestants, analgesics, and nasal saline spray.

## THE APPROACH TO CELLULITIS
In addition to antimicrobial therapy, several non-pharmacological treatments
improve the outcome of cellulitis.Elevation and immobilization of the
affected limb reduces swelling. Heat reduces discomfort.
Prevent tinea pedis infection by keeping feet clean and dry. In patients with
peripheral edema, good skin hygiene and support stockings reduce the incidence
of recurrent infection.
In many cases of cellulitis, the affected area is usually not well-
differeniated from unaffected areas of the skin. Erysipelas is a special case
with typically a well-defined border and raised, orange-peel appearance.
Erysipelas

menus.Name: more-about-pharyngitis
menus.Text:
## MORE ABOUT PHARYNGITIS/ TONSILLITIS AND THE MODIFIED CENTOR SCORE
## Inpatient/Outpatient

As most cases are of viral origin, antimicrobials are not indicated in these
cases. Warm saltwater gargle rinses and throat lozenges provide temporary relief
of throat pain. Five to 10% of cases are caused by group A Streptococcus.
Antimicrobial treatment reduces symptoms by one day, prevents suppurative
complications and prevents acute rheumatic fever, an uncommon disease in US
adults.
Streptococcal pharyngitis or tonsillitis should be suspected when patients have
fever and exudate on the pharyngeal wall or tonsils without symptoms like cough,
nasal congestion, or runny nose that suggest viral infection or common cold. If
streptococcal pharyngitis is suspected in adults, perform PCR testing for group
A streptococci and treat only if positive.
Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a rare cause of pharyngitis. N. gonorrhoeae should be
considered for patients with risk factors for sexually transmitted diseases. N.
gonorrhoeae infections must be reported to the state health department and this
will be done by Infection Control if the culture is positive.
## The Modified Centor score
Used to estimate the likelihood that a patient with sore throat has
streptococcal pharyngitis and whether rapid PCR testing should be performed.
1) Absence of cough = 1 point
2) Swollen and tender anterior cervical nodes = 1 point
3) Temperature greater than 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Centigrade) = 1
point
4) Tonsillar exudates or swelling = 1 point
5) Age: 3-14 years = 1 point
15-44 years = 0 points
45 years and older = -1 point
Patients with a score of 0 or 1 are at very low risk. PCR testing and antibiotic
treatment are not indicated. Patients with a score of 2 to 4 are at moderate to
high risk. PCR testing should be obtained in these patients to determine if GAS
is present. In patients with a score of 4 or greater, consider empiric
antibiotic treatment.

menus.Name: necrotizing-infections
menus.Text:
## NECROTIZING INFECTIONS
Call Surgery immediately and consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.
Necrotizing infections involve tissues skin and/or deeper structures, including
fascia and muscle. These infections destroy tissue, often rapidly, and are
often fatal if not treated promptly and appropriately. Necrotizing infections
usually result from trauma, surgery, and/or ischemia. These infections can be
monomicrobial (e.g., with streptococci or clostridia) or polymicrobial (usually
with a mixture of aerobes and anaerobes). Fournier gangrene is usually
associated with mixed infection. Myonecrosis is most commonly associated with
Clostridium species.
Necrotizing infections differ from cellulitis in several ways. Necrotic
infections typically have one or more of the following: (1) severe, constant
pain, (2) bullae, (3) bruising or necrosis of overlying skin, (4) gas in tissues
which can be felt or seen on images, (5) edema that extends beyond areas of
erythema, (6) local anesthesia, and (7) signs of systemic toxicity, such as
fever, leukocytosis, delirium, or renal failure.
Necrotizing infections must be treated with both antimicrobial therapy and
surgical procedures (excision and/or drainage). Call surgery to see the patient
immediately in all cases. Obtain tissue and blood cultures and begin empirical
antimicrobials. For several necrotic diseases and/or pathogens, a combination
of two antimicrobials is recommended including a bactericidal antimicrobial
active at the cell wall or membrane (e.g., beta-lactam or glycopeptide) and an
antimicrobial that rapidly inhibits protein synthesis and thus inhibits toxin
production, typically clindamycin.
Repeat debridement should be performed daily until no further debridement is
necessary. Antibiotic therapy should be tailored as soon as culture results
become available.
Administer antibiotics until further debridement is no longer necessary, the
patient has improved clinically, and fever has been absent for 48-72 hours.

## OROLABIAL HERPES
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Immunocompetent patients
## _______________________________________________________________________________
Antiviral therapy is not beneficial after formation of vesicles. However, when
started as soon as prodromal symptoms of burning or tingling occur, antivirals
reduce duration of pain and lesions.
Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 5 days ($) [R]
Alternative
Valacyclovir 2 gm q12h for 1 day ($) [R]
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Immunocompromised patients
## _______________________________________________________________________________
Immunocompromised patients in whom herpes simplex infections can be more severe
include: patients with HIV infection, organ transplant recipients, patients
undergoing chemotherapy, malnourished patients, and those with compromised skin
integrity.
## Treatment for mild to moderate disease
Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 7-14 days($) [R]
< OR >
Valacyclovir 1 gm q12h for 7-14 days ($) [R]
## Treatment for severe disease
Acyclovir 5 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days ($$) [R]
## _______________________________________________________________________________
## Chronic suppressive therapy
## _______________________________________________________________________________
Indicated for patients with greater than 6 recurrences or severe recurrences,
immunocompromised patients or as adjunct to prevent transmission. Suppressive
therapy is optional, and some patients may find episodic treatment more
convenient. Patients should be reassessed every few years to evaluate if chronic
suppressive therapy is still necessary.
Acyclovir 400 mg PO q12h ($) [R]

Valacyclovir 500 mg PO Q24h ($) [R]

immunocompetent patients

Guidance

# LYME DISEASE AND OTHER TICK-BORNE ILLNESSES

Patients who display signs of illness or fever within 30 days of removing an

attached tick should be evaluated for tick-borne illness. In the upper Midwest

these are Lyme, anaplasmosis, babesiosis, ehrlichiosis, and Powassan vir

disease. Patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick (deer tick) but

who do not display signs or symptoms of infection should not be treated with

antimicrobials. Refer to recommendations below for pathogen specific

recommendations.

Powassan virus disease - contact Infectious Diseases for more Information.

# Lyme Disease

Lyme disease results from the transmission of Borrelia burgdorferi from an

Ixodes spp. tick bite. Refer to CDC for map of endemic areas.

[CDC Lyme Disease Case Map](orz-gtx-abx-cdc-lyme-disease-case-map)

Prophylactic antimicrobial treatment may be beneficial in certain patients that

have been bitten while in endemic areas.

[Lyme Disease Prophylaxis](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-lyme-disease-prophylaxis)

Except for erythema migrans, Lyme disease is a complicated, difficult disease to

diagnose and treat. Infectious Diseases consultation is strongly encouraged.

Refer to recommendations below for

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC ACUTE SINUSITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# ACUTE SINUSITIS

Most cases of acute sinusitis are viral and resolve within 10 days. Symptoms

(nasal congestion, purulent nasal discharge, and tooth or facial pain) can be

treated with decongestants, analgesics, and nasal saline. Diagnosis of acute

sinusitis is based on the presence of at least 2 major or 1 major and at least 2

minor symptoms.

# Major Symptoms

1. Purulent anterior nasal discharge

2. Purulent or discolored posterior nasal discharge

3. Nasal congestion or fullness

4. Facial pain or pressure

5. Hyposmia or anosmia

6. Fever

# Minor Symptoms

1. Headache

2. Ear pain, pressure or fullness

3. Halitosis

4. Dental pain

5. Cough

6. Fatigue

If patient meets criteria above for acute sinusitis, treat with antimicrobials

according to the following criteria for mild to moderate or severe bacterial

sinusitis.

# Mild to moderate bacterial sinusitis

1. Symptoms persisting beyond 10 days

< OR >

2. Double-sickening - Symptoms typical of viral upper respiratory infection

initially improving for 5-6 days then worsening with new development of fever,

headache or increased nasal discharge.

[CLICK HERE for treatment of mild to moderate bacterial sinusitis - Opt CDSS](orzid3-gmenu-acute-sinusitis-mild-to-mod)

# Severe bacterial sinusitis

Severe signs or symptoms of high fever (>/= 102 degrees Fahrenheit, >/= 39

degrees Celsius) and purulent nasal discharge for 3-4 consecutive days or facial

pain lasting for at least 3-4 consecutive days at the beginning of illness.

[CLICK HERE for treatment of severe bacterial sinusitis](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-severe-sinusitis)

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC APPENDICITIS W/O PERFORATION
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# APPENDICITIS WITHOUT PERFORATION

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid3-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Patients with an acutely inflamed appendix and no gangrene or perforation are

considered to have uncomplicated appendicitis. Patients with gangrene,

perforation, peritonitis, or abscess have complicated appendicitis. Treatment

with antibiotics is an option for patients who are unfit for surgery or refuse

surgery. Treatment with antibiotics should not be used routinely as an

alternative to surgery.

# Select for treatment of complicated appendicitis

[Link to appendicitis with perforation menu](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-appendicitis-with-perforation)

# Treatment of uncomplicated appendicitis

Surgical management:  Administer prophylaxis regimen below prior to surgery

only. Stop antibiotics after the surgery.

Surgical prophylaxis:

[Cefazolin weight-based dosing preop < AND >  metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT](orz-set-abx-cefaz-2gm-metro-500mg-iv-once-surgery-er-uc)

[DI]

Post-surgical: antibiotics not recommended after appendectomy

# Interval appendectomy or no appendectomy

Duration of therapy: Treat with antibiotics for 7 days total

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-metro-500mg-iv-once-stat)

Healthcare-associated infection, critical illness, or immunosuppression:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV once STAT R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2gm-iv-metro-500mg-iv-once-stat)

Alternative for severe Beta-lactam reaction:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV once STAT R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT](orz-set-abx-cipro-400mg-metro-500mg-iv-once-stat)

[DI]

Incomplete source control & no abscess: 5-7 days tailored to improvement.

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA

When a larger than usual volume of orogastric content is aspirated,

mechanical/chemical irritation occurs.  Some of these develop into bacterial

pneumonia.

It is reasonable to wait before starting antimicrobials to see if respiratory

impairment improves or worsens before starting bacterial pneumonia treatment, in

hemodynamically stable patients.

Therapy directed towards anaerobic pathogens is usually unnecessary.

Antimicrobial treatment is warranted if pneumonia is confirmed.

# Preferred

See below for prior respiratory isolation of MRSA or P. aeruginosa

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV STAT M](psjizid-pna-ceftriaxone-2gm-stat-er-uc)

< OR >

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV STAT R](psjizid-pna-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-stat-er-uc)

# Prior Respiratory Isolation of MRSA within last 12 months:

ADD MRSA coverage to a regimen above or antipseudomonal regimen below.

Obtain cultures/nasal PCR to allow for de-escalation.

[< ADD > Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV STAT R](psjizid-vancomycin-15-mg-kg-iv-once-stat-er-uc)

# Prior Respiratory Isolation of P. aeruginosa within last 12 months:

Select antipseudomonal regimen below, obtain cultures to allow de-escalation

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV STAT R](psjizid-pna-piperacillin-tazobactam-4-5-gm-stat-er-uc)

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV STAT R](psjizid-pna-cefepime-2gm-iv-stat-er-uc)

# Alternative

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC BACT MENING W/O GRM STAIN RES
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS (WITHOUT GRAM STAIN RESULTS)

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely,

antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures

should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients

to obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for establishing diagnosis and determining

infectious organism/susceptibility. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize

therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

Intravenous dexamethasone therapy improves outcomes for meningitis with

Streptococcus pneumoniae and is recommended for empirical treatment of all

community acquired cases that might be associated with S. pneumoniae.

Dexamethasone must be given before (1 to 20 minutes) with antimicrobials.

If meningococcal meningitis is identified, antimicrobial prophylaxis should be

considered for close contacts. Contact Infectious Diseases/Epidemiology for

advice and assistance.

# Consult Infectious Diseases

# Step 1 of Treatment

[Dexamethasone 10 mg IV once STAT \($\)](psczid-dexamethasone-10mg-iv-once-er-uc)

(Discontinue if isolated pathogen is not S. pneumoniae)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Step 2 of Treatment, Select One of the Following:

# Treatment for Adults < 50 Years Without Alcoholism, Debilitating Disease, or

# Any Other Condition Associated with Impaired Cellular Immunity.

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT \($\) M <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV once STAT](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-once-stat)

($) [R]

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV once STAT \($$\) R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg once STAT \($\) R](orz-set-abx-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h-stat)

# Treatment for Adults >= 50 Years or With Alcoholism, Debilitating Disease, or

# Impaired Cellular Immunity. Listeria Monocytogenes is One Important Pathogen.

Preferred:

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV once STAT \($$\) R <AND> ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT](orz-set-abx-ampicillin-2gm-ceftr-2gm-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-once-stat)

($) [M] vancomycin 15mg/kg once STAT ($) [R]

Alternative:

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# BITE WOUNDS

Bite wounds are prone to infection because of the pathogenic oral flora carried

into tissues by teeth. Clean wounds with soap and water as soon as possible.

Consult Orthopedic surgery for bite wounds involving the hand.

# Antibiotic Prophylaxis Indications:

Severe injury less than 8 hours, Crush injury, Bone or joint penetration, Wound

of the face or hands or genitals, Immunocompromised host, Asplenia, Advanced

liver disease

*Routine use of prophylactic antibiotics for non-immunocompromised patients with

superficial wounds with no puncture that do not involve the face/ genitals/hands

is not recommended.

# Antimicrobial Treatment:

Empiric treatment for suspected or established infection following bite wound In

these cases, therapy should be directed against pathogen identified by Gram

stain and culture whenever possible.

# Rabies Prophylaxis:

Consider rabies post-exposure prophylaxis for all animal bite cases. Contact

Infectious diseases for assistance.

# Consider tetanus immunization status:

If immunization is up to date, nothing more needs to be done to prevent tetanus.

If immunization is lacking, and: wound IS NOT tetanus prone, bring immunization

up to date with Td wound IS tetanus prone, bring immunization up to date with Td

< AND > Human Tetanus Immune Globulin Inject 250 units deeply into muscle (deep

IM)

# Select below for Tetanus vaccination information page:

[Tetanus, Diphtheria and Acellular Pertussis Vaccine Information Page](orzid3-gmenu-abx-tdap-vaccine-information-page)

# Prophylaxis:

Duration 3 to 5 days:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID for 5 days R](psozid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-5ds-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-5ds-po-bid)

for 5 days

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-5d-metro-500mg-bid-5d)

# Empiric treatment for suspected or established infection:

# BRONCHITIS

Acute bronchitis should not be treated with antimicrobials except in specific

circumstances. If pneumonia is suspected, order a chest x-ray. If an infiltrate

is not present, the patient does not have bacterial pneumonia and need not be

treated for it. If a patient has chronic pulmonary disease, see COPD

exacerbation menu.

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC CAP INPATIENT TREATED SETTING NON-SEVERE CAP
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP) TREATED IN AN INPATIENT SETTING

Be sure of the diagnosis.  Careful reviews have shown that over half of

people treated for community-acquired pneumonia do not in fact have

pneumonia.  Pneumonia is likely in persons with 3 or more signs or symptoms

including a) new infiltrate (or, no prior film for comparison) b) new

crackles, egophony, or dullness c) pleuritic pain, d) fever and/or chills

e) leukocytosis f) cough g) purulent sputum and h) new or worsened dyspnea

or tachypnea, and no likely alternative explanation for the presentation.

Common alternative explanations include heart failure, thromboembolic

disease, COPD exacerbation, viral pneumonitis, aspiration pneumonitis, or

tumor. Most of the latter conditions do NOT benefit from antimicrobials.

# Recommendation for duration of antibiotic therapy for CAP:

Patients with CAP should be treated for a minimum of 5 days, should be

afebrile for 48-72 hours, and should have no more than 1 CAP-

associated sign of clinical instability before discontinuation

of therapy.

# Criteria for clinical stability:

Temperature less than/equal to 100 degrees F

Heart rate less than/equal to 100 beats/minute

Respiratory rate less than/equal to 24 breaths/minute

Systolic blood pressure greater than/equal to 90 mm Hg

Arterial oxygen saturation greater than/equal to 90% --OR--

PO2 greater than/equal to 60 mm Hg on room air

Ability to maintain oral intake

Normal mental status

# __________________________________________________________________

# Inpatient, non-severe CAP (NOTE: DURATION of therapy)

# __________________________________________________________________

# Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for MRSA:

Obtain cultures BUT withhold MRSA coverage unless cultures or nasal carriage

positive for MRSA. (See below for prior respiratory isolation of MRSA)

# Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for P. aeruginosa:

Obtain cultures BUT withhold anti-pseudomonal coverage unless cultures

are positive for P. aeruginosa. (See below for prior respiratory isolation

of P. aeruginosa)

# Preferred: (no prior respiratory isolation of MRSA or P. aeruginosa)

[Ceftriaxone 2GM IV STAT \($\) M <AND> Azithromycin 500mg PO STAT \($\) M](orz-set-abx-pna-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-azithromycin-500mg-po-stat)

# Alternative:

[Link Fluoroquinolones FDA Serious Adverse Reactions](orz-gtx-abx-idp-fluoroquinolones-fda-warnings)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg PO STAT \($\) R,DI](psczid-pna-levofloxacin-750mg-po-stat-er-uc)

# Prior Respiratory Isolation of MRSA within last 12months: ADD MRSA COVERAGE

ADD MRSA coverage to above regimen, otain cultures/nasal PCR to allow

for deescalation

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV STAT \($\) R](psczid-pna-vancomycin-15mg-kg-iv-stat-er-uc)

# Prior Respiratory Isolation of P.aeruginosa within last 12months: SELECT BELOW

Select regimen below for P.aeruginosa, obtain cultures to allow deescalation

[Piperacillin 4.5GM IV STAT \($$\) R <AND> Azithromycin 500mg PO STAT](orz-set-abx-pna-piper-tazo-4-5-gm-azithromycin-500mg-po-stat)

< OR >

# SEVERE COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (CAP) TREATED IN INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU)

# Criteria for Defining SEVERE Community-acquired Pneumonia

Validated definition includes either one major or three or more minor criteria

MAJOR CRITERIA:

Septic shock with need for vasopressors

Respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation

MINOR CRITERIA:

Respiratory rate greater than or equal to 30 breaths/minute

PaO2/FiO2 ratio less than or equal to 250

Multilobar infiltrates Confusion/disorientation

Uremia (blood urea nitrogen level greater than 20 mg/dl)

Leukopenia* (WBC less than 4,000 cells/microliter)

*Due to infection alone (i.e., not chemotherapy induced)

Thrombocytopenia (platelet count less than 100,000 microliters)

Hypothermia (core temperature less than 36 degrees C)

Hypotension requiring aggressive fluid resuscitation

# Recommend blood and lower respiratory tract specimen cultures for all patients

# with Severe CAP.

[Lab Order: Sputum Culture & Gram Stain](orz-set-lab-sputum-cult-gram-stain)

[Lab order: Blood culture x2](orz-set-lab-blood-culture-x2)

# Duration of therapy

Patients with CAP should be treated for a minimum of 5 days, should be afebrile

for 48-72 hours, and should have no more than 1 CAP- associated sign of clinical

instability before discontinuation of therapy.

# CELLULITIS & ERYSIPELAS

Skin and soft tissue infections without abscess or other sign of purulence.

MRSA coverage is typically unnecessary when there is no purulence, even in

patients with a history of MRSA colonization or infection. It may be considered

for specific patients with the considerations listed below but is not

recommended as the default choice.

Elevation, good skin hygiene, and support stockings are recommended.

# Duration: Treat for 5 - 7 days

# Cellulitis without systemic signs of infection, oral transition

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC CHOLANGITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# CHOLANGITIS

[Oral Step-down treatment](orzid3-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Most cases are due to common bile duct obstruction. Obstruction (if present)

must be relieved with an endoscopical, transcutaneous, or surgical procedure.

The most common pathogens isolated are E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus and

Enterobacter. Pseudomonas coverage is recommended in severe (grade 3)

cholangitis.  Anaerobic coverage is recommended if biliary-enteric abnormality

is present.

Antimicrobials' role in cholangitis is to allow patients to have elective and

not emergently scheduled drainage procedures.

Due to increasing resistance, fluoroquinolones are only recommended in cases of

severe penicillin and cephalosporin allergy.

# Treatment of patients on ward without systemic symptoms of infection

Treat for 4-7 days after source control

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm once STAT M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC CHOLECYSTITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# CHOLECYSTITIS

[Step down treatment](orzid3-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Adequate biliary drainage is the definitive treatment. Antimicrobials should be

prescribed only if signs of infection like leukocytosis or fever are present or

if the patient is elderly. Surgery and Gastroenterology involvement are

essential.

For acute cholecystitis in grade 1 disease, antimicrobials are primarily

prophylactic. For moderate to severe disease grades 2-3, antimicrobials should

be continued for 4-7 days.

Most cases are associated with E. coli, Enterococcus, Klebsiella, and

Enterobacter. Anaerobic coverage is not indicated unless a biliary-enteric

abnormality is present. For community-acquired acute cholecystitis, enterococcal

coverage is not required because Enterococcus has not been shown to be

pathogenic in these patients

Due to increasing resistance, fluoroquinolones are only recommended in cases of

severe penicillin and cephalosporin allergy.

# Treatment of patient on ward without systemic symptoms of infection

Duration of Therapy: Antimicrobials should be discontinued within 24 hours of

drainage procedure

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV once STAT R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-once-er-uc)

Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:

[< ADD > Metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT DI to above regimen](psjizid-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-once-er-uc)

# Treatment of patient on ward with systemic symptoms of infection

Duration of Therapy: Treat for 4-7 days after source control

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV once STAT R](psjizid-pip-tazo-3-375-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:

[< ADD >  Metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT DI  to one of the regimens above](psjizid-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-once-er-uc)

Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV once STAT R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT](orz-set-abx-levoflox-750mg-iv-metro-500mg-iv-once-stat)

[DI]

# Treatment of ICU patients

Duration of Therapy: Most can be treated for 4-7 days after source control.

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV once STAT R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2gm-iv-metro-500mg-iv-once-stat)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ED\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# CATHETER ASSOCIATED URINARY TRACT INFECTION

# Rule out obstruction.

When patients who require parenteral therapy are afebrile, clinically stable,

and can take oral medication, convert to oral therapy based on the

identification and susceptibility of the isolate.

# Duration

Treat for 5 days with fluoroquinolones or 7 days with non-fluoroquinolone

antibiotics.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Empirical treatment

# PO therapy options

Preferred:

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h R,DI for 7 days](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

*Avoid trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in the first and third trimesters

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

< OR >

[Nitrofurantoin SA 100 mg PO q12h R,O, CrCl =/>30mL/min, for 7 days](psozid-nitrofurantoin-sa-7ds-100-mg-po-bid)

*Avoid nitrofurantoin in the third trimester

*Not for infections outside of the bladder

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-nitrofurantoin-sa-7ds-100-mg-po-bid)

Primary alternatives:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h R for 7 days](psozid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

< OR >

[Fosfomycin 3 gm sachet PO every other day M x 3 doses](psozid-fosfomycin-3gm-po-qotherday-for-3doses)

*Not for infections outside of the bladder

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-fosfomycin-3gm-po-qotherday-for-3doses)

< OR >

[Cefpodoxime 400 mg PO q12h R for 7 days](psozid2-cefpodoxime-400mg-po-bid-7ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefpodoxime-400mg-po-bid-7ds)

Secondary alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h R,DI for 5 days](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-5ds-500mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-5ds-500mg-po-bid)

# IV therapy options

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV ONCE STAT M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

History of ESBL or severe beta-lactam allergy:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ertapenem 1 gm IV ONCE STAT R,O](psjizid-ertapenem-1gm-once-er-uc)

History of Pseudomonas or Gram-negative MDR bacteria:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV ONCE STAT R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV ONCE STAT R](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-once-er-uc)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment for specific pathogens based on susceptibilities

# Enterobacteria including E. coli, Klebsiella, and Proteus

Preferred:

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h R for 7 days](psozid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-7days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-7days)

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV ONCE STAT M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h R,DI for 7 days](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

*Avoid trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole in the first and third trimesters

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

# Staphylococcus aureus

S. aureus is an uncommon urinary tract pathogen and presence in the urine may be

due to hematogenous seeding from another site. Blood cultures are indicated to

rule out bacteremia in patients who have S. aureus isolated from the urine.

Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Pseudomonas

[Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO q12h R,DI for 5 days](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-750mg-po-bid-5ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-750mg-po-bid-5ds)

< OR >

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV ONCE STAT R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV ONCE STAT R](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-once-er-uc)

# Enterococcus

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin 1000 mg PO q8h R for 7 days](psozid2-amoxicillin-1000mg-po-tid-7days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-amoxicillin-1000mg-po-tid-7days)

< OR >

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV ONCE STAT R](psjizid-ampicillin-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Alternatives:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Fosfomycin 3 gm sachet PO every other day M x 3 doses](psozid-fosfomycin-3gm-po-qotherday-for-3doses)

*Not for infections outside of the bladder

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-fosfomycin-3gm-po-qotherday-for-3doses)

< OR >

[Nitrofurantoin SA 100 mg PO q12h R,O, CrCl =/>30 mL/min, for 7 days](psozid-nitrofurantoin-sa-7ds-100-mg-po-bid)

*Avoid nitrofurantoin in the third trimester

*Not for infections outside of the bladder

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-nitrofurantoin-sa-7ds-100-mg-po-bid)

< OR >

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV ONCE STAT R](psjizid-vancomycin-15-mg-kg-iv-once-stat-er-uc)

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# COMPLICATED UTI (NO CATHETER)

# Complicated UTI is an infection beyond the bladder accompanied by symptoms

# including fever/other signs of systemic illness, flank pain, and costovertebral

# tenderness. This includes pyelonephritis and febrile or bacteremic UTI.

NOT signs or symptoms: abnormal urinalysis alone, pyuria, falls, change in urine

odor or color, delirium (acute mental status change, confusion) without systemic

signs of infection. These may occur in patients with a UTI but alone are

inadequate for diagnosis and empiric treatment.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

For patients without signs or symptoms of UTI:

[Asymptomatic bacteriuria \(Outpatient Antimicrobial CDSS\)](orzid3-gmenu-asymp-bacteriuria)

For patients presenting with septic shock from a suspected urinary tract

infection:

[Sepsis or Shock with Suspected Urinary Tract Infection](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-sepsis-suspected-uro-sepsis)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Duration

Treat for 5 days with fluoroquinolones or 7 days with non-fluoroquinolone

organisms, presence of obstruction, underlying renal disease, immunosuppression,

and neurologic or structural abnormality in some cases. Often therapy can be

completed with an oral agent pending clinical stability and susceptibility

testing.

CUTANEOUS ABSCESS

Incise and drain and cover the site with a dry dressing.  For small abscesses,

If the patient is neutropenic, has multiple lesions, or has fever or

leukocytosis, antimicrobial treatment may be necessary.  Contact Infectious

Diseases for assistance.

# Uncomplicated diverticulitis not requiring admission and not immunocompromised

Antimicrobials not indicated

# Uncomplicated diverticulitis requiring admission or immunocompromised

Duration of therapy: Treatment duration  depends on clinical response, typically

requiring 7-10 days of antimicroibal therapy.

Preferred:

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV once STAT R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT DI](orz-set-abx-cefazolin-2gm-iv-metro-500mg-iv-once-stat)

< OR >

[Piperacillin-Tazobactam 3.375g IV once STAT R](psjizid-pip-tazo-3-375-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV once STAT R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV once STAT](orz-set-abx-cipro-400mg-metro-500mg-iv-once-stat)

[DI]

# Complicated diverticulitis (perforation, abscess, fistula, obstruction) OR meets

# sepsis criteria OR patient is immunocompromised

Consult General Surgery

Duration of therapy: Treatment duration depends on clinical response and source

control, typically requiring 10-14 days of antimicrobial therapy.

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

< OR >

[Meropenem 1 gm IV once STAT R,O](psjizid-meropenem-1gm-iv-once-er-uc)

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC EPIDIDYMITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# EPIDIDYMITIS AND EPIDIDYMO-ORCHITIS

Epididymitis is inflammation of the epididymis and when testicles are involved

is referred to as epididymo-orchitis. Acute epididymitis is the most common

cause of scrotal pain in adults. Other features include scrotal erythema and

edema, pyuria, dysuria, thickened epididymis, swollen testis, and is usually

unilateral. It is primarily caused by infection but can also result from trauma

and autoimmune diseases. Testicular torsion should be ruled out before

treatment. Most cases in men aged 35 and older, those with recent urinary tract

instrumentation or surgery (e.g., prostate biopsy, vasectomy) are associated

with enteric Gram-negative rods. Most cases in men under age 35 are associated

with N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis. Resistant organisms are more likely if

the patient has been in the hospital for more than 48 hours or received a course

of antibiotics. There is increasing resistance in urinary pathogens to

ciprofloxacin.

A urine analysis, urine culture and urine nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)

should be performed in all cases of suspected epididymitis before starting

treatment to guide therapy:

[Lab menu](orzid2-gmenu-abx-lab-menu)

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for

treatment. Refer to the Urogenital section of the Antimicrobial CDSS for more

information.

Patients with bacterial epididymitis treated with antibiotics should improve

within two or three days. If no improvement is noted, other causes of scrotal

pain and referral to a urologist should be considered.

Management should include bed rest, analgesics, and scrotal elevation. Older men

should have their residual urinary volume checked. If the residual volume is

elevated, the patient should be seen by a urologist as epididymitis is unlikely

to respond if the prostate is blocking the vas deferens.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Empirical treatment in men who practice insertive anal intercourse

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once \($\) M < AND > levofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h](orz-set-abx-op-ceftr-500mg-im-x1-levoflox-500mg-qday-10days)

for 10 days ($) [R, DI]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-ceftr-500mg-im-x1-levoflox-500mg-qday-10days)

# Empirical treatment in men who do not practice insertive anal intercourse

# Age >/= 35 years or

# Recent urinary tract instrumentation or urinary tract surgery (e.g., prostate

# biopsy, vasectomy):

Preferred:

[Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h \($\) R, DI for 10 days](psozid2-levofloxacin-10ds-750mg-po-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-levofloxacin-10ds-750mg-po-qday)

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC FOOT ULCER W/ INFECT SURR TISSUES
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# DIABETES-RELATED FOOT INFECTIONS (DIABETIC FOOT INFECTIONS-DFI)

# Wound Cultures:

If there are no systemic symptoms of infection or at least 2 local symptoms

(pain, erythema > 0.5cm, purulent drainage, warmth), do not culture or treat

with abx.

Do NOT:

-Culture a wound that appears uninfected (at least 2 of following: local pain,

erythema >0.5cm, purulent drainage)

-Swab the wound to obtain a culture

-Culture without first cleaning and debriding a wound DFI Do:

-Obtain culture by deep tissue biopsy after cleaning and debriding the wound

# Imaging:

-An x-ray is recommended for all new foot ulcers in patients with diabetes to

evaluate for deformity, bony destruction, soft tissue gas, and/or foreign

bodies. Antimicrobials aren't indicated unless local cellulitis or systemic

infectious symptoms are present.

[Click here for Osteomyelitis Evaluation **Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS](orzid2-gmenu-osteomyelitis-evaluation)

# INFECTION SEVERITY (IWGDF/IDSA Classification)

# __________________________________________________________________

# Uninfected DFI (Class 1/Uninfected): Chronic ulceration without s/s infection

-if no pain, erythema > 0.5cm, purulent drainage, do not culture or treat

Do not culture wound -Do not treat with antibiotics If osteomyelitis identified

arrange for bone biopsy --hold antibiotics

# _________________________________________________________________

# Infected DFI (Class 2/Mild):

At least two of the following are present: -Local swelling or induration

-Erythema >0.5cm but <2cm around wound -Local tenderness or pain -Local

increased warmth -Purulent drainage

# Primarily Outpatient Treatment:

Duration of therapy: 1-2 weeks

# Preferred Regimens:

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h x 7 days R](psozid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-7days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-7days)

< OR >

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID for 7 days R](psozid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

# Treatment with previous MRSA infection or severe PCN allergy:

[Beta-lactam Reaction Assessment](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid x 7 days R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

< OR >

[Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 7 days DI,O](psozid2-linezolid-600mg-po-bid-x7days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-linezolid-600mg-po-bid-7days)

# __________________________________________________________________

# Infected DFI (Class 3/Moderate):

-Erythema extending >2cm from the wound margin, and/or -Tissue deeper than skin

and subcutaneous tissues (e.g., tendon, muscle, joint, and bone)

# Outpatient/Often Hospitalized Treatment:

Oral or IV with change to PO with improvement

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-amox-clav-875-bid-tmp-sulfa-1ds-7days)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV ONCE STAT M < AND > vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-iv-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-once-stat)

# Infected DFI (Class 4/Severe):

Infection with associated systemic manifestations as indicated by 2 or more of

the following: -Fever, Tachycardia, Leukocytosis, Hypotension, Sepsis,

Necrotizing infection

Duration: usually 2-4 weeks, unless source control/amputation occurs

Obtain cultures of inflamed ulcer or wound to permit targeted antimicrobial

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC FURUNCLES, CARBUNCLES, CUT ABSCESS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

FURUNCLES AND CARBUNCLES

Localized purulent infections include furuncles, carbuncles and cutaneous

abscesses. Nearly all are caused by Staphylococcus aureus. A furuncle is a

inflamed nodule that usually develops as a complication of folliculitis. A

carbuncle is a more extensive lesion that extends further into the subcutaneous

tissue.  Contact a wound care nurse for more information.

Incision and drainage is the mainstay of therapy for carbuncles, cutaneous

abscesses, and large furuncles.

The decision to administer antibiotics directed against S. aureus as an adjunct

to incision and drainage should be made based on the presence of systemic

inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) or in patients with markedly impaired

host defenses.

# For recurrent skin abscesses in addition to culture and antibiotic therapy

# recommended consider a decolonization regimen.

[Select here for Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization](orzid3-gmenu-abx-sa-decolonization)

# Mild infection: Purulent infection without systemic signs of infection

Recommend incision and drainage. No antibiotic indicated.

# Moderate Infection: Purulent infection with signs of systemic infection.

Recommend incision and drainage. Culture material and use results to guide

therapy.

Treat for 5 days and extend/modify treatment if not improved in this time.

# Preferred treatment

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO bid for 5 days \($\) R](psozid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-x5days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-x5days)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid \($\) R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-5days-1ds-tab-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-5days-1ds-tab-bid)

# Alternatives

[Doxycycline 100 mg po BID \($\) DI](psozid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-5d)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-5d)

# If methicillin-RESISTANT Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is suspected or proved

[Doxycycline 100 mg po BID \($\) DI](psozid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-5d)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-5d)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID \($\) R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-5days-1ds-tab-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-5days-1ds-tab-bid)

# Severe Infections:

Patients who have failed incision and drainage along with oral antibiotics

or those with SIRS or for infections in those with neutropenia or diminished

neutrophil function.

Recommend incision and drainage. Culture material and use results to guide

therapy.

Treat for 5 days. Reevaluate patient and extend or modify treatment if not

improved in this time.

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV STAT \($\) R](psjizid-vancomycin-15-mg-kg-iv-once-stat-er-uc)

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC IMMUNOCOM NEUT FEVER
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# NEUTROPENIC FEVER

The risk of severe, rapidly progressive infections increases when the absolute

neutrophil count (ANC, segmented neutrophils plus bands) is less than 500

cells/microliter. The risk increases dramatically when the ANC is <100

cells/microliter. Because of these risks, patients with fever and neutropenia

to this degree should receive empirical antimicrobial therapy immediately.

Empirical therapy should also be given to patients with fever and ANC 500-1000

cells/microliter when the concentration is expected to be <500 cells/microliter

within the next 48 hours. For this purpose, fever is defined as a single

temperature greater than 38.3 degrees Celsius.

# Initial therapy

Since infection can be rapidly progressive and severe, broad-spectrum

antimicrobials are given urgently to patients with neutropenic fever as defined

above. Vancomycin should only be given when there are clear indications for its

use.

Candidates for empirical treatment with oral antimicrobials include those who

are febrile but who have no evidence of focal infection or signs or symptoms of

severe disease, like hypotension. Outpatient antimicrobials for neutropenic

fever must be ordered only in consultation with Hematology-Oncology or

Infectious Diseases.

# Treatment

[If patient IS a candidate for oral therapy](orzid3-gmenu-neut-cand-oral-therapy)

[If patient is NOT a candidate for oral therapy](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-neut-fever-cand-not-oral-thera)

[Link to a scoring tool that identifies low risk patients for oral therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-scoring-tool)

# Modification to therapy

Refer to the Systemic Infections section of the Antimicrobial CDSS

Hughes WT Clin Infect Dis 2002, 34: 730

Rolston KVI Clin Infect Dis 2004, 39: S44

Sipsas NV Cancer 2005, 103: 1103

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC LYME ACUTE NEURO DISEASE
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# ACUTE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH LYME DISEASE

Neurological disease is a common manifestation of Lyme Disease that typically

occurs within weeks to months after the tick bite. Unilateral or bilateral

facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy) can be treated with oral antimicrobials. Other

neurological manifestations, including meningitis, require treatment with

intravenous antimicrobials.

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases

# Duration of therapy

Treat for at least 14 days. Longer durations, up to 21 days for facial nerve

palsy and 28 days for other neurologic disease, may be required in severe cases.

# Treatment of isolated facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy)

Preferred:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI](psozid2-doxycycline-14ds-100mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-14ds-100mg-po-bid)

For pregnant patients or those with contraindications to doxycycline:

[Amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h \($\) R](psozid2-amoxicillin-14ds-500mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-amoxicillin-14ds-500mg-po-tid)

# Treatment of neurological disease other than facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT \($\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Carditis is a rare manifestation of Lyme Disease and typically occurs within one

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC LYME DISEASE PROPHYLAXIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# LYME DISEASE PROPHYLAXIS

Patients who have been bitten while in endemic areas of New England, Mid-

Atlantic States, Minnesota, and Wisconsin where local rate of Ixodes spp. tick

infection rate with Borrelia burgdorferi in an endemic area may be treated with

prophylactic antibiotics for prevention of Lyme disease. Using a wait and see

method by monitoring for signs and symptoms of Lyme disease is also an

acceptable approach in patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick.

# All following criteria must be met to be considered for prophylactic treatment

1. Doxycycline is not contraindicated (i.e. allergy, pregnant, lactating)

2. Attached tick is reliably identified as an adult or nymphal Ixodes spp.

[Ixodes spp. identification](orz-gtx-abx-tick-identification-link)

3. Tick is attached for greater than or equal to 36 hours based on degree of

tick engorgement with blood or likely time of exposure to tick infested area.

4. Prophylaxis must be started within 72 hours after time tick was removed.

5. Bite occurs in a highly endemic area.

[CDC Lyme Disease Case Map](orz-gtx-abx-cdc-lyme-disease-case-map)

# Prophylactic treatment if all of the above criteria are met

[Doxycycline PO 200mg once \($\) DI](psczid-doxycycline-200mg-stat)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC MORE ABOUT CELLULITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# THE APPROACH TO CELLULITIS

In addition to antimicrobial therapy, several non-pharmacological treatments

improve the outcome of cellulitis. Elevation and immobilization of the

affected limb reduces swelling. Heat reduces discomfort.

Prevent tinea pedis infection by keeping feet clean and dry. In patients with

peripheral edema, good skin hygiene and support stockings reduce the incidence

of recurrent infection.

In many cases of cellulitis, the affected area is usually not well-

differentiated from unaffected areas of the skin. Erysipelas is a special case

with typically a well-defined border and raised, orange-peel appearance.

For treatment of erysipelas refer to the Soft Tissue Section of the inpatient or

outpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

Use broad-spectrum therapy for cellulitis arising in feet of patients with

advanced diabetes.

[Foot ulcer in patient with diabetes mellitus](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-foot-ulcer-with-dm)

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC NECROTIZING INFECTIONS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

NECROTIZING INFECTIONS

Call Surgery immediately and consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Necrotizing infections involve tissues skin and/or deeper structures, including

fascia and muscle.These infections destroy tissue, often rapidly, and are

often fatal if not treated promptly and appropriately.Necrotizing infections

usually result from trauma, surgery, and/or ischemia.These infections can be

monomicrobial (e.g., with streptococci or clostridia) or polymicrobial (usually

with a mixture of aerobes and anaerobes).Fournier gangrene is usually

associated with mixed infection.Myonecrosis is most commonly associated with

Clostridium species.

Necrotizing infections differ from cellulitis in several ways.Necrotic

infections typically have one or more of the following: (1) severe, constant

pain, (2) bullae, (3) bruising or necrosis of overlying skin, (4) gas in tissues

which can be felt or seen on images, (5) edema that extends beyond areas of

erythema, (6) local anesthesia, and (7) signs of systemic toxicity, such as

fever, leukocytosis, delirium, or renal failure.

Necrotizing infections must be treated with both antimicrobial therapy and

surgical procedures (excision and/or drainage).Call surgery to see the patient

immediately in all cases.Obtain tissue and blood cultures and begin empirical

antimicrobials.For several necrotic diseases and/or pathogens, a combination

of two antimicrobials is recommended including a bactericidal antimicrobial

active at the cell wall or membrane (e.g., beta-lactam or glycopeptide) and an

antimicrobial that rapidly inhibits protein synthesis and thus inhibits toxin

production, typically clindamycin.

Repeat debridement should be performed daily until no further debridement is

necessary. Antibiotic therapy should be tailored as soon as culture results

become available.

Administer antibiotics until further debridement is no longer necessary, the

patient has improved clinically, and fever has been absent for 48-72 hours.

# Empirical antimicrobials

[Empirical therapy of necrotizing infections](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-necrot-infect-emp-therapy)

menus.Name: ORZID GMENU ER/UC OTITIS EXTERNA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# OTITIS EXTERNA

# Acute Localized Disease

Often due to furunculosis and usually associated with Staphylococcus aureus.

Treat mild cases with moist local heat. For cases with cellulitis or deep

invasion, incision and drainage as well as systemic antibiotics may be needed.

Refer to the Furuncules and Carbuncles page for antibiotic recommendations.

[Furuncles and carbuncles](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-furuncles-carbuncles-cut-abscess)

__________________________________________________________________

# Acute diffuse and chronic otitis externa

Most commonly associated with Pseudomonas aerogenosa and Staphylococcus

aureus/epidermidis. Irrigate to remove cerumen, desquamated skin and purulent

material which can improve effectiveness of topical antibiotics. Avoid products

that contain neomycin if the tympanic membrane is perforated.

Treat for 7 to 10 days

# Preferred treatment if tympanic membrane is intact

[Neomycin-polymixin-hydrocortisone ear drops 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) QID](psozid2-neomycin-polymyxin-hydroc-ear-4-drps-qid-7days)

($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-neomycin-polymyxin-hydroc-ear-4-drps-qid-7days)

# Alternative if tympanic membrane is perforated or allergy to preferred treatmen

[Ciprofloxacin-Dexamethasone otic 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) BID \($\) M](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-bid-7days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-bid-7days)

__________________________________________________________________

# Complicated Cases

For cases resistant to topical therapy alone, diabetic patients,

immunocompromised patients, cases where infection has spread beyond ear canal

and in those where topical therapy cannot be delivered effectively. Culture

secretions to guide therapy.

# Empirical Treatment

In addition to topical therapy above <ADD>

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID \($\) R,DI](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-bid)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# PHARYNGITIS AND TONSILLITIS

Most cases are viral, primarily due to adenovirus. Aside from streptococcal and

gonococcal pharyngitis, antimicrobials are not indicated. For gonococcal

pharyngitis, use link below for recommendations.

[Treatment of Gonorrheal Infections - Opt CDSS, change parental orders to STAT](orzid3-gmenu-gonococcal)

Consider HIV screening for patients with pharyngitis

[HIV Rapid Test](lrtzhiv-rapid-qualitative)

# Streptococcal Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis

Diagnosis of group A streptococcal (GAS) infection is made through detection by

rapid PCR and should be reserved for patients who have a moderate to high risk

of GAS infection according to the Modified Centor Score. Use link below for

Modified Centor score criteria and for more details.

[More About Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis and Modified Centor score - Opt CDSS](orzid3-gmenu-more-about-pharyngitis)

[Rapid Strep A throat PCR testing lab order](lrtz-strep-a-pcr)

# PCR Negative, Viral and Other Non-GAS Causes of Pharyngitis Treatment

Antimicrobials are not indicated

# GAS Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis Treatment

Preferred

[Penicillin V 500 mg PO BID for 10 days \($\) R](psozid2-penicillin-v-500mg-po-bid-10ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-penicillin-v-500mg-po-bid-10ds)

< OR >

[Benzathine penicillin 1.2 million units IM once STAT \($$$\) M](psczid-benzathine-penciillin-1-2mu-im-once-er-uc)

Primary alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO BID x10days \($\) R](psozid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-x10days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-x10days)

Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

[Azithromycin 500 mg PO once on day one then 250mg PO qday for 4 days \($\)](psozid2-azith-500mg-po-once-then-250mg-po-qday-x4ds)

[M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-azith-500mg-po-once-then-250mg-po-qday-x4ds)
