# EMPIRIC TREATMENT: HOSPITAL ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (HAP)

Development of pneumonia 48 hours or more after hospital admission.

# Empiric Treatment (see below for MRSA history or clinically unstable patients)

Obtain MRSA nasal PCR and sputum culture before antibiotics, whenever possible.

Narrow therapy based on results of culture and susceptibility tests. Discontinue

MRSA and/or Pseudomonas coverage if not isolated from respiratory cultures.

[Re-evaluate Nosocomial pneumonia at 72 hours](orzid2-gmenu-abx-re-evaluate-72hrs-n-pneumo)

Preferred:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV STAT R](psjizid-pna-cefepime-2gm-iv-stat-er-uc)

<OR >

[Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV STAT R](psjizid-pna-piperacillin-tazobactam-4-5-gm-stat-er-uc)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV STAT R](psjizid-pna-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-stat-er-uc)

# History of MRSA infection/colonization

# < OR > clinically unstable (e.g., intubation, hypotension)

ADD MRSA coverage to a regimen above. Discontinue MRSA coverage if MRSA nasal

PCR negative.

# Clinically unstable (ICU level care, hypotensive, intubation)

# < AND > history of multi-drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# SEPSIS AND SEPTIC SHOCK

Per the Sepsis-3 task force, sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ

dysfunction caused by dysregulated host response to infection.

Septic shock is a subset of sepsis in which profound circulatory, cellular, and

metabolic abnormalities occur. Septic shock requires vasopressor therapy and is

associated with in-hospital mortality greater than 40%.

Early intervention is crucial to prevention of death from sepsis. Antimicrobials

active against likely pathogens, based on source infection, and supportive

treatment to maintain vascular perfusion should be initiated immediately (within

the first hour of patient presentation). Reassess antimicrobial therapy daily to

narrow therapeutic spectrum when culture and susceptibility data are available.

# Sepsis/septic shock management bundle (includes empiric antimicrobial treatment)

[Emergency department \(ED\)](orz-gmenu-uc-ed-sepsis-2)

Utilize management bundle above for treatment in patients. The link below is

provided to view antimicrobial recommendations as a reference.

[Sepsis antimicrobial treatment recommendations](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-sepsis-protocol-antimicrobials)

# SEPSIS WITH INTRAABDOMINAL INFECTION OR UNCLEAR INFECTIOUS SOURCE

# Consult Infectious Diseases

Empirical regimens listed below have broad coverage of likely pathogens based on

infectious site. Resistant gram-negative rods and MRSA coverage is not necessary

in most patients except those with recent isolates of these organisms. Strongly

consider rapid de-escalation of therapy in the first 24-48 hours based on MRSA

nares, isolated pathogen(s), and patient response to therapy. Refer to pathogen

specific sections of the Antimicrobial CDSS for additional treatment

recommendations.

# Empirical Treatment

Preferred:

[Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-once-er-uc-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Penicillin allergy:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV once STAT](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Severe beta-lactam reaction:

[Treatment of Sepsis with Severe Beta-Lactam Reaction](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-sepsis-severe-beta-lactam-reaction)

# Recent MRSA isolate

[<ADD> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV once STAT to one of the above regimens](psjizid-vancomycin-15-mg-kg-iv-once-stat-er-uc)

# Clinically unstable (ICU level care/hypotensive/tachycardic) AND recent multi-

# drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate

[<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV once STAT to one of the above regimens](psjizid-tobramycin-5-mg-kg-iv-er-uc)

*If CrCl < 50 ml/min: 2 mg/kg once STAT (use order above and modify dose)

Pharmacy to follow

# Consider abdominal CT

# TREATMENT OF SEPSIS WITH SEVERE BETA-LACTAM REACTION

[For more info, refer to Assessment of Beta-Lactam Reaction document CLICK HERE](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

# The following regimen(s) should only be used if the patient has a history of a

# severe reaction to a Beta-Lactam antimicrobial including but not limited to:

Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN)

Anaphylaxis

Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

Generalized exanthematous pustulosis

Hemolytic anemia

Immune hepatitis

Interstitial nephritis

Mucosal, cardiovascular, or respiratory system involvement

Reaction needed medical intervention

Skin desquamation

Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS)

Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)

# Treatment

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV once STAT](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-once-er-uc)

# Recent MRSA isolate

[<ADD> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h to above regimen](psjizid-vancomycin-15-mg-kg-iv-once-stat-er-uc)

# Clinically unstable (ICU level care/hypotensive/tachycardic) AND recent multi-

# drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate

[<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV x 1 dose to above regimen](psjizid-tobramycin-5-mg-kg-iv-er-uc)

*If CrCl less than 50 ml/min: 2 mg/kg x 1 dose (use order above and modify dose)

Pharmacy to follow

# SEPSIS WITH SUSPECTED ENDOCARDITIS

Consider consulting Infectious Diseases if endocarditis is not strongly

suspected as the source of infection.

Empirical regimens listed below have broad coverage of likely pathogens based on

infectious site. Resistant gram-negative rods and MRSA coverage is not necessary

in most patients except those with recent isolates of these organisms. Strongly

consider rapid de-escalation of therapy in the first 24-48 hours based on MRSA

nares, isolated pathogen(s), and patient response to therapy. Refer to pathogen

specific sections of the Antimicrobial CDSS for additional treatment

recommendations.

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV once STAT](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-once-er-uc)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(ER\)](orzid-gmenu-er-uc-abx-general-information-ed)

# SEVERE SINUSITIS

Community-acquired bacterial sinusitis is most often due to Streptococcus

pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenza or Moraxella catarrhalis. Group A

Streptococci, Staphylococcus aureus and anaerobes are isolated less frequently.

For patients who present with severe symptoms (high fever (>/= 102 degrees

Fahrenheit, >/= 39 degrees Celsius) and purulent nasal discharge for 3-4

consecutive days or facial pain lasting for at least 3-4 consecutive days at the

beginning of illness), initiate empiric antimicrobials and obtain CT of sinuses

to determine the extent of infection. If the CT shows extension of sinusitis

infection into surrounding structures (i.e. the cranium or orbit) consult ENT

immediately. Closely monitor all patients who present with severe signs and

symptoms to ensure that signs and symptoms improve within 72 hours.

# Outpatient Treatment

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 7 days](psozid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

Alternatives:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 7 days](psozid2-cefdinir-300mg-po-bid-7days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefdinir-300mg-po-bid-7days)

< OR >

broaden coverage, switch to different antimicrobial class and treat 7 days. If

symptoms continue to worsen or there is no improvement after 3-5 more days of

consultation is recommended. If sinuses are aspirated, specimens should be

# SPONTANEOUS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS (SBP)

SBP is infection of the peritoneal cavity in the absence of apparent trauma or

other obvious cause. SBP occurs primarily in people with end-stage liver disease

and ascites. The diagnosis is made when a peritoneal fluid sample has >/= 250

polymorphonuclear leukocyte cells per microliter, or when bacterial pathogens

are isolated.

Long-term SBP prophylaxis is indicated for patients who experience a first

episode of SBP.

# SBP

Duration of therapy: Treat for 5 days

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV once STAT  R,DI](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-once-er-uc)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Prophylaxis in a patient with a previous SBP episode

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q24h R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-90days-1ds-tab-po-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-90days-1ds-tab-po-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-ciprofloxacin-500mg-po-qday-prophylaxis)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Prophylaxis in a patient with cirrhosis and variceal hemorrhage

Treat initially with an intravenous antimicrobial then step down to an oral

antimicrobial when the patient can tolerate oral treatment.

Duration of therapy: Treat for a total of 7 days (intravenous and oral)

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV once STAT M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-once-er-uc)

Alternative:

# PURULENT SKIN/SOFT TISSUE INFECTIONS

Includes furuncles/boils, carbuncles and cutaneous abscesses with or without

surrounding inflammation. The predominant pathogen is Staphylococcus aureus

(MSSA or MRSA).

Incision and drainage are recommended whenever feasible. Adjunctive antibiotics

are typically recommended. Incision and drainage alone are reasonable based on

patient preferences when abscess is smaller, limited surrounding inflammation,

no systemic signs of infections, and/or limited comorbidities.

# For recurrent skin abscesses in addition to culture and antibiotic therapy

# recommend considering a decolonization regimen.

[Click Here for Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization *Inpatient CDSS](orzid2-gmenu-abx-staphylococcus-aureus-decolonization)

Surgical drainage, scaling and antimicrobial treatment are essential and tooth

extraction is required in most cases. All patients should be referred to the

dental service for assessment and direction of treatment. Empirical coverage for

likely pathogens (streptococci, Peptostreptococcus, Finegoldia, Bacteriodes and

coverage for Pseudomonas aeruginosa.

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX ABOUT THE CDSS
menus.Text:
# ABOUT THE ANTIMICROBIAL COMPUTERIZED DECISION SUPPORT SYSTEM (CDSS)

The Antimicrobial CDSS is a tool within the Computerized Patient Record System

that offers antimicrobial prescribing advice to clinicians at the point of order

entry. The system is structured as an order menu decision tree that contains

quick orders pre-programmed with appropriate antimicrobial regimens for specific

infectious diseases.

# Goals

Improve patient outcomes, reduce rates of microbial resistance, prevent adverse

patient outcomes, optimize costs and improve providers' lives. In addition to

these goals, the program fulfills antimicrobial stewardship quality standards

implemented by the Joint Commission.

# Rationale

*Improved patient outcomes

In a 2013 study, Minneapolis Veterans Affairs Medical Center (MVAMC)

antimicrobial courses ordered through the Antimicrobial CDSS were significantly

more likely to be appropriate from start to completion, (44%) compared to non-

CDSS courses (33%, P = 0.013). This is consistent with other studies that have

shown significant improvement in appropriate use of antimicrobials when CDSS

programs are utilized.

*Restricted formulary

The Minneapolis VAHCS has a restricted antimicrobial formulary. A restricted

formulary reduces cost of health care and is an integral part of antimicrobial

stewardship. The Antimicrobial CDSS provides a method of formulary restriction

that doesn't require a call back from pharmacy or a prior authorization for the

antimicrobial to be approved.

[More information on antimicrobial restriction policy](orzid2-gmenu-abx-abx-restriction-policy)

*Increased efficiency

Along with being able to order restricted antimicrobials without a prior

authorization or call back from pharmacy, the Antimicrobial CDSS provides quick

orders pre-programmed with appropriate antimicrobial regimens for specific

infectious diseases. Using the system saves time and increases the efficiency of

the ordering provider.

# Features

The CDSS has been developed locally with input from a broad, representative

group of clinicians. Recommendations have been based on local susceptibility

patterns, clinical evidence, local preferences, and national guidelines. The

CDSS provides a way for clinicians to select alternative drugs when the

recommended drugs are contraindicated.

Detailed instructions can be found in the link below.

[How to use the CDSS](orzid2-gmenu-abx-how-to-use-cdss)

References

Dellit et al. Clinical Infectious Diseases 2007, 44:159-7

Filice et al. Infection Control and Hospital Epidemiology. 2013, 34.6

Rawson et al. Clinical Microbiology and Infection. 2017, 1e9

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX ABX RESTRICTION POLICY
menus.Text:
# ANTIMICROBIAL RESTRICTION POLICY

Medication orders placed using the CDSS system will NOT require Infectious

Disease approval. Because prescribing advice within the system has been

developed with input from a broad, representative group of clinicians and the

recommendations that have emerged are based on site-specific susceptibility

patterns, clinical evidence, local preferences, and national guidelines,

INFECTIOUS DISEASE APPROVAL FOR RESTRICTED ANTIMICROBIALS WILL NOT BE NEEDED at

participating VA sites. Clinicians are still encouraged to seek advice from

Infectious Diseases whenever it would be helpful.

Restricted antimicrobials ordered outside the CDSS system will continue to need

ID approval.

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# ACNE

Acne is an inflammatory skin condition caused by excess sebum production, gland

obstruction and infection with Cutibacterum acnes. Early disease manifests with

black heads and white heads and little inflammation. Small papules and pustules

are present in mild disease. Severe disease occurs when comedones, papules,

pustules and less often cysts are present.

The goal of treatment is prevention and reeducation of new comedones and

creating an environment that is inhibitory for C. acnes. General skin care

treatment measures include utilizing gentle skin cleansers, avoiding aggressive

scrubbing, using non-comedogenic skin products, and avoiding picking of lesions.

Diet's role in therapy remains uncertain.

Non-Antimicrobial therapy includes benzoyl peroxide topical/wash, salicylic acid

topical, and tretinoin topical. These agents can be used as monotherapy in early

disease and in addition to antimicrobial treatment in mild to severe disease.

# Early Disease:

[Clindamycin 1% lotion topically q12h \($\) M](psjzid-clindamycin-1-lotion-topically-q12h)

< OR >

[Erythromycin 2% gel topically q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-erythromycin-2-gel-topically-q12h)

# Mild Disease:

[Erythromycin 2% gel topically q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-erythromycin-2-gel-topically-q12h)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 50 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 12 weeks](psjzid2-doxycycline-12wks-50mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Minocycline 50 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 12 weeks](psjzid2-minocylcine-12wks-50mg-po-q12h)

# Severe Disease:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h  \($\) DI for 12 weeks <AND> erythromycin 2% gel](orz-set-abx-doxy-100mg-po-bid-12wks-erythromycin-2-gel-q12h)

topically q12h

topically q12h

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ACUTE BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS

Acute bacterial prostatitis typically presents with fever, dysuria, chills,

malaise, myalgia, pelvic or perianal pain. On exam, the prostate gland is tense,

boggy, and extremely tender. The urinalysis reveals pyuria, and the urine

culture is positive. Men with dysuria and fever but without pyuria and/or

bacteriuria should be seen by a urologist. If there is any suspicion of abscess,

especially in men older than 40 years, the patient should be seen by a urologist

and transurethral prostate resection for drainage should be considered.

Most cases in men aged 35 and older, those with recent urinary tract

instrumentation or surgery (e.g., prostate biopsy, vasectomy) are associated

with enteric Gram-negative rods. Most cases in men under age 35 and those who

are at high risk of sexually transmitted infections are associated with N.

gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis. Resistant organisms are more likely if the

patient has been in the hospital for more than 48 hours or received a course of

antibiotics. There is increasing resistance in urinary pathogens to

ciprofloxacin.

A urine Gram stain and culture should be performed in all patients to guide

antimicrobial therapy:

[Lab menu](orzid2-gmenu-abx-lab-menu)

# Duration

There is limited data on duration of antimicrobial treatment for prostatitis. 14

days minimum is required. 4 to 6 weeks may be necessary to completely eradicate

bacteria in the prostate to ensure patient does not progress to chronic

bacterial prostatitis.

# _____________________________________________________________________________

# Empirical treatment

Hydration, bed rest and analgesics are recommended along with antimicrobials

treatment.

# Age < 35 years and those at high risk of sexually transmitted infections

Patient weighing less than 300 lbs:

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once \($\) M <AND> doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-500mg-im-once-doxy-100mg-po-q12h)

14 days

Patients weighing 300 lbs or greater:

[Ceftriaxone 1 gm IM once \($\) M <AND> doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-1gm-im-once-doxy-po-100mg-q12h-gonococc)

14 days

# Age >/= 35 years

Preferred:

[Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h \($\) R, DI for 14 days](psjzid-levofloxacin-750mg-po-q24h)

< OR >

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h \($\) R, DI for 14 days](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

Alternative:

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q12h \($\) R,DI for 14 days](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Lipsky et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2010, 50(12)1641-1652

Mandell chapter: Prostatitis, Epididymitis and Orchitis

Sanford keyword: Prostatitis

Up-To-Date article: Acute Bacterial Prostatitis

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX ANTIVIRAL TREATMENT
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# INFLUENZA ANTIVIRAL THERAPY RECOMMENDATIONS

# Who to Treat:

The decision to treat should be based on clinical symptoms and/or presence of a

high-risk condition and should NOT be delayed until laboratory test results are

available.

It is important to use antiviral drugs early to treat influenza in people who

are very sick with influenza (for example hospitalized people) and people who

are sick with influenza and have a greater chance of getting severe

complications. If a patient is not in a high-risk group or is not hospitalized,

healthcare providers should use clinical judgment to guide treatment decisions.

# People who have a greater chance of serious influenza complications include:

*Adults aged 65 years or older

*Persons who have chronic pulmonary (including

asthma) or cardiovascular (except isolated hypertension), renal, hepatic,

hematologic, metabolic disorders (including diabetes mellitus), neurologic and

neuro-developmental disorders

*Persons who are immunocompromised due to any

cause (including immunosuppression caused by medications or by HIV infection)

*Pregnant women and women up to 2 weeks after the end of pregnancy

*Persons younger than 19 years of age who are receiving long-term aspirin- or

salicylate-containing medications and who might be at risk for experiencing Reye

syndrome after influenza virus infection *Residents of nursing homes and other

long-term care facilities

*Non-Hispanic Black persons, Hispanic or Latino persons, and American Indian or

Alaska Native persons

*Persons who are extremely obese (BMI greater than or equal to 40)

# Antiviral Treatment:

If indicated, antivirals should be started as soon as possible.  Maximal benefit

occurs when treatment is started within 48 hours of symptom onset.  However,

antivirals should not be withheld if symptoms begin more than 48 hours prior and

the patient meets criteria for treatment and remains severely ill.

# Treatment Dosing:

Zanamivir is not recommended for patients with chronic respiratory diseases such

as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. These patients may have

bronchospasm with zanamivir. If zanamivir must be used, and patients are using

an inhaled bronchodilator, zanamivir should be taken just after the

bronchodilator.

Extending the duration of treatment for oseltamivir or peramivir may be needed

for those patients with prolonged illness or who are immunosuppressed.

# Preferred:

[Oseltamivir 75 mg po bid R for 5 days](psjzid-oseltamivir-75-mg-po-bid-5days)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# **Below is for information only, quick orders are not available

# Alternative:

Requires Infectious Disease Approval

Zanamivir 2 inhalations (2 x 5 mg) BID [O] for 5 days

< OR >

Baloxavir 80 mg PO x1 dose patients wt 80 kg or greater, 40 mg PO x 1 dose for

patients wt < 80 kg [DI]

# Alternative for patients unable to tolerate or absorb oral oseltamivir:

Peramivir may not be available. Contact ID for more information.

Requires Infectious Disease Approval

Hospitalized, high risk:

Peramivir 600 mg IV q24h [R] for 5 days

Acute, uncomplicated:

Peramivir 600mg IV Once [R]

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# References:

Centers for Disease Control (CDC) (Accessed 9/20/23)

https://www.cdc.gov/flu/professionals/antivirals/summary-clinician

UpToDate Seasonal influenza in adults: Treatment

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX APPRO TO BACTEREMIA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# APPROACH TO BACTEREMIA

Bacteremia usually results from a focal infection somewhere in the body. If a

focal infection is not obvious, a careful search should be made beginning with a

detailed history and physical examination.

If a focal infection seems to be the source of the bacteremia, select

antimicrobials active against pathogens likely to be present in the focal

infection. Return to the main menu and select the relevant diagnosis or

syndrome.

# For infections with signs and/or symptoms of severe sepsis, like hypotension or

# end organ dysfunction

[Sepsis, severe sepsis, and septic shock](orzid2-gmenu-sepsis-and-shock)

# Sequence of evaluation

Obtain blood cultures before starting antibiotics when signs or symptoms suggest

bacteremia. Obtain 2 or 3 blood culture sets from different venipuncture sites

within a 24 hour period. When suspicion is strong and the patient's signs and

symptoms have not responded, obtain 2 blood culture sets the next day. For more

information about blood cultures, see recommendations on the Q-drive

Q:\MICROBIOL INFO FOR CLINICIANS\BLOOD CULTURE Recommendations.doc

# Empirical treatment of suspected bacteremia if local infection is not apparent

# and blood cultures are not yet positive

[Suspected bacteremia, blood cultures not yet positive](orzid2-gmenu-abx-susp-bact-bld-cx-not-yet-pos)

Cultures usually become positive after 1 or more days. Usually interim results

are reported first, followed by final identification and sensitivities after

another day or two. Adjust antimicrobials as appropriate as this sequence

unfolds.

# Preliminary results of a positive culture are available

When a focal infection is not apparent, the type of bacteria growing in blood

culture might suggest a focal infection and direct the search for a diagnosis.

When a focal infection is apparent, it may suggest the identity of the bacteria

growing in blood cultures before the laboratory completes its identification.

Preliminary positive results should lead to changes in antimicrobial therapy to

target suspected pathogens, narrow the spectrum, reduce toxicity, and reduce

costs.

[Interim report of Gram-positive cocci in pairs](orzid2-gmenu-int-rpt-gpc-in-pairs)

[Interim report of Gram-positive cocci in pairs and clusters](orzid2-gmenu-int-rpt-gpc-pairs-clusters)

[Interim report of Gram-positive cocci in pairs and chains](orzid2-gmenu-int-rpt-gpc-prs-chains)

[Interim report of Gram-negative bacilli](orzid2-gmenu-int-rpt-gnb)

[Interim report of Gram-negative cocci](orzid2-gmenu-int-rpt-gnc)

[Interim report of Gram-positive bacilli](orzid2-gmenu-int-rpt-gpr)

[Interim report of yeast](orzid2-gmenu-int-rpt-yeast)

References

Mandell Chapter Sepsis, Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX APPRO TO ENDOCARDITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# APPROACH TO ENDOCARDITIS

Infectious Diseases and Cardiology consults are essential for proved cases and

encouraged for suspected cases. See diagnosis page for more information.

[Diagnosis with Duke Criteria](orzid2-gmenu-abx-duke-criteria)

Attempt to identify the pathogen before starting antimicrobials. At least three

sets of blood cultures should be obtained from different venipuncture sites.

These cultures should be drawn at different times with the first and last

culture separated by at least one hour.

For a patient who is not clinically stable, or if the progression of the illness

is rapid, draw 3 sets of blood cultures and then initiate empirical

antimicrobial therapy and/or surgical intervention.

Ascertain whether any antimicrobials were taken during the previous 2 weeks to

help interpret culture results.

Penicillin susceptibility data are used to determine appropriate antimicrobial

therapy for streptococcal endocarditis. Because bacteria in cardiac vegetations

are not actively dividing, and are protected from host defense mechanisms,

bactericidal antimicrobial regimens are necessary to treat bacterial

endocarditis. The minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) cut-off levels used to

select therapy for endocarditis differ from those used to select therapy for

other infectious diseases (see below).

# Penicillin allergy

Beta-lactam antibiotics are more effective than vancomycin for treating

susceptible gram-positive pathogens. For patients with penicillin allergy that

is known or suspected to be class I (anaphylaxis, angioedema, or hives),

penicillin desensitization or therapy with a cephalosporin is usually the best

approach.

[Penicillin Desensitization protocol](orzid2-gmenu-abx-penicillin-desens-protocol)

When gentamicin is used for synergy against gram positive bacteria, serum

concentrations should be 3-4 mcg/ml peak and < 1 mcg/ml trough. Once daily

gentamicin dosing can be used for streptococcal cases but not for staphylococcal

or enterococcal cases.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Baddour et al., Circulation 2015, 132:1-52

Mandell chapter: Endocarditis and intravascular infections

Sanford keyword: Endocarditis

Up-To-Date article: Overview of management of infective endocarditis in adults

Wang et al., JAMA 2018, 320.1:72-83

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX APPROACH TO ACUTE MENINGITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# APPROACH TO ACUTE MENINGITIS

Meningitis is an inflammation of the meninges and tissues surrounding the brain

and spinal cord. It is characterized by an abnormal amount of white blood cells

in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and symptoms include headache, fever, mental

status changes, nuchal rigidity, and nausea.

# Acute Meningitis

The sudden onset of meningeal symptoms within hours to days caused by several

infectious etiologies, including bacterial, viral, fungal and protozoa, as well

as non-infectious etiologies. Bacterial meningitis is the most common type of

meningitis, accounting for up to 90% of cases where a CSF culture was obtained

prior to starting antimicrobials. Non-bacterial meningitis is commonly referred

to as aseptic meningitis (refer to "Negative CSF culture" below for

recommendations).

Patients with acute bacterial meningitis often have severe symptoms and present

soon after onset of infection. The relationship between predisposing factors and

common bacterial pathogen are listed below.

# Predisposing Factors and Common Bacterial Pathogens

*Age 2-50 years - S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis

*Age > 50 years - S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, L. monocytogenes, aerobic

gram-negative bacilli

*Immunocompromised state - S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, L. monocytogenes,

aerobic gram-negative bacilli (including Pseudomonas aeruginosa)

*Basilar skull fracture - S. pneumoniae: H. influenzae, group A and

beta-hemolytic streptococci

*Head trauma: after neurosurgery - Staphylococcus aureus, coagulase-negative

staphylococci (especially Staphylococcus epidermidis), aerobic gram-negative

bacilli (including P. aeruginosa)

# Initial Management of Suspected Acute Bacterial Meningitis

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely,

antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures

should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients

to obtain CSF for establishing diagnosis and determining infectious

organism/susceptibility. Computed tomography (CT) should be performed prior to

LP in some patients (see list below). If CT must be obtained prior to LP or

there is another delay in performing LP, empiric antimicrobials should not be

delayed and initiated immediately after obtaining blood cultures only.

Relative LP contraindications (no absolute contraindications exist):

Anticoagulation therapy or bleeding disorder, spinal epidural abscess, raised

intracranial pressure.

Computed tomography scan should be performed prior to lumbar puncture in cases

with the following: Immunocompromise, history of CNS disease, new onset seizure,

papilledema, abnormal level of consciousness, focal neurologic deficit.

# LP and CSF Analysis

LP opening pressure is often elevated in bacterial meningitis. CSF findings

characteristic of bacterial meningitis include CSF glucose <40mg/dL, CSF to

serum glucose ratio </=0.4, CSF protein concentration >/=200 mg/dL and CSF WBC

>1000 microL.

# Empiric Treatment After Blood Cultures are Drawn, and CSF is Obtained, or if LP

# Must be Delayed

[Community acquired meningitis](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-w-o-grm-stain-res)

[Meningitis associated with trauma or nosocomial infection](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-assoc-trauma)

# Empiric Treatment Based on CSF Gram-Stain Results

When gram stain results are available, adjust antimicrobials to optimize therapy

[Gram-positive diplococci suggesting Streptococcus pneumoniae](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-grm-pos-diplo-s-pneumo)

[Gram-negative diplococci suggesting Neisseria meningitidis](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-grm-neg-dipl-n-mening)

[Gram-positive bacilli/coccobacilli suggesting Listeria monocytogenes](orzid2-gmenu-bac-mening-grm-pos-bacilli-l-monocyto)

[Gram negative bacilli](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-gnb)

# Treatment Based on CSF Isolated Organism

When infectious organism is identified, adjust antimicrobials to optimize therap

[S. pneumoniae](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-s-pneumoniae)

[N. meningitidis](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-n-meningitidis)

[L. monocytogenes](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-l-monocytogenes)

[E. Coli, Pseudomonas, or another organism](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-e-coli-pseudomonas)

# Negative CSF Culture

Patients who have a negative CSF culture but have symptoms and CSF findings

consistent with bacterial meningitis should be treated based on likely pathogen.

Patients with negative CSF culture, symptoms of acute meningitis but have labs

inconsistent with bacterial meningitis should be considered to have aseptic

meningitis. Aseptic meningitis is caused by a variety of non-bacterial

infectious etiologies and non-infectious etiologies. Consult Infectious Disease

for more information.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Mandell chapter: Acute meningitis

Sanford keyword: Meningitis, bacterial, positive gram stain

Tunkel et al., Clin Infect Dis, 2004, 39.1267-84

Up-to-Date Article: Clinical features and diagnosis of acute bacterial

meningitis in adults

Up-to-Date Article: Treatment of bacterial meningitis caused by specific

pathogens in adults

Van de Beek et al., Clin Microbiol Infect, 2016, 22.S37-S62

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# APPROACH TO URINARY TRACT INFECTION (UTI)

# IDSA 2025 complicated and uncomplicated UTI definition updates:

Uncomplicated UTI is an infection confined to the bladder in afebrile women or

men without urinary catheter.

[Uncomplicated urinary tract infection](orzid2-gmenu-abx-uncomp-uti)

Complicated UTI is an infection beyond the bladder and accompanied by symptoms

including fever/other signs of systemic illness. Complicated UTI includes

pyelonephritis, febrile or bacteremic UTI, catheter-associated (CAUTI).

[Complicated UTI without catheter](orzid2-gmenu-abx-complicated-uti-no-catheter)

[Complicated UTI catheter associated](orzid2-gmenu-abx-complicated-uti-catheter-associated)

[Acute prostatitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-acute-bact-prostatitis)

For patients presenting with septic shock from a suspected urinary tract

infection:

[Sepsis or shock with suspected urinary tract infection](orzid2-gmenu-sepsis-suspected-uro-sepsis)

Asymptomatic bacteriuria occurs in patients who have bacteria in the urine but

do not have symptoms of a urinary tract infection.

[Asymptomatic bacteriuria](orzid2-gmenu-abx-asymp-bacteriuria)

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for

treatment:

[Sexually Transmitted Infections and HIV Exposure](orzid2-gmenu-abx-sexually-transmitted-infection)

Candida urinary tract infections are discussed elsewhere:

[Candida urinary tract infections](orzid2-gmenu-abx-candida-uti)

_______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Gupta et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2011, 52(5)e103-20

Trautner et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2025, ciaf459

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ASPIRATION PNEUMONIA

When a larger than usual volume of orogastric content is aspirated,

mechanical/chemical irritation occurs.  Some of these develop into bacterial

pneumonia.

It is reasonable to wait before starting antimicrobials to see if respiratory

impairment improves or worsens before starting bacterial pneumonia treatment, in

hemodynamically stable patients.

Therapy directed towards anaerobic pathogens is usually unnecessary.

Antimicrobial treatment is warranted if pneumonia is confirmed.

# Preferred

See below for prior respiratory isolation of MRSA or P. aeruginosa.

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M  for 5 days](psjizid-pna-ceftriaxone-2-gm-iv-q24h-for-5-days)

< OR >

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h R for 5 days](psjizid-pna-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

# Prior Respiratory Isolation of MRSA within last 12 months:

ADD MRSA coverage to a regimen above or antipseudomonal regimen below.

Obtain cultures/nasal PCR to allow for de-escalation.

# CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

# Initial CDI diagnosis (all are required)

(1) Unexplained diarrhea (e.g., no laxative or increase in tube feed)

(2) New onset diarrhea (e.g., 3 or more unformed stools in 24 hours)

(3) Laboratory confirmation of CDI

[Click here Information on C. difficile lab testing](orzid2-gmenu-abx-c-difficile-2-step-testing)

The Infectious Disease service is available to discuss CDI testing and results.

# Recurrence

Typically defined as symptomatic, laboratory confirmed CDI within 12 weeks after

a prior episode. Recurrence rates are up to 25%. Recurrence is usually due to

failure of normal colonic flora to re-establish itself, rather than

antimicrobial treatment failure.

# Fulminant CDI

Hypotension, shock, ileus, megacolon: General Surgery consult is essential for

ileus or megacolon.

# Treatment

[Initial Episode](orzid2-gmenu-abx-ini-epi-abx-assoc-colitis)

[First Recurrence](orzid2-gmenu-abx-first-recurrence-abx-assoc)

[Second Recurrence](orzid2-gmenu-abx-second-recur-abx-assoc-colitis)

[Fulminant](orzid2-gmenu-abx-toxic-megacolon)

# Third Recurrence: Consult Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Disease

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ASYMPTOMATIC BACTERIURIA

Asymptomatic bacteriuria is common in women and elderly people, especially in

those with chronic medical problems (e.g., diabetes, spinal cord injury,

institutionalized patients, catheterized patients). Most patients have no

adverse outcomes and receive no benefit from treatment of asymptomatic

bacteriuria.

Patients who have no symptoms of cystitis (i.e., no dysuria, pain, urgency)

should not be treated. The presence of pyuria (>7 wbc/hpf) or positive leukocyte

esterase, urine nitrate, or urine bacteria is not a sufficient indication for

antibiotic treatment. Screening and treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria is

indicated for pregnant women and patients who will have urological procedures

and may be indicated in patients < 1-month post-renal transplant. If an

indwelling catheter is in place and can be removed safely, it should be done as

the bacteriuria may clear.

Bacteriuria in pregnant women is associated with pyelonephritis, premature

delivery, and lower birth weight. Screening for bacteriuria is recommended at

least once early in pregnancy. If bacteriuria is not found upon initial testing,

further screening cultures are not needed. If bacteriuria (>10,000 CFU/mL) is

present, the patient should be treated. Testing should be repeated throughout

the pregnancy to detect recurrences.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Pregnant women, empirical treatment

Preferred:

[Nitrofurantoin SA 100 mg PO q12h \($\) R,O, CrCl >30 mL/min, for 5 days](psjzid-nitrofurantoin-sa-100-mg-po-bid)

*Avoid nitrofurantoin in the third trimester

Alternatives:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 5 days](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg q12h \($\) R for 5 days](psjzid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-q12h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Patients having urological procedures

[Antimicrobial prophylaxis for urological procedures](orzid2-gmenu-surg-urology-preop)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Renal transplant recipients < 1 month after transplant

Screening and treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria may be indicated. Consult

nephrology for recommendations.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# AZITHROMYCIN FOR PREVENTION OF EXACERBATIONS IN ADVANCED COPD

# Eligibility Criteria:

*Age >40 years

*Clinical diagnosis of COPD (>= 10 pack-years cigarette smoking, a ratio of

postbronchodilator forced expiratory volume in 1 second [FEV1] to forced vital

capacity of <70%, and a postbronchodilator FEV1 of <80% of the predicted value),

*AND*

*Were either using continuous supplemental oxygen or had received systemic

glucocorticoids within the previous year, *OR*

*Had gone to an emergency room or had been hospitalized for an acute

exacerbation of COPD.

# Exclusion criteria:

*Asthma

*People with hearing impairments

*Congestive heart failure

*Resting heart rate > 100 beats per minute

*Use of medications that are associated with torsades de pointes (except for

amiodarone)

*Prolonged QTc interval (>450 msec)

*Use of medications that prolong the QTc interval

[Please Click Here for Resource for Drugs that Cause QTc Prolongation](orz-gtx-abx-resource-qtc)

If, after trying all the standard treatments, patients are still having acute

exacerbations of COPD, long-term antibiotic treatment with Azithromycin may be

considered. Note: Guidelines for COPD can be found on the CPRS Tools Menu.

# Select below for Inpatient COPD order sets for comprehensive management:

[Inpatient COPD Exacerbation Orders](orz-gmenu-copd-exacerbation-main-ip)

If the patient meets the criteria and is willing to have audiometric testing and

an electrocardiogram, please place a Pulmonary Consult for long-term

Azithromycin therapy for the prevention COPD exacerbations.

# Pulmonary is the only approved provider for ordering long-term Azithromycin

# therapy for COPD.

[Azithromycin 250 mg po daily long-term for COPD DI](psjzid-azithromycin-longterm-copd-pulm)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BALANITIS AND BALANOPOSTHITIS

Balanitis is inflammation of the glans penis and is often associated with

erythema and pruritis. When the foreskin is also involved, the condition is

known as balanoposthitis (also referred to as balanitis in this discussion).

There are a variety of causes of balanitis, but most are due to poor hygiene of

the foreskin in uncircumcised men resulting in candida infection. Other, less

common causes, include bacterial infection (typically sexually transmitted or

anaerobic bacteria), dermatologic conditions, malignancy as well as others. Men

with Candidal balanitis often have a white curd-like exudate compared to a thick

foul-smelling purulent exudate in menu with anaerobic bacterial balanitis.

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for

treatment:

[Sexually Transmitted Infections and HIV Exposure](orzid2-gmenu-abx-sexually-transmitted-infection)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Candidal balanitis empirical treatment

# Mild to moderate cases

Preferred:

[Clotrimazole 1% cream topically q12h \($\) M for 7 days](psjzid-clotrimazole-1-cream-topical-bid)

Alternative:

[Nystatin cream 100,000 units/g cream topically q12h \($\) M for 7 days](psjzid-nystatin-cream-bid)

# Severe cases

[Fluconazole 150 mg PO once \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-150mg-po-once)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Bacterial balanitis empirical treatment

Mild cases

[Metronidazole 0.75% cream topically q12h \($\)DI for 7 days](psjzid-metronidazole-0-75-cream-topically-q12h)

Moderate to severe cases

[Metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 7 days](psjzid-metronidazole-500mg-po-q12h)

# ___________________________________________________________________________

References:

Edwards et al., International Journal of STD & AIDS, 2014, 25(9)615-526

# BELL'S PALSY

Herpes simplex and varicella-zoster are possible causes of Bell's palsy. Others

include Borrelia burgdorferi or trauma. Some cases are idiopathic. Risk factors

Bell's Palsy include pregnancy, diabetes, obesity, hypertension, and upper

respiratory infections. Neurology consult is encouraged.

If Lyme disease is suspected, refer to the Lyme disease treatment page:

[Lyme Disease](orzid2-gmenu-abx-lyme-disease)

Treatment with prednisone and an antiviral within 72 hours of symptoms onset

improves the chances of a complete recovery.

# Treatment

Preferred:

[Prednisone 60 mg q24h PO for 7 days <AND> valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-prednisone-60mg-q24h-7d-valacyclovir-1000mg-po-q8h)

for 7 days

Alternative:

[Prednisone 60 mg q24h PO for 7 days <AND> acyclovir 400 mg PO 5X/day \($\) R](orz-set-abx-prednisone-60mg-q24h-7d-acyclovir-400mg-po-5x-day)

for 10 days

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX BETA-LACTAM ALLERGY ASSESMENT
menus.Text:
# ASSESSMENT OF BETA-LACTAM REACTION AND ALTERNATIVE TREATMENT

# Streamlined Version (PDF form)

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction CLICK HERE](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

This guide is intended to aid clinicians in assessment of beta-lactam

reactions and selection of appropriate alternative therapy. It is not a

substitute for clinical judgment and should not be used as a sole resource when

selecting antimicrobial therapy.

[Important Beta-Lactam Allergy Facts and Obtaining a Detailed Reaction History](orzid2-gmenu-abx-important-beta-lactam-allergy-facts)

# Reaction Assessment and Selection of an Alternative Beta-lactam

- If the same or a different beta-lactam was subsequently tolerated without

reaction, that beta-lactam may be used.

- If reaction was intolerance (e.g. headache, GI symptoms), family history of

reaction, or if the patient denies allergy, any beta-lactam may be used.

- See below for treatment based on type of reaction (severe vs non-severe).

- If reaction is unknown and patient denies any severe reactions (see below for

list of severe reactions), reaction is considered non-severe.

- If patient is in a suitable care setting, observation during the first 15

minutes to 1 hour after first dose of therapy may be performed to monitor for

signs/symptoms of an allergic reaction.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# SEVERE REACTION TO BETA-LACTAM:

# _______________________________________________________________________________

If the patient experienced a known severe reaction (use link below for severe

reaction list), AVOID ALL Beta-Lactam Antibiotics. If beta-lactam therapy is

ideal, contact Infectious Diseases for desensitization or alternative.

Severe Reaction Examples:

- Anaphylaxis

- Reaction needed medical intervention

- Mucosal, cardiovascular or respiratory system involvement

- Hemolytic anemia

- Immune hepatitis

- Interstitial nephritis

- Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN)

- Skin desquamation

- Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

- Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS)

- Generalized exanthematous pustulosis

- Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# NON-SEVERE REACTION TO BETA-LACTAM:

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Select an alternative non-cross-reactive beta-lactam for therapy based on

beta-lactam class patient had a reaction to. Refer to PDF document above for

detailed cross-reactivity chart.

# PENICILLIN CLASS REACTION

(e.g. Amoxicillin, ampicillin, cloxacillin, dicloxacillin, nafcillin, oxacillin,

penicillin, piperacillin, ticarcillin)

# Use: Cefazolin, cefdinir, cefuroxime, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, cefepime,

# ertapenem, imipenem, or meropenem

# 1ST GENERATION CEPHALOSPORIN CLASS REACTION

(e.g. Cefadroxil, cefatrizine, cefazolin, ceftezole, cephalexin, cephalothin,

cephapirin)

# Use: Dicloxacillin, nafcillin, cefazolin (unless reaction was to cefazolin)

# cefdinir, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, cefepime, ertapenem, imipenem,

# or meropenem

# 2ND GENERATION CEPHALOSPORIN CLASS REACTION

(e.g. Cefaclor, cefamandole, cefonicid, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefprozil,

cefuroxime)

# Use: Amoxicillin, ampicillin, dicloxacillin, nafcillin, piperacillin,

# cefadroxil cefazolin, cefdinir, ceftazidime, ceftriaxone, cephalexin, cefepime,

# ertapenem imipenem, or meropenem

# 3RD-5TH GENERATION CEPHALOSPORIN CLASS REACTION

(e.g. Cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefiderocol,cefixime, cefpirome,

cefoperazone, cefotaxime, cefpodoxime, ceftaroline, ceftazidime, ceftibuten,

ceftizoxime, ceftolozane, ceftriaxone)

# Use: Amoxicillin, ampicillin, dicloxacillin, nafcillin, penicillin,

# piperacillin, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cephalexin, ertapenem, imipenem, or

# meropenem

# CARBAPENEM CLASS REACTION

(e.g. Ertapenem, imipenem and meropenem)

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BRONCHITIS, NO BENEFIT FROM ANTIBACTERIAL THERAPY

Acute bronchitis is a clinical syndrome with a brief, self-limited pneumonia on

chest radiograph. It is accompanied by dry or productive cough lasting up to 3

weeks, is most prevalent in winter, and is primarily caused by viruses. More

than 1 in 20 people have acute bronchitis per year, with highest rates during

the winter months.  This discussion does not pertain to acute exacerbations of

chronic bronchitis, a clinical syndrome also frequently associated with viral

infection, but in which bacteria play a more important role.

Narcotic cough suppressants, expectorants, antihistamines, decongestants, and

beta 2-agonists have been used to treat patients with acute bronchitis, but

controlled trials have not clearly concluded that they are beneficial.

Empirical antibacterial therapy has repeatedly been shown to provide no benefit

for most patients.  Acute bronchitis remains one of the five most frequently

cited rationales for excessive antibiotic use in outpatients. Acute bronchitis

and other acute respiratory syndromes (otitis media, sinusitis, pharyngitis,

upper respiratory infections) account for approximately 75% of ambulatory

prescriptions in the United States.  Current guidelines, endorsed by several

national societies, including the Infectious Diseases Society of America, do not

recommend the routine use of antibiotics for uncomplicated acute bronchitis in

normal people.

If pertussis is suspected, early therapy with macrolides or tetracyclines is

indicated to prevent transmission, although the clinical findings early in

pertussis infection are indistinguishable from viral causes of bronchitis, and

the incidence of disease is very low.  Treat for pertussis only when a patient

has likely been exposed to other cases.

Asthma attacks often have symptoms resembling bronchitis.  Asthma attacks do not

benefit from antimicrobial therapy.

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX C DIFF TESTING 2 STEP
menus.Text:
# Clostridioides difficile (C diff) 2-step lab testing

C diff 2-step testing helps differentiate between C diff infections vs.

colonization allowing providers to avoid unnecessary antibiotic use for

Veterans. With improved C diff testing, Veterans benefit with reduced

incidence of health-care acquired C diff and appropriate antimicrobial use.

New testing process will provide more accurate CDI test results. Our previous

method of testing for C diff infections was very sensitive, leading to an

over-diagnosis of C diff infections (CDI).

# New 2-step C diff testing:

All positive C diff PCR tests are now tested for C diff toxin for confirmation.

1st step (PCR): high sensitivity for C diff

2nd step (reflex test): automatically completed if the PCR is positive-

detects toxin

# Ordering criteria for C diff lab panel:

-Symptomatic (patient has had 3 or more watery stools in 24 hours or

presents with ileus suspected to be due to C diff)

-Only acceptable specimen is unformed stool (i.e. stool that conforms to the

the shape of the container)

-No other explanation for diarrhea such as laxative use or recent initiation

of tube feedings

-Testing should NOT be ordered for formed stool, asymptomatic patient, or

to perform "test of cure"

-Repeat orders within 7 days not accepted without Infectious Disease approval

# Place laboratory order for C diff panel:

[Click here C diff lab panel](lrtz-mb-c-difficile-toxin-pcr)

# ***Interpretation of C diff lab panel:

# PCR Negative (Toxin testing will not be performed):

Interpretation: CDI Not Present

i) No treatment or isolation needed for CDI

ii) Evaluate for other causes of diarrhea

# PCR Positive -and- Toxin Positive:

Interpretation: CDI Present

i) Initiate severity-based CDI therapy

[Click here C diff treatment recommendations](orzid2-gmenu-abx-assoc-colitis)

ii) Stop acid suppressive medications and concomitant antimicrobials if

possible

iii) Place patient in enteric isolation

# PCR Positive -and- Toxin Negative:

Interpretation: CDI MAY be Present

i) PCR positive, toxin negative may represent colonization or infection,

clinical judgement is needed

ii) Place patient in enteric isolation

iii) Treatment decision should be individualized, consider treatment for

severe, non-resolving, or otherwise unexplained diarrhea strongly

suggestive of CDI

[Click here C diff treatment recommendations](orzid2-gmenu-abx-assoc-colitis)

References:

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX C DIFFICILE 2 STEP TESTING
menus.Text:
[Minneapolis Clinical On-Call Schedule \(Infectious Disease\)](orz-min-on-call-schedule)

# Clostridioides difficile 2-step Testing

The Minneapolis VA Health Care System (MVAHCS) is using 2-step testing for

C. difficile infection (CDI), updating our current testing method which is a

single Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) test.

Benefits of 2-step testing are that it can be useful in differentiating patients

with true infection vs. those that may simply be colonized.

# What will change:

-All positive PCR tests for CDI (whether stand-alone CDI tests or the enteric

pathogen panel testing for CDI and other pathogens) will reflex to a toxin test

(a test that detects C. difficile toxin responsible for disease).

-Patients with BOTH a positive PCR and toxin will be reported as

"Toxigenic C. difficile detected. Repeat testing should not be performed."

-Patients with a positive PCR but a NEGATIVE toxin test will be reported as

"C. difficile detected by PCR, toxin negative by EIA. Possible disease or

colonization. Interpretation requires clinical judgement."

# What will not change:

-C. difficile testing should be performed on patients with high suspicion of

of CDI, WITHOUT other potential causes of diarrhea (e.g., laxatives, tube

feedings, other medications)

-Negative PCR tests will be reported as negative

-Repeat testing within 7 days is strongly discouraged, unless there is a

significant change in stool pattern/disease severity

-Patients with ongoing diarrhea (regardless of cause) should be placed in

contact plus precautions

-Formed stool will not be tested

# Infectious Disease Service is always available to discuss CDI testing/results.

# Test Interpretation:

Negative PCR: "Negative"

Positive PCR, Positive Toxin: "Toxin producing C. difficile detected"

Positive PCR, negative toxin: "C. difficile present, no toxin detected.

This may represent colonization or disease. Interpretation requires clinical

judgement. Consider treatment for severe illness otherwise consistent with

CDI. Discussion with Infectious Disease may be helpful."

**From 11pm to 7am, PCR test results will be reported WITHOUT the confirmatory

toxin test, which will be run the next morning. Postive PCR results will be

reported as:

"C. difficile detected by PCR, confirmatory toxin testing pending. Recommend

deferring antibiotic treatment in clinically stable patients where the

diagnosis of C. difficile is not certain."

Isolation for patients who are suspected of having CDI and who are receiving

treatment.

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CANDIDA URINARY TRACT INFECTIONS

A positive urine culture for candida usually reflects colonization. Treat

cystitis only if the patient has symptoms of urinary tract infection (e.g.

dysuria, frequency, urgency, and/or suprapubic tenderness) or if the patient

will undergo invasive urological manipulation

Asymptomatic candiduria in a patient with a urinary catheter should not be

treated without an additional indication. Removal of catheter is strongly

recommended. Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

Neutropenic patients with asymptomatic candiduria should be assessed for

candidemia because they are at risk of dissemination. Obtain blood cultures and

assess potential sources of candidemia such as central venous catheters. Refer

to fungemia page for treatment recommendations.

[Fungemia Associated with Candida spp.](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-candida-spp)

# Treatment

Patient undergoing invasive urological manipulation:

[Fluconazole 400 mg \(6 mg/kg\) PO q24h \($\) R,DI for 3 days before and 3 days](psjzid-fluconazole-400mg-po-q24h)

after procedure

< OR >

[Fluconazole 400 mg \(6 mg/kg\) IV q24h \($\) R,DI for 3 days before and 3 days](psjizid-fluconazole-400mg-iv-q24h)

after procedure

Symptomatic candida cystitis:

[Fluconazole 200 mg \(3 mg/kg\) PO q24h \($\) R,DI for 14 days](psjzid-fluconazole-200mg-po-q24h)

< OR >

[Fluconazole 200 mg \(3 mg/kg\) IV q24h \($\) R,DI for 14 days](psjizid-fluconazole-200-400mg-iv-q24h)

Pyelonephritis:

[Fluconazole 400 mg \(6 mg/kg\) PO q24h \($\) R,DI for 14 days](psjzid-fluconazole-400mg-po-q24h)

< OR >

[Fluconazole 400 mg \(6 mg/kg\) IV q24h \($\) R,DI for 14 days](psjizid-fluconazole-400mg-iv-q24h)

Resistant candida:

Consult Infectious Diseases for treatment options

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX CANDIDA VULVO-VAGINITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CANDIDA VULVOVAGINITIS

Candida vulvovaginitis typically presents with valvular irritation, burning or

pruritus. Vaginal pH should be measured, and the specimen should be examined

under the microscope for clue cells (epithelial cell coated with bacteria) to

exclude bacterial vaginosis. In candida vulvovaginitis, the vaginal pH is

typically normal (4-4.5) and vaginal discharge is typically thick and curdy with

white plaques on vaginal mucosa. Diagnosis is confirmed by identifying fungus or

yeast with KOH prep.

Most non-C. albicans species respond to fluconazole treatment except C. krusei

and C. glabrata. C. krusei can be treated with topical agents as for complicated

candida vulvovaginitis below. C. glabrata treatment is complicated and azole

therapy is frequently unsuccessful. Consult Infectious Diseases in patients with

C. glabrata vulvovaginitis.

Recurrent candida vulvovaginitis is treated as complicated candida

vulvovaginitis for induction treatment, followed by maintenance regimen for 6

months.

# Candida vulvovaginitis in pregnancy:

[Clotrimazole vaginal cream 1% 1 applicatorful qhs for 7 days](psjzid-clotrimazole-vaginal-crm-1-1-applful-qhs)

# Treatment of uncomplicated candida vulvovaginitis

[Fluconazole 150 mg PO once \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-150mg-po-once)

< OR >

[Clotrimazole vaginal 1% cream 1 applicator full qhs \($\) M for 7 to 14 days](psjzid-clotrimazole-vaginal-crm-1-1-applful-qhs)

< OR >

[Terconazole 0.4% vaginal cream 1 applicator full qhs \($\) M for 7 days](psjzid-terconazole-0-4-crm-vag-qhs)

# Treatment of complicated candida vulvovaginitis (e.g. immunocompromised, severe

# disease) or recurrent infection induction treatment

[Fluconazole 150 mg PO q72h for 7 days \(3 doses\) \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-150mg-po-q72h)

< OR >

[Clotrimazole vaginal 1% cream 1 applicator full qhs \($\) M for 10-14 days](psjzid-clotrimazole-vaginal-crm-1-1-applful-qhs)

< OR >

[Terconazole 0.4% vaginal cream 1 applicator full qhs \($\) M for 10-14 days](psjzid-terconazole-0-4-crm-vag-qhs)

# Recurrent candida vulvovaginitis maintenance regimen following induction

# treatment above

[Fluconazole 150 mg PO every 7 days \($\) R,DI for 6 months](psjzid-fluconazole-150mg-po-qweek)

# Treatment of C. glabrata vulvovaginitis

Failure of azole therapy is common, alternative topical treatments below require

compounding by a pharmacist. Please call pharmacy to order.

Topical boric acid capsule 600 mg intravaginal qhs for 14 days

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CELLULITIS & ERYSIPELAS

Skin and soft tissue infections without abscess or other sign of purulence.

MRSA coverage is typically unnecessary when there is no purulence, even in

patients with a history of MRSA colonization or infection. It may be considered

for specific patients with the considerations listed below but is not

recommended as the default choice.

Elevation, good skin hygiene, and support stockings are recommended.

# Duration: Treat for 5 - 7 days

# Cellulitis without systemic signs of infection, oral transition

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h R](psjzid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-q12h)

# Alternative for Penicillin Allergy or with MRSA considerations*

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Cellulitis with systemic signs of infection

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

< OR >

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h DI](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

# Alternative for penicillin allergy or with MRSA considerations*

*Penetrating trauma (including injection drug use), a history of MRSA infection,

or infections not responding to first line beta-lactams

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

< OR >

[Linezolid 600 mg PO q12h DI,O](psjzid-linezolid-600mg-po-q12h)

# Cellulitis in patients with signs of complicated or deeper infections

(e.g. bullae, skin sloughing, hypotension, evidence of organ dysfunction, severe

immunosuppression).

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Alternative for penicillin allergy:

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h R,DI <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R <AND>](orz-set-abx-vanco-15mg-kg-cipro-400mg-metro-500mg-iv-q8h)

metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI,H]

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CERVICITIS ASSOCIATED WITH SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES

The main diagnostic signs that characterize cervicitis are 1)women who present

with purulent or mucopurulent exudate in the endocervical canal or on an

endocervical swab specimen and 2)sustained endocervical bleeding induced by

gentle passage of cotton swab through the cervical os. One or both signs may be

present.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis are the two most common sexually

transmitted cervicitis pathogens. Nucleic acid amplification tests for these

pathogens are more sensitive than culture and should be used for patients at

risk for sexually transmitted cervicitis.

[Chlamydia & GC PCR/LCR test](lrtzid-chlamydia-gc-urine-naat)

# For patients who have recently been treated for cervicitis

[Treatment of recurrent or persistent cervicitis](orzid2-gmenu-recurrent-persist-urethritis)

When diagnosed with sexually transmitted cervicitis, the patient's sexual

partner(s) during the previous 60 days should be evaluated for sexually

transmitted infection. If diagnostic tests for the cause of cervicitis are not

feasible, therapy for both N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis should be given to

partners.

# Initial treatment of patients and sex partners

Patients and partners are often infected with both N. gonorrhoeae and C.

trachomatis. Treat for both pathogens unless one is ruled out by lab test.

[Treatment for chlamydial or non-gonococcal cervicitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-chlamydia-urethritis-cervicitis-or-proctitis)

[Treatment for gonorrhea cervicitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-gonococcal)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CHOLANGITIS

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Most cases are due to common bile duct obstruction. Obstruction (if present)

must be relieved with an endoscopical, transcutaneous, or surgical procedure.

The most common pathogens isolated are E. coli, Klebsiella, Enterococcus and

Enterobacter. Pseudomonas coverage is recommended in severe (grade 3)

cholangitis.  Anaerobic coverage is recommended if biliary-enteric abnormality

is present.

Antimicrobials' role in cholangitis is to allow patients to have elective and

not emergently scheduled drainage procedures.

Due to increasing resistance, fluoroquinolones are only recommended in cases of

severe penicillin and cephalosporin allergy.

# Treatment of patients on ward without systemic symptoms of infection

Treat for 4-7 days after source control

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:

[<ADD> Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI to above regimen](psjizid-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

# Treatment of patients in ICU with systemic symptoms of infection

Treat for 4-7 days after source control

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ciprof-400mg-iv-q12-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX CHOLECYSTITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CHOLECYSTITIS

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Adequate biliary drainage is the definitive treatment. Antimicrobials should be

prescribed only if signs of infection like leukocytosis or fever are present or

if the patient is elderly. Surgery and Gastroenterology involvement are

essential.

For acute cholecystitis in grade 1 disease, antimicrobials are primarily

prophylactic. For moderate to severe disease grades 2-3, antimicrobials should

be continued for 4-7 days.

Most cases are associated with E. coli, Enterococcus, Klebsiella, and

Enterobacter. Anaerobic coverage is not indicated unless a biliary-enteric

abnormality is present. For community-acquired acute cholecystitis, enterococcal

coverage is not required because Enterococcus has not been shown to be

pathogenic in these patients

Due to increasing resistance, fluoroquinolones are only recommended in cases of

severe penicillin and cephalosporin allergy.

# Treatment of patient on ward without systemic symptoms of infection

Duration of Therapy: Antimicrobials should be discontinued within 24 hours of

drainage procedure

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:

[< ADD > Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI to above regimen](psjizid-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

# Treatment of patient on ward with systemic symptoms of infection

Duration of Therapy: Treat for 4-7 days after source control

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-3-375-gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

Biliary structural abnormality, including stent:

[< ADD >  Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI  to one of the regimens above](psjizid-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-and-metro-500mg-iv)

# Treatment of ICU patients

Duration of Therapy: Most can be treated for 4-7 days after source control.

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q12h DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

< OR >

[Meropenem 1 gm IV q8h R,O](psjizid-meropenem-1gm-iv-q8h)

# CHRONIC PROSTATITIS / CHRONIC PELVIC PAIN SYNDROME

This syndrome presents with intermittent perineal and/or low back pain,

obstructive voiding symptoms, relatively normal examination, and negative urine

cultures. Antimicrobial therapy is not indicated.

Consult urology for non-antimicrobial therapy recommendations (e.g.

alpha-adrenergic antagonists, anti-inflammatory medications) to reduce symptoms.

# Anti-inflammatory treatment

[Ibuprofen 400 mg PO q8h for 2 to 3 weeks](psjzid-ibuprofen-400mg-po-q8h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX CHRONIC BACT PROSTATITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CHRONIC BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS

Chronic bacterial prostatitis usually presents as recurrent urinary tract

infections with the same bacterial etiology. Pain, tenderness, and fever may

accompany intermittent episodes of cystitis, but men are usually asymptomatic

between episodes and the prostate examination may be normal. Non-steroidal anti-

inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) often relieve pain. If the diagnosis is uncertain or

if the patient's symptoms do not respond to therapy, consult urology. The

presence of hematuria may be a sign of carcinoma, especially in older men, and a

urology consult should be requested.

A urine culture should be performed in all patients to guide antimicrobial

therapy.

Chronic prostate pain syndrome should be considered in patients who have

symptoms of prostatitis but have negative urine cultures. Chronic prostate pain

syndrome is discussed elsewhere:

[Chronic prostate pain syndrome](orzid2-gmenu-abx-chron-pros-pelvic-pain-syn)

# Duration

4 weeks minimum and up to 6 weeks of treatment is required. Durations longer

than 6 weeks may be needed in treatment of resistant organisms. Treatment with

trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole requires a treatment duration of 1 to 3 months.

# Empirical treatment

Preferred:

[Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI for 4 weeks](psjzid-levofloxacin-750mg-po-q24h)

< OR >

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h \($\) R,DI for 4 weeks](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

Alternative:

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h \($\) R,DI for 4 weeks](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

# CHRONIC MENINGITIS

Subacute meningeal symptoms, including headache, fever, and nausea for 4 weeks

or more. Chronic meningitis is caused by a long list of infectious and

non-infectious etiologies. Treatment is based on etiology and empirical

treatment is not urgent unless tuberculosis is suspected. Consult Infectious

Diseases for more information.

menus.Text:

# CMV COLITIS OR ESOPHAGITIS

Infection in immunocompetent patients is rare and usually associated with

minimal or no symptoms. Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased

include solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving

prolonged immunosuppressive chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease

indicated by a CD4 count of less than 50 cells/microliter. Treatment is complex

and requires Infectious Diseases consultation.

# Duration of therapy

Treat for 3-6 weeks. Patients may be converted to oral therapy after initial

intravenous therapy and after clinical improvement of severe disease.

# Treatment of mild to moderate disease or following clinical improvement of

# severe disease

[Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q12h R,O](psjzid-valganciclovir-900mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment of severe disease

[Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h R,O](psjizid-ganciclovir-5-mg-kg-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h R,O](psjizid-foscarnet-0-09-gm-kg-iv-q12h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX CMV MAIN PAGE
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CYTOMEGALOVIRUS (CMV)

# Antiviral toxicity information

The major toxicities of both ganciclovir and valganciclovir are neutropenia.

Nephrotoxicity is the major toxicity associated with foscarnet, which may be

reduced by concomitant saline administration (generally 0.5-1L).

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompetent patient

Infection is rare and usually associated with minimal or no symptoms.

Mononucleosis can be associated with CMV, but is more commonly associated with

Epstein Barr virus. Antiviral treatment is not usually necessary as most

patients recover without intervention.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompromised patient

Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased include solid organ and

bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving prolonged immunosuppressive

chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease indicated by a CD4 count of

less than 50 cells/microliter.

# CMV treatment recommendations

# CMV PNEUMONIA

CMV pneumonia occurs almost exclusively in bone marrow transplant recipients,

usually within the first 120 days after transplantation. In these patients, CMV

pneumonia is severe and requires aggressive treatment. Treatment is complex and

requires Infectious Diseases consultation.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Induction therapy is indicated for 3 to 6 weeks, followed by maintenance

therapy. Duration of maintenance therapy is not well established.

# Treatment

[Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,O <AND> intravenous immune globulin](orz-set-abx-ganciclovir-5-mg-kg-iv-q12h-immune-ig-0-5-gm-kg)

0.5 grams/kg IV every other day

# Maintenance therapy

[Valganciclovir 900 mg PO Q24h \($$$\) R,O](psjzid-valganciclovir-900-mg-po-q24h)

# CMV POLYRADICULOPATHY

Infection in immunocompetent patients is rare and usually associated with

minimal or no symptoms. Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased

include solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving

prolonged immunosuppressive chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease

indicated by a CD4 count of less than 50 cells/microliter. Treatment is complex

and requires Infectious Diseases consultation.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Duration is likely to be prolonged and is individualized based on response.

Patients may be converted to oral therapy after initial intravenous therapy and

after clinical improvement of severe disease.

# Treatment of mild to moderate disease or following clinical improvement of

# severe disease

[Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q12h \($$$\) R,O](psjzid-valganciclovir-900mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment of severe disease

[Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,O](psjizid-ganciclovir-5-mg-kg-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,O](psjizid-foscarnet-0-09-gm-kg-iv-q12h)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CMV RETINITIS AND ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS

Infection in immunocompetent patients is rare and usually associated with

minimal or no symptoms. Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased

include solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving

prolonged immunosuppressive chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease

indicated by a CD4 count of less than 50 cells/microliter. Treatment is complex

and requires Infectious Diseases consultation.

For sight threatening lesions (lesions within 1500 microns of the fovea)

intravitreal infections of ganciclovir or foscarnet are recommended in addition

to systemic treatment. Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat retinitis for 14 to 21 days. Patients may be converted to oral therapy

after initial intravenous therapy and after clinical improvement of severe

disease. Treat acute retinal necrosis with IV therapy for at least 7 days and

until disease stabilizes then oral therapy for a minimum of 6 weeks. Maintenance

therapy after completion of treatment is indicated when CD4 count <100.

Discontinue maintenance therapy when CD4 count is >100 for 6 months.

# Treatment acute retinal necrosis or severe disease

Intravitreal antiviral in addition to systemic antiviral may provide added

therapeutic efficacy.

[Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,O](psjizid-ganciclovir-5-mg-kg-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,O](psjizid-foscarnet-0-09-gm-kg-iv-q12h)

Optional add-on therapy for acute retinal necrosis

[Ganciclovir 4mg/0.1mL intravitreal injection STAT \($$$$\) R,O](psjzid-ganciclovir-2mg-intravitreous-inject-once)

< OR >

[Foscarnet 2.4mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT \($$$$\) R,O](psjzid-foscarnet-2-4mg-intravitreous-inject-once)

# For cases not responsive to Intravenous therapy with foscarnet and ganciclovir

# used alone

[Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,O <AND> foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h](orz-set-abx-ganciclovir-5mg-kg-iv-q12h-foscar-90mg-kg-iv-q12h)

($$$$) [R,O]

In cases not responsive to first-line therapy, second-line therapies may be

effective. Their use is highly specialized and must be done by someone

experienced with HIV/AIDS medicine.

# Treatment of mild to moderate retinitis or after clinical improvement of severe

# retinitis/acute retinal necrosis

[Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q12h\($$$\) R,O](psjzid-valganciclovir-900mg-po-q12h)

# Maintenance therapy

[Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q24h \($$$\) R,O](psjzid-valganciclovir-900-mg-po-q24h)
