menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX IMPORTANT BETA-LACTAM ALLERGY FACTS
menus.Text:
# Important Beta-lactam Allergy Facts

1. 10% of patients report an allergy to penicillin.

2. Less than 1% of patients are truly allergic to penicillin.

3. 80% of patients who had an immediate allergic reaction (Type I,

Immunoglobulin E (IgE)-mediated) to penicillin lose sensitivity after 10

years.

4. Cross-reactivity between penicillin and cephalosporins occurs in only 2% of

patients and most patients do not have clinically significant reactions.

# Obtaining a Detailed Reaction History

- Locate documented reaction information within the Computerized Patient Record

System (CPRS)

> Reported reactions can be found in the Cover Sheet under Allergies/Adverse

Reactions. Double click on the specific reaction for more information,

including signs/symptoms and date of reaction.

> A reaction report can also be found here: Reports tab -> Clinical Reports -

Allergies.

- Determine beta-lactam medication history. A list of all locally prescribed

medications can be found here: Reports tab -> Clinical Reports -> Pharmacy ->

All Medications.

- Interview the patient or family for details about the reaction. Questions to

ask during the interview:

> What medication were you taking when the reaction occurred? DO NOT accept

Penicillin or Cephalosporin as an allergy, ensure specific offending

medication is identified.

> How long after taking the medication did the reaction occur? Immediate

reactions typically occur within 1 hour and up to 72 hours after

administration. Delayed reactions occur after 72 hours.

> How long ago did the reaction occur? Did it occur over 10 years ago?

> What kind of reaction occurred? Did the reaction require medical attention?

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# INFECTIONS INVOLVING CARDIOVASCULAR DEVICES (EXCLUDING VALVES)

Most infections are associated with Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative

staphylococci.  Many of these staphylococci are resistant to methicillin, so

initial empiric therapy with vancomycin is required. Consultation with

Infectious Diseases is encouraged for patients with severe allergies to

vancomycin or for those who have vancomycin-resistant infections.

At least 3 blood cultures should be drawn prior to the initiation of empirical

antimicrobial. Modify antimicrobial regimen and narrow coverage based on results

of culture and susceptibility tests Infectious Disease and Cardiothoracic

surgery consultations are encouraged.

Device removal is necessary for cure in most cases.  However, it may be

difficult depending on the nature of the device and specific clinical

circumstances.  Device removal should be discussed with Cardiology, Infectious

Disease, or Cardiothoracic surgery consultants.

If the device removal is not possible add rifampin.

# Duration of therapy

Duration of therapy should be determined in concert with Cardiology, Infectious

Disease, or Cardiothoracic surgery consultants.

# Empiric treatment in cases where device removal is planned

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Empiric treatment in cases where surgery cannot be performed

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> rifampin 300 mg PO/NG q8h \($\)](orz-set-abx-vanco-rifamp-300mg-po-q8h)

[DI,O]

# For hemodynamically unstable patients, add gentamicin to one of the above

# treatment regimens

[< ADD > gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h \($\) R,O](psjizid-gentamicin-1-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# EARLY TREATMENT OF INFLUENZA AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO CHEMOPROPHYLAXIS

In most cases, if a person is suspected of having been exposed to influenza,

early treatment, should signs or symptoms develop, is preferred rather than

chemoprophylaxis.

The provider should explain the early signs and symptoms of influenza to the

patient and advise the patient to immediately contact a health care provider for

evaluation and possible early treatment if these symptoms or signs develop.

Influenza-like symptoms or signs include fever, cough, sore throat, runny or

stuffy nose, body aches, headache, chills, fatigue, vomiting, and diarrhea.

Influenza can present without fever.

Health care providers should use clinical judgment regarding situations where

early recognition of illness and treatment might be an appropriate alternative

to chemoprophylaxis.

# Early treatment alternative or chemoprophylaxis may be considered:

*Persons who are part of a high-risk group and are household or close contacts

of someone with influenza-like illness Chemoprophylaxis duration: 7 days after

last known exposure

# Chemoprophylaxis recommended:

*For control of outbreaks in institutional settings (long-term care facilities

and hospitals)

Chemoprophylaxis duration: minimum of 2 weeks and continuing up to 1 week after

the last known case is identified.

Note: Antiviral chemoprophylaxis is recommended for all residents, including

those who have received influenza vaccination.

# Chemoprophylaxis considered:

*Atypical situations (such as case clusters). Contact the state health

department for consultation.

# Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommendations

Preferred:

[Oseltamivir 75 mg po q24h R](psjzid-oseltamivir-75-mg-po-daily-prophy)

(See information above for length of prophylaxis)

# **Below is for information only, quick orders are not available

Alternative treatment:

Zanamivir is not recommended for patients with chronic respiratory diseases such

as asthma or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease. These patients may have

bronchospasm with zanamivir. If zanamivir must be used, and patients are using

an inhaled bronchodilator, zanamivir should be taken just after the

bronchodilator.

Requires Infectious Disease Approval

Zanamivir 2 inhalations (2 x 5 mg) daily [O] (see above for duration of

prophylaxis)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Centers for Disease Control (CDC) (Accessed 9/8/23)

# INFLUENZA VACCINATION RECOMMENDATIONS

[Influenza Vaccine Outpatient and Inpatient Guidelines](orz-gtx-influenza-info)

Annual influenza vaccination is recommended for all persons aged 6 months and

older without a specific contraindication.

Eggs and latex allergies are NOT considered contraindications to receiving the

vaccine, the only contraindication to the flu vaccination is severe allergic

reaction (i.e. Anaphylactic reactions).

# Recommend observing all patients for 15 minutes after receiving any influenza

# vaccine. A previous severe allergic reaction to influenza vaccine, regardless of

# the component suspected of being responsible for the reaction, is a

# contraindication to future receipt of ANY influenza vaccine.

# INITIAL EPISODE OF CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

Discontinue implicated antibiotic(s). Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic

therapy is still needed. Avoid antiperistaltic agents (narcotics, loperamide,

etc.). Avoid antacid therapy without clear indication. If diarrhea has improved

or resolved prior to starting C. difficile treatment, consider re-assessing the

diagnosis before initiating therapy. C. difficile infection usually responds to

antimicrobial therapy. If symptoms do not respond to appropriate antimicrobial

therapy, re-consider the diagnosis.

# Patient at increased risk of CDI recurrence:

(e.g., age >65 years old, concomitant antibiotic use during CDI treatment,

and/or immunosuppression)

[Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days M](psjzid-fidaxomicin-200mg-q12h-10d)

# Patient not meeting criteria above for increased risk of CDI recurrence:

[Vancomycin 125mg PO q6h for 10 days M](psjzid-vancomycin-125mg-po-q6h-x10days-cdiff)

_______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PERITONITIS ASSOCIATED WITH PERITONEAL DIALYSIS

# Peritonitis associated with peritoneal dialysis usually presents with abdominal

# pain, fever, nausea or vomiting, and cloudy effluent. The leukocyte

# concentration is greater than 100 cells/microliter of dialysate, with more than

# 50% neutrophils.

# Obtain Gram stain, culture, and cell count with differential of dialysate before

# antimicrobials are given.

Nephrology consultation is essential. If cultures show Gram-negative or mixed

bacterial infection, a gastrointestinal tract infectious source is more likely.

Gram-positive organisms like staphylococci usually result from external

contamination. Fungal peritonitis is rare and requires immediate catheter

removal.

**Antimicrobial recommendations are for empirical therapy only. Regimens should

be tailored according to patient response and microbiology results in

consultation with Nephrology and/or Infectious Diseases for more information.

If vancomycin is used, trough serum concentrations should be kept above 15

mcg/ml to ensure adequate intraperitoneal levels. Usually vancomycin must be

given every 3 to 7 days. Contact Nephrology and/or Pharmacy for more

information.

# Consult Nephrology in all cases.

[Peritonitis labs](orz-set-peritonitis-labs)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Antimicrobial therapy

# Duration

Duration of therapy depends on the pathogen identified. Treat staphylococcal and

streptococcal infections for 2 weeks and all other gram-positive infections for

3 weeks. In patients who have Staphylococcus isolated and had a previous

staphylococcal infection, treat for 3 weeks

# All antimicrobials below are administered via 2.5% dextrose 2000 mL peritoneal

# dialysate bag over 6 hours with heparin 1000 units, unless contraindicated

# Empirical treatment while waiting for results of gram stain

[Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days \($\) R <AND>](orzid2-gmenu-pd-cefepime-1gm-q24h-vanco-15-30mg-kg-q5-7d)

cefepime 1 gm PD q24h ($) [R]

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Antifungal prophylaxis:

Antifungal prophylaxis may be used for the duration of antimicrobial therapy to

possibly reduce the risk of fungal peritonitis. *Order if previous peritonitis*

[Fluconazole 200 mg PO every other day \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-200mg-po-q48h)

<OR>

[Fluconazole 100 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-100mg-po-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

De Vin et al, Peritoneal Dialysis International, 2009, Vol. 39, pp. 5-15

Li et al, Peritoneal Dialysis International, 2016, Vol. 36, pp. 481-508

Mandell chapter: Peritonitis and Intraperitoneal Abscesses

Sanford keyword: Peritonitis, Dialysis (CAPD) Associated

dialysis

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# EPIDIDYMITIS AND EPIDIDYMO-ORCHITIS

Epididymitis is inflammation of the epididymis and when testicles are involved

is referred to as epididymo-orchitis. Acute epididymitis is the most common

cause of scrotal pain in adults. Other features include scrotal erythema and

edema, pyuria, dysuria, thickened epididymis, swollen testis, and is usually

unilateral. It is primarily caused by infection but can also result from trauma

and autoimmune diseases. Testicular torsion should be ruled out before

treatment. Most cases in men aged 35 and older, those with recent urinary tract

instrumentation or surgery (e.g., prostate biopsy, vasectomy) are associated

with enteric Gram-negative rods. Most cases in men under age 35 are associated

with N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis. Resistant organisms are more likely if

the patient has been in the hospital for more than 48 hours or received a course

of antibiotics. There is increasing resistance in urinary pathogens to

ciprofloxacin.

A urine analysis, urine culture and urine nucleic acid amplification test (NAAT)

should be performed in all cases of suspected epididymitis before starting

treatment to guide therapy:

[Lab menu](orzid2-gmenu-abx-lab-menu)

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for

treatment. Refer to the Urogenital section of the Antimicrobial CDSS for more

information.

Patients with bacterial epididymitis treated with antibiotics should improve

within two or three days. If no improvement is noted, other causes of scrotal

pain and referral to a urologist should be considered.

Management should include bed rest, analgesics, and scrotal elevation. Older men

should have their residual urinary volume checked. If the residual volume is

elevated, the patient should be seen by a urologist as epididymitis is unlikely

to respond if the prostate is blocking the vas deferens.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Empirical treatment in men who practice insertive anal intercourse

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once \($\) M < AND > levofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-500mg-im-once-levoflox-500mg-po-q24h)

for 10 days ($) [R, DI]

# Age >/= 35 years or

# Recent urinary tract instrumentation or urinary tract surgery (e.g., prostate

# biopsy, vasectomy):

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# LIVER ABSCESS

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Liver abscess should be suspected in all patients with fever, leukocytosis, and

a space-occupying liver lesion. Liver abscesses fall broadly into two

categories: pyogenic and amebic. In the United States, pyogenic liver abscess is

much more common. Amebic liver abscess occurs almost exclusively in travelers

and immigrants.

Infectious Diseases consultation is recommended due to prolonged treatment and

need for follow-up.

# Duration of therapy

A typical course for pyogenic liver abscess is 4 to 6 weeks based on improvement

and follow-up imaging.

# Treatment

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

Critical illness or immunosuppression:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative for critical illness or suppression:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative for severe beta lactam reaction:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ciprof-400mg-iv-q12-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# LYME DISEASE AND OTHER TICK-BORNE ILLNESSES

Patients who display signs of illness or fever within 30 days of removing an

attached tick should be evaluated for tick-borne illness. In the upper Midwest

these are Lyme, anaplasmosis, babesiosis, ehrlichiosis, and Powassan virus

disease. Patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick (deer tick) but

who do not display signs or symptoms of infection should not be treated with

antimicrobials. Refer to recommendations below for pathogen specific

recommendations.

[Anaplasmosis](orzid2-gmenu-anaplasma-phatocytophilum)

[Ehrlichioisis](orzid2-gmenu-ehrlichia-chaffeensis)

[Babesiosis](orzid2-gmenu-babesia-spp)

Powassan virus disease - contact Infectious Diseases for more Information.

# Lyme Disease

Lyme disease results from the transmission of Borrelia burgdorferi from an

Ixodes spp. tick bite. Refer to CDC for map of endemic areas.

[CDC Lyme Disease Case Map](orz-gtx-abx-cdc-lyme-disease-case-map)

Prophylactic antimicrobial treatment may be beneficial in certain patients who

have been bitten while in endemic areas.

[Lyme Disease Prophylaxis](orzid2-gmenu-lyme-disease-prophylaxis)

Except for erythema migrans, Lyme disease is a complicated, difficult disease to

diagnose and treat. Infectious Diseases consultation is strongly encouraged.

Refer to recommendations below for

[Erythema migrans](orzid2-gmenu-lyme-erythema-migrans)

[Acute neurological disease](orzid2-gmenu-lyme-acute-neuro-disease)

[Arthritis](orzid2-gmenu-lyme-arthritis)

[Cardiac disease](orzid2-gmenu-lyme-cardiac-disease)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX MANAGEMENT OF FEBRILE EPISODE ASPLENIA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# FEVER IN AN ASPLENIC PATIENT

Patients with impaired splenic function are at risk for severe and overwhelming

infection with encapsulated bacteria. Streptococcus pneumoniae is the most

common cause of fulminant sepsis in patients with impaired splenic function,

followed by Haemophilus influenzae and Neisseria meningitidis. Infection with

Capnocytophaga species is possible in asplenic patients with anteceding

scratches and animal bites, especially dog bites. Babesiosis is also more likely

in asplenic patients exposed to tick bites.

If fever develops in an asplenic patient, immediate administration of an

antimicrobial agent is indicated, because fever can be the initial manifestation

of a fulminant infection and prompt administration of an antimicrobial agent may

prevent the development of clinical sepsis.

Administration of antibiotics should not be delayed for performing diagnostic

studies, including lumbar puncture.

# Streptococcus pneumoniae meningitis suspected

[Bacterial meningitis with S. pneumoniae](orzid2-gmenu-bact-mening-s-pneumoniae)

# Anteceding animal bite or scratch

Consult Infectious Diseases

For tick bites consider treatment for Babesia species

[Babesia Species](orzid2-gmenu-babesia-spp)

Other animal bites or scratches

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

_______________________________________________________________________________

# MEDIASTINITIS

Mediastinitis occurs after cardiothoracic procedures or less commonly after

esophageal perforation.

# Treatment AFTER CARDIOTHORACIC SURGERY

Preferred:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-pip-taz4-5gm-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro-vanco15mg-kg)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-levo-750mg-iv-q24h-and-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Treatment AFTER ESOPHAGEAL PERFORATION OR RUPTURE

Mixed aerobic/anaerobic infection is often present.

Preferred:

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

Alternative:

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# MORE ABOUT NOSOCOMIAL PNEUMONIA

# Types of nosocomial pneumonia

Hospital acquired pneumonia (HAP): Development of pneumonia 48 hours or more

after hospital admission.

Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP): Pneumonia occurring 48 hours or more

after endotracheal intubation.

# Criteria for diagnosis of pneumonia

1.  Presence of new or progressive infiltrate <AND>

2.  At least two of the following:

> Fever greater than 38 C (100.4 F)

> Leukocytosis or leukopenia

> Purulent bronchial secretions

# HAP OR VAP suspected:

Gram stain and culture of lower respiratory tract secretions and blood cultures

are important for guiding therapy.

[Re-evaluate Nosocomial pneumonia at 72 hours](orzid2-gmenu-abx-re-evaluate-72hrs-n-pneumo)

# Duration of therapy

Treatment for 7 days is generally sufficient if the initial empiric therapy

covered the pathogen and the patient is clinically responding. Narrow therapy to

treat specific pathogen(s) based on results of culture and susceptibility tests.

Longer duration of therapy is recommended for more resistant organisms (e.g.

Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Acinetobacter baumanni, and Legionella pneumophila).

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX MYOCARDITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# MYOCARDITIS

Myocarditis is most commonly associated with enterovirus or coxsackie virus

infection. Less common pathogens include pyogenic bacteria, rickettsia,

toxoplasmosis, and fungi.

Empirical antimicrobial treatment is not indicated. Supportive care and

treatment of CHF are essential. Consult Cardiology and/or Infectious Diseases

for more assistance.

Avoid non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDS) and corticosteroids in

these patients, as the use of NSAIDs in myocarditis has been associated with

worse outcomes.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Mandell chapter: Myocarditis and Pericarditis

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PREVENTION OF INFECTION IN PATIENTS WITH NASAL PACKING

Antimicrobial prophylaxis to prevent infection and toxic shock syndrome in

patients with nasal packing is not recommended. Antibiotics increase the risk of

adverse events in patients with nasal packing with no proven effectiveness in

preventing infection.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# NON-CHOLERA VIBRIO

Non-cholera vibrio is associated with gastroenteritis, septicemia, and wound

infections. Vibrio vulnificans infections are acquired from contact with

seawater or seafood, especially raw oysters. V. vulnificans cases are more

severe than cases with other species. V. parahaemolyticus causes

gastroenteritis and milder wound infections.

Antimicrobials do not shorten the course of disease in immunocompetent patients

with mild gastroenteritis.

# Primary treatment for gastroenteritis

Hydration and electrolyte replacement

# Antimicrobial treatment of minor wound infection, severe gastroenteritis or

# immunocompromised patient with gastroenteritis

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 3-5 days \($\) R,DI](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-500mg-po-q12h)

Alternative for patient intolerant of fluoroquinolones

[Doxycycline 100 mg BID for 3-5 days \($\) DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

For patients who are hospitalized or unable to take oral medications

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h for 3-5 days \($\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# Antimicrobial treatment of severe wound infection or septicemia

Consult Infectious Diseases for advice on duration of treatment.

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M <AND> doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h \($$\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-q24h-doxy-iv-100mg-iv-q12h)

for 7 to 14 days

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M <AND> doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-doxi-100mg-po)

for 7 to 14 days

Alternative

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h for 7 to 14 days \($\) R,DI](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX NOT BENEFITED PHARYNGITIS
menus.Text:
# PHARYNGITIS

Acute pharyngitis is common, accounting for 2 percent of all

ambulatory visits in the United States.  The major treatable pathogen, group

A streptococcus (GAS), is the cause of pharyngitis in only approximately 10

percent of adults who seek medical care.  The vast majority of patients

receive presumptive antibiotic therapy for pharyngitis which in most cases is

unnecessary and results in adverse effects including death, increases costs,

and adds to pressure on antimicrobial resistance.  Typical causes of

pharyngitis include viruses in about ï¿½, beta-hemolytic streptococci other

than group A in 18%, Mycoplasma pneumoniae in 10%, Chlamydophila pneumoniae

in 8%, Group A streptococci in 5%, and no microbe identified in 1/3.

Rheumatic fever is rare in the United States, especially in adults, so

that some authorities recommend no treatment even if GAS is a potential cause

of pharyngitis.Others feel it is important to detect GAS  since antibiotic

therapy can slightly shorten the acute illness, prevent acute rheumatic fever

and possibly prevent suppurative sequelae.  Other potential causes of

pharyngitis that should be considered and diagnosed if likely include

Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) mononucleosis, primary HIV infection, influenza,

gonococcal pharyngitis, diphtheria, and suppurative pharyngeal infections.

The Centor criteria are used to predict whether GAS pharyngitis is present.

*  Tonsillar exudates

*  Tender anterior cervical adenopathy

*  Fever by history

*  Absence of cough

If three or four of these criteria are met, the positive predictive value is

40 to 60 percent.  If fewer than three criteria are present, the likelihood

GAS is causing pharyngitis is less than 20 percent.  If 3 or > Centor criteria

are met, obtain a throat culture for group A streptococcus.  Treat

empirically for GAS if the patient has severe symptoms or treat later for GAS

if the throat culture is positive.

[References:](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Mandell chapter: Pharyngitis

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX NOT BENEFITTED BACTERIURIA
menus.Text:
# BACTERIURIA, CANDIDURIA, AND PYURIA

Asymptomatic bacteriuria (>= 100,000 bacteria per ml of urine) is common in

middle aged and older people, especially those who have chronic medical

conditions. Pyuria is common in persons with bacteriuria and individuals with

indwelling catheters in place. By itself, the presence of pyuria is not

sufficient to diagnose bacteriuria, and the presence or absence of pyuria does

not differentiate symptomatic from asymptomatic urinary infection. Candiduria is

less common than bacteriuria, but the implications of candiduria are similar to

those of bacteriuria.

Many studies, including randomized clinical trials have shown that

treatment of asymptomatic bacteriuria and candiduria, with or without pyuria is

of no benefit, except in certain well-defined circumstances. Antimicrobial

therapy is always accompanied by risk of harms, including drug reactions,

Clostridium difficile colitis, anaphylaxis and death. Except in circumstances

specified below, it is best to not order urinalysis or urine culture in

asymptomatic persons. If bacteriuria, candiduria or pyuria is discovered in an

asymptomatic person for some reason, antimicrobial therapy should not be given

except as specified below.

# Pregnant women or patients undergoing urological procedures with bacteriuria

[Treatment of Asymptomatic Bacteriuria](orzid2-gmenu-abx-asymp-bacteriuria)

# Patients undergoing urological procedures or neutropenic patients with

# candiduria

[Treatment of Candida Urinary Tract Infections](orzid2-gmenu-abx-candida-uti)

References

Pappas et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2016, 62.409

Nicolle et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2005, 40:643

# CONDITIONS NOT BENEFITTED BY ANTIMICROBIAL THERAPY

Several common conditions associated with inflammation or

microorganisms do not benefit from antibiotic therapy in most or all cases.

Yet, antimicrobials are frequently prescribed for these conditions leading to

unnecessary toxicity and costs, rare deaths, and the relentless increase in

antimicrobial resistance. Please review these conditions and do not give

antimicrobials for these conditions unless there are extraordinary

circumstances that make your situation different. If you have any questions,

please contact the infectious disease physician on call.

# ANTIMICROBIAL CDSS WEB APP LINK AND MOBILE APP INSTALL/UPDATE INSTRUCTIONS

# Link to Antimicrobial CDSS Web App:

[CLICK HERE](orz-gtx-abx-antimicrobial-cdss-web-app)

The Antimicrobial CDSS Web App can be used on any device with an internet

connection to view current local antimicrobial recommendations. The Mobile

App can be installed on your device to have quick access to recommendations even

when you do not have an internet connection. The Mobile App must be updated by

the user periodically to ensure the most current recommendations are downloaded.

# Directions to Install/Update Mobile App:

Use the link above to navigate to the Antimicrobial CDSS Web App. The current

version of the Antimicrobial CDSS App is listed at the top of the Home Page.

Ensure you have the most recent version by following the directions below for

your respective device.

You must be using the Web App to install or update the Mobile App on your

device. It is currently not possible to update the Mobile App from within the

Mobile App.

PC and Android Devices:

Once the Mobile App is ready to install or update on your PC or Android device,

a button with the text "Install/Update App" will appear at the bottom of the

home screen or at the top right of the screen when CDSS version (e.g.

Minneapolis) is selected. Press the button and follow the prompts to complete

the installation or update.

If the "Install/Update App" button is not visible, wait a few minutes for

the button to appear. If the button does not appear, you have the current

version of the Mobile App installed on your device.

Apple Devices:

Select the "Share" button located at the bottom or at the top right of the

screen (appears as a box with an upward facing arrow). Select "Add to Home

Screen" option will appear. Select the option and follow the prompts to complete

the installation or update.

# OROLABIAL HERPES

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompetent patients

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Antiviral therapy is not beneficial after formation of vesicles. However, when

started as soon as prodromal symptoms of burning or tingling occur, antivirals

reduce duration of pain and lesions.

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 5 days \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-400mg-po-q8h)

Alternative

[Valacyclovir 2 gm q12h for 1 day \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-2gm-po-q12h-1-day)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompromised patients

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Immunocompromised patients in whom herpes simplex infections can be more severe

include: patients with HIV infection, organ transplant recipients, patients

undergoing chemotherapy, malnourished patients, and those with compromised skin

integrity.

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 7-14 days\($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-400mg-po-q8h)

< OR >

[Valacyclovir 1 gm q12h for 7-14 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q12h)

# Treatment for severe disease

[Acyclovir 5 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days \($$\) R](psjizid-acyclovir-5-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Chronic suppressive therapy

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Indicated for patients with greater than 6 recurrences or severe recurrences,

immunocompromised patients or as adjunct to prevent transmission. Suppressive

therapy is optional, and some patients may find episodic treatment more

convenient. Patients should be reassessed every few years to evaluate if chronic

suppressive therapy is still necessary.

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO q12h \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-400mg-po-bid)

< OR >

[Valacyclovir 500 mg PO Q24h \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-500mg-po-q24h)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PANCREATITIS

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Antimicrobials are not indicated for uncomplicated pancreatitis.

In cases of necrotizing pancreatitis without infection, antimicrobial

prophylaxis does not improve patient outcomes. Antimicrobials increase the risk

of fungal superinfection and should not be used.

Antimicrobials are indicated for cases with pancreatic abscess, infected

pancreatic pseudocyst, or infected necrotic pancreas (phlegmon). The diagnosis

of infection can be difficult and may require aspiration. Consultation with

Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases is encouraged.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Uncomplicated pancreatitis

No antimicrobials are indicated.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Pancreatic abscess, infected pancreatic pseudocyst, or infected necrotic

# pancreas (phlegmon)

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Total duration of antimicrobial therapy is typically 2 to 4 weeks

# Treatment

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-3-375-gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX PAROTITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PAROTITIS

Infection of salivary tissue is a relatively common disease. It is usually

caused by a stone in the parotid duct, dehydration, or a viral infection.

Sialolithiasis in elderly patients often leads to ductal obstruction and

secondary infection. Other predisposing factors for ductal occlusion include

dehydration, anticholinergic medications such as tricyclics and diphenhydramine,

general disability and trauma. Once culture results are available adjust

antimicrobial therapy based on specific etiologic organism.

For more information click on the link below

[More information on Parotitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-parotitis-more-information)

# Duration of Therapy

Therapy duration varies based on clinical response to treatment and is typically

10-14 days.

# Suppurative Parotitis or Chronic Bacterial Parotitis Exacerbation Empiric

# Treatment

# Immunocompetent Patient

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-2-gm-iv-qd-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-2-gm-iv-qd-metronidazole-500-mg-po-q8h)

< OR >

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h \($\) R](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

If MRSA suspected or alternative to above:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-vanco-15-mg-kg-q12-metron-500-mg-q8)

< OR >

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg PO q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-vanco-15-mg-kg-q12h-metro-500mg-po-q8h)

# Immunocompromised Patient

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](orz-set-abx-pip-taz3-375gm-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro-vanc15mg-kg)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

# Viral Parotitis

Suspect mumps parotitis if there is fever, malaise, earache and bilateral tender

swelling of the parotid glands. For mumps parotitis treat with warm compresses

and analgesics and maintain good hydration to prevent secondary bacterial

infection. Other viral causes of parotitis include influenza and enteroviruses.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Wilson et al., Am Fam Physician. 2014, 89(11)882-888

Mandell chapter:Principles and Practice of Infectious Diseases

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX PAROTITIS MORE INFORMATION
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# MORE ABOUT PAROTITIS

Suppurative Parotitis. Acute bacterial parotitis affects primarily elderly,

malnourished, dehydrated or post-operative patients. Symptoms include fever,

toxicity, and tender swelling along the mandible with purulent drainage from the

parotid duct. Suppurative parotitis is usually unilateral whereas viral

parotitis is usually bilateral. Pain is intense and aggressive, analgesic

therapy is required. Progression of infection may lead to massive swelling of

the neck, respiratory obstruction, septicemia and osteomyelitis of adjacent

facial bones. Empiric antibiotics are required for coverage of Staphylococcus

aureus if bacterial, and surgical drainage is usually necessary.

Chronic Parotitis. Parotitis is recurrent with intermittent acute exacerbations.

Chronic, low-grade bacterial infection results in functional destruction of the

salivary gland. It may be confused with Sjogren's syndrome, a noninfectious

illness. Therapy includes systemic antibiotics. Parotidectomy may eventually be

required for patients with long-standing infection.

Viral Parotitis. Mumps parotitis is characterized by the rapid, painful swelling

of one or both parotid glands within 2 to 3 weeks after exposure to the mumps

virus. Mumps usually involves both parotid glands whereas bacterial parotitis is

unilateral. Other viral causes of parotitis include influenza and enteroviruses.

Mumps parotitis usually resolves spontaneously in 5 to 10 days. Provide

symptomatic relief of pain and fever and maintain hydration to prevent secondary

bacterial infection.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Wilson et al., Am Fam Physician. 2014, 89(11)882-888

Mandell chapter:  Principles and Practice of Infectious Diseases

Sanford keyword: Parotitis

menus.Text:
# PENICILLIN DESENSITIZATION PROTOCOL

Pharmacy Service must be involved. Contact satellite pharmacist at ext. 2040 or

menu 648-6746. Infectious Diseases Consult strongly recommended.

When penicillin is the drug of choice for an infectious disease in a patient

with Type I penicillin allergy, one option is to desensitize the patient.

Severe reactions cannot be predicted accurately with skin testing in the

clinical setting.

# Penicillin Desensitization

> Perform in an ICU or similar setting.

> Discontinue all beta-adrenergic antagonists.

> Have IV line in place and EKG and spirometer ready.

> Once desensitization has been accomplished, therapy with this drug must not

lapse or the risk of allergic reactions increases.

> A history of Stevens Johnson syndrome, exfoliative dermatitis, or erythroderma

are nearly absolute contraindications to desensitization.

# _____________________________________

# ORAL ROUTE

# _____________________________________

Oral route is preferred if oral preparation is available and GI tract is

functional. 1/3 of patients will develop transient reaction, usually mild.

# [Step, 15 minute intervals] concentration, volume

[1] 0.5mg/ml, 0.1ml

[2] 0.5mg/ml, 0.2ml

[3] 0.5mg/ml, 0.4ml

[4] 0.5mg/ml, 0.8ml

[5] 0.5mg/ml, 1.6ml

[6] 0.5mg/ml, 3.2ml

[7] 0.5mg/ml, 6.4ml

[10] 5mg/ml, 4.8ml

[11] 50mg/ml, 1ml

[12] 50mg/ml, 2ml

[13] 50mg/ml, 4ml

[14] 50mg/ml, 8ml

After step 14, observe 30 minutes. If no reaction, give 1 gm IV.

# _____________________________________

# PARENTERAL ROUTE

# _____________________________________

# [Step, 15 minute intervals] concentration, volume

[1] 0.1mg/ml, 0.1ml

[2] 0.1mg/ml, 0.2ml

[3] 0.1mg/ml, 0.4ml

[4] 0.1mg/ml, 0.8ml

[5] 1mg/ml, 0.16ml

[14] 100mg/ml, 0.8ml

[15] 1000mg/ml, 0.16ml

[16] 1000mg/ml, 0.32ml

[17] 1000mg/ml, 0.64ml

After step 17, observe 30 minutes. If no reaction, give 1 gm IV.

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX PERI ASSOC W PERI DIAL
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PERITONITIS ASSOCIATED WITH PERITONEAL DIALYSIS

Peritonitis associated with peritoneal dialysis usually presents with abdominal

pain, fever, nausea or vomiting, and cloudy effluent. The leukocyte

concentration is greater than 100 cells/microliter of dialysate, with more than

50% neutrophils.

Obtain Gram stain, culture, and cell count with differential of dialysate before

antimicrobials are given. Nephrology consultation is essential. If cultures

show Gram-negative or mixed bacterial infection, a gastrointestinal tract

infectious source is more likely. Gram-positive organisms like staphylococci

usually result from external contamination. Fungal peritonitis is rare and

requires immediate catheter removal.

**Antimicrobial recommendations are for empirical therapy only. Regimens should

be tailored according to patient response and microbiology results in

consultation with Nephrology and/or Infectious Diseases for more information.

To prevent catheter occlusion by turbid dialysate, add 1,000 units of heparin

per dialysis bag each day until one day after the dialysate is clear.

If vancomycin is used, trough serum concentrations should be kept above 15

mcg/ml to ensure adequate intraperitoneal levels. Usually vancomycin must be

given every 3 to 7 days. Contact Nephrology and/or Pharmacy for more

information.

# Consult Nephrology in all cases.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Antimicrobial therapy

# Duration

Duration of therapy depends on the pathogen identified. Treat staphylococcal and

streptococcal infections for 2 weeks and all other gram-positive infections for

3 weeks. In patients who have Staphylococcus isolated and had a previous

staphylococcal infection, treat for 3 weeks

# All antimicrobials below are administered via peritoneal dialysate bag over 6

# hours with the option to include heparin 1000 units.

# Empirical treatment while waiting for results of gram stain

[Cefepime 1 gm PD q24h \($$\) R](orzid2-gmenu-pd-cefepime-1-gm-q24h)

<OR>

[Cefazolin 15 mg/kg \($\) R <AND> gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg \($\) R,O PD q24h](orzid2-gmenu-pd-cefazolin-15mg-kg-q24h-and-gent-0-6mg-kg-q24h)

MRSA risk factors

[Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days \($\) R <AND>](orzid2-gmenu-pd-cefepime-1gm-q24h-vanco-15-30mg-kg-q5-7d)

cefepime 1 gm PD q24h ($) [R]

Alternative for severe penicillin or cephalosporin allergy

[Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days \($\) R <AND>](orzid2-gmenu-pd-vanco-15-30mg-kg-q5-7d-and-gent-0-6mg-kg-q24h)

gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg PD q24h ($) [R,O]

# Gram positive organism

[Cefazolin 15 mg/kg PD q24h \($\) R](orzid2-gmenu-pd-cefazolin-15mg-kg-q24h)

< OR >

[Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days \($\) R](orzid2-gmenu-pd-vanco-15-30mg-kg-q5-7d)

# Gram negative organism

[Cefepime 1 gm PD q24h \($$\) R](orzid2-gmenu-pd-cefepime-1-gm-q24h)

Alternative for severe penicillin allergy

[Gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg PD q24h \($\) R,O](orzid2-gmenu-pd-gentamicin-0-6mg-kg-q24h)

# Alternative treatments for narrowing coverage based on isolate susceptibilities

[Cefazolin 15 mg/kg PD q24h \($\) R](orzid2-gmenu-pd-cefazolin-15mg-kg-q24h)

< OR >

[Ceftazidime 1 gm PD q24h \($\) R](orzid2-gmenu-pd-ceftazidime-1gm-q24h)

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 1 gm PD q24h \($\) M](orzid2-gmenu-pd-ceftriaxone-1gm-q24h)

< OR >

[Gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg PD q24h \($\) R,O](orzid2-gmenu-pd-gentamicin-0-6mg-kg-q24h)

< OR >

[Vancomycin 30 mg/kg PD LD then 15 mg/kg PD every 3 to 7 days \($\) R](orzid2-gmenu-pd-vanco-15-30mg-kg-q5-7d)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Antifungal prophylaxis:

Antifungal prophylaxis may be used for the duration of antimicrobial therapy to

possibly reduce the risk of fungal peritonitis.

[Fluconazole 200 mg PO every other day \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-200mg-po-q48h)

<OR>

[Fluconazole 100 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-100mg-po-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# PERIANAL/ANORECTAL ABSCESS

Antibiotics should typically be reserved for patients with an anorectal abscess

complicated by cellulitis, systemic signs of infection, underlying

immunosuppression, or failure to improve with drainage alone.

Cultures of abscess fluid are not routinely recommended. Consider in patients

who will be treated with adjunctive antibiotic treatment for systemic signs of

infection, recurrent infection or nonhealing wounds, or underlying

immunosuppression.

# Primary therapy: abscess drainage

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Adjunctive antimicrobial treatment for patients with above complications.

# Duration of treatment

5 days of antibiotics after incision and drainage is recommended. In the absence

of source control, recommended duration is 7-14 days based on severity of

infection, underlying immunosuppression, and clinical response.

# Mild disease, outpatients, oral transition

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h R](psjzid-amoxicillin-clavulanate-875-125-mg-po-q12h)

mg PO q12h [DI]

# Inpatient treatment

# Severe - critical illness

# PERICARDITIS

Most cases arise from non-infectious causes or are associated with viruses.

Antimicrobial therapy is not indicated unless pericardial fluid is purulent. If

fluid is purulent, pericardial drainage is required in most cases. Modify

antimicrobial regimen and narrow coverage based on results of culture and

susceptibility tests.

Cardiology consultation is essential for management of therapy. Infectious

Diseases consultation is recommended if an infectious origin is suspected.

# Duration of therapy

Duration is based on patient specific factors such as resolution of fever and

clinical signs of infection. Generally, duration is 2 to 4 weeks depending on

how adequacy  of drainage of pericardial fluid and susceptibility of infectious

organism.

# Empirical Treatment

Preferred:

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) R,DI](orz-set-abx-vanco-15-mg-kg-iv-q12h-ceftriax-2gm-iv-q24h)

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PERTUSSIS

Pertussis also known as "whooping cough" is caused by Bordetella pertussis. CDC

recommends antibiotic therapy for those presenting within three weeks of

symptoms (cough). After three weeks, patients may  not be infectious, and thus

antibiotic administration is not routinely recommended.

[Diagnosis of pertussis](orzid2-gmenu-diagnosis-pertussis)

[Prevention of pertussis](orzid2-gmenu-prev-of-pertussis)

# Treatment

[Azithromycin 500mg po day 1, then 250mg q24h for days 2-5 O](orz-set-abx-azithromycin-po-500-250-once-q24h-x4days)

# PHARYNGITIS AND TONSILLITIS

Most cases are viral, primarily due to adenovirus. Aside from streptococcal and

gonococcal pharyngitis, antimicrobials are not indicated. For gonococcal

pharyngitis, use link below for recommendations.

[Treatment of Gonorrheal Infections](orzid2-gmenu-abx-gonococcal)

Consider HIV screening for patients with pharyngitis

[HIV Rapid Test](lrtzhiv-rapid-qualitative)

# Streptococcal Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis

Diagnosis of group A streptococcal (GAS) infection is made through detection by

rapid PCR and should be reserved for patients who have a moderate to high risk

of GAS infection according to the Modified Centor Score. Use link below for

Modified Centor score criteria and for more details.

[More About Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis and Modified Centor score](orzid2-gmenu-more-about-pharyngitis)

[Rapid Strep A throat PCR testing lab order](lrtz-strep-a-pcr)

# PCR Negative, Viral and Other Non-GAS Causes of Pharyngitis Treatment

Antimicrobials are not indicated

# GAS Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis Treatment

Preferred

[Penicillin V 500 mg PO q12h for 10 days \($\) R](psjzid-penicillin-v-500-mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Benzathine penicillin 1.2 million units IM x 1 \($$$\) M](psjzid-benzathine-penicillin-1-2mu-im-once)

[Azithromycin 500mg po day 1, then 250mg q24h for days 2-5 \($\)O](orz-set-abx-azithromycin-po-500-250-once-q24h-x4days)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE (PID)

Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) refers to bacterial infection of the upper

female reproductive tract. Likely bacterial pathogens include Neisseria

gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, anaerobes, enteric Gram-negative rods, and

Streptococcus agalactiae. PID should be considered in sexually active women

with pelvic tenderness and signs of lower genital tract inflammation. Signs and

symptoms may be mild or non-specific, and providers should have a low threshold

to initiate treatment. All women who are diagnosed with acute PID should be

tested for N. gonorrohoeae, C. trachomatis, and HIV. Male sex partners of

patients with PID should be examined and treated (see below) if they had sexual

contact within the 60 days before onset of the patient's symptoms.

Judge severity of infection based on clinical signs and symptoms, including

blood pressure, pulse, mental status, and degree of fever.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

Treat for 14 days.

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once \($\) M < AND > doxycycline 100 mg q12h for 14](orz-set-abx-ceftr-500mg-im-doxyc-100mg-po-metro-500mg-po)

days ($) [DI] < OPTIONAL > metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h ($) [DI]

# For patients who cannot regimen above, call ID

# Treatment of sex partner who is a veteran

Treat for both Chlamydia and Gonorrhea

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once \($\) M < AND > doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 7](orz-set-abx-cef-500mg-im-once-doxycl-100mg-po-q12h)

days ($) [DI]

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once \($\) M < AND > azithromycin 1 gm PO once \($\) M](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-500mg-im-once-azithromycin-1gm-po-once)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment for severe disease

Treat for 14 days.

[Ceftriaxone 1 gm IV q24h M < AND > doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h DI](orz-set-abx-ceftr1gmivq24h-doxy-100mg-iv-q12h-metro500mgiv12h)

<AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q12h [DI]

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PNEUMOCYSTIS JIROVECII PROPHYLAXIS (PCP Prophylaxis)

Indications for primary prophylaxis of P. jirovecii include:

1) HIV/AIDS patients with CD4 count <200 cells/microliter

2) Hematopoietic or organ transplantation patients during immunosuppression

3) Patients receiving Alemtuzumab, temozolomide or fludarabine

4) Patients receiving >/= 20mg equivalent of prednisone per day for over 1 month

5) Patients with acute lymphocytic leukemia, rheumatologic disease receiving

immunosuppressive therapy and certain primary immunodeficiencies (e.g. severe

combined immunodeficiency, idiopathic CD4 T-lymphocytopenia, hyper-IgM

syndrome)

Dose and duration of prophylaxis varies with the indication. Please contact

Infectious Diseases or Hematology/Oncology for more information.

Prophylaxis should be discontinued when host defenses are restored. In persons

with AIDS on highly active antiretroviral therapy, Prophylaxis should be

discontinued when the CD4 cell concentrations remain over 200 cells/microliter

for 3 to 6 months in patients, except that prophylaxis should be continued for

life in those who have had P. jirovecii disease.

# Recommended FIRST-LINE prophylaxis:

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q day \($\) R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-q24h)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 SS tablet q day \($\) R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-ss-q24h)

# Alternative when trimethoprim/sulfa is poorly tolerated or contraindicated:

**Patient should be tested for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6-PD)

deficiency before starting dapsone. Individuals deficient in G6-PD

show about a 2-fold increase in sensitivity toward dapsone-induced hemolytic

anemia.

G6-PD lab test are resulted the same day or next day. May be add on lab.

G6-PD lab result should be "normal" to start dapsone therapy.

[Click here G6-PD Screen Lab Order](lrtz-g6-pd-screen)

[Dapsone 100mg PO q day \($\) DI](psjzid-dapsone-100mg-po-qday-pcp-prophlaxis)

# Alternative to the above preferred regimens:

# Atovaquone is alternative for patient for clinical reason:

(e.g. patients with SLE, hematologic concerns, G6PD deficiency)

[Atovaquone 1500mg q day for PCP prophylaxis \($$\) DI](psjzid-atovaquone-1500mg-qday-pcp-prophylaxis)

References

# EMPIRIC TREATMENT: HOSPITAL ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA (HAP)

Development of pneumonia 48 hours or more after hospital admission.

# Empiric Treatment (see below for MRSA history or clinically unstable patients)

Obtain MRSA nasal PCR and sputum culture before antibiotics, whenever possible.

Narrow therapy based on results of culture and susceptibility tests. Discontinue

MRSA and/or Pseudomonas coverage if not isolated from respiratory cultures.

Discontinue MRSA coverage if MRSA nasal PCR negative.

[Re-evaluate Nosocomial pneumonia at 72 hours](orzid2-gmenu-abx-re-evaluate-72hrs-n-pneumo)

Preferred:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R for 7 days](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h)

<OR >

[Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R for 7 days](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h R for 7 days](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

# History of MRSA infection/colonization

# < OR > clinically unstable (e.g., intubation, hypotension)

ADD MRSA coverage to a regimen above. Discontinue MRSA coverage if MRSA nasal

PCR negative.

[< ADD > Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h  R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Clinically unstable (ICU level care, hypotensive, intubation)

# < AND > history of multi-drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate

[<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV once R,O to an antimicrobial regimen above](psjizid-tobramycin-5-mg-kg-iv-once)

menus.Term1: Coagulase-negative staphylococci, single blood culture positive
menus.Term2: Blood culture, single positive  for coag-neg staph
menus.Text:
# BLOOD CULTURE POSITIVE FOR COAGULASE NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCI (CNS)

CNS are the most common contaminants isolated from blood cultures. When CNS

isolated from blood cultures represent true bacteremia, the blood is usually

obtained from a patient with plastic or metal in the body. The most common

source of coagulase negative staphylococcal bacteremia is an infected

intravascular catheter.

When CNS are isolated from blood, the physician should carefully assess the

patient to decide whether the isolation represents disease or colonization.

Colonization is more likely if a single bottle is positive or both bottles from

a single blood draw are positive. If multiple bottles are positive from separate

blood draws, it is more likely that the isolates reflect disease or colonization

of an intravascular device. Isolates from contaminated bottles often take

several days to become positive. If the patient has risk factors for true

coagulase negative staphylococcal bacteremia, catheter-related blood stream

infection and/or the patient is severely ill, antimicrobials should be given

(see below). If there is a plastic or metal prosthesis in the body, the

physician should evaluate the site for possible infection. If the isolates are

likely to represent contamination and the patient does not seem ill with CNS,

antimicrobial therapy would not be helpful and should not be given.

[Treatment of CNS Bacteremia](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-coag-neg-staph)

[Treatment of CNS Infected Intravascular Catheters](orzid2-gmenu-intravas-cath-coag-neg-staph)

Staphylococci

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PRIMARY INFECTION (CHICKENPOX)

# ________________________________

# Immunocompetent patients

# ________________________________

# Prevention

Vaccinate all adults without evidence of immunity except for pregnant women.

Test antibody first in adults who have uncertain history of chickenpox or

vaccination.

Give Varicella vaccine x 2, 2nd dose 4-8 weeks after 1st dose

# Treatment

Therapy must be started within 24 hrs onset of rash.

[Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/d for 5-7 days \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-800mg-po-5x-d)

# Alternative

Therapy must be started within 24 hrs onset of rash.

[Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q8h for 5 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q8h)

# ________________________________

# Immunocompromised patients

# ________________________________

# Prevention

Immunocompromised patients without prior immunity to varicella who are at risk

for disease include: patients with malignancy, current immunosuppressive

therapy, or HIV infection. Vaccination is not recommended while patients are

immunocompromised.

Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

[Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/day for 7 days \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-800mg-po-5x-d)

< OR >

[Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h for 7 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q8h)

# Treatment for severe disease, or if mild to moderate disease doesn't improve on

# above therapy

[Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h for 7 days \($$\) R](psjizid-acyclovir-10-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

References:

Kim et al. Annals Intern Med. 2018, 168(3):210-220

# SUBOPTIMAL VANCOMYCIN RESPONSE AT 72 HOURS

If the patient has not improved, consider the following:

1. The patient has pneumonia with a pathogen resistant to empirical

antimicrobials (e.g., resistant bacteria, fungi, mycobacteria)

2. The patient does not have bacterial pneumonia.  Consider alternative

diagnoses including pulmonary edema, atelectasis, pulmonary embolus, ARDS,

pulmonary hemorrhage, underlying disease, and neoplasm.

3. The patient has infectious disease outside the lungs.

4. The patient has one or more complications of pneumonia (e.g., empyema, lung

abscess, mediastinitis, or pericarditis)

5. The patient has an adverse drug event

Infectious Disease or Pulmonary consultation is strongly encouraged for patients

who do not respond to initial therapy.

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX REACT PRIM INFECT ZOSTER
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# REACTIVATION OF PRIMARY INFECTION (ZOSTER OR SHINGLES)

Zoster represents reactivation of varicella-zoster virus. After primary

infection, virus remains latent in the sensory dorsal root ganglia.

Reactivation syndrome is characterized by painful, unilateral, vesicular,

dermatomal rash.

# Prevention

Vaccinate all adults greater than or equal to 50 years of age with the

recombinant zoster vaccine regardless of past episode or receipt of the live

zoster vaccine.

Give recombinant zoster vaccine x2, 2nd dose 2-6 months after the first

# ________________________________

# Immunocompetent patients

# ________________________________

# Treatment in persons <50 years

Treatment is not beneficial, none is recommended.

# Treatment in persons >=50 years

Treatment with antivirals can shorten duration of pain and rash in patients over

50 years old. Treatment must be started within 72 hours of onset.

[Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h for 7 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q8h)

There is evidence that addition of corticosteroids to antiviral

therapy decreases pain and duration of rash and improves quality of life

modestly during the acute shingles episode. Corticosteroids do not decrease the

incidence of post-herpetic neuralgia. Some authorities recommend addition of

corticosteroid therapy to antiviral therapy for patients over age 50 years.

Corticosteroids are not recommended for patients at greater risk for steroid

toxicities (e.g., insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, hypertension, peptic

ulcer disease) or for immunocompromised patients.

Optional Recommendation:

[Prednisone 60 mg daily for 7 days then 30 mg daily for 7 days, then 15 mg](psjzid-prednisone-taper-herpes-zoster-tx)

daily for 7 days. ($)

# ________________________________

# Immunocompromised patients

# ________________________________

# Treatment

Immunocompromised patients at increased risk for complications of VZV disease

include: patients with malignancy, current immunosuppressive therapy, or HIV

infection. Treatment with antivirals shortens duration of symptoms and reduces

incidence of complications. In immunocompromised patients, treatment is

recommended to be started at any point during an active infection.

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

[Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO q8h for 7 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q8h)

# Treatment for severe disease or progression from mild to moderate disease in

# patients <=65 years

[Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days \($$\) R](psjizid-acyclovir-10-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

# Treatment for severe disease or progression from mild to moderate disease in

# patients >65 years

[Acyclovir 7.5 mg/kg IV q8h for 7-14 days\($$\) R](psjizid-acyclovir-7-5-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

References:

Kim et al. Annals Intern Med. 2018, 168(3):210-220

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ROSACEA

Rosacea is an inflammatory skin condition resulting in erythema and

telangiectasia of nose, cheeks, eyelids, and forehead. It typically occurs in

mid-life and the etiology is unknown. Erythematous rosacea is the early stage of

the disease and usually manifests with flushing reactions and persistently

erythematous skin. Late-stage disease is known as papulopustular rosace.

Symptoms include papular, pustular, cysts and nodules. Severe disease results in

tissue atrophy and rhinophyma (bulbus nose).

The goal of treatment is control of symptoms, not cure. General treatment

measures include avoiding triggers (e.g. spicy food, alcohol), skin care (e.g.

moisturizing, gentle cleansing, avoiding topical irritants) and using sun

screen. Medical treatment includes topical agents as first line therapy and oral

treatment for refractory disease.

# Papulopustular rosacea

Preferred:

[Metronidazole 0.75% cream topically q24h \($\) DI](psjzid-metronidazole-0-75-cream-topically-q24h)

Alternative:

[Doxycycline 50 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 12 weeks](psjzid2-doxycycline-12wks-50mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Minocycline 50 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 12 weeks](psjzid2-minocylcine-12wks-50mg-po-q12h)

________________________________________________________________________________

**FOR DERMATOLOGY USE ONLY, REQUIRES DERMATOLOGY CONSULT PRIOR TO TREATMENT**

# COMPLICATED INTRA-ABDOMINAL INFECTIONS: SECONDARY PERITONITIS, INTRAABDOMINAL

# ABSCESS, INTRAPERITONEAL ABSCESS

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Complicated Intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) include any infectious process

that extends from an intra-abdominal organ into a sterile space and is

associated with peritonitis with or without abscess.

Community-acquired cIAI: patients without recent procedure related to site of

perforation or abscess

Healthcare-associated cIAI: patients developing a new infection > 48 hours after

an incident intra-abdominal procedure

# Primary therapy: abscess drainage

CT or US-guided percutaneous or surgical drainage should be considered in all

cases for diagnostic confirmation, microbiologic evaluation, and therapy.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Adequate source control: 4 days after source control

Incomplete source control and no abscess: 5-7 days tailored to improvement.

Re-evaluate need for source control if ongoing signs/symptoms of infection

beyond 7 days

Abscess: 2-6 weeks depending on resolution on repeat imaging. ID Consult

recommended.

# Community-acquired infection without severe illness or immunosuppression

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h for 5 days M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ciprof-400mg-iv-q12-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

# Healthcare-associated infection, severe illness, or immunosuppression

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative for severe beta-lactam reaction:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ciprof-400mg-iv-q12-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

Consider vancomycin for enterococcal coverage in critically ill or

immunosuppressed patients:

[<ADD> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R to one of the regimens above](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# SECOND RECURRENCE OF CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

Discontinue implicated antibiotic(s). Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic

therapy is still needed. Avoid antiperistaltic agents (narcotics, loperamide,

etc.). Avoid antacid therapy without clear indication. If diarrhea has improved

or resolved prior to starting C. difficile treatment, consider re-assessing the

diagnosis before initiating therapy. C. difficile infection usually responds to

antimicrobial therapy. If symptoms do not respond to appropriate antimicrobial

therapy, re-consider the diagnosis.

# Second Recurrence CDI:

[Vancomycin Extended Pulse-Taper Regimen M](psjzid-vancomycin-taper-and-pulse-dosing)

(Vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h for 10 days, then taper and pulse with 125 mg po q12h

for 7 days, then 125mg po qday for 7 days, then 125mg every other day for 6

weeks)

< OR >

If fidaxomicin not previously used:

[Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days M](psjzid-fidaxomicin-200mg-q12h-10d)

< OR>

If fidaxomicin extended-pulse regimen not previously used:

[Fidaxomicin Extended-Pulse Regimen M](psjzid-fidaxomicin-extended-pulse-regimen)

(Fidaxomicin 200mg po bid x5days,then 200mg every other day x20days)

# Third or more recurrence: Consult Gastroenterology or Infectious Disease

# Sotrovimab (EUA)

-Sotrovimab is available via FDA Emergency Use Authorization (EUA)

for treating patients that meet specific criteria. Sotrovimab is

not FDA approved drug.

-Sotrovimab EUA does NOT include post-exposure prophylaxis.

# Sotrovimab Emergency Use Authorization (EUA)

[Click here PROVIDER/PHARMACIST to complete EUA prior to ordering/administering](orz-gtx-abx-url-link-for-eua-fill-out-by-provider)

# Printable Fact Sheets

[Click here Fact Sheet for Patients/Caregivers EUA Sotrovimab](orz-gtx-abx-url-sotrovimab-patient-eua-fact-sheet)

[Click here Fact Sheet for Health Care Providers EUA Sotrovimab](orz-gtx-abx-url-sotrovimab-provider-fact-sheet-eua)

# **Treatment:**

# Note: See below for inclusion criteria. Does not require ID approval.

ID available to discuss if needed.

# Inclusion Criteria

# ALL of the following criteria must be met for a patient to receive:

1) Patient has a laboratory-confirmed diagnosis of mild to moderate COVID-19.

2) Patient is not hospitalized due to COVID-19.

Note: patient may be hospitalized for some other reason.

3) Patient does NOT require oxygen therapy for COVID-19.

For patients on chronic oxygen therapy: patient does NOT require an

increase in baseline oxygen flow rate due to COVID-19.

4) Administration will begin within 7 days of symptom onset.

5) Patient does not have known hypersensitivity to sotrovimab or components.

6) Patient has at least one risk factor for progression to severe disease

including hospitalization or death.

See link below for complete list:

[Click Here Fact Sheet for HCP - Medical Conditions or Other Factors](orz-gtx-abx-url-sotrovimab-provider-fact-sheet-eua)

7) Counseling is provided and documented in the electronic health record per EUA

The provider has communicated with the patient/caregiver regarding

information contained in the "Fact Sheet for Patients". The patient/

caregiver has been given the Fact sheet, informed that the drug is an

unapproved drug that is authorized for use under an EUA, given information

on alternatives and their risks and benefits, and the patient/caregiver

has the right to refuse or accept. (See top of page for Fact Sheet)

# Exclusion Criteria

If patient recieved tixagevimab plus cilgavimab previously, discuss with ID.

# If above requirements are met, place medication order:

[INV-Sotrovimab 500mg IVPB ONCE](orz-set-abx-inv-sotrovimab-nursing-inst)

Monitor patient during infusion and 1 hour after infusion completed.

*Patients treated with this drug should continue to self-isolate and use

infection control measures (wear mask, isolate, social distance, avoid

sharing personal items, clean and disinfect "high touch" surfaces, and

frequent handwashing) according to CDC guidelines.

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# Daily Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Asplenia

The need for daily antibiotic prophylaxis and its duration is typically

determined individually based on patient age, immune status, history of

infection, potential for adverse drug reactions and other factors.

# Consider Prophylaxis:

1) Approximately 1 year prophylaxis for all patients following splenectomy.

2) Lifelong prophylaxis for patients with history of sepsis or other severe

infections caused by encapsulated organisms.

3) Prophylaxis for as long as the patient is immunocompromised or for life

for patients with concurrent immunocompromising conditions (e.g. hematologic

malignancy, hypogammaglobulinemia, solid-organ transplant, advanced liver

disease, or HIV infection).

# Daily antibiotic prophylaxis is in addition to the emergency supply.

# Preferred:

[Amoxicillin 500MG PO bid for daily prophylaxis asplenic patient \($\) R](psjzid-amoxicillin-500mg-po-bid-for-daily-prophy-asplenia)

# Alternative:

[Cephalexin 250MG PO bid for daily prophylaxis asplenic patient \($\) R](psjzid-cephalexin-250mg-po-bid-for-daily-prophy-asplenia)

# Alternative for penicillin and beta lactam allergy:

[Azithromycin 250MG PO qday for daily prophylaxis for asplenic patients \($\) DI](psjzid-azithromycin-250mg-po-qday-daily-prophy-asplenia)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# Asplenia Functional or Anatomical

Following a splenectomy there is considerably increased risk of developing

septicemia from invasive encapsulated organisms, namely Streptococcus pneumonia,

Haemophilus inluenza type b and meningococcus. Key measures to prevent

such infections include education, vaccination, prophylactic antimicrobial

therapy in selected patients, and early empirical therapy for febrile

epsisodes. It is critically important to educate patients regarding the

lifelong risk of postsplenectomy sepsis, the importance of vaccinations,

and the need for urgent action in response to a febrile episode.

# Management of an Episode of Fever in an Asplenic Patient

[Management of an Episode of Fever in an Asplenic Patient](orzid2-gmenu-abx-management-of-febrile-episode-asplenia)

# Initiation of vaccine regimen:

ROUTINE VACCINATIONS SHOULD BE UP TO DATE.

See CDSS immunization section to order, if needed.

[click here Recommendations: Vaccinations for Adults without a Spleen](orz-gtx-abx-url-asplenia-vaccination-recommendations)

# Specific Asplenia Vaccines:

Ideally splenectomy vaccinations should be given 10 to 12 weeks before

elective splenectomy.  Where this is not possible they can be given up to

two weeks before or at least two weeks post-splenectomy.

[click here Place Order for specific vaccines for asplenia](orzid2-gmenu-abx-splenectomy-chart)

# Use of Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Asplenia:

Use of antibiotic prophylaxis, in addition to vaccination, further reduces

the risk of infection and poor outcomes.

# Daily Antibiotic Prophylaxis: (in addition to emergency supply)

[Daily Antibiotic Prophylaxis INPATIENT](orzid2-gmenu-abx-splenectomy-daily-antibiotics)

# Emergency Supply Empiric Abx for Fever or Other Signs of Systemic Infection:

# **OUTPATIENT ORDERS**

[Self-medicate Empiric Antibiotics](orzid3-gmenu-splenectomy-empiric-abx)

# SPONTANEOUS BACTERIAL PERITONITIS (SBP)

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

SBP is infection of the peritoneal cavity in the absence of apparent trauma or

other obvious cause. SBP occurs primarily in people with end-stage liver disease

and ascites. The diagnosis is made when a peritoneal fluid sample has >/= 250

polymorphonuclear leukocyte cells per microliter, or when bacterial pathogens

are isolated.

Long-term SBP prophylaxis is indicated for patients who experience a first

episode of SBP.

# SBP

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h for 5 days M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h for 5 days R,DI](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Prophylaxis in a patient with a previous SBP episode

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q24h R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-q24h)

< OR >

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h R,DI](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-500mg-po-qday-prophylaxis)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Prophylaxis in a patient with cirrhosis and variceal hemorrhage

Treat initially with an intravenous antimicrobial then step down to an oral

antimicrobial when the patient can tolerate oral treatment.

Duration of therapy: Treat for a total of 7 days (intravenous and oral)

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h R,DI](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Prophylaxis for hospitalized patients with refractory low-protein ascites

# (less than 1 gm/dL peritoneal fluid)

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q24h until discharge from](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-q24h)

hospital [R,DI]

< OR >

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h until discharge from hospital R,DI](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-500mg-po-qday-prophylaxis)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS DECOLONIZATION
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS DECOLONIZATION

From 10% to 40% of adults are colonized with Staphylococcus aureus, and the

anterior nares is the most common site of colonization. A majority of people

never have disease with S. aureus, but a tiny fraction of people develop

clinical infections with the S. aureus that has colonized their skin or anterior

nares. Steps to decolonize the skin and anterior nares can transiently diminish

or eradicate S. aureus colonization and can prevent post-operative wound

infection in certain high-risk circumstances. For people who have other forms of

recurrent S. aureus disease, not associated with an operation, results with

decolonization have been disappointing, and decolonization is not routinely

recommended. Colonization typically reappears in most patients within a few days

or weeks after decolonization has been attempted. Clinicians occasionally wish

to attempt decolonization for patients with frequent, troublesome recurrences.

The procedure here is one of several that have been studied, but none have been

particularly effective over the long run.

Consultation with Infectious Diseases is recommended.

# Inpatient Decolonization Order Set:

[Mupirocin 2% ointment topically q12h M <AND> chlorhexidine 4% liquid](orz-set-abx-chlorhexidine-mupirocin-decolonization)

topically q24h nursing text order [M] for 5 days

# Outpatient Decolonization Order Set:

Order if patient is being discharged within 5 days

[Mupirocin 2% ointment topically BID M <AND> chlorhexidine 4% liquid](orz-set-abx-op-chlorhexidine-mupirocin-decolonization)

topically qday [M] for 5 days

# Instructions

* Patient must wear clean clothes after bathing to prevent recontamination

* Bedding and linens must be changed/cleaned daily until the end of the

decolonization protocol.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# References:

Bradley S Clin Infect Dis 2007, 44: 186

Lonneke G NEJM 2010, 362: 9

Schweizer et al, JAMA 2015, 313.212:162-2171
