menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX STASIS DERMATITIS
menus.Text:
# STASIS DERMATITIS

Stasis dermatitis is a common condition that is often confused with

bacterial cellulitis. Stasis dermatitis does not benefit from antimicrobial

therapy. It is important to distinguish between the two. The provider

should be mindful of the fact that bacterial cellulitis can occur on skin

with underlying stasis dermatitis. (See link below for bacterial cellulitis)

Common risk factors for venous stasis include advancing age, family

history of venous disease, increased body mass index, smoking, a history of

trauma, prior venous thrombosis and pregnancy. Chronic venous disease and

arterial vascular disease have some common risk factors (eg, smoking,

obesity) and pathophysiological processes. The most common symptoms reported

by patients with chronic venous disease are limb discomfort (tired, heavy

legs), pain, and limb swelling. Swelling is often worse with prolonged

standing and improves with leg elevation and walking. The skin of the

anterior surfaces of the lower legs often has brown or blue-grey

hyperpigmentation.

People with venous stasis are prone to develop stasis dermatitis which

is one of the most common and earliest dermatologic signs of chronic venous

insufficiency. Stasis dermatitis is an inflammatory process that presents as

an eczematous rash characterized by itching, erythema, scaling, weeping,

erosions, and crusting. Longstanding cases may develop lipodermatosclerosis

a fibrosing panniculitis of the subcutaneous tissue. Lipodermatosclerosis

typically starts with a firm area of induration at the medial ankle. As the

process progresses, the entire leg lower leg can become involved with

extension up to the mid leg in more advanced cases. The skin overlying the

panniculitis is typically heavily pigmented and bound down to the

subcutaneous tissues. Brawny edema above the fibrotic area and on the foot

below is seen in advanced cases. Leukocytosis and fever are common in people

with stasis dermatitis.

Chronic venous disease is the most common cause of leg ulcers. They

are usually found low on the medial ankle over a perforating vein, or along

the course of the great or small saphenous veins. They occur more proximally

if precipitated by trauma. Venous ulcers are not found on the forefoot or

above the level of the knee. Venous ulcers can be multiple or single, and

can be exquisitely tender, shallow, exudative and have a granulation base.

The ulcer borders are usually irregular but not undermined. They can extend

circumferentially around the leg if left untreated.

Arterial ulcers are typically painful, and punched out or stellate. The

surrounding skin is red and taut. Some arterial ulcers are pale - others have

a black or yellow eschar. They are often associated with trauma and commonly

occur on the foot over pressure points. There may be other signs of arterial

insufficiency on the lower limb including thin atrophic or hairless skin,

poor pedal pulses, diminished capillary refill, or hypertrophic deformed

nails.

Patients with stasis or lipodermatosclerosis are prone to bouts of

bacterial cellulitis, usually caused by Staphylococcus aureus or encapsulated

streptococci. Typically, stasis dermatitis develops slowly, over a week or

more. It is often bilateral. The onset of bacterial cellulitis is usually

abrupt, typically developing over 1 or 2 days. Bacterial cellulitis often

starts in one area and spreads to adjacent areas. Bacterial cellulitis is

unilateral. Both can present with fever and leukocytosis.

In a patient with stasis and cellulitis and the physician is uncertain

about whether bacterial cellulitis is present, the physician should consider

a trial of bed rest, leg elevation, and if there is fluid overload, diuresis

If the cellulitis improves in 24-48 hours, antibacterial therapy and the

attendant adverse reactions can be avoided. If it is clear that bacterial

cellulitis has occurred, antimicrobial therapy should be given.

[Bacterial Cellulitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-cellulitis)

References

Stevens et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2014, 59(2): e10-52

Up-to-Date article: Stasis dermatitis

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX SUPPURATIVE THROMBO EMP THERAPY
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SUPPURATIVE THROMBOPHLEBITIS - EMPIRICAL THERAPY

Obtain blood cultures before starting empirical antimicrobials.

Peripheral vein suppurative thrombophlebitis may require surgical intervention

in addition to antimicrobial therapy. The usual treatment for jugular vein

suppurative thrombophlebitis (Lemierre's syndrome) and vena cava suppurative

thrombophlebitis is prolonged antimicrobial therapy, with or without

radiological or thrombolytic clot removal. Consult Infectious Diseases and

Vascular Surgery for more information.

Modify antimicrobial regimen and narrow coverage based on results of culture and

susceptibility tests.

# Duration of therapy

A minimum of 4 to 6 weeks of antimicrobial therapy is appropriate and may be

abbreviated in peripheral vein infections based on patient specific factors.

Antimicrobial therapy should be continued until there is definite clinical

response and oral antimicrobial therapy may be used after completion of initial

course of intravenous therapy.

# Empirical treatment for peripheral vein infections and central vein infections

# associated with a venous catheter

Preferred:

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M](orz-set-abx-vanc-15-mg-kg-iv-q12h-ceftriax-2-gm-iv-q24h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h \($\)](orz-set-abx-vanco-15-mg-kg-iv-q12h-gent-5-mg-kg-iv-q24h)

[R,O]

# Empirical treatment for jugular vein infection (also known as Lemierre's) or

# suppurative pelvic vein infection

Consultation with Surgery and Infectious Diseases is encouraged.

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

# For catheter-associated infection, add vancomycin to one of the above treatment

# regimens

[< ADD > Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SYPHILIS

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases. Evaluation and management are complex.

Syphilis is a sexually transmitted disease caused by the spirochete Treponema

pallidum that can manifest as a variety of signs or symptoms. Primary syphilis

typically consists of painless ulcers or chancre at the site of infection with

regional adenopathy. Secondary syphilis often includes a skin rash (disseminated

and/or including the palms and soles), fever, malaise, mucocutaneous lesions and

lymphadenopathy. Tertiary syphilis includes those with cardiovascular or

gummatous disease.

Latent syphilis is a period of disease when a patient does not have symptoms but

is found to be infected through serologic testing. Early latent syphilis refers

to latent syphilis acquired within the preceding year and late latent syphilis

refers to all other cases of latent syphilis. Neurosyphilis, Ocular syphilis or

Otosyphilis, can occur at any stage of syphilis with early manifestations (e.g.

meningitis, stroke, vision or hearing loss) occurring within the first months to

years of infection and late manifestations (e.g. dementia, tabes dorsalis)

occurring after 10-30 years.

# Diagnosis

A presumptive diagnosis is made through use of a nontreponemal or serologic test

(i.e. rapid plasma reagin [RPR]) and a treponemal test (i.e. fluorescent

treponemal antibody absorbed [FTA-ABS]). Direct methods through darkfield

microscopy and direct fluorescent antibody (DFA) must be used for definitive

diagnosis since T. pallidum cannot be cultured.

[Syphilis antibody test with reflex to rapid plasma reagin \(RPR\)](lrtz-syphilis-ab-w-reflex-to-rpr-w-titer)

# Management of sex partners

Persons with sexual contact with a person with primary, secondary or early

latent syphilis within the last 90 days should be presumptively treated even if

serologic test is negative.

# Primary, Secondary and Early Latent Syphilis

Preferred treatment

[Benzathine Penicillin 2.4 million units IM once \($$$\) M](psjzid-benzathine-penicillin-2-4mu-im-once)

Secondary treatment for patients who are not pregnant

[Beta-lactam Reaction Assessment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 14 days](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Tertiary and Late Latent Syphilis

Preferred treatment

[Benzathine Penicillin 2.4 million units IM qweek \($$$\) M x3 doses](psjzid2-benzathine-penicillin-2-4mu-im-qweek-x3-syphilis)

Secondary treatment for patients who are not pregnant

[Beta-lactam Reaction Assessment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 28 days](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Neurosyphilis, Ocular syphilis or Otosyphilis

Consult Infectious Disease for treatment

# TOCILIZUMAB (IL- 6 RECEPTOR BLOCKER) FOR TREATMENT OF COVID-19

# Inclusion Criteria:

o Confirmed COVID-19 <AND>

o Hospitalized <AND>

o Clinical evidence of progressive COVID-19 (supplemental oxygen, high-flow

oxygen, or noninvasive or invasive ventilation) <AND>

o Patient does not have a known hypersensitivity to tocilizumab

# Exclusion Criteria:

o Outpatient

o Current documented or suspected bacterial or fungal infection

o Active tuberculosis

o ANC < 1000/mm3, platelet count < 50,000/mm3, ALT/AST> 10x ULN

o GI perforation

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# **1ST DOSE**

# If all the above inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria, the 1st

# dose of tocilizumab may be ordered below based on patient's weight.

# Patient weight >/= 90 kg

[Tocilizumab 800 mg IV x 1 \($$$$\) DI,O](psjizid-tocilizumab-800mg-iv-x1-covid-19-dose-1)

# Patient weight >/= 65 kg and < 90 kg

[Tocilizumab 600 mg IV x 1 \($$$$\) DI,O](psjizid-tocilizumab-600mg-iv-x1-covid-19-dose-1)

# Patient weight >/= 40 kg and < 65 kg

[Tocilizumab 400 mg IV x 1 \($$$$\) DI,O](psjizid-tocilizumab-400mg-iv-x1-covid-19-dose-1)

# Patient weight < 40 kg

[Tocilizumab 8 mg/kg IV x 1 \($$$$\) DI,O](psjizid-tocilizumab-8mg-kg-iv-x1-covid-19-dose-1)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# **2ND DOSE**

# If the patient's condition has not improved in 12-24 hours after receiving the

# 1st dose, a second dose may be considered in select patients. Please page ID for

# discussion of 2nd dose.

References:

Horby, Peter W., et al. Tocilizumab in patients admitted to hospital with

COVID-19 (RECOVERY): preliminary results of a randomized, controlled, open-

label, platform trial. Medrxiv (2021).

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# FULMINANT CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

# Discontinue any antibiotics if possible.

# Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic therapy is still needed.

# Discontinue antacid therapy if possible.

# There are no available data supporting the use of fidaxomicin for treatment of

# fulminant CDI.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Antimicrobial therapy for CDI should be continued for 10 days. In patients being

treated with antibiotics for predisposing infections, consider continuing

treatment for 7 days after completion of those antibiotics. If patient is being

treated for CDI recurrence, pulse taper therapy is indicated after resolution of

severe disease. Refer to mild to moderate CDI treatment menu for

recommendations.

# Treatment if ileus is present

General Surgery consult is essential for ileus or megacolon. Recommend

Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Disease consults for fulminant CDI. Deliver

antimicrobials by intravenous, oral, and rectal routes.

[Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI <AND> vancomycin 500 mg PO q6h M](orz-set-abx-metronidazole-500mg-iv-q8h-vanco-500mg-caps-po-q6h)

<AND> vancomycin enema 500 mg in 100 ml normal saline q6h [M]

**ONLY for Vancomycin NG administration**

[Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI <AND> vancomycin 500 mg NG soln q6h M](orz-set-abx-metro-500mg-iv-q8h-vanco-500mg-po-ng-q6h)

<AND> vancomycin enema 500 mg in 100 ml normal saline q6h [M]

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment if ileus is not present

Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases consults are recommended.

[Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI <AND> vancomycin 500 mg PO q6h M](orz-set-abx-metro-500mg-iv-q8h-vanco-cap-500mg-q6h-w-o-enema)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX TPOXX MONKEYPOX TREATMENT
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CDC MPOX TREATMENT WITH TPOXX

# Eligibility:

o Consent: Must have documented consent by patient or legally authorized

representative in paper or i-Med consent

o Primary/empiric treatment: Confirmed diagnosis or suspected infection based

on exposure and/or symptoms while testing is pending.

o Secondary Treatment: Complications from replication competent vaccinia

infection from vaccination, secondary transmission, or other exposure. TPOXX may

be used after VIGIV treatment or in conjunction with VIGIV and/or with other

therapies based on clinical judgement.

o Post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP): May be considered on a case-by-case basis in

consultation with the CDC. Eligibility for PEP use depends on high risk exposure

confirmed or probable case and alternative or complement to PEP vaccination

is needed based on clinical judgment (e.g. vaccine allergy, immunocompromise).

o Dosage and duration: Weight based dosing for 14 days. But it may be longer

based on clinical progress but not to exceed 90 days. Oral tecovirimat capsule

should be taken by mouth with a full glass of water within 30 minutes after

eating a full meal of moderate or high fat (ideally about 600 calories and 25

grams of fat).

o CDC Case Reports Forms:  To be completed and returned to CDC by treating

physicians per IND protocol.

[CLICK HERE for link to required documents \(MPox Taskforce Teams group\)](orz-gtx-abx-tpoxx-documents-link)

# Exclusions:

o Patient or legally authorized representative unwilling to sign an informed

consent and refuse tecovirimat treatment

o  Known allergy to tecovirimat and/or excipients of tecovirimat

o  Upon negative test results for orthopoxvirus whose treatment was initiated

based on clinical manifestations prior to laboratory results.

o For IV tecovirimat only: patients with severe renal impairment (creatinine

clearance <30 mL/min)

# Oral Treatment:

Patients 40kg to < 120 kg

[INV-Tecovirimat 600 mg \(3 capsules\) orally q12h for 14 days](orz-set-abx-inv-tecovirimat-600-mg-orally-q12h-14-days)

*Places medication orders for inpatient and outpatient (included in order set)

Patients 120 kg and Above

[INV-Tecovirimat 600 mg \(3 capsules\) orally q8h for 14 days](orz-set-abx-inv-tecovirimat-600-mg-orally-q8h-14-days)

*Places medication orders for inpatient and outpatient (included in order set)

# Intravenous Treatment:

o Very ill hospitalized patients who are unable to take oral therapy or for whom

there is a concern that oral drug absorption may be altered.

o IV tecovirimat should not be administered in patients with severe renal

impairment (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min) and should be used with caution in

patients with moderate (creatinine clearance 30-49 mL/min) or mild (creatinine

clearance 50-80 mL/min) renal impairment.

o IV tecovirimat should be switched to the oral formulation as soon as patients

can take oral medications and/or gastrointestinal disfunction impacting

absorption has resolved.

Patients 35 kg to < 120 kg

[INV-Tecovirimat 200 mg IV q12h over 6 hours for 14 days](orz-set-abx-inv-tecovirimat-200mg-iv-q12h-x14-days)

*Places medication orders for 2 seperate INV-tecovirimat IV 100mg q12h orders

for a total of 400 mg over 24hrs via slow infusion.

Patients 120 kg and Above

[INV-Tecovirimat 300 mg IV q12h over 6 hours for 14 days](orz-set-abx-inv-tecovirimat-300mg-iv-q12h-x14-days)

*Places medication orders for 2 seperate INV-tecovirimat IV 150 mg q12h orders

for a total of 600 mg over 24hrs via slow infusion.

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# TRICHOMONAS VAGINITIS AND URETHRITIS

Male sexual partners of women with trichomonas vaginitis will not have symptoms

but should be treated to prevent recurrent vaginitis in the female sexual

partner.

Recommended to treat all sexual partners exposed during the last 60 days.

# Diagnosis

The discharge is purulent, malodorous, and thin. The vaginal pH is greater

than 4.5. Nucleic Acid amplification test (NAAT) for trichomonas has improved

sensitivities and specificities compared to wet mount.

# Treatment of Initial Episode WOMEN ONLY  (See below for MEN)

Pregnant women with trichomonas infection may be treated with metronidazole

during any trimester.

[Metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) DI](psjzid-metronidazole-500mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment of Initial Episode MEN ONLY  (See above for WOMEN)

[Metronidazole 2 gm PO once \($\) DI](psjzid-metronidazole-2gm-po-once)

# Treatment failure

1st failure

[Metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) DI](psjzid-metronidazole-500mg-po-q12h)

2nd failure

[Metronidazole 2 gm PO q24h for 7 days \($\) DI](psjizid-metronidazole-2gm-po-q24h)

3rd failure

Consult Infectious Disease

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX TYPHLITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# NEUTROPENIC ENTEROCOLITIS (TYPHLITIS)

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Neutropenic enterocolitis, also known as "typhlitis" or "necrotizing

enterocolitis", is a severe intraabdominal infection that occurs in neutropenic

patients, especially in those with acute leukemia.

Send stool for C. difficile testing to exclude of C. difficile infection.

[Clostridioides difficile infection](orzid2-gmenu-abx-assoc-colitis)

Hematology-oncology, Infectious Diseases and general surgery consults are

essential.

Broad spectrum antimicrobials that include anaerobic coverage should be

initiated promptly.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Continue antimicrobial therapy until normalization of body temperature, recovery

of neutropenia (unless planning to transition back to antimicrobial

prophylaxis), recovery of thrombocytopenia, return of normal gastrointestinal

function and resolution of bacteremia if initially present. Infectious Disease

consult recommended to guide duration if perforation, abscess, or other

complicating feature present.

# Treatment

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

# Alternative

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ciprof-400mg-iv-q12-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

# Uncomplicated UTI is an infection confined to the bladder in afebrile women or

# and urgency.

odor or color, delirium (acute mental status change, confusion) without systemic

menus.Text:
# UPPER RESPIRATORY INFECTION (URI)

Upper respiratory infections include several common syndromes including

the common cold, bronchitis (see below), pharyngitis (see below) and sinusitis

(see below). Most are caused by viruses and there is no benefit from

antimicrobial therapy. If a patient presents with a URI, consider specific

infections that do respond to antimicrobial therapy like herpes simplex

stomatitis, pertussis or thrush. If no condition that benefits from

antimicrobial therapy is present, antimicrobials will almost certainly not help

but will likely select for antimicrobial resistance and may lead to other

adverse effects.

[Bronchitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-bronchitis)

[Sinusitis](orzid2-gmenu-acute-sinusitis)

[Pharyngitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-pharyngitis)

References

Kogawa et al, General medicine, 2009, 10:7-15

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# URETHRITIS ASSOCIATED WITH SEXUALLY TRANSMITTED DISEASES

The main differential in a person who presents with dysuria is between cystitis

and urethritis. Bacterial urethritis is more likely in people with mild

dysuria, onset over a few days, or recent sexual contact.

The two most common sexually transmitted urethritis pathogens are Neisseria

gonorrhoeae and Chlamydia trachomatis. Nucleic acid amplification tests for

these pathogens are more sensitive than culture and should be used for patients

at risk for sexually transmitted urethritis.

[Chlamydia & GC PCR/LCR test](lrtzid-chlamydia-gc-urine-naat)

# For patients who have recently been treated for urethritis

[Treatment of recurrent or persistent urethritis](orzid2-gmenu-recurrent-persist-urethritis)

When dysuria is from a sexually transmitted disease, the patient's sexual

partner(s) during the previous 60 days should be evaluated for sexually

transmitted infection.

If diagnostic tests for the cause of urethritis are not feasible, therapy for

both N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis should be given to partners.

# Initial treatment of patients and sex partners

Patients and partners are often infected with both N. gonorrhoeae and C.

trachomatis. Treat for both pathogens unless one is ruled out by lab test.

[Treatment for gonococcal urethritis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-gonococcal)

[Treatment for chlamydial or non-gonococcal urethritis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-chlamydia-urethritis-cervicitis-or-proctitis)

menus.Text:
# HELP, additional information:

[Consult Urology \(inpatient\)](gmrctz-urology-inpt)

# Urinary Catheters:

Bladder catheters are used for urinary drainage, or as a means to collect

urine for measurement. Many clinical situations are appropriate for the

placement of catheters, BUT too frequently they are used without proper

indication or continued longer than needed.  Unwarranted urinary catheters

are placed in 21 to 50 percent of hospitalized patients.

Daily evaluation of the ongoing need for the catheter is essential to reduce

complications including catheter-assosciated urinary tract infection.

Hospital-acquired urinary tract infection is the most common type of

nosocomial infection.

Alternatives to indwelling urethral catheterization should be considered

and include intermittent catheterization, external sheath (ie,condom)

catheters, suprapubic catheters, and in some cases, supportive management

with protective garments.

# 04 Description of types of catheters and insertion

# Indications for Catheterization:

[Management of immobilized patients \(eg, stroke, pelvic fracture\)](orzid2-gmenu-urinary-catheter-due-to-immobilization)

[Management of patients with neurogenic bladder/spinal cord injury](orzid2-gmenu-abx-urinary-catheter-neurogenic-bladder)

1) Urinary blockage due to clots

2) Urinary blockage due to urinary obstruction (not clots)

3) Urinary retention due to neurological condition

4) Urinary incontinence

5) Prolonged surgical procedure

6) Monitoring of urinary output

7) Open sacral wound

8) Suprapubic catheter

9) Nephrostomy tubes present

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX URINARY CATHETER NEUROGENIC BLADDER
menus.Text:
# HELP, additional information:

[Urology Consult \(Inpatient\)](gmrctz-urology-inpt)

# Management of patients with neurogenic bladder/spinal cord injury

The goal of an SCI bladder program is to preserve renal function while

eliminating urine at regular and socially acceptable times, avoiding high

bladder pressures, retention, incontinence, and infection.

Clean intermittent catheterization, which is the removal of the catheter

immediately after bladder decompression with recatheterization on a scheduled

basis is  preferred. Clean intermittent catheterization is performed at regular

intervals, usually every 4 hours. A bladder volume of less than 500 mls

of urine is targeted in order to avoid bladder distention, pressure, and reflux

as well as to reduce the incidence of infections.

Clean technique intermittent catheterization has a lower infection rate

compared with with the use of indwelling catheters.

# 08 Order for  Intermittent Catheterization Q4Hours

Intermittent urinary incontinence is expected. Condom catheters (for men)

and adult diapers are important short-term interventions. Recommend rule

out infection and adjust the frequency of intermittent catheterization

and fluid intake.

# 10 Order for condom catheter for men

# 12 Order for adult diapers

For patients unable to perform intermittent catheterization and without

available caregivers, a chronic indwelling catheter may be necessary.

The indwelling catheter should be changed each month to minimize infections.

For admitted patients who normally use chronic indwelling catheter:

# 13 Order for indwelling catheter

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ABX VAGINITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BACTERIAL VAGINOSIS

Vaginitis usually presents with discharge, itching, irritation, odor, or pain.

Bacterial vaginosis is the most common form of vaginitis. Normal hydrogen

peroxide and lactic acid producing vaginal flora, including Lactobacillus

species, is reduced and high concentrations of anaerobic bacterial pathogens are

present. Pathogenic bacteria commonly include Gardnerella vaginalis, Mycoplasma

hominis, Nobiluncus, Prevotella and other Gram-negative anaerobes.

Vaginal pH should be measured, and the specimen should be examined under the

microscope for identification of clue cells (epithelial cell coated with

bacteria). In bacterial vaginosis the vaginal pH is high (> 4.5), the discharge

is homogenous and gray-white, and the specimen has a positive amine or whiff

test characterized by a fishy odor before or after addition of 10% KOH.

Bacterial vaginosis nucleic acid amplification tests are available for common

pathogens to aide in identification of pathogen(s).

Bacterial vaginosis may be transmitted sexually. Patients at risk of sexually

transmitted infections should be assessed for treatment.

[Sexually Transmitted Infections and HIV Exposure](orzid2-gmenu-abx-sexually-transmitted-infection)

# Treatment

Preferred:

[Metronidazole 500 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 7 days](psjzid-metronidazole-500mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Metronidazole vaginal gel 0.75%, contents of 1 applicator intravaginally qhs \($\)](psjzid-metronidazole-0-75-gel-vaginal-qhs)

[DI] for 5 days

< OR >

[Clindamycin phosphate vaginal cream 2%, contents of 1 applicator](psjzid-clindamycin-2-crm-vag-1applful-cream-qhs)

intravaginally qhs ($) [H,O] for 7 days

Alternative:

[Clindamycin 300 mg PO q12h \($\) H,O for 7 days](psjzid-clindamycin-300mg-po-q12h)

menus.Text:
# Information on adding MRSA nares screening with new IV Vancomycin starts:

MRSA nares screening will be ordered on all new IV Vancomycin starts.

MRSA nares may be a helpful tool in identifying patients with low risk of

MRSA infection in whom empiric vancomycin may not be required.

A negative MRSA nares does not definitively rule out the presence of MRSA

elsewhere and is one factor to consider in the de-escalation of vancomycin

(and other anti-MRSA antimicrobials).

# References

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ACUTE SINUSITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ACUTE SINUSITIS

Most cases of acute sinusitis are viral and resolve within 10 days. Symptoms

(nasal congestion, purulent nasal discharge, and tooth or facial pain) can be

treated with decongestants, analgesics, and nasal saline. Diagnosis of acute

sinusitis is based on the presence of at least 2 major or 1 major and at least 2

minor symptoms.

# Major Symptoms

1. Purulent anterior nasal discharge

2. Purulent or discolored posterior nasal discharge

3. Nasal congestion or fullness

4. Facial pain or pressure

5. Hyposmia or anosmia

6. Fever

# Minor Symptoms

1. Headache

2. Ear pain, pressure or fullness

3. Halitosis

4. Dental pain

5. Cough

6. Fatigue

If patient meets criteria above for acute sinusitis, treat with antimicrobials

according to the following criteria for mild to moderate or severe bacterial

sinusitis.

# Mild to moderate bacterial sinusitis

1. Symptoms persisting beyond 10 days

< OR >

2. Double-sickening - Symptoms typical of viral upper respiratory infection

initially improving for 5-6 days then worsening with new development of fever,

headache or increased nasal discharge.

[CLICK HERE for treatment of mild to moderate bacterial sinusitis](orzid2-gmenu-mild-to-mod-sinusitis)

# Severe bacterial sinusitis

Severe signs or symptoms of high fever (>/= 102 degrees Fahrenheit, >/= 39

degrees Celsius) and purulent nasal discharge for 3-4 consecutive days or facial

pain lasting for at least 3-4 consecutive days at the beginning of illness.

[CLICK HERE for treatment of severe bacterial sinusitis](orzid2-gmenu-severe-sinusitis)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PREVENTION OF ANTIVIRAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

# Severly Immunosuppressive Chemo-immunotherapy

# Purine Analogues

Chemotherapy with purine analogues such as fludarabine, cladribine, or

pentostatin results in major cellular-immunodeficiency that may outlast the

exposure by months and enhances the risk for viral infections.

Recommend antiviral prophylaxis for patients treated with purine analogues,

if at least one of the following risk factors is present:

a) Second-line chemotherapy

b) Treatment with corticosteroids

c) CD4 cell count <50/ul

d) Age >65 years

e) Prolonged Mild or Moderate Neutropenia: Mild<1000 Neutrophils /

ï¿½L (Grade III neutropenia) OR Moderate: <500 Neutrophils/ï¿½L

(Grade IV neutropenia)

# Recommendations:

Duration: Antiviral prophylaxis should be initiated in the first week of

therapy and continued until 2 months after completion of therapy.

[Acyclovir 800 MG PO q12h \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-800-mg-po-bid-prophylaxis)

# Alemtuzumab Therapy:

Alemtuzumab is a potent reactivator of latent intracellular pathogens,

including CMV. Chemotherapy with alemtuzumab results in major cellular-

immunodeficiency that may outlast the exposure by months and enhances the

risk for viral infections. The risk of viral disease increases with the

intensity and duration of functional T-cell suppression experienced with

recipients of alemtuzumab.

# Recommendations:

Duration: Initiate antiviral prophylaxis with alemtuzumab therapy and

continue therapy for at least 2 months after last dose or until CD4 counts

are greater than or equal to 200 cells/ul, whichever is later.

[Acyclovir 800 MG PO q12h \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-800-mg-po-bid-prophylaxis)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PREVENTION OF VIRAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

# Prophylaxis for Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) or Varicella Zoster Virus (VZV)

[Select for recommendations for antiviral prophylaxis](orzid2-gmenu-antiviral-immunosuppressive-malignancy)

# Prophylaxis for Influenza and Other Respiratory Viruses

Yearly influenza vaccination with inactivated vaccine is recommended for all

patients receiving chemotherapy for malignancy and all family and household

contacts and health care providers.

Optimal timing of vaccination for patients being treated for cancer is not

established, but serologic responses may be best between chemotherapy cycles

(greater than 7 days after the last treatment) or greater than 2 weeks

before chemotherapy starts.

Patients with active malignant disease are at higher risk for upper

respiratory infections due to influenza, parainfluenza or respiratory

syncytial virus (RSV). Although response to vaccination with the attenuated

influenza vaccine in patients on chemotherapy is variable, ranging

from 24-75%, immnunoprophylaxis with the influenza vaccine is recommended for

patients with active malignant disease or chemotherapy, lymphoproliferative

disease, or multiple myeloma. In areas and seasons where influenza is

endemic, chemoprophylaxis can be considered in addition to vaccination in

exposed patients with a high risk of influenza complications.

# Recommendations:

[Seasonal Influenza Recommendations](orzid2-gmenu-abx-influenza-recommendations)

# Prophylaxis for Cytomegalovirus (CMV)

Prophylaxis and monitoring for CMV reactivation is not recommended unless the

patient has received an allogeneic HSCT. Usually the recommendations for

surveillance and prophylaxis of CMV infections from the institution

performing the HSCT will be followed.

# Recommendations:

[Consult Infectious Disease](gmrctz-infectious-disease-inpt)

# Prophylaxis for Chronic Hepatitis B

Reactivation of chronic hepatitis B in patients undergoing immunosuppressive

or antineoplastic treatment is a severe complication. Patients with positive

HBsAg, chronic hepatitis B infection, or a previous episode of HBV

reactivation who will receive immunosuppressive therapy should receive

prophylaxis.

Recommend routine testing for Hepatitis B prior to initiating Rituximab

(Anti-CD20 antibody) therapy in patients.

# Recommendations:

[Hepatitis B Evaluation Anti-CD20 Antibody](orzid3-gmenu-hepatitis-b-evaluation-anti-cd20-antibody)

[Consult Infectious Disease](gmrctz-infectious-disease-inpt)

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PREVENTION OF VIRAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

Viral infections reactivate in a small percentage of people with malignancy.

Most viral infections in patients with hematologic malignancies or solid

tumors result from reactivation of asymptomatic latent infections,

predominantly of herpes viruses, including herpes simplex virus (HSV),

varicella zoster virus (VZV) and cytomegalovirus (CMV). Exogenous

respiratory tract infections caused by influenza, parainfluenza

or respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) are less common.

The main risk factor for clinically relevant reactivation is profound

disruption of cellular immune response, usually due to chemotherapy.

The duration and severity of neutropenia are of lesser importance.

The risk of viral disease increases with the intensity and duration

of functional T-cell suppression. Patients receiving conventionally

dosed chemotherapy regimens for solid tumors experience no major

T-cell suppression and do not have a higher incidence of

invasive viral infections.

# This section is organized mainly by type of malignancy.

There are separate sections for purine analogues (fludarabine,

cladribine, pentostatin), alemtuzumab and rituximab.

Select below for recommended antiviral prophylaxis:

[Solid Tumors, Acute Leukemia, or Lymphoma](orzid2-gmenu-antiviral-type-of-malignancy)

[Purine analogues or Alemtuzumab](orzid2-gmenu-antiviral-immunosuppressive-malignancy)

[Stem cell transplant recipients \(autologous or allogeneic\)](orzid2-gmenu-antiviral-stem-cell-malignancy)

[Rituximab therapy](orzid2-gmenu-antiviral-stem-cell-malignancy)

Select below for recommended antiviral prophylaxis:

menus.Term1: Viral prophylaxis in solid tumors, acute leukemia, or lymphoma
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PREVENTION OF ANTIVIRAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

# **Solid Tumors**

# No Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommended

Solid tumors do not significantly compromise the cellular immune system.

Therefore, patients are at low risk for opportunistic viral infections.

Documented invasive viral infections are very rare. Coincidental

mucocutaneous infections by herpes simplex are easily treated and do not

result in life-threatening invasive infections. Reactivation of

Cytomegalovirus (CMV) or Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) is rarely observed.

# **Acute Leukemia**

# Herpes simplex virus-seronegative patients

No Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommended

In patients with acute leukemia, treatment is highly aggressive and consists

of a combination of various cytotoxic agents administered in sequential

cycles as induction, consolidation and maintenance therapy. Persistent, i.e.

>10 days and profound neutropenia (<500 neutrophils) regularly occurs and

correlates with the risk of developing fever and infections. Almost all viral

infections during neutropenia constitute reactivations of herpes viruses.

None of the available studies demonstrated an effect of antiviral prophylaxis

on the initiation of antibiotic treatment, number of febrile days, duration

of antibiotic treatment, and onset of opportunistic infections. Therefore, no

recommendation for antiviral prophylaxis in patients with acute leukemia can

be given.

# Herpes simplex virus-seropostive patients

Patients undergoing leukemia induction therapy should receive prophylaxis.

[Acyclovir 800 MG PO q12h \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-800-mg-po-bid-prophylaxis)

# **Lymphoma**

# No Antiviral Prophylaxis Recommended

Rituximab is a monoclonal anti-CD-20 antibody used for treatment of

lymphomas. It leads to a profound depletion of circulating B-cells. B-cells

recover usually within 3-6 months after treatment. Prolonged administration

of rituximab (e.g., maintenance treatment >12 months) may result in a

significant decrease of levels of immunoglobulin M. Parvovirus B19 and JC-

papovavirus infections have been reported with maintenance rituximab therapy,

but drugs that would prevent these infections are not available. There is no

substantial increase in risk of reactivation of herpes viruses (including

HSV, VZV, and CMV).

Recommend routine testing for Hepatitis B virus prior to initiating Rituximab

therapy in patients.

[Hepatitis B information page](orzid2-gmenu-abx-hepatitis-b)

[Hepatitis B Evaluation Anti-CD20 Antibody](orzid3-gmenu-hepatitis-b-evaluation-anti-cd20-antibody)

Cancer Patients

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# APPENDICITIS WITHOUT PERFORATION

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid2-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Patients with an acutely inflamed appendix and no gangrene or perforation are

considered to have uncomplicated appendicitis. Patients with gangrene,

perforation, peritonitis, or abscess have complicated appendicitis. Treatment

with antibiotics is an option for patients who are unfit for surgery or refuse

surgery. Treatment with antibiotics should not be used routinely as an

alternative to surgery.

# Select for treatment of complicated appendicitis

[Link to appendicitis with perforation menu](orzid2-gmenu-appendicitis-with-perforation)

# Treatment of uncomplicated appendicitis

Surgical management:  Administer prophylaxis regimen below prior to surgery

only. Stop antibiotics after the surgery.

Surgical prophylaxis:

[Cefazolin weight-based dosing preop < AND >  metronidazole 500 mg IV once](orz-set-abx-cefaz-2gm-ivpb-x1-metro-500mg-iv-x1)

Post-surgical: antibiotics not recommended after appendectomy

# Interval appendectomy or no appendectomy

Duration of therapy: Treat with antibiotics for 7 days total

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

Healthcare-associated infection, critical illness, or immunosuppression:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-metronidazole-500-mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative for severe Beta-lactam reaction:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI](orz-set-abx-ciprof-400mg-iv-q12-metron-500mg-iv-q8h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU APPRO INTRAVAS CATH-ASSOC INFECT
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# APPROACH TO INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED INFECTION

The likelihood of colonization of an intravenous catheter increases with time,

increasing noticeably after 3 days. Patients whose catheters become colonized

may or may not develop local or systemic signs or symptoms. All types of

catheters are associated with risk of local and catheter-associated bacteremia.

Since central catheters are usually used for more days than peripheral

catheters, central catheters have a greater risk of catheter-associated

bacteremia.

When catheter-related bacteremia is suspected, draw blood cultures from both the

catheter and a peripheral vein. Growth rate between the two cultures may be used

to determine if the source of bacteremia is likely catheter-associated. If the

catheter obtained culture's time to positivity is 2 hours or more before the

peripheral vein obtained culture's time to positivity, this suggests catheter-

associated infection. Sample any exudate at the catheter site for gram stain and

culture.

Suppurative thrombophlebitis presents with inflammation in and around a vein.

There may be local thrombosis and/or bacteremia. Cases may be life-threatening

and can require surgical drainage.

[Suppurative thrombophlebitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-suppurative-thrombo-emp-therapy)

For patients with catheter-associated bacteremia with virulent pathogens like

Staphylococcus aureus, gram-negative bacilli, or candida, catheter removal is

almost always necessary. For mild or moderate cases with less virulent

organisms like coagulase-negative staphylococci, antimicrobial therapy is

successful without catheter removal about half of the time. The decision about

whether to remove the catheter depends on severity of illness, the need for the

catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.

# Antimicrobial lock therapy

For cases in which an infected catheter is not removed, the success rate is

improved when the infected catheter is filled with an antimicrobial solution

during periods when the catheter is not used. Consult Infectious Diseases or

Pharmacy for information.

In Staphylococcus aureus cases, document that bacteremia has cleared during

antimicrobial therapy. Infectious Disease consultation is required for all

cases of S. aureus bacteremia.

For a patient whose blood cultures remain positive for more than 3 days or with

a catheter tunnel abscess or who has a prosthetic device, contact Infectious

diseases.

References

Gaur et al., Clinical infectious diseases 2003, 37.4

Mandell chapter: Infections Caused by Percutaneous Intravascular Devices

Mandell chapter Sepsis, Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock

Mermel et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases 49 (2009)

Up-to-Date article: Prevention of Intravascular Catheter Associated Infection

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# APPROACH TO BRAIN ABSCESS

Brain abscess is a focal infection of the brain parenchyma. Symptoms often

include headache, fever, altered mental status, seizures, and focal neural

deficits. Pathogens vary based on primary site of infection and patient's immune

status. Bacteria cause most infections in immunocompetent patients whereas a

wider array of pathogens, including fungi, cause infection in immunocompromised

patients.

Streptococci are the most isolated pathogen, often isolated from mixed

infections. Bacteroides are also commonly isolated in mixed cultures. Enteric

gram-negative bacilli are typically isolated in patients with otitic foci,

bacteremia, or post-neurosurgery. Staphylococcus aureus is commonly isolated in

a pure culture and in patients with endocarditis or cranial trauma. Brain

abscess caused by Listeria and Nocardia may occur in patients who are

immunocompromised.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) should be obtained in all patients with

suspected brain abscess for diagnosis and determining number of lesions. Prior

to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic (CT) -

guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess material for

determination of infectious pathogen.

Solitary brain abscesses usually result from the spread of focal ear, sinus, or

dental infection (contiguous source). Cases with multiple abscesses often result

from hematogenous spread from infections such as endocarditis, abdominal

infection, or lung abscess.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Empiric Treatment After Obtaining Abscess Sample, When Possible

[Brain abscess from contiguous or hematogenous spread of infection](orzid2-gmenu-brn-absc-cont-hemato-sprd-infect)

[Post-surgical or post-traumatic brain abscess](orzid2-gmenu-brn-absc-post-surg-post-traumatic)

# Treatment Based on Isolated Pathogen

When infectious organism is identified, adjust antimicrobials to optimize

therapy

[Nocardia spp.](orzid2-gmenu-brn-absc-nocardia-spp)

[Pseudomonas spp.](orzid2-gmenu-brn-absc-pseudomonas-spp)

[Toxoplasma gondii](orzid2-gmenu-brn-absc-toxoplasma-gondii)

# BABESIA SPECIES

Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat for 7-10 days. If patient has persistent relapsing disease, treat for 6

weeks including 2 weeks after babesia are no longer detected in blood smear.

# Treatment of mild to moderate disease

[Azithromycin 500 mg PO once on day 1, then 250 mg PO q24h \($\) O for 6](orz-set-abx-azithro-500-then-250-q24h-atovaquone-750-q12h)

Alternative

# Treatment of severe disease

[Azithromycin 500 IV q24h \($\) M <AND> atovaquone 750 mg PO q12h \($\) M](orz-set-abx-azithro-500mg-iv-q24h-atova-750mg-po-q12h)

[Dexamethasone 10 mg IV q6h \($\) for 4 days](psjzid-dexamethasone-10mg-iv-q6h-4d)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Antimicrobial Treatment

Note: Antimicrobials depend on S. pneumoniae MIC results. In most cases results

will usually be known only after 2 or 3 days of therapy.

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for a total duration of 10-14 days.

Preferred:

< OR >

# CANDIDEMIA

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

If other yeasts (e.g. Cryptococcus, Histoplasma) are suspected, refer to fungi

section and contact Infectious Diseases for treatment recommendations.

[Fungi](orzid2-gmenu-abx-fungus)

Identification and treatment of the source of infection, in addition to

antimicrobial therapy, is crucial for resolution of infection. This may include

removal of catheters and draining of abscesses if present. Call Infectious

Diseases for advice.

Follow-up blood cultures should be obtained within 24-48 hours after initiating

antimicrobial therapy. Obtain at least 2, preferably 3 blood culture sets from

different venipuncture sites within a 24-hour period.

Treat for 2 weeks after last negative blood culture, resolution of neutropenia,

and candidemia symptoms have resolved.

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH COAGULASE-NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCI (CoNS)

CoNS are normal commensal human skin flora and are not typically pathogenic.

However, they are the most common cause of health care associated blood stream

infections (30%). Unlike other commonly isolated CoNS, S. lugdunensis can cause

severe disease like S. aureus. Refer to Bacteremia Associated S. lugdunensis

recommendations for treatment.

[Bacteremia associated with Staphylococcus lugdunensis](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-s-lugdunensis)

Other commonly isolated CoNS are S. epidermidis, S. haemolyticus, and S.

saprophyticus. In a patient without signs or symptoms of infection, a single

positive blood culture for these CoNS isolates often represents contamination

and not infection. CoNS are more likely to be pathogens in patients with a

prosthetic device. Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-appro-to-endocarditis)

Treatment is indicated when there are more than 1 blood culture bottle is

positive for CoNS. Follow-up blood cultures should be obtained within 24-48

hours after initiating antimicrobial therapy. Identification and treatment of

the source of infection, in addition to antimicrobial therapy, is crucial for

resolution of infection. This may include removal of catheters and draining of

abscesses if present.

# Duration of therapy:

Treat for 7 - 14 days. A longer duration is required in metastatic infection.

Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Treatment for methicillin-susceptible staphylococci (mecA negative)

Preferred:

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

Alternatives:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

# Treatment for methicillin-resistant staphylococci (mecA positive)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH ENTEROCOCCI

Enterococcus faecalis is almost always susceptible to penicillins locally,

ampicillin is more effective than vancomycin in susceptible isolates.

Enterococcus faecium is typically resistant to some beta-lactams,

aminoglycosides, and vancomycin. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-appro-to-endocarditis)

# Duration of treatment

For uncomplicated infections where blood cultures are sterile after 24 hours of

treatment, treat for 7-14 days. A longer duration is needed if infection is

complicated or repeat blood cultures are positive.

# Treatment of susceptible E. Faecalis (Van A/B negative)

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-ampicillin-2-gm-iv-q4h)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment of resistant enterococcus (Van A/B positive)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) should be performed to rule out infectious

endocarditis. Consult Cardiology or Infectious Diseases for more information.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-appro-to-endocarditis)

Follow-up blood cultures should be obtained within 24-48 hours after initiating

antimicrobial therapy.

# Duration of therapy:

Treatment duration requires assessing complexity of infection. Uncomplicated

bacteremia are those who meet the following criteria:

1. Infectious endocarditis has been excluded via TTE

2. Resolution of fever within 3 days of initiating anti-staphylococci

antimicrobial therapy

3. The primary focus of infection has been promptly removed

4. Negative blood cultures within 2-3 days of removing focus of infection and

initiating anti-staphylococci antimicrobial therapy

5. No hematogenous spread of infection to secondary foci

6. No presence of implanted devices

Treat for 2 weeks after last negative blood culture set in uncomplicated

bacteremia. If there is an easily removable or drainable focus (e.g. infected

intravenous catheter, minor abscess, urinary cystitis, or mild to moderate

pneumonia), and this focus has been treated, give parenteral antimicrobials for

2 weeks. Complicated bacteremia requires 4-6 weeks of treatment.

# Treatment of methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA) (mec-A

# negative)

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

< OR >

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

# Treatment of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) (mec-A positive)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH STAPHYLOCOCCUS LUGDUNENSIS

S. lugdunensis is the most pathogenic of the coagulase negative staphylococci

with a severity of infection like that caused by S. aureus.

Transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) should be performed to rule out infectious

endocarditis. Consult Cardiology or Infectious Diseases for more information.

Refer to cardiovascular section for suspected infectious endocarditis.

[Approach to Endocarditis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-appro-to-endocarditis)

Follow-up blood cultures should be obtained within 24-48 hours after initiating

antimicrobial therapy to guide treatment.

# Duration of therapy:

The optimal duration of therapy has not been well established.  In patients with

adequate source control and without complications, treatment for at least 2

weeks after last negative blood culture set is likely adequate. A longer

duration may be required in complicated cases.

# Treatment for methicillin-susceptible S. lugdunensis (mecA negative)

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

# BACTEREMIA ASSOCIATED WITH STREPTOCOCCI

Bacteremia is typically caused by S. pyogenes (Group A), S. agalactiae (Group B)

and S. pneumoniae. If other streptococcal species are isolated contamination is

likely. Treat only if greater than one blood culture is positive. Identification

Treatment duration is not well established. Treat for 7 -14 days depending on

source control and response to treatment. Consult ID for more information.

# Bispecific Antibody Inpatient Administration (Oncology)

Note: The oncologist will see the patient in clinic the day prior to admission

for bispecific antibody treatment. The oncologist will enter the treatment

orders in VCM, our oncology-interfaced software. Once the patient is admitted

the oncology pharmacist will release the orders from VCM to CPRS.

# Guidance on managing Cytokine Release Syndrome (CRS)

# CRS GRADE & DEFINING SYMPTOMS

# MANAGEMENT

# GRADE 1 CRS (Floor patients)

# Administer symptomatic treatment:

# Symptoms require symptomatic treatment only.

# Note: Acetaminophen order below placed with Bispecific medication order.

# If temperature >/=100.4 F or headache or rigors,

[Acetaminophen 650mg PO q6h prn Temp>/=100.4 F or headache or rigors](psjizid-acetamin-650mg-po-q6h-prn-temp-100-4-ha-rigors-crs)

# without hypotension or hypoxia.

Give and then NOTIFY Inpatient Medicine Provider.

# GRADE 2 CRS (Floor patients)

# In addition to Grade 1 treatment above:

# Symptoms require and respond to moderate intervention.

[Sodium Chloride 0.9% 1000 ml IV initial bolus over 2 hours for hypotension](psjizid-sodium-chloride-0-9-first-bolus-crs)

# -Fever greater than or equal to 100.4F

[Sodium Chloride 0.9% 1000 ml IV bolus over 2 hours \(2nd bolus for hypotension\)](psjizid-sodium-chloride-0-9-second-bolus-crs)

# -Hypoxia requiring oxygen therapy, AND/OR

# If hypotension not responsive to 2 liters NS, administer dexamethasone:

# -Hypotension responsive to fluids not requiring

[Dexamethasone 8MG IV x1 STAT for CRS Grade 2](psjzid-dexamethasone-8-mg-iv-x1-crs-grade-2)

# vasopressors.

# If patient not responding to interventions above, call a rapid response to

# transfer patient to ICU.

# Note: Tocilizumab may be given on 3D if delay in transferring patient to ICU.

# GRADE 3 AND 4 CRS (ICU patients)

# In addition to GRADE 2 treatment above:

# Severe symptoms defined as temperature >/=100.4F with:

[Transfer Patient to ICU](orz-set-pcm-transfer-to-micu)

# -Hemodynamic instability requiring a vasopressor (with or

# without vasopressin) OR

# Provider must order EACH dose of Tocilizumab as needed:

# -Worsening hypoxia or respiratory distress requiring high-flow

May repeat q8h if no improvement, no more than 3 doses/24hours and 4 doses total

# oxygen.

Maximum for each dose 800MG

Tocilizumab may be given with corticosteroids.

[Tocilizumab 8 MG/KG IV STAT DOSE#1 \(Grade 3-4 CRS\)](psjizid-tocilizumab-8mg-kg-iv-once-dose-1)

[Tocilizumab 8 MG/KG IV STAT DOSE#2 \(Grade 3-4 CRS\)](psjizid-tocilizumab-8mg-kg-iv-once-dose-2)

[Tocilizumab 8 MG/KG IV STAT DOSE#3 \(Grade 3-4 CRS\)](psjizid-tocilizumab-8mg-kg-iv-once-dose-3)

[Tocilizumab 8 MG/KG IV STAT DOSE#4 \(Grade 3-4 CRS\)](psjizid-tocilizumab-8mg-kg-iv-once-dose-4)

# VASOPRESSORS: use ICU specific orders/order sets

# Reference:

Lee D., et al. ASTCT Consensus Grading for Cytokine Release Syndrome

and Neurologic Toxicity Associated with Immune Effector Cells

Biology of Blood and Marrow Transplantation (2018) 25:625-638

# Guidelines for management of neurologic toxicity, including ICANS

# (Immune Effector Cell-Associated Neurotoxicity Syndrome)

# Immune Effector Cell-Associated Encephalopathy (ICE) Score

[Click here Calculate ICE Score](orzid2-gmenu-ice-assessment-for-icans)

# ICANS GRADE & DEFINING SYMPTOMS

# MANAGEMENT

# Grade 1

-ICE score 7-9 with no depressed level of consciousness

-Supportive care

# Grade 2

-ICE score 3-6 and/or

-Supportive care

-Mild somnolence awaking to voice

[Click here to order Dexamethasone 10mg IV ONCE STAT](psjzid-dexamethasone-10mg-iv-once-stat)

[Click here to order Dexamethasone 10mg IV q12h](psjzid-dexamethasone-10mg-ivp-q12h)

-Monitor neurologic symptoms and consider consultation with neurologist

and other specialists for further evaluation and management.

# Grade 3

-ICE score 0-2 and/or

-Recommend intensive monitoring ICU

-Depressed level of consciousness awakening only to tactile stimulus and/or

-Consider mechanical ventilation for airway protection

-Any clinical seizure focal or generalized that resolves rapidly or

[Click here to order Dexamethasone 10mg IV q6h](psjzid-dexamethasone-10mg-iv-q6h-no-stop-date)

-Nonconvulsive seizures on EEG that resolve with intervention and/or

-Consider repeat neuroimaging (CT or MRI) q 2-3 days if patient has persistent

-Focal or local edema on neuroimaging

Grade >/=3 neurotoxicity

-Consult neurology for seizure control.

# Grade 4

-ICE score 0 (patient is unarousable and unable to perform ICE) and/or

-ICU care

-Stupor or coma and/or

-Consider mechanical ventilation for airway protection

-Life threatening prolonged seizure (>5minutes) or

[Click here to order High dose Methylpred 500mg IV q12h x3days THEN taper](psjzid-methylpred-high-dose-icans-with-taper)

-Repetitive clinical or electrical seizures without return to baseline

[Taper: 250mg IV q12hx2days, then 125mg IV q12hx2days, then 60mg IV q12hx2days]

in between and/or

-Consider repeat neuroimaging (CT or MRI) every 2-3 days if patient has

-Diffuse cerebral edema on neuroimaging, decerebrate or decorticate posturing

persistent Grade >/=3 neurotoxicity

or papilledema, cranial nerve VI palsy, or Cushing's triad

-Treat convulsive status epilepticus (ICU)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BITE WOUNDS

Bite wounds are prone to infection because of the pathogenic oral flora carried

into tissues by teeth. Clean wounds with soap and water as soon as possible.

Consult Orthopedic surgery for bite wounds involving the hand.

# Antibiotic Prophylaxis Indications:

Severe injury less than 8 hours, Crush injury, Bone or joint penetration, Wound

of the face or hands or genitals, Immunocompromised host, Asplenia, Advanced

liver disease

*Routine use of prophylactic antibiotics for non-immunocompromised patients with

superficial wounds with no puncture that do not involve the face/ genitals/hands

is not recommended.

# Antimicrobial Treatment:

Empiric treatment for suspected or established infection following bite wound In

these cases, therapy should be directed against pathogen identified by Gram

stain and culture whenever possible.

# Rabies Prophylaxis:

Consider rabies post-exposure prophylaxis for all animal bite cases. Contact

Infectious diseases for assistance.

# Consider tetanus immunization status:

If immunization is up to date, nothing more needs to be done to prevent tetanus.

If immunization is lacking, and: wound IS NOT tetanus prone, bring immunization

up to date with Td wound IS tetanus prone, bring immunization up to date with Td

< AND > Human Tetanus Immune Globulin Inject 250 units deeply into muscle (deep

IM)

# Select below for Tetanus vaccination information page:

[Tetanus, Diphtheria and Acellular Pertussis Vaccine Information Page](orzid3-gmenu-abx-tdap-vaccine-information-page)

# Prophylaxis:

Duration 3 to 5 days:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID for 5 days R](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

Unable to take oral antimicrobials:

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

Alternative for patients with penicillin allergy:

depends on the bite: call ID if further questions

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 5 days < AND > metronidazole 500 mg PO](orz-set-abx-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-metro-500mg-po-bid)

BID for 5 days

# Empiric treatment for suspected or established infection:

Duration 7 to 14 days:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID for 10 days R](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

Unable to take oral antimicrobials:

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

Alternative for patients with penicillin allergy:

depends on the bite, call ID if further questions

[Moxifloxacin 400 MG PO qday for 10 days R,DI](psjzid-moxifloxacin-400-mg-po-q24h)

BODY LICE (PEDICULOSIS CORPORIS)

Lice are parasitic insects. Human lice survive by feeding on human blood.

Body lice proliferate in places where crowding of persons with poor hygiene is

common, especially homeless persons.

Infested clothing and bed linen should be heat washed or discarded.

Itching is the most common symptom, but some patients present only with

excoriations and inflammation on the neck and trunk.

# Treatment

A repeat application may be used if live lice are seen 7-10 days after

treatment.

[Permethrin 1% lotion Apply to affected area for 10 minutes then comb out](psjzid-permethrin-1-lotion-to-affect-area-10min)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BRAIN ABSCESS FROM CONTIGUOUS OR HEMATOGENOUS SPREAD OF INFECTION

Prior to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic

(CT) - guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess

material for determination of infectious pathogen. Adjust antimicrobial regimen

to optimize therapy and treatment duration to optimize therapy based on pathogen

once isolated.

Broad spectrum empiric antimicrobials are indicated initially for brain abscess.

Staphylococcus aureus is a common pathogen. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more

effective than vancomycin for susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus is

isolated, once methicillin- resistance is ruled out, switch to an

anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen

in post-surgical patients, and those who are known to be colonized with

Pseudomonas.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Duration is typically 6-8 weeks, with the shorter duration for those with

cerebritis only or drained abscess, longer for undrained or encapsulated

abscesses, multiple or loculated abscesses, abscess in an immunocompromised

host.

# Empiric Treatment for Solitary Brain Abscess from Contiguous Source

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-2gm-iv-q12h-metro-500mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative:

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O](psjizid-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h)

# Empiric Treatment for Solitary Brain Abscess from Unknown Source, From

# Hematogenous Spread, Multiple Brain Abscesses or History of MRSA Infection or

# Colonization

Preferred if Pseudomonas is not likely:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-metro-500mg-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Preferred if Pseudomonas is likely:

[Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h \($$\) R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-cefe2gmivq8h-metro500mgivq8h-vanco15mg-kgivq12hstat)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BRAIN ABSCESS WITH NOCARDIA SPP.

Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) should be obtained in all patients with

suspected brain abscess for diagnosis and determining number of lesions. Prior

to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic (CT) -

guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess material for

determination of infectious pathogen.

Nocardia brain abscesses typically occur in immunocompromised patients and is

often concomitant with disseminated or pulmonary infection. May occur with

meningitis and/or ventriculitis.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat with IV therapy for total duration of 3-6 weeks in immunocompetent and 6

weeks in immunocompromised patients. Switch to oral antimicrobials after

completing IV therapy and treat for an additional 3 months or more (longer for

meningitis, immunocompromise or extensive disease).

# Initial IV Therapy

[Sulfamethoxazole 75 mg/kg - trimethoprim 15 mg/kg IV q8h \($$$\) R,DI <AND>](orz-set-abx-tmp-smz-15-75mg-kg-iv-q8h-imipenem-1gm-iv-q8h)

imipenem 1000 mg IV q8h ($$) [R]

If Nocardia isolate is susceptible to third generation cephalosporins

[Sulfamethoxazole 75 mg/kg - trimethoprim 15 mg/kg IV q8h \($$$\) R,DI <AND>](orz-set-abx-tmp-smz-25-75mg-kg-iv-q8h-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q12h)

ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h ($) [M]

If multiorgan or rapidly progressive disease, in addition to above therapy

[< ADD > Amikacin 7.5 mg/kg IV q12h \($$\)](psjizid-amikacin-7-5-mg-kg-iv-q12h)

Alternative

[Linezolid 600 mg IV q12h \($$$$\) DI,O < AND > imipenem 1 gm IV q8h \($$\) R](orz-set-abx-linezolid-600mg-iv-q12h-imipenem-1gm-iv-q8h)

# Oral Therapy, After Completing IV Therapy Above

For immunocompetent patients, treat with one of the below PO antimicrobials for

at least 3 months after initial IV treatment. For immunocompromised patients,

Treat with 2 of the below antimicrobials for at least one year.

[Sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim 2 DS PO q12h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-2ds-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Minocycline 100mg q12h\($\) DI](psjzid-minocycline-100mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h \($\) R](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

to optimize therapy based on pathogen once isolated.

Broad spectrum empiric antimicrobials are indicated initially for brain abscess.

Staphylococcus aureus is a common pathogen. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more

effective than vancomycin for susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus is

isolated, once methicillin- resistance is ruled out, switch to an

anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen

in post-surgical patients, and those who are known to be colonized with

# BRAIN ABSCESS WITH TOXOPLASMA GONDII

Prior to beginning antimicrobial therapy, when possible, computed topographic

(CT) - guided aspiration or surgery should be performed to obtain abscess

material for determination of infectious pathogen. Adjust antimicrobial regimen

to optimize therapy based on pathogen once isolated.

Central nervous system toxoplasmosis occurs mostly in HIV-infected patients.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Continue treatment for a minimum of 6 weeks after resolution of signs/symptoms,

followed by suppressive therapy until sustained immune reconstitution occurs.

Suppression can be discontinued if CD4 count >200 for 6 months.

# Treatment

Preferred:

Patient weight >/= 60 kg

menus.Text:

# NON-SEVERE COMMUNITY-ACQUIRED PNEUMONIA TREATED IN AN INPATIENT SETTING

Common alternative explanations include heart failure, thromboembolic disease,

COPD exacerbation, viral pneumonitis, aspiration pneumonitis, or tumor. Most of

the latter conditions do NOT benefit from antimicrobials.

# Duration of therapy

Patients with CAP should be treated for a minimum of 5 days, should be afebrile

for 48-72 hours, and should have no more than 1 CAP- associated sign of clinical

instability before discontinuation of therapy.

# Criteria for clinical stability

Temperature less than/equal to 100 degrees F Heart rate less than/equal to 100

beats/minute Respiratory rate less than/equal to 24 breaths/minute Systolic

blood pressure greater than/equal to 90 mm Hg Arterial oxygen saturation greater

than/equal to 90% --OR-- PO2 greater than/equal to 60 mm Hg on room air Ability

to maintain oral intake Normal mental status

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Stepdown empiric treatment for CAP (Intravenous to Oral conversion)

[Stepdown empiric treatment for CAP with oral antibiotics](orzid2-gmenu-cap-outpatient-treated-setting)

Note: These regimens may also be used to convert patients to oral medications

prior to discharge.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Preferred

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h for 5 days M <AND> azithromycin 500 mg PO x1 on](orz-set-abx-pna-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-qd-and-azithromycin-500mg-po)

day 1, then 250 mg PO Q24H for 4 days [M]

# Prior respiratory isolation of MRSA within the last 12 months

ADD MRSA coverage to preferred regimen above or antipseudomonal regimen below.

Obtain cultures/nasal PCR to allow for de-escalation.

[< ADD > Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-vanco-pna-new-start-mrsa-nares)

# Prior respiratory isolation of P. aeruginosa within the last 12 months

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R <AND> azithromycin 500mg PO x1 on](orz-set-abx-pna-piperacillin-tazo-and-azithromycin-500-250-po)

day 1, then 250 mg PO Q24H for 4 days [M]

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV Q8H R <AND> azithromycin 500 mg PO x1 on day 1, then 250 mg](orz-set-abx-pna-cefepime-2gm-q8h-and-azith-500-250-po)

PO Q24H for 4 days [M]

# Alternative

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SEVERE Community-Acquired Pneumonia (CAP) Treated in Intensive Care Unit (ICU)

# Criteria for Defining SEVERE Community-acquired Pneumonia

Validated definition includes either one major or three or more minor criteria

MAJOR CRITERIA:

Septic shock with need for vasopressors

Respiratory failure requiring mechanical ventilation

MINOR CRITERIA:

Respiratory rate greater than or equal to 30 breaths/minute

PaO2/FiO2 ratio less than or equal to 250

Multilobar infiltrates

Confusion/disorientation

Uremia (blood urea nitrogen level greater than 20 mg/dl)

Leukopenia* (WBC less than 4,000 cells/microliter)

*Due to infection alone (i.e., not chemotherapy induced)

Thrombocytopenia (platelet count less than 100,000 microliters)

Hypothermia (core temperature less than 36 degrees C)

Hypotension requiring aggressive fluid resuscitation

# Recommendation for duration of antibiotic therapy for CAP:

Patients with CAP should be treated for a minimum of 5 days, should be

afebrile for 48-72 hours, and should have no more than 1 CAP-

associated sign of clinical instability before discontinuation

of therapy.

# Criteria for clinical stability:

Temperature less than/equal to 100 degrees F

Heart rate less than/equal to 100 beats/minute

Respiratory rate less than/equal to 24 breaths/minute

Systolic blood pressure greater than/equal to 90 mm Hg

Arterial oxygen saturation greater than/equal to 90% --OR--

PO2 greater than/equal to 60 mm Hg on room air

Ability to maintain oral intake

Normal mental status

# _____________________________________________________________

# Treatment on INTENSIVE CARE UNIT (ICU)

# _____________________________________________________________

# Stepdown empiric treatment for CAP (Intravenous to Oral conversion)

(Specific therapy should be guided by culture results.)

[Link Stepdown empiric treatment for CAP with oral antibiotics](orzid2-gmenu-cap-outpatient-treated-setting)

# Recommend blood and lower respiratory tract specimen cultures for all patients

# with Severe CAP.

[Lab Order: Sputum Culture & Gram Stain](orz-set-lab-sputum-cult-gram-stain)

[Lab order: Blood culture x2](orz-set-lab-blood-culture-x2)

# Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for MRSA -OR-

# Prior Respiratory Isolation of MRSA within last 12 months:

ADD MRSA COVERAGE. Obtain nasal PCR and cultures to allow deescalation or

confirmation of need for continued therapy. SEE MRSA Section below

# Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for P. aeruginosa-OR

# Prior Respiratory Isolation of P. aeruginosa in the last 12 months:

COVER for P. aeruginosa. Obtain cultures to allow deescalation or

confirmation of need for continued therapy. SEE P. aeruginosa section below

# Preferred Standard Regimen: (no MRSA or P. aeruginosa coverage)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h\($\) M <AND> azithromycin 500 mg IV once](orz-set-abx-pna-cef-2gm-iv-and-azithromycin-500mg-iv)

on day 1, then 250 mg IV Q24H for 4 days ($) [M]

# Alternative Standard Regimen:

[Link Fluoroquinolones FDA Serious Adverse Reactions](orz-gtx-abx-idp-fluoroquinolones-fda-warnings)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h \($\) R,DI](psjizid-pna-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

< OR >

[Levofloxacin 750 mg po q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid2-pna-levofloxacin-750-mg-po-q24h)

# Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for MRSA -OR-

# Prior respiratory isolation of MRSA in the last 12 months: ADD MRSA coverage

ADD MRSA coverage to Standard Regimen above or Antipseudomonal regimen below:

[< ADD > Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-pna-new-start-mrsa-nares)

# Recent hospitalization and IV antibiotics and risk factors for P. aeruginosa-OR

# Prior respiratory isolation of P. aeruginosa in the last 12 months:

# SELECT REGIMEN BELOW:

# Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV Q6H \($$\) R <AND> Azithromycin 500 mg IV](orz-set-abx-pna-piperacillin-tazo-and-azithromycin-500-250-iv)

on day 1, then 250 mg IV Q24H for 4 days ($) [M]

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R <AND> Azithromycin 500 mg IV x1 on day 1,](orz-set-abx-pna-cefepime-and-azithromycin-iv)

then 250 mg IV Q24H for 4days ($) [M]

# Alternative:

[Link Fluoroquinolones FDA Serious Adverse Reactions](orz-gtx-abx-idp-fluoroquinolones-fda-warnings)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h \($\) R,DI](psjizid-pna-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU CHRONIC SINUSITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CHRONIC SINUSITIS

Diagnosis of chronic sinusitis is based on presence of at least 2 of the 4

cardinal signs/symptoms lasting >/= 12 weeks. In addition, diagnosis requires

objective evidence of mucosal inflammation using nasal endoscopy and/or CT

imaging. The initial therapy for chronic sinusitis is treatment with intranasal

corticosteroids and saline. For patients with severe nasal blockage by polyps,

treat with a short course of oral glucocorticoids. Reassess patient after 1 to 3

months of intranasal therapy or after completion of glucocorticoid therapy. If

signs/symptoms have not improved, consult surgery, ENT and Infectious Diseases

as treatment is complex.

Acute exacerbations of chronic sinusitis can be caused by discontinuing medical

therapy, viral infections, allergens, noxious inhalants and bacterial or fungal

infections. Bacterial infections should be suspected when the patient has

increased signs/symptoms persisting for more than 10 days. Refer to Severe

Sinusitis recommendations for choice of antimicrobial therapy in these patients.

Repeated use of the same agent should be avoided to prevent promotion of drug

resistant bacteria or increased fungal colonization.

[Severe Sinusitis](orzid2-gmenu-severe-sinusitis)

# Cardinal Signs/Symptoms of Chronic Sinusitis

1. Anterior and/or posterior nasal mucopurulent drainage

2. Nasal obstruction/nasal blockage/congestion

3. Facial pain, pressure, and/or fullness

4. Reduction or loss of sense of smell

# Objective Evidence mucosal inflammation

1. Purulent (not clear) mucus or edema in the middle meatus or ethmoid regions

2. Polyps in the nasal cavity or the middle meatus

3. Radiographic imaging demonstrating mucosal thickening or partial or complete

opacification of the paranasal sinuses

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Chow et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2012, 54(8) e72-e112

Mandell chapter: Sinusitis

Meltzer et al, J Allergy Clin Immunol. 2004, 114(6) S155-S212.

Rosenfeld et al, Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery. 2015, 152(4) 598-609

Rudmik et al., JAMA. 2015, 314(9) 926-939
