menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU CMI DEFECTS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

CELL-MEDIATED IMMUNITY (CMI) DEFECTS

Patients with reduced CMI include those with HIV/AIDS, hematologic malignancies,

cytotoxic chemotherapy, and congenital abnormalities.  Patients with cell-

mediated immune defects are more susceptible to infections from ubiquitous

microorganisms that do not usually cause infection in healthy patients.  The

specific organisms that are more likely to be associated with disease vary

depending on the specific type of immune defect present, but include:

Pneumocystis jirovecii (formerly Pneumocystis carinii), Mycobacterium avium,

Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Salmonella spp., Candida spp., Aspergillus spp.,

Toxoplasma gondii, varicella-zoster virus, cytomegalovirus, Epstein-Barr virus,

and Cryptosporidium parvum.

These infectious diseases usually have a subacute or chronic presentation.  The

best approach in most circumstances is for the clinician to conduct a methodical

diagnostic workup to identify the specific pathogen and guide therapy.

Empirical antimicrobials are not indicated for patients with CMI defects who

present only with fever.  Contact Infectious Disease for more information.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

# COMMUNITY ACQUIRED DIARRHEA (NO RECENT TRAVEL)

Consider Clostridioides difficile infection:

[Clostridioides difficile treatment recommendations](orzid2-gmenu-abx-assoc-colitis)

# Primary treatment

Hydration and electrolyte replacement

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Empiric antimicrobial treatment

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 3-5 days R,DI](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-500mg-po-q12h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Subacute or chronic (>/= 14 days of symptoms)

Primary treatment is hydration and electrolyte replacement. Empiric

antimicrobial therapy is not indicated. Investigate for the cause of diarrhea.

Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases involvement is encouraged.

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# VIRAL GASTROENTERITIS

Infectious diarrhea caused by viral pathogens such as Adenovirus, Astrovirus,

Norovirus, Rotavirus, and Sapovirus is usually self-limited. Treatment includes

supportive measures such as oral rehydration and unrestricted nutrition.

Antiviral therapy is not recommended and for most viruses is unavailable.

Antimotility agents may be used for one or two days in patients with mild to

moderate volume depletion. Antiemetic agents may be used for one or two days in

patients with vomiting.

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU CONJUNCTIVITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CONJUNCTIVITIS

Conjunctivitis is associated with viral or bacterial pathogens. Viral

conjunctivitis presents with watery discharge. Bacterial infections are more

likely to present with thick exudate and conjunctival injection. Allergic

conjunctivitis typically presents with stringy mucus. If there is pus

(hypopion), corneal involvement, possible bacterial conjunctivitis, or

keratitis, consult ophthalmology.

Viral conjunctivitis is most commonly caused by adenovirus. It is self-limited

and antivirals provide no benefit. Symptomatic treatment with ophthalmic

antihistamine/decongestants and warm or cool compresses may relieve symptoms.

Bacterial conjunctivitis is most commonly associated with Staphylococcus aureus,

Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus spp., Moraxella catarrhalis,

Corynebacterium diphtheriae, Neisseria spp. or enteric gram-negative rods. It is

generally self-limited, but topical antimicrobials reduce duration of symptoms

and limit person-to-person spread of infection. If symptoms do not improve after

2 days of antimicrobial therapy, the patient should be seen by an

ophthalmologist.

# Treatment for acute bacterial conjunctivitis

[Trimethoprim/polymixin B ophthalmic solution 1 drop in affected eye\(s\)](psjzid-trimethoprim-polymixin-b-ophth-1-drop-q3h)

q3h for 7 days ($) [M]

# Treatment for severe cases of bacterial conjunctivitis involving suppuration or

# contact lens wearers

Consult ophthalmology and begin topical antimicrobials.

[Ofloxacin 0.3% ophthalmic solution 2 drops in affected eye q2h while awake for 2](psjzid-ofloxacin-opth-2-drps-q2h-x2d-then-qid-x5d)

days then 2 drops QID for 5 days ($) [M]

Azari eta al, JAMA (2013) 1721-1730

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU CRANIAL EPIDURAL ABSCESS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CRANIAL EPIDURAL ABSCESS

Treatment involves source control by drainage procedure and antimicrobial

therapy.

Beta-lactam antibiotics are more effective than vancomycin against susceptible

Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus is isolated, once methicillin-resistance is

ruled out, switch to an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas

is a potential pathogen in post-surgical patients or patients with known

Pseudomonas colonization.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 6 weeks after surgical drainage. In patients with associated

osteomyelitis, patients in whom surgical drainage did not occur, and patients in

whom the response to therapy has been slow, treat for 6 to 8 weeks.

# Empiric Treatment

Preferred if Pseudomonas is not suspected:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-metro-500mg-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Preferred if Pseudomonas is suspected:

[Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h \($$\) R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-cefe2gmivq8h-metro500mgivq8h-vanco15mg-kgivq12hstat)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Treatment if methicillin-sensitive S. aureus is isolated

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R,DI](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

< OR >

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# DECUBITUS ULCERS

Decubitus ulcers are colonized with bacteria.  Antimicrobial therapy is

unnecessary unless the patient has infection of surrounding tissues signified by

erythema, warmth, local tenderness, or purulent discharge.  Rectal or groin

decubitus ulcers with surrounding infection need broad spectrum antimicrobials.

Ulcers located in other sites are usually treated with antimicrobials for

staphylococci and streptococci.

# Duration of therapy: 5 - 7 days, but adjust to clinical response

Use treatment durations for soft tissue infection even in the presence of

osteomyelitis if managed without plastic surgery. Treatment with prolonged

antibiotics for osteomyelitis is typically reserved for when patients are

managed with surgical debridement, bone biopsy, and/or wound closure. ID consult

recommended.

For deep abscesses away from the rectal area, obtain material for Gram stain and

culture and treat with:

# Treatment for Mild to Moderate Infections:

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h x 7days R](psjzid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 7 days DI,O](psjzid-linezolid-600mg-po-q12h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU DEEP OROPHAR INFECT
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# DEEP OROPHARYNGEAL INFECTIONS

Deep oropharyngeal infections may threaten life and must be treated immediately.

Assess the risk of airway compromise and monitor the airway if it is threatened.

These infections are more common in people with diabetes mellitus and are caused

by mixed organisms including streptococcus sp., Staphylococcus aureus and

anaerobes . Perform CT scan to diagnose abscess. ENT and Infectious Diseases

consults are essential.

# Duration of therapy

If the patient's condition worsens or does not improve during the first 48 hours

of antimicrobial therapy, surgical drainage is indicated. If surgical drainage

is done, antimicrobials are usually continued for 48 hours after the procedure.

If surgical drainage is not done, 2 weeks of antimicrobial therapy until

clinical improvement is observed (e.g. resolution of fever and leukocytosis) is

appropriate.

# Empiric Treatment

Preferred:

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h for 7 days \($\) R](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

Alternative: Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction

# DISSEMINATED MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM DISEASE TREATMENT

Many of these patients have HIV/AIDS. Management is complex. Consult

Infectious Diseases.

Rifabutin is optional for disseminated disease. Rifabutin can improve cure

rates, but may decrease blood concentrations of many drugs. Consult Infectious

Diseases or Pharmacy for more information.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treatment is continued for 12 months and until CD4 count is >100 cells per

microliter for at least 6 months.

# Two-drug treatment

Preferred treatment

[Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h \($\) R,DI <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h](orz-set-abx-clarithromycin-500-po-q12h-ehtambutol-15-q24h)

($$) [R]

Alternative

[Azithromycin 250 mg PO q24h \($\) M <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h R](orz-set-abx-azithro-250mg-po-q24h-ethambutol-15-po-q24h)

# Three-drug treatment

Preferred treatment

[Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h\($\) R,DI <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h](orz-set-abx-clarithromycin-ethambutol-rifabutin)

($$) [R] <AND> rifabutin 300 mg PO q24h ($$) [R,DI]

Alternative

[Azithromycin 250 mg PO q24h \($\) M <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h R](orz-set-abx-azith-250-ethambutol-rifabutin-300)

<AND> rifabutin 300 mg q24h ($$) [R,DI]

Cultures are often negative in cases of infection with fastidious organisms like

Abiotrophia (formerly nutritionally variant Streptococci), Bartonella, Coxiella,

Chlamydia, Legionella spp., or Trophyrema or when antimicrobials are given

before blood cultures are obtained. Consult Infectious Diseases and Cardiology.

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ENDOCARDITIS WITH ENTEROCOCCI

Infectious diseases and cardiology should be consulted in all cases

# Duration of therapy

Native valve endocarditis (NVE):

Duration of therapy depends on duration of symptoms, susceptibility of the

enterococcus isolate to antimicrobials, and the effectiveness of the

antimicrobials that can be used. For patients who have experienced symptoms for

less than 3 months and who can be treated with ampicillin or penicillin plus

gentamicin, treat for 4. Treat all other patients including any patient

receiving vancomycin for at least 6 weeks. Duration should be determined with

input from Infectious Diseases.

Prosthetic Valve endocarditis (PVE):

Treat for at least 6 weeks, duration should be determined with input from

Infectious Diseases.

# Organism Susceptibility

# Isolate is susceptible to penicillin (MIC </= 16 mcg/mL) and high concentration

# gentamicin (MIC </= 500 mcg/mL)

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R < AND > ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) for 6](orz-set-abx-ampicil-2gm-iv-q4h-ceftriaxone-2g-q12h)

weeks

< OR >

[Penicillin G 4 MU IV q4h \($$\) R < AND > gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h \($\)](orz-set-abx-penicil-4mu-iv-q4h-gent-1mg-kg-iv-q8h)

[R,O] for 4 to 6 weeks (NVE) for 6 weeks (PVE)

< OR >

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R < AND > gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h \($\) R,O](orz-set-abx-ampici-2gm-iv-q4h-gent-1mg-kg-iv-q8h)

for 4 to 6 weeks (NVE) for 6 weeks (PVE)

# Isolate is resistant to gentamicin (MIC > 500 mcg/mL)

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R < AND > ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) for 6](orz-set-abx-ampicil-2gm-iv-q4h-ceftriaxone-2g-q12h)

weeks

# Isolate is penicillin-resistant (MIC > 16 mcg/mL)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R < AND > gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h \($\)](orz-set-abx-vanc-q12h-15mg-kg-gent-1mg-kg-iv-q8h)

[R,O] for 6 weeks

# Isolate is penicillin resistant (MIC > 16 mcg/mL), gentamicin resistant (MIC >

# 500 mcg/mL) and vancomycin resistant

[Linezolid 600 mg IV q12h \($$$$\) DI for 6 weeks](psjizid-linezolid-600mg-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Daptomycin 10-12 mg/kg IV q24h \($$$$\) R,DI for 6 weeks](psjizid-daptomycin-10-12mg-kg-q24h)

# ENDOCARDITIS WITH GRAM NEGATIVE BACILLI OTHER THAN HACEK ORGANISMS

Pseudomonas aeruginosa and various Enterobacteriaceae are uncommon endocarditis

pathogens. Risk factors include cirrhosis, IV drug use and prosthetic valve.

Choice of agents should be based on in vitro susceptibilities.

Begin treatment with a beta-lactam agent, and when appropriate, Infectious

Diseases will initiate treatment with add-on aminoglycoside or fluroquinolone

agent for additional coverage.

Consult Infectious Diseases and Cardiothoracic surgery in all cases.

# Treatment for Enterobacteriaceae

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M for 6 weeks](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# Treatment for Pseudomonas

Most cases of pseudomonas endocarditis occur in IV drug users.

[Cefepime  2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R for 6 weeks](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h)

# ENDOCARDITIS WITH HACEK BACTERIA

HACEK bacteria are the fastidious Gram-negative bacilli, including Haemophilus

parainfluenzae, Haemophilus paraphrophilus, Haemophilus influenzae,

Aggregatibacter aphrophilus (Haemophilus aphrophilus), Actinobacillus

actinomycetemcomitans, Cardiobacterium hominis, Eikenella corrodens, Kingella

kingae and Kingella denitrificans. It may take up three weeks for the

microbiology laboratory to isolate these organisms.

Treatment options are limited for patients with allergies to beta-lactam

antibiotics. Consult Infectious Diseases for advice.

# Duration of therapy

Native valve endocarditis (NVE): 4 weeks

Prosthetic valve endocarditis (PVE): 6 weeks

# Treatment

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M for 4 weeks \(NVE\) or 6 weeks \(PVE\)](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# Isolate is susceptible to ampicillin

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h \($\) R for 4 weeks \(NVE\) or 6 weeks \(PVE\)](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

# NATIVE VALVE ENDOCARDITIS--EMPIRICAL THERAPY

# Empirical treatment in a non-intravenous drug user

Wait for identification of pathogen before initiating antimicrobial therapy in

most cases. If empiric antimicrobial treatment is necessary, due to hemodynamic

instability or other severe disease, use:

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\)](orz-set-abx-vanco-15-mg-kg-iv-q12h-ceftriax-2gm-iv-q24h)

< OR >

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h \($\)](orz-set-abx-van-15-mg-kg-iv-q12h-gent-1-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

[R,O]

# Empirical treatment in an intravenous drug user

Staphylococcus aureus is the most likely pathogen, followed by streptococci and

enterococci. However, gram negative pathogens are often associated with

endocarditis in these patients. Culture results are key for appropriate therapy.

Consult Cardiology and Infectious Diseases for more information.

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R <AND> gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h \($\)](orz-set-abx-van-15-mg-kg-iv-q12h-gent-1-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

[R,O]

# NATIVE VALVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH STAPHYLOCOCCI

Endocarditis with Staphylococcus aureus and coagulase-negative staphylococci are

treated similarly.

Retrospective studies show that patients with native valve staphylococcal

endocarditis treated with valve replacement and antimicrobials have a lower

mortality rate than those treated with antimicrobials alone. Consult

cardiothoracic surgery for all patients with staphylococcal endocarditis.

Most patients need 6 weeks of antimicrobial treatment. For vancomycin-resistant

strains Infectious Disease consultation is recommended.

# Treatment for methicillin-susceptible strains

Preferred:

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) DI for 6 weeks](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

Primary alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

Treat for 6 weeks:

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R for 6 weeks](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment for methicillin-resistant strains

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R for 6 weeks](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU EC NV STREPTOCOCCI
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# NATIVE VALVE ENDOCARDITIS WITH STREPTOCOCCI

Selection is based on susceptibility to penicillin.

# Treatment of highly susceptible viridians streptococci or Streptococcus

# gallolyticus (bovis) (penicillin MIC less than or equal to 0.12 mcg/ml)

The addition of gentamicin provides a synergistic effect and is reasonable to

add in patients with uncomplicated endocarditis, rapid response to therapy and

no underlying renal disease

Preferred:

[Penicillin G 3 million units IV q4h \($$\) R for 4 weeks](psjizid-penicillin-g-3-million-units-iv-q4h)

< OR >

[Penicillin G 3 million units IV q4h \($$\) R for 2 weeks <AND> gentamicin](orz-set-abx-penicillin-3mu-iv-q4h-gent-3-mg-kg-once-daily)

3 mg/kg IV q24h ($) [R,O] for 2 weeks

Primary alternatives:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M for 4 weeks](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) for 2 weeks <AND> gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV once](orz-set-abx-ceft-2gm-iv-q24h-gent-3-mg-kg-iv-once-daily)

daily ($) [R,O] for 2 weeks

Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R for 4 weeks](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment of relatively resistant viridians streptococci or S. gallolyticus

# (bovis) (penicillin MIC greater than 0.12 and less than or equal to 0.5 mcg/ml)

For ceftriaxone susceptible isolates (MIC < 0.5 mcg/mL):

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) for 4 weeks](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

For ceftriaxone resistant isolates (MIC >/= 0.5 mcg/mL):

[Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h \($$\) R for 4 weeks <AND> gentamicin](orz-set-abx-penicillin-4mu-iv-q4h-gent-3-mg-kg-iv-qd)

3 mg/kg IV q24h ($) [R,O] for first 2 weeks

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) for 4 weeks <AND> gentamicin 3 mg/kg IV q24h](orz-set-abx-ceft-2gm-iv-q24h-gent-3-mg-kg-iv-once-daily)

($) [R,O] for first 2 weeks

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R for 4 weeks](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment of highly resistant viridians streptococci or S. gallolyticus (bovis)

# (penicillin MIC greater than or equal to 0.5 mcg/mL)

Preferred:

[Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h \($$\) R <AND> gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q24h](orz-set-abx-penicil-4mu-iv-q4h-gent-1mg-kg-iv-q8h)

($) [R,O] for 4 weeks

< OR>

[Ampicillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R <AND> gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h \($\) R,O](orz-set-abx-ampici-2gm-iv-q4h-gent-1mg-kg-iv-q8h)

for 4 weeks

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction CLICK HERE](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R for 4 weeks](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment of Streptococci pneumonia, Streptococcus pyogenes, and Groups B, C, F

# and G beta-hemolytic streptococci

Treatment is non-standardized and must be tailored to each patient. Consult

Infectious Diseases.

# PROSTHETIC VALVE ENDOCARDITIS--EMPIRICAL THERAPY

Early surgical consultation is essential.

If a patient is hemodynamically stable and the diagnosis is uncertain,

antimicrobial therapy can safely be withheld until the diagnosis is clear and

blood culture results are available to guide therapy. In all cases, be sure

adequate numbers of blood cultures are obtained before antimicrobials are given.

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ECTHYMA GANGRENOSUM
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

ECTHYMA GANGRENOSUM

Ecthyma gangrenosum lesions commonly begin as painless red macules which

rapidly evolve into areas of induration that develop into pustules and-or

bullae. Ultimately, these become gangrenous ulcers. Ecthyma lesions

typically progress rapidly within 12 to 18 hours. They are often associated

with Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteremia, especially in neutropenic patients.

Recommend blood cultures and culture of skin exudates.

Infectious disease consult is suggested.

Consider combination therapy in patients with severe infections.

Treat for 7 days.

# Preferred treatment

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h \($\) R,DI](psjizid-ciproflox-400mg-iv-q8h)

[Gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h \($\) R,O](psjizid-gentamicin-5-mg-kg-iv-q24h)

# Alternative for severe infections

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R < AND > gentamicin](orz-set-abx-pip-tazo-4-5-gm-iv-q6h-gent-5mg-iv-qd)

5 mg/kg IV q24h ($) [R,O]

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h \($\) R,DI < AND > gentamicin 5 mg/kg](orz-set-abx-cip-400mg-iv-q8h-gent-5mg-iv-qd)

IV q24h ($) [R,O]

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Up-to-date website

Stevens DL Clin Infect Dis 2014, 59: 147

Montravers P Curr Opin Infect Dis 2016, 29:131

EMPIRICAL INTRAVENOUS REGIMENS WITH VANCOMYCIN

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ENDOPHTHALMITIS

Endophthalmitis is a medical emergency and presents with eye pain and visual

loss. It may be associated with gram positive or gram-negative bacteria,

including Staphylococcus aureus and Pseudomonas aeruginosa, or with fungi.

Consult ophthalmology immediately. The ophthalmologist will obtain an aqueous or

vitreous fluid sample for gram stain and culture and begin intravitreal

antimicrobials.

# Treatment with intravitreal antimicrobials

[Vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT \($\) R < AND > ceftazidime](orz-set-abx-vanco-1mg-intra-inj-ceftaz-2-25mg-intra-inj)

2.25 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$) [M]

< OR >

[Vancomycin 1 mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT \($\) R < AND > amikacin 0.4](orz-set-abx-vanco-1mg-intravitreous-amik-0-4mg-intr-inj)

mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT ($$) [M]

# Fungal endophthalmitis

Fungal endophthalmitis is rarely diagnosed in temperate climates and treatment

is complicated. Ophthalmology and Infectious Diseases involvement is essential.

[Amphotericin B 5mcg/0.1mL intravitreal injection STAT \($$$\) R,O](psjizid-ampho-b-5mcg-intravitreous-injection-once)

< OR >

[Voriconazole 100 mcg/0.1mL intravitreal injection STAT \($$$$\) R,H,DI](psjzid-voriconazole-100mcg-intravitreous-injection-once)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ERYSIPELAS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

ERYSIPELAS

In contrast to cellulitis, erysipelas has sharply demarcated borders and a

characteristic raised, orange-peel appearance.  Most cases are associated with

streptococcus.  In a minority of cases, especially those involving the face,

Staphylococcus aureus is also a potential pathogen.  In severe cases,

methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) coverage must be provided

until microbiology results are available.

Treat for 5 to 10days, longer if patient is bacteremic.

# _________________________________

# Facial

# _________________________________

Sudden onset of rapidly spreading red edematous tender plaque-like skin on the

face in an otherwise healthy host.

# If erysipelas-like on the face treat as if MRSA is present:

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# _________________________________

# Non-facial

# _________________________________

# MILD TO MODERATE disease

[Penicillin VK 250 - 500 mg PO q6h \($\) R](psjzid-penicillin-v-500mg-po-q6h)

# Alternative for penicillin allergy

[Erythromycin 500 mg po q6h \($\) DI](psjzid-erythromycin-500mg-po-q6h)

# SEVERE disease

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

[Penicillin 3 million units IV q6h \($\) R](psjizid-penicillin-3-million-units-iv-q6h)

# Alternative for penicillin allergy or MRSA suspected

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

< OR >

[Clindamycin 600 mg IV q8h \($\) H,O](psjizid-clindamycin-600mg-iv-q8h)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Stevens DL Clin Infect Dis 2014, 59: 147

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU ERYSIPELOID
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

ERYSIPELOID (ERYSIPELOTHRIX RHUSOPATHIAE INFECTION)

Erysipeloid is a localized cutaneous infection with Erysipelothrix rhusopathiae.

It is a zoonotic infection of fisherman, fish handlers, and butchers acquired by

direct animal contact, most commonly with fish, but also with other animals

(e.g., swine). It usually affects the hand or fingers and is characterized by

throbbing pain and a red rash with a purple center and an elevated border.

Localized infections can be treated with oral antimicrobials.

Severe, diffuse cutaneous infections or systemic infections with E.

rhusopathiae occur rarely after ingestion of undercooked pork or contaminated

seafood in immunosuppressed individuals.  These infections are treated

initially with intravenous antimicrobials.

# _____________________________________________________________

# Treatment of localized infection (erysipeloid)

# _____________________________________________________________

Treat for 7 days

[Penicillin V 500 mg PO QID \($\) R](psjzid-penicillin-v-500mg-po-q6h)

# Alternative

[Erythromycin 500 mg PO QID \($\) DI](psjzid-erythromycin-500mg-po-q6h)

# ___________________________________________________________________

# Treatment of systemic or severe diffuse cutaneous infection with E.

# rhusopathiae.

# ___________________________________________________________________

# Treatment duration is at least 4 weeks. Infectious Disease Consult recommended.

[Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h \($\) R](psjizid-penicillin-g-4-million-units-iv-q4h)

# Alternative

[Ceftriaxone 2 GM IV q24h \($$\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

[Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h \($\) R,DI](psjizid-levofloxacin-750mg-iv-q24h)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

# ERYTHRASMA

Erythrasma presents as brownish-red, well circumscribed, irregularly shaped

patches in or near skin folds. Patches in the groin often itch.

Most cases respond to topical therapy.

# Treatment

[Clindamycin 1% topical solution apply twice daily M for 14 days](psjzid-clindamycin-1-topical-soln-q12h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU FEVER OF UNK ORIGIN
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# FEVER OF UNKNOWN ORIGIN

Fever of unknown origin (FUO) is the occurrence of several episodes of fever

greater than 101 degrees Fahrenheit over a period of at least 3 weeks despite 1

week of hospital evaluation. Cases with FUO are often classified in four

categories: (1) classical, (2) neutropenic, (3) nosocomial, and (4) fever in

persons with HIV/AIDS. Empirical antimicrobial therapy is rarely indicated in

patients with FUO.

Note that FUO in neutropenic patients refers to persistent fever that has

remained undiagnosed after extensive diagnostic work and empirical antimicrobial

therapy. New fever in patients with profound neutropenia is a different syndrome

and does require empirical antimicrobial therapy. Infectious Diseases should be

involved in any case where empirical treatment for fever of unknown origin is

being considered. For more information refer to the neutropenic fever

recommendations.

[Neutropenic fever](orzid2-gmenu-immunocom-neut-fever)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Mandell Chapter: Fever of Unknown Origin

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU FOLLICULITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

FOLLICULITIS

Folliculitis is an infection of the hair follicle with purulent exudate in the

epidermis. It is usually associated with Staphylococcus aureus.  In patients

exposed to swimming pools or hot tubs, folliculitis may be associated with

Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Candida albicans can cause folliculitis in patients

receiving antimicrobials and/or corticosteroids. For folliculitis in patients

with severe acne, consult Dermatology.  For extensive folliculitis or in

patients with HIV, consult Infectious Diseases.

# Treatment

Usually self-limiting. For most cases, treat with daily saline compresses until

symptoms resolve.

# For moderate to severe cases associated with Staphylococcus aureus:

[Mupirocin ointment to affected area q8h for 7 days \($\) M](psjzid-mupirocin-2-oint-top-to-affect-area-q8h)

# For cases associated with Candida albicans

[Clotrimazole cream q8h for 7 days \($\) M](psjzid-clotrimazole-1-crm-top-q8h)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

# Diabetes-Related Foot Infections (Diabetic Foot Infections-DFI)

# Infected DFI (Class 3/Moderate)

Infection with no systemic manifestations and envolving:

-Erythema extending >2cm from the wound margin, and/or

-Tissue deeper than skin and subcutaneous tissues

(e.g., tendon, muscle, joint, and bone)

# Duration of therapy: 1-3 weeks

# Preferred Treatments:

**Oral options**

[Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h \($\) R](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

**IV options**

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h \($\) DI,H](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-2gm-iv-q12h-metro-500mg-iv-q8h)

# Treatment with MRSA risk factors:

**Oral options**

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h \($\) R <AND> Trimethoprim-](orz-set-abx-amox-clav-875-po-q12h-trimeth-sulfa-1ds-po-q12)

PO BID for 14 days ($) [DI]

**IV options**

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M <AND> Metronidazole 500mg IV q8h \($\) DI,H](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-q24h-metro-500gm-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-q12h)

<AND> Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

< OR >

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h \($\) R <AND> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV](orz-set-abx-ampi-sulb-3gm-iv-q6h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

q12h ($) [R,DI]

# Treatment with Penicillin Allergy:

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU FOOT ULCER W/ INFECT SURR TISSUES
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# DIABETES-RELATED FOOT INFECTIONS (DIABETIC FOOT INFECTIONS-DFI)

# Wound Cultures:

If there are no systemic symptoms of infection or at least 2 local symptoms

(pain, erythema > 0.5cm, purulent drainage, warmth), do not culture or treat

with abx.

Do NOT:

-Culture a wound that appears uninfected (at least 2 of following: local pain,

erythema >0.5cm, purulent drainage)

-Swab the wound to obtain a culture

-Culture without first cleaning and debriding a wound DFI Do:

-Obtain culture by deep tissue biopsy after cleaning and debriding the wound

# Imaging:

-An x-ray is recommended for all new foot ulcers in patients with diabetes to

evaluate for deformity, bony destruction, soft tissue gas, and/or foreign

bodies. Antimicrobials aren't indicated unless local cellulitis or systemic

infectious symptoms are present.

[Click here for Osteomyelitis Evaluation](orzid2-gmenu-osteomyelitis-evaluation)

# INFECTION SEVERITY (IWGDF/IDSA Classification)

# __________________________________________________________________

# Uninfected DFI (Class 1/Uninfected): Chronic ulceration without s/s infection

-if no pain, erythema > 0.5cm, purulent drainage, do not culture or treat

Do not culture wound -Do not treat with antibiotics If osteomyelitis identified

arrange for bone biopsy --hold antibiotics

# _________________________________________________________________

# Infected DFI (Class 2/Mild):

At least two of the following are present: -Local swelling or induration

-Erythema >0.5cm but <2cm around wound -Local tenderness or pain -Local

increased warmth -Purulent drainage

# Primarily Outpatient Treatment:

Duration of therapy: 1-2 weeks

# Preferred Regimens:

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h x 7 days R](psjzid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID for 7 days R](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment with previous MRSA infection or severe PCN allergy:

[Beta-lactam Reaction Assessment](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid x 7 days R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

< OR >

[Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 7 days DI,O](psjzid-linezolid-600mg-po-q12h)

# __________________________________________________________________

# Infected DFI (Class 3/Moderate):

-Erythema extending >2cm from the wound margin, and/or -Tissue deeper than skin

and subcutaneous tissues (e.g., tendon, muscle, joint, and bone)

# Outpatient/Often Hospitalized Treatment:

Oral or IV with change to PO with improvement

Duration of therapy: 1-3 weeks

# Preferred Treatments:

[Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875/125mg po bid R for 7 days](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment with history of previous MRSA infection:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg po BID R <AND> doxycycline](orz-set-abx-amox-clav-875-q12h-doxycycline-100mg-q12h)

100 mg PO bid [DI] for 7 days

< OR >

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125mg PO bid R <AND> trimethoprim-](orz-set-abx-amox-clav-875-po-q12h-trimeth-sulfa-1ds-po-q12)

sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO bid [R,DI] for 7 days

# Intravenous regimens with MRSA coverage: if previous history of MRSA

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M < AND > vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-ceft-2gm-iv-q24h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R,DI](orz-set-abx-ampi-sulb-3gm-iv-q6h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Treatment with Severe PCN allergy:

[Beta-lactam Allergy Assessment](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Levofloxacin 500mg PO qday R,DI <AND> metronidazole 500mg PO bid DI](orz-set-abx-levoflox-500mg-qd-metro-500mg)

for 7 days

# __________________________________________________________________

# Infected DFI (Class 4/Severe):

Infection with associated systemic manifestations as indicated by 2 or more of

the following: -Fever, Tachycardia, Leukocytosis, Hypotension, Sepsis,

Necrotizing infection

Duration: usually 2-4 weeks, unless source control/amputation occurs

Obtain cultures of inflamed ulcer or wound to permit targeted antimicrobial

therapy, de-escalate/modify regimen based on culture and susceptibility data. A

switch to an oral regimen is reasonable

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV q6h R <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg](orz-set-abx-pip-taz3-375gm-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro-vanc15mg-kg)

IV q12h [R,DI]

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R,DI <AND>](orz-set-abx-cefe2gmivq8h-metro500mgivq8h-vanco15mg-kgivq12hstat)

metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h [DI]

Alternative:

[Beta-lactam Reaction Assessment](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h DI <AND>](orz-set-abx-ciprofl-400mg-iv-q8h-metroni-vanco)

vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h [R]

# __________________________________________________________________

References:

Senneville E Cin Infect Dis 2023:

Senneville Diabetes Metab Res Rev. (2024) 40(3):e3687

Stevens DL Clin Infect Dis 2014, 59:147

Lipsky BA Clin Infect Dis 2012, 54:e132

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ASPERGILLUS SPECIES

For localized disease (fungus ball), antifungal therapy is ineffective.

Consult Surgery and Pulmonary for cases of localized disease without systemic

infection. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat invasive disease with intravenous antifungals initially, then

switch to oral antifungals for a total duration of therapy of 6-12

weeks dependent on the degree and duration of immunosuppression, site of disease

and evidence of disease improvement.

# Preferred intravenous therapy

[Voriconazole 6 mg/kg IV q12h for 2 doses, then 4 mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,H,](psjizid-voriconazole-6mg-kg-q12h-then-4mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Alternative intravenous therapy for patients intolerant to voriconazole

[Amphotericin B Liposomal 3-5MG/KG IV q24h \($$$$\)R,O+ NS Hydratio](orz-set-abx-amphotericin-liposomal-fluid-flush-orders)

# Oral therapy after disease has stabilized

[Voriconazole 200 mg PO q12h \($$\) R,H,DI](psjzid-voriconazole-200mg-po-bid)

References:

Mandell Chapter: Aspergillus Species

Patterson et al. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2016, 63(4): e1-60

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# BLASTOMYCES DERMATITIDIS

Contact Infectious Diseases in all cases. Lifelong suppressive therapy may be

required in immunosuppressed patients if immunosuppression cannot be reversed.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Disease outside of the central nervous system

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat for 6-12 months. It is recommended that immunocompromised patients be

treated with at least 1-2 weeks of intravenous treatment and a total treatment

duration of 12 months.

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

[Itraconazole 200 mg PO q8h for 3 days then q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-itraconazole-200-po-tidx3days-then-200-bid)

# Treatment for severe disease

Change to oral itraconazole after the patient's condition has stabilized.

[Amphotericin B Liposomal 3-5MG/KG IV q24h \($$$$\)R,O+ NS Hydratio](orz-set-abx-amphotericin-liposomal-fluid-flush-orders)

# Oral therapy after disease has stabilized

[Itraconazole 200 mg PO q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-itraconazole-200mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Fluconazole 400-800 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-400mg-po-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Central nervous system infection

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat with intravenous therapy for 4-6 weeks followed by oral azole for at least

12 months.

# Initial intravenous treatment

[Amphotericin B Liposomal 3-5MG/KG IV q24h \($$$$\)R,O+ NS Hydratio](orz-set-abx-amphotericin-liposomal-fluid-flush-orders)

# Oral therapy after disease has stabilized

[Itraconazole 200 mg PO q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-itraconazole-200mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Fluconazole 800 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-800mg-po-q24h)

References:

Stanley et al. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2008, (46)1801-12

Sanford keyword: Blastomycosis

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU FUNGI CANDIDA ALBICANS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# CANDIDA ALBICANS

Avoid using fluconazole empirically to treat candidal infections in patients who

have received an imidazole in the previous year.

# Treatment of thrush or oropharyngeal candidiasis

Oropharyngeal candidal disease may present in different patterns, like white

plaques in the oropharyngeal area, erythematous macules (often in patients with

dentures), or as pseudomembranes. Thrush infection often recurs, especially in

patients with AIDS. Consult MRTC clinic or Infectious Diseases (MRTC may also be

consulted in the MVAHCS) for more information on treatment of recurrent

infection.

Mild disease:

[Nystatin swish and swallow q6h for 7-14 days M](psjzid-nystatin-swish-and-swallow-5ml-q6h)

< OR >

[Clotrimazole troche 10 mg PO 5X/day for 7-14 days M](psjzid-clotrimazole-troche-10mg-po-5x-day)

Moderate to severe disease:

[Fluconazole 200 mg PO q24h for 7-14 days R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-200mg-po-q24h)

# Esophageal candidiasis

Esophageal infection requires systemic therapy.

Preferred:

[Fluconazole 400 mg PO q24h for 14-21 days R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-400mg-po-q24h)

Alternative for patient who cannot swallow tablets:

[Fluconazole 400 IV q24h for 14-21 days R,DI](psjizid-fluconazole-400mg-iv-q24h)

<OR>

[Micafungin 100-150mg IV q24h for 14-21 days](psjizid-micafungin-100mg-iv-q24h)

# Systemic candidal infection

Fluconazole is preferred empirical therapy in most cases. Amphotericin B should

be used empirically in patients who have received an azole antifungal drug

recently, or in patients who are critically ill.

Duration of Therapy: Duration of therapy is dependent upon location, severity of

infection, and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more

information.

Preferred:

[Fluconazole 800 mg PO once then 400 mg PO q24h R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-800mg-po-once-then-400mg-q24h)

< OR >

[Fluconazole 800 mg IV once then 400 mg IV q24h R,DI](orz-set-abx-fluconazole-iv-800mg-once-then-400mg-q24h)

Recent azole antifungal treatment:

[Liposomal amphotericin \(Ambisome\) 3-5 mg/kg IV q24h R,O](orz-set-abx-amphotericin-liposomal-fluid-flush-orders)

< OR >

[Micafungin 100-150 mg IV q24h H,DI](psjizid-micafungin-100mg-iv-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Mandell chapter: Candida Species

Pappas et al. Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2016, 62(4)e1-50

Sanford Guide article: Candidiasis, Candidemia or Disseminated

Up-to-Date article: Treatment of candidemia and invasive candidiasis in adults

# CANDIDA GLABRATA

C. glabrata is often resistant to fluconazole and occasionally has some degree

of resistance to amphotericin. Higher doses of amphotericin are recommended due

to delayed killing effects against Candida glabrata.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Duration of therapy is dependent upon location and severity of infection,

and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Preferred treatment

[Micafungin 100-150 mg IV q24h \($$$\) H,DI](psjizid-micafungin-100mg-iv-q24h)

< OR >

[Amphotericin B Liposomal 3-5MG/KG IV q24h \($$$$\)R,O+ NS Hydratio](orz-set-abx-amphotericin-liposomal-fluid-flush-orders)

# Alternative for susceptible isolates

[Voriconazole 6mg/kg IV q12h for 2 doses, then 4mg/kg IV q12h \($$$$\) R,H,DI](psjizid-voriconazole-6mg-kg-q12h-then-4mg-kg-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Voriconazole 400 mg PO q12h for 2 doses, then 200 mg PO q12h \($$\) R,H,DI](psjzid-voriconazole-400mg-po-q12h-then-200mg-q12h)

# COCCIDIOIDOMYCES

Pulmonary and Infectious Diseases consultations are essential for diagnosis and

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Mild to moderate disease

Observation alone is indicated for some cases. Consult Infectious Diseases for

more information. If antifungal treatment is indicated:

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# HISTOPLASMA CAPSULATUM

Intravenous antifungals are indicated initially for severe or progressive

disease. After disease has stabilized, oral antifungals may be used to complete

the course. Contact Infectious Diseases and Pulmonary services for advice.

Contact HIV expert for advice on cases involving patients with HIV.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Duration of therapy is dependent upon location and severity of infection,

and response to therapy. Consult Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Preferred initial therapy for meningitis, severe pulmonary or disseminated

# disease

[Amphotericin B Liposomal 3-5MG/KG IV q24h \($$$$\)R,O+ NS Hydratio](orz-set-abx-amphotericin-liposomal-fluid-flush-orders)

# Treatment after disease has stabilized

Itraconazole is more effective than fluconazole, but fluconazole may be used in

patients who cannot tolerate itraconazole.

Preferred

[Itraconazole 200 mg PO q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-itraconazole-200mg-po-q12h)

Alternative

[Fluconazole 400-800 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-400mg-po-q24h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU FURUNCLES AND CARBUNCLES
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

FURUNCLES AND CARBUNCLES

Localized purulent infections include furuncles, carbuncles and cutaneous

abscesses. Nearly all are caused by Staphylococcus aureus. A furuncle is an

inflamed nodule that usually develops as a complication of folliculitis.  A

carbuncle is a more extensive lesion that extends further into the subcutaneous

tissue.  Contact a wound care nurse for more information.

Incision and drainage is the mainstay of therapy for carbuncles, cutaneous

abscesses, and large furuncles.

The decision to administer antibiotics directed against S. aureus as an adjunct

to incision and drainage should be made based on the presence of systemic

inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) or in patients with markedly impaired

host defenses.

# For recurrent skin abscesses in addition to culture and antibiotic therapy

# recommended consider a decolonization regimen.

[Select here for Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization](orzid2-gmenu-abx-staphylococcus-aureus-decolonization)

# Mild infection: Purulent infection without systemic signs of infection

Recommend incision and drainage. No antibiotic indicated.

# Moderate Infection: Purulent infection with signs of systemic infection.

Recommend incision and drainage. Culture material and use results to guide

therapy.

Treat for 5 days and extend/modify treatment if not improved in this time.

# Preferred treatment:

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h \($\) R](psjzid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-q12h)

[Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

# Alternative:

[Doxycycline 100 mg po q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# If methicillin-RESISTANT Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) is suspected or proved

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

[Linezolid 600 mg PO q12h \($\) DI,O](psjzid-linezolid-600mg-po-q12h)

# Severe Infections:

Patients who have failed incision and drainage along with oral antibiotics

or those with SIRS or for infections in those with neutropenia or diminished

neutrophil function.

Recommend incision and drainage. Culture material and use results to guide

therapy.

Treat for 5 days. Reevaluate patient and extend or modify treatment if not

improved in this time.

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

References:

Up-to-Date website

Stevens DL Clin Infect Dis 2014, 59: 147

Montravers P Curr Opin Infect Dis 2016, 29:131

# Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Placement of Percutaneous Gastrostomy (PEG) Tube

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# HEAD LICE (PEDICULOSIS CAPITIS)

Lice are parasitic insects. Human lice survive by feeding on human blood. To

make a diagnosis, use a nit comb, bright light, or lens to find a louse living

on the scalp.  Dead nits may remain for months after successful treatment.  Dead

nits are usually located more than 6 mm from the scalp.

Lice are often transmitted by infected clothing and bedclothes but not by

ordinary furniture that is not typically in contact with hair or scalp.  Refer

to the following for advice on household cleaning for lice infestations:

[https://www.cdc.gov/lice/treatment/index.html](orz-gtx-abx-treat-head-lice-url)

# Treatment

Repeat if live lice are seen 7-10 days after treatment.

[Permethrin 1% lotion Apply to affected area for 10 minutes then comb out nits](psjzid-permethrin-1-lotion-to-affect-area-10min)

[M]

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# HIDRADENITIS SUPPURATIVA

A chronic inflammatory condition that typically involves occlusion, rupture,

abscess formation and infection of hair follicles as well as secondary infection

of apocrine glands/surrounding tissues. Lesions most often occur in the

intertriginous areas (axillae, inguinal and anogenital) in is associated with

smoking and obesity. There is a 40% genetic predisposition for hidradenitis

suppurativa (HS) and is often accompanied by pain, malodor, and drainage.

Cultures are negative 50% of the time and often are polymicrobial with S.

epidermidis and S. aureus most isolated. The Hurley Staging System is often used

to determine severity of HS.

Therapy generally consists of treatment of comorbidities that can exacerbate HS,

avoidance of triggers, pain management, wound care, and topical/oral

antimicrobials. Hormonal agents, steroids, retinoids, and surgery can also be

used to treat certain patients. Biologics may be considered in Stage II-III HS.

# Consult Dermatology in all cases

# Hurley Staging System:

Stage I: recurrent nodules and abscesses with minimal scarring

Stage II: limited number of sinuses and/or scarring within a body region

Stage III: multiple or extensive sinuses and/or scarring

# Duration of Therapy:

Treatment is typically for 12 weeks but may require longer durations in certain

cases. Metronidazole should only be used for a maximum of 6 weeks to avoid

neurologic toxicity.

# Interventions for All Patients:

Smoking cessation, weight loss, avoidance of triggers, and pain management

should be part of all treatment plans. Consult Dermatology for use of hormonal

agents, steroids, retinoids, and surgery.

# Optional Topical Treatment, May be Used in Addition to Oral Therapies Below:

[Chlorhexidine gluconate 4% liquid topically wash affected area q24h \($\) M](psjzid-chlorhexidine-gluconate-wash-qday)

< OR >

[Benzoyl peroxide 10% soap topically wash affected area q24h \($\) M](psjzid-benzoyl-peroxide-10-wash-topically-q24h)

< ADD ON THERAPY FOR FLARES - MUST USE IN ADDITION TO ONE OF THE AGENTS ABOVE>

[Clindamycin 1% solution topically to affected areas q12h prn for flares \($\) M](psjzid-clindamycin-1-topical-soln-q12h)

# Stage I-II Initial Treatment:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 12 weeks](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Minocycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 12 weeks](psjzid-minocycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Stage III Initial Treatment and Stage I-II Failure of Oral Doxycycline:

[Clindamycin 300 mg PO q12h for 12 weeks \($\) H,O](psjzid-clindamycin-300mg-po-q12h)

# Stage II-III Failure of Oral Clindamycin:

[Moxifloxacin 400 mg PO q24h \($\)R,DI for 12 weeks <AND> metronidazole 500](orz-set-abx-moxi400mgpoq24h-metro500mgpoq8h-rifamp300mgpoq12h)

mg q8h ($) [DI] for 6 weeks <AND> rifampin 300 mg PO q12h ($) [DI,O] for 12

weeks

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IG HIS DEFICIENCY
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

IMMUNOGLOBULIN DEFICIENCY (HUMORAL IMMUNE SYSTEM)

Antibody deficiency typically leads to recurrent, severe respiratory tract

infections associated with encapsulated bacteria, especially Streptococcus

pneumoniae and Haemophilus influenzae, and to a lesser extent, Staphylococcus

aureus. Recurrent otitis media, sinusitis, and pneumonia are common syndromes.

Gastrointestinal disease associated with Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, or

rotavirus is also common in some patients.

# Preferred empirical treatment

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($5.71/day\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# Alternative for severe penicillin allergy

Chloramphenicol is not currently available.  Contact Infectious Diseases for

advice.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM ALTERED MICRO FLORA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

ALTERED MICROBIAL FLORA

A rich, diverse microbial flora lives on or in skin, mucosal surfaces, and

respiratory and gastrointestinal tracts of healthy people.  This flora prevents

disease by inhibiting the growth of potential pathogens.  Disruption of the

normal flora, usually by antimicrobial therapy, reduces this barrier and

increases the risk of infectious disease.  Patients exposed to broad-spectrum

antimicrobials are at greater risk for colonization with resistant bacteria,

fungal infections, and Clostridium difficile colitis.  During hospitalization,

many patients become colonized with more resistant organisms like methicillin-

resistant Staphylococcus aureus and resistant Gram-negative bacilli.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM BASIC CONCEPTS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

BASIC CONCEPTS

Humans are protected by a broad array of host defenses that fall into two major

categories: innate and immune host defenses.  Innate defense operate

continuously without specific antigenic stimulation and immune defenses are

primed by and respond to antigenic stimulation.

Each type of host defense protects against a specific set of organisms.  As a

result, infectious diseases more common because of host defense defects in an

individual patient are usually predictable from that patient's host defense

defects.  For example, antibody or complement deficiencies predispose patients

to disease with encapsulated organisms but not fungi.  Defects in cell-mediated

immunity predispose patients to infections with mycobacteria or cytomegalovirus

but not Escherichia coli or influenza virus.  Suspected cases of infectious

disease must be evaluated in the context of the patient's host defects.

Management, including possible antimicrobial therapy, should be initiated on the

basis of the most likely offending pathogens.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

LinkTargets.Text: Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more (Inpt)
LinkTargets.Item: ORZID2 GMENU ABX GENERAL INFORMATION INPATIENT

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM COMP DEFICIENCY
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

COMPLEMENT DEFICIENCY

Complement deficiency can be inherited or acquired.  Acquired defects are

usually a consequence of other diseases like systemic lupus erythematosus.

Complement deficiency leads to increased rates of infections, usually of the

upper respiratory tract, but also occasionally with bacteremia or meningitis.

Pathogens are usually Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and

Neisseria gonorrhea.

Patients presenting with fever or other symptoms suggesting systemic bacterial

infection should be treated immediately with antimicrobials active against these

pathogens.

# Preferred empirical treatment

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($5.71/day\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# Alternative for severe penicillin allergy

Chloramphenicol is not currently available.  Contact Infectious Diseases for

advice.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM DIABETES MELLITUS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

DIABETES MELLITUS

Hyperglycemia increases the risk of infectious diseases in diabetic patients,

and increased blood glucose slows infection resolution.  Diabetic patients are

prone to a variety of infections including urinary tract infections,

cholecystitis, and bacteremia.  Peripheral neuropathy and arterial insufficiency

predispose to infections of skin, soft tissue, and bone infection in the lower

legs and feet.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

Joshi N  New Eng J Med 1999, 341: 1906

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM HYPOCHLORHYDRIA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

HYPOCHLORHYDRIA

Diminished gastric acid allows increased numbers of bacteria in the stomach and

predisposes to infection with several potentially pathogenic bacterial species.

These changes increase the risk of nosocomial pneumonia and possibly the risk of

community-acquired respiratory infections.  However, interventions to

decontaminate the upper gastrointestinal tract do not prevent infectious

disease.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM MALIGNANCY
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

MALIGNANCY

Malignancies affect host defenses in many ways.  Hematogenous malignancies can

diminish the effectiveness of neutrophils and other cells involved in host

defense.  Tumors often disrupt mucous membranes or blood vessels and allow

contaminating organisms into hollow cavities or the bloodstream.  Chemotherapy

used to treat these malignancies often impairs mucus membranes and suppresses

neutrophil production and function.

Ordinarily, empirical antimicrobials are not indicated for patients with

malignancy and fever unless they have neutropenia or a specific infectious

disease.

[Neutropenic fever](orzid2-gmenu-immunocom-neut-fever)

[Prevention of bacterial infections in a patient with malignancy](orzid2-gmenu-prev-infect-bact-prophyl)

[Prevention of fungal infections in a patient with malignancy](orzid2-gmenu-prev-infect-fungal-prophyl)

[Prevention of viral infection in a patient with malignancy](orzid2-gmenu-antiviral-prophylaxis-malignancy)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM MALNUTRITION
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

MALNUTRITION

Adequate nutrition is necessary for optimal host defense function.  A few days

of malnutrition can decrease host defenses, mainly cell-mediated immunity. The

degree of compromised immunity increases with the duration of malnutrition.

However, nutritional replacement has not been shown to improve outcomes in

patients with mild-moderate malnutrition.  Enteral nutritional replacement is

far superior to and safer than intravenous hyperalimentation.

# Treatment

Empirical antimicrobials are not indicated for malnourished patients with fever

but without evidence of a specific infectious disease.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM NEUROL DYSFUNCTION
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

NEUROLOGICAL DYSFUNCTION

Several types of neurological dysfunction predispose patients to infectious

diseases.  Comatose patients are unable to keep weight off dependent tissues,

predisposing them to decubitus ulcers and pressure necrosis.  Atelectasis is

common in obtunded patients who cannot cough or breathe deeply.  When patients

require artificial ventilation, intubation compounds the risk of respiratory

infection.

Neurological dysfunction of the bladder can interfere with normal bladder

emptying and predisposes patients to bacteriuria.  The risk of bacteruria

increases if patients are catheterized.  Antimicrobial treatment is not

indicated for asymptomatic bacteriuria.  It provides no benefit and increases

risk of colonization with resistant organisms.

Neurological dysfunction predisposes patients to aspiration of oropharyngeal or

gastric contents.  Aspiration causes fever, inflammation, and/or pulmonary

infiltrate, but does not require antimicrobial treatment. Bacterial pneumonia

occurs in a minority of patients who experience significant aspiration,

typically about 3 days later.  Typically, the patient improves for the first 2

days and then worsens as bacterial pneumonia develops with increased fever, new

or progressive infiltrates, leukocytosis, and newly purulent sputum.

[Aspiration pneumonia](orzid2-gmenu-abx-aspiration-pneumonia)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

LinkTargets.Text: Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more (Inpt)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM NEUT FEVER
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

NEUTROPENIC FEVER

The risk of severe, rapidly progressive infections increases when the absolute

neutrophil count (ANC, segmented neutrophils plus bands) is less than 500

cells/microliter.  The risk increases dramatically when the ANC is <100

cells/microliter.  Because of these risks, patients with fever and neutropenia

to this degree should receive empirical antimicrobial therapy immediately.

Empirical therapy should also be given to patients with fever and ANC 500-1000

cells/microliter when the concentration is expected to be <500 cells/microliter

within the next 48 hours.  For this purpose, fever is defined as a single

temperature greater than 38.3 degrees Celsius.

# Initial therapy

Since infection can be rapidly progressive and severe, broad-spectrum

antimicrobials are given urgently to patients with neutropenic fever as defined

above.  Vancomycin should only be given when there are clear indications for its

use.

Candidates for empirical treatment with oral antimicrobials include those who

are febrile but who have no evidence of focal infection or signs or symptoms of

severe disease, like hypotension.  Outpatient antimicrobials for neutropenic

fever must be ordered only in consultation with Hematology-Oncology or

Infectious Diseases.

# Treatment

[If patient IS a candidate for oral therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-cand-oral-thera)

[If patient is NOT a candidate for oral therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-cand-not-oral-thera)

[Link to a scoring tool that identifies low risk patients for oral therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-scoring-tool)

# Modifcation to therapy

[Modification to neutropenic fever therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-mod-therapy)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Hughes WT  Clin Infect Dis 2002, 34: 730

Rolston KVI Clin Infect Dis 2004, 39: S44

Sipsas NV  Cancer 2005, 103: 1103

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM NEUTROPENIA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

NEUTROPENIA

Patients with neutropenia are at risk of infection from pyogenic organisms

including Staphylococcus aureus, streptococci, Gram-negative bacilli,

Pseudomonas aeruginosa, candida, and certain filamentous fungi, most notably

Aspergillus and the zygomycetes.  The risk is inversely related to the absolute

neutrophil count (ANC), the disease or condition associated with neutropenia,

duration of neutropenia, and the presence of other host defense defects or

underlying diseases.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

LinkTargets.Item: ORZID2 GMENU ABX GENERAL INFORMATION INPATIENT

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM STRESS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

STRESS

Acute psychological stress is associated with immune stimulation and increased

cellular host defenses.  However, chronic stress decrease humoral and cell-

mediated immunity.  Chronic stress has been correlated with increased risk of

respiratory tract infection.

Critically ill patients are usually profoundly stressed.  The risk of infection

is subtle and the defects are non-specific.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

LinkTargets.Text: Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more (Inpt)
LinkTargets.Item: ORZID2 GMENU ABX GENERAL INFORMATION INPATIENT

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU IMMUNOCOM TOBACCO SMOKE
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

TOBACCO SMOKE

Active or passive exposure to tobacco smoke is associated with increased

susceptibility to respiratory infectious diseases and several systemic

infectious diseases with bacterial and viral pathogens.  Compounds found in

tobacco or tobacco smoke interfere with several host defense mechanisms in the

respiratory tract and elsewhere in the body.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Rich RR, et al, eds.  Clinical Immunology

Roitt I, et al, eds.  Immunology

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# INFECTIOUS DIARRHEA / GASTROENTERITIS

Most episodes of acute diarrhea are self-limited. In most mild to moderate

cases, antimicrobial therapy does not provide benefit.

# Bloody diarrhea

Bloody diarrhea can represent hemorrhagic colitis or dysentery. Antimicrobial

therapy and antimotility agents are not recommended in most patients with bloody

diarrhea due to an increased risk of hemolytic uremic syndrome when using these

agents.

# Primary treatment

Hydration and electrolyte replacement

# Empirical antimicrobial treatment of diarrhea

[Community acquired diarrhea \(no recent travel\)](orzid2-gmenu-comm-acq-diarrhea)

[Traveler's diarrhea](orzid2-gmenu-travelers-diarrhea)

# Treatment of diarrhea caused by specific bacteria, parasites, and viruses

[Campylobacter](orzid2-gmenu-abx-campylobacter)

[Mild to moderate disease](orzid2-gmenu-abx-assoc-colitis)

[Escherichia coli, including varieties listed below:](orzid2-gmenu-abx-e-coli-infect)

Enteroaggretive E. coli (EAEC), Enterotoxigenic E. coli (ETEC),

# INTERIM REPORT OF GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLI

Most Gram-negative bacilli grow in aerobic or anaerobic bottles. Pseudomonas

nearly always grows in aerobic bottles. One drug is sufficient to treat Gram-

negative bacillus bacteremia, unless the patient is critically ill.

# Empirical treatment

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# __________________________________________________________________

For patients with severe penicillin allergy

[Aztreonam 2 gm IV q8h \(Cost $$$$\) R](psjizid-aztreonam-2gm-iv-q8h)

# __________________________________________________________________

# INTERIM REPORT OF GRAM-POSITIVE COCCI IN PAIRS

A preliminary report of gram-positive cocci in pairs suggests staphylococci,

streptococci, or enterococci. If the patient is severely ill, is likely

colonized with resistant organisms, or if staphylococci or enterococci are

likely, treat with vancomycin until susceptibility results are known.

# INTERIM REPORT OF GRAM-POSITIVE COCCI IN PAIRS AND CHAINS

If chains are reported, streptococci are likely. If short chains are

reported, enterococci are likely. Beta-lactam antimicrobials are more effective

organisms, treat with vancomycin until susceptibility results are known.

INTERIM REPORT OF GRAM-POSITIVE BACILLI

There are three typical morphologies (1)large and regular, (2)medium sized and

variable, and (3)small and pleomorphic.  The large, uniformly rod-shaped Gram-

positive bacilli are usually Bacillus spp. (aerobic) or Clostridium species

(anaerobic).  Bacillus spp. include Bacillus subtilis (usually a contaminant),

Bacillus cereus, and Bacillus anthracis.  Medium-sized Gram-positive bacilli are

usually Lactobacilli (anaerobic).  Small and pleomorphic bacilli are usually

Listeria (aerobic), diphtheroids (aerobic), Propionibacteria (anaerobic), and

Corynebacteria (aerobic).

[LARGE UNIFORM BACILLI in an AEROBIC bottle](orzid2-gmenu-int-lrg-unif-rds-aerobic-bot)

# INTERIM REPORT OF YEAST

Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases. If the yeast appear to be or are

known to be Candida species treat as follows. If other yeasts (e.g.

Cryptococcus, Histoplasma) are suspected, contact Infectious Diseases for

treatment advice.

Refer to specific organism for yeasts other than candida

[Fungi](orzid2-gmenu-abx-fungus)

Most Candida can be treated with fluconazole. If the patient is critically ill

or neutropenic or has recently taken an azole antifungal, or if Candida krusei

or C. glabrata are suspected, micafungin should be used initially. Removal of

central venous catheter is associated with decreased mortality. Call Infectious

Diseases for advice.

# Empirical treatment for patients with mild to moderate illness who have no

# prior azole antifungal therapy

[Fluconazole 800 mg PO once then 400 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-800mg-po-once-then-400mg-q24h)

For patients who cannot take oral medication

[Fluconazole 800 mg IV once then 400 mg IV q24h \($\) R,DI](orz-set-abx-fluconazole-iv-800mg-once-then-400mg-q24h)

# Empirical treatment for critically ill patients, neutropenic patients, patients

# who have recently taken azole antifungals, or if C. glabrata or C. krusei are

# suspected

[Micafungin 100 mg IV q24h \($$$\) DI](psjizid-micafungin-100mg-iv-q24h)

References

Andes et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases 2012, 54.8

Mandell chapter: Candida Species

# SMALL PLEOMORPHIC BACILLI IN AEROBIC BOTTLE

Small pleomorphic bacilli in aerobic bottle are usually diphtheroids. These are

usually contaminants. Uncommonly such organisms prove to be Listeria

monocytogenes, which when present in a blood culture is likely a pathogen.

Listeria is more likely in patients with impaired cell-mediated immunity,

pregnant women, elderly and patients on immunosuppressive therapy for

transplantation.

# INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED COAGULASE-NEGATIVE STAPHYLOCOCCUS INFECTION

# (CNS)

Catheter removal is optional. However, treatment is more likely to be successful

with removal of catheter. The decision about whether to remove the catheter

depends on severity of illness, presence of resistant organisms, the need for

the catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment if the catheter is removed

# Duration of therapy

In cases where bacteremia is rapidly cleared, treat for 5-7 days. In cases where

rapid clearance of bacteremia does not occur, treat for up to 14 days.

Refer to coagulase-negative staphylococcus bacteremia recommendations for

antimicrobial selection.

[Coagulase-negative staphylococcus bacteremia](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-coag-neg-staph)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment if the catheter is retained

Consult infectious diseases in all cases. Treatment success rate is improved

when the infected catheter is filled with an antimicrobial solution during

periods when the catheter is not used. Consult Infectious Diseases or Pharmacy

for information.

# Duration of therapy

Treat concurrently with systemic therapy and antibiotic lock therapy for 10 to

14 days. If follow up blood cultures are persistently positive after 72 hours,

catheter should be removed promptly.

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# Treatment for methicillin-susceptible staphylococci (mecA negative)

[Cefazolin 2 gm IVPB q8h \($\) R <AND> cefazolin antibiotic lock therapy](orz-set-abx-cefazo-2gm-q8h-cefaz-abx-lock-therapy)

# INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED ENTEROCOCCUS INFECTION

Catheter removal is preferred but not required. Treatment is much more likely to

be successful with removal of catheter. The decision about whether to remove the

catheter depends on severity of illness, presence of resistant organisms, the

need for the catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# Treatment if the catheter is removed (preferred)

Duration of therapy:

For ampicillin or vancomycin susceptible isolates, treat for 7-14 days. A longer

duration is required for resistant isolates. Consult Infectious Diseases for

more information.

Refer to enterococcus bacteremia recommendations for antimicrobial selection

[Enterococci bacteremia](orzid2-gmenu-bacteremia-enterococci)

# Treatment if catheter removal is not possible (less desirable)

Duration of therapy:

For ampicillin or vancomycin susceptible isolates, treat concurrently with

systemic and antibiotic lock therapy for 14 days. Consult Infectious Diseases

for ampicillin and vancomycin resistant isolates.

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases

# INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED GRAM-NEGATIVE BACILLI INFECTION

Catheter removal is strongly recommended, especially when resistant isolates are

present. Delayed catheter removal is associated with increased mortality in

patients with drug resistant organisms. The decision about whether to remove the

catheter depends on severity of illness, presence of resistant organisms, the

need for the catheter, and how difficult catheter replacement would be.

# Treatment if catheter is removed (preferred)

Duration of therapy

Treat uncomplicated cases for 7 to 14 days. A longer duration may be required

for complicated or critically ill patients. Consult Infectious Diseases for more

information.

Treatment

antimicrobial.

Duration of therapy

Treat uncomplicated cases with concurrent systemic and antibiotic lock therapy

for 14 days. A longer duration may be required for complicated or critically ill

patients.

# INTRAVASCULAR CATHETER-ASSOCIATED INFECTION

[Approach to intravascular catheter-associated infection and antimicrobial](orzid2-gmenu-appro-intravas-cath-assoc-infect)

lock therapy

When catheter-related bacteremia is suspected, draw blood cultures from both the

catheter and a peripheral vein. If patient is seriously ill (hypotension,

hypoperfusion, signs and symptoms of organ failure) remove catheter and culture

tip. In patients who are moderately ill (e.g. hypotension, organ failure),

remove catheter and culture tip if patient has a prosthetic valve, pacemaker or

vascular graft. Start empirical antibiotics while awaiting culture results.

Narrow therapeutic spectrum based on sensitivities of cultured pathogens.

# Empirical therapy

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU KERATITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# KERATITIS

Keratitis is an emergency requiring prompt treatment to prevent vision loss.

Contact Ophthalmology immediately.

Keratitis is associated with viral or bacterial infection, trauma, foreign

bodies, or allergies. About half of cases of infectious keratitis are caused by

bacterial pathogens, most commonly Staphylococcus spp., Streptococcus spp., and

gram-negative bacilli. Viruses are the second leading cause. Fungi and parasites

have also been associated with corneal infection. Obtain corneal scrapings for

gram stain and bacterial and viral cultures and start empirical therapy

immediately.

Link to herpes keratitis page

[Herpes keratitis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-herpes-keratitis)

If bacterial keratitis is likely, contact ophthalmology to obtain a corneal

scraping and give empirical antibacterial drops immediately. Modify therapy

based on Ophthalmology and/or Infectious Diseases recommendations. Ophthalmic

corticosteroids are contraindicated in patients with keratitis.

# Duration of therapy

Treatment should be continued until ulcer and other signs of infectious

keratitis have resolved. A minimum of two weeks and in rare cases, up to a month

of therapy may be required.

# Mild to moderate bacterial keratitis empirical treatment

[Moxifloxacin 0.5% ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops in affected eye\(s\) q1h \($\) M](psjzid-moxifloxacin-0-5-opth-1-2-drop-q1h)

# Severe (vision-threatening) bacterial keratitis empirical treatment

[Cefazolin 50 mg/ml ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops q1h <AND> gentamicin 15 mg/ml](orz-set-abx-cefz-50mg-ml-oph-gent-15mg-ml-oph-q1h)

ophthalmic drops: 1-2 drops q1h ($) [M] in affected eye(s)

# Suspected MRSA

Patient may require vancomycin 50mg/mL eye drops q1h in addition to gentamicin

eye drops. Vancomycin eye drops must be specially compounded and managed by

Ophthalmology.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Lin et al., Ophthalmology. 2019,126(1):1-55

Mandell chapter: Microbial keratitis

Sanford keyword: Keratitis
