menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU LEUKOCYTOSIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# LEUKOCYTOSIS

The majority of leukocytosis cases are due to infection, but a sizable minority

are associated with physiological stress, inflammation, medications (e.g.

glucocorticoids), and hematological conditions. In a review of 100 cases of

extreme leukocytosis (more than 25,000 leukocytes per microliter with more than

50% granulocytes) at the Minneapolis VA, only 48 were from infectious problems.

Infection should be considered as a possible stimulus for leukocytosis in a

patient with leukocytosis, especially when total white blood cell count is

greater than or equal to 25,000 per micro liter. Antimicrobials should be

administered if the patient has a syndrome or disease that calls for

antimicrobials. Refer to those recommendations for treatment. Antimicrobials

should not be administered solely to treat a patient with leukocytosis and no

other sign or symptom of infection.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Wanahita et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases (2002), 34.1585-92

Reding et al., The American Journal of Medicine (1998), 104.12-16

menus.Term1: Neurological disease associated with Lyme disease
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ACUTE NEUROLOGICAL DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH LYME DISEASE

Neurological disease is a common manifestation of Lyme Disease that typically

occurs within weeks to months after the tick bite. Unilateral or bilateral

facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy) can be treated with oral antimicrobials. Other

neurological manifestations, including meningitis, require treatment with

intravenous antimicrobials.

# Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases

# Duration of therapy

Treat for at least 14 days. Longer durations, up to 21 days for facial nerve

palsy and 28 days for other neurologic disease, may be required in severe cases.

# Treatment of isolated facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy)

Preferred:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

For pregnant patients or those with contraindications to doxycycline:

[Amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h \($\) R](psjzid-amoxicillin-500mg-po-q8h)

# Treatment of neurological disease other than facial nerve palsy (Bell's palsy)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Halperin et. al., Neurology (2007) 69.91-102

# CARDIAC DISEASE ASSOCIATED WITH LYME DISEASE

Carditis is a rare manifestation of Lyme Disease and typically occurs within one

to two months after onset of infection.

# Consult Infectious Diseases and Cardiology in all cases

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU LYME DISEASE PROPHYLAXIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# LYME DISEASE PROPHYLAXIS

Patients who have been bitten while in endemic areas of New England, Mid-

Atlantic States, Minnesota, and Wisconsin where local rate of Ixodes spp. tick

infection rate with Borrelia burgdorferi in an endemic area may be treated with

prophylactic antibiotics for prevention of Lyme disease. Using a wait and see

method by monitoring for signs and symptoms of Lyme disease is also an

acceptable approach in patients who have been bitten by an Ixodes spp. tick.

# All following criteria must be met to be considered for prophylactic treatment

1. Doxycycline is not contraindicated (i.e. allergy, pregnant, lactating)

2. Attached tick is reliably identified as an adult or nymphal Ixodes spp.

[Ixodes spp. identification](orz-gtx-abx-tick-identification-link)

3. Tick is attached for greater than or equal to 36 hours based on degree of

tick engorgement with blood or likely time of exposure to tick infested area.

4. Prophylaxis must be started within 72 hours after time tick was removed.

5. Bite occurs in a highly endemic area.

[CDC Lyme Disease Case Map](orz-gtx-abx-cdc-lyme-disease-case-map)

# Prophylactic treatment if all of the above criteria are met

[Doxycycline PO 200mg once \($\) DI](psjzid-doxycycline-200mg-po-once)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Term1: Erythema migrans associated with Lyme disease
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# ERYTHEMA MIGRANS ASSOCIATED WITH LYME DISEASE

Erythema migrans is the first manifestation of Lyme disease in 70-80% of cases.

It is typically an erythematous circular rash, 5cm or larger in diameter, with

induration and central clearing (although other patterns occur). It usually

develops at the site of the bite and/or in one or more distant locations. The

rash occurs 3 to 30 days after the bite. Rashes with onset less than 3 days

after a tick bite are not from Lyme disease.

If suspected erythema migrans is atypical, serology testing is recommended

with repeat in three weeks if negative.

[Lyme Panel, Serum](lrtz-lyme-panel)

# Treatment

Preferred:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 10 days](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

For pregnant patients or those with contraindications to doxycycline:

[Amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h \($\) R for 14 days](psjzid-amoxicillin-500mg-po-q8h)

menus.Text:

# MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM INTRACELLULARE (MAI OR MAC)

MAI colonization in patients with chronic lung disease is common. These

patients should not be treated with antimicrobials.

Occasionally, MAI causes pulmonary disease in patients who are not

immunosuppressed. Diagnosis and management are complex. Consult Infectious

Diseases and/or Pulmonary.

MAI causes systemic disease commonly in patients with HIV/AIDS. Most of these

cases do not involve the lungs. After treatment, long-term prophylaxis is

usually given. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM PNEUMONIA

Diagnosis and treatment are complex. Regimens containing 3 or 4 drugs are

usually recommended, but two drug regimens may be sufficient in some cases.

Consult Infectious Diseases and/or Pulmonary in all cases.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treatment is continued until sputum cultures are consecutively negative for 12

months.

# Three-drug regimens

Preferred treatment

[Clarithromycin 500 mg PO q12h \($\) R,DI <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h](orz-set-abx-clarithromycin-ethambutol-rifabutin)

($$) [R] <AND> rifabutin 300 mg PO q24h ($$) [R,DI]

Alternative

[Azithromycin 250 mg PO q24h \($\) M <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO q24h R](orz-set-abx-azith-250-ethambutol-rifabutin-300)

<AND> rifabutin 300 mg q24h ($$) [R,DI]

# Four-drug regimens may be recommended for advanced (severe) or previously

# treated disease-Consult Infectious Diseases

# MALIGNANT OTITIS EXTERNA

Those who are elderly, diabetic, immunocompromised and debilitated are at

highest risk. Most cases are associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, but other

pathogens can be involved. Obtain culture to identify etiologic agent and

susceptibilities. Obtain a CT scan to determine whether osteomyelitis is

present. ENT and Infectious Disease consultations are recommended.

# Treatment

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q12h for 6 weeks \($$\) R](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q12h)

< OR >

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

for 6 weeks

< OR >

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q8h for 6 weeks \($\) R,DI](psjizid-ciprofloxacin-400mg-iv-q12h)

# Treatment of early infection or step-down treatment after initial intravenous

# antimicrobial therapy. Adjust for a total duration of 6 weeks of antimicrobial

# therapy.

[Ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO q12h for 6 weeks \($\) R,DI](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-750mg-po-q12h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU MASTOIDITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# MASTOIDITIS

# Acute Mastoiditis

Acute mastoiditis most commonly occurs as a suppurative complication of acute

otitis media. Diagnosis is supported by CT or MRI imaging and culture of

drainage. Antibiotics and drainage of middle ear are sufficient treatment in

most cases. Mastoidectomy is necessary if abscess has formed in the mastoid

bone. If complication of first episode of acute otitis media, etiologies

typically include Streptococcus pneumonia (most common), Streptococcus pyogenes,

or Staphylococcus aureus. If secondary to chronic otitis media, etiologies

typically include Staphylococcus aureus or Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Patients

usually too ill for outpatient therapy. ENT consultation recommended. Obtain

cultures of auditory canal or middle ear fluid (preferred).

# Empirical Treatment

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](orz-set-abx-pip-taz4-5gm-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro-vanco15mg-kg)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q 12 hours ($) [R] for 7 days

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q 12 hours \($\) R < AND > cefepime 2 gm IV q12h \($$\) R](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q12h-vanco-15mg-kg-q12h)

for 7 days

# Step down treatment after initial intravenous antibiotic treatment in patients

# who can tolerate oral therapy. Base selection on culture results. Adjust for a

# total duration of 7 days of antimicrobial therapy.

[Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) R](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Cefuroxime 500mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) R](psjzid-cefuroxime-500mg-q12h)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# __________________________________________________________________

# Chronic Mastoiditis

Chronic mastoiditis is usually the result of chronic otitis media with

perforation of the tympanic membrane. There is often associated formation of a

cholesteatoma (keratoma). Diagnosis is supported by CT or MRI imaging and

culture of drainage. Long term treatment with topical antimicrobials is first

line therapy. Infection is often polymicrobial, including Staphylococcus aureus,

Pseudomonas aeruginosa and anaerobes. Treatment should be managed in

collaboration with otolaryngology and includes topical antimicrobials, care of

external auditory canal, and is some cases mastoidectomy. If possible, withhold

therapy until a pathogen is identified by culture of drainage to direct therapy.

Specific drug choice dictated by culture results.

# Empirical Treatment

Preferred:

[Ciprofloxacin-Dexamethasone otic 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) BID for 4 weeks \($\)](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-4-drps-bid)

[M]

Alternative:

[Neomycin-polymyxin-hydrocortisone ear drops 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) QID for 4](psjzid-neomycin-polymixin-hc-otic-4-drps-qid)

weeks ($) [M]

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Mandell chapter: Otitis Externa, Otitis Media, and Mastoiditis

Loh et. al., The Journal of Laryngology & Otology. 2018, 132(2)96-104.

Sanford keyword: Mastoiditis

adults

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU MILD TO MOD SINUSITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# MILD TO MODERATE SINUSITIS

Community-acquired bacterial sinusitis is most often due to Streptococcus

pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae or Moraxella catarrhalis. Streptococci,

Staphylococcus aureus and anaerobes are isolated less frequently.

# Treatment for first 10 days of illness

Treat with decongestants, analgesics, and nasal saline spray.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment of cases that have not improved in 10 days despite

# treatment with decongestants, analgesics, and nasal saline.

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 5 days](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

Alternatives:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 5 days](psjzid-cefdinir-300mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h \($\) DI for 5 days](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment Failure

If symptoms worsen despite 72 hours or  fail to improve after 3-5 days of

initial empirical antimicrobial therapy, broaden coverage, switch to different

antimicrobial class and treat 7-10 days. If symptoms continue to worsen or there

is no improvement after 3-5 more days of treatment, obtain CT to investigate

non-infectious or suppurative causes. ENT consultation is recommended. If

sinuses are aspirated, specimens should be cultured.

[Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h \($\) R,DI for 7 days](psjzid-levofloxacin-750mg-po-q24h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

THE APPROACH TO CELLULITIS

In addition to antimicrobial therapy, several non-pharmacological treatments

improve the outcome of cellulitis.Elevation and immobilization of the

affected limb reduces swelling.  Heat reduces discomfort.

Prevent tinea pedis infection by keeping feet clean and dry.  In patients with

peripheral edema, good skin hygiene and support stockings reduce the incidence

of recurrent infection.

In many cases of cellulitis, the affected area is usually not well-

differeniated from unaffected areas of the skin. Erysipelas is a special case

with typically a well-defined border and raised, orange-peel appearance.

[Erysipelas](orzid2-gmenu-erysipelas)

Use broad-spectrum therapy for cellulitis arising in feet of patients with

advanced diabetes.

[Foot ulcer in patient with diabetes mellitus](orzid2-gmenu-foot-ulcer-with-dm)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU MORE ABOUT PHARYNGITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# MORE ABOUT PHARYNGITIS/ TONSILLITIS AND THE MODIFIED CENTOR SCORE

As most cases are of viral origin, antimicrobials are not indicated in these

cases. Warm saltwater gargle rinses and throat lozenges provide temporary relief

of throat pain. Five to 10% of cases are caused by group A Streptococcus.

Antimicrobial treatment reduces symptoms by one day, prevents suppurative

complications and prevents acute rheumatic fever, an uncommon disease in US

adults.

Streptococcal pharyngitis or tonsillitis should be suspected when patients have

fever and exudate on the pharyngeal wall or tonsils without symptoms like cough,

nasal congestion, or runny nose that suggest viral infection or common cold. If

streptococcal pharyngitis is suspected in adults, perform PCR testing for group

A streptococci and treat only if positive.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a rare cause of pharyngitis. N. gonorrhoeae should be

considered for patients with risk factors for sexually transmitted diseases. N.

gonorrhoeae infections must be reported to the state health department and this

will be done by Infection Control if the culture is positive.

# The Modified Centor score

Used to estimate the likelihood that a patient with sore throat has

streptococcal pharyngitis and whether rapid PCR testing should be performed.

1) Absence of cough = 1 point

2) Swollen and tender anterior cervical nodes = 1 point

3) Temperature greater than 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Centigrade) = 1

point

4) Tonsillar exudates or swelling = 1 point

5) Age: 3-14 years = 1 point

15-44 years = 0 points

45 years and older = -1 point

Patients with a score of 0 or 1 are at very low risk. PCR testing and antibiotic

treatment are not indicated. Patients with a score of 2 to 4 are at moderate to

high risk. PCR testing should be obtained in these patients to determine if GAS

is present. In patients with a score of 4 or greater, consider empiric

antibiotic treatment.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Choby, Am Fam Physician. 2009 79(5) 383-390

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

NECROTIZING INFECTIONS

Call Surgery immediately and consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Necrotizing infections involve tissues skin and/or deeper structures, including

fascia and muscle.  These infections destroy tissue, often rapidly, and are

often fatal if not treated promptly and appropriately.  Necrotizing infections

usually result from trauma, surgery, and/or ischemia.  These infections can be

monomicrobial (e.g., with streptococci or clostridia) or polymicrobial (usually

with a mixture of aerobes and anaerobes).  Fournier gangrene is usually

associated with mixed infection.  Myonecrosis is most commonly associated with

Clostridium species.

Necrotizing infections differ from cellulitis in several ways.  Necrotic

infections typically have one or more of the following: (1) severe, constant

pain, (2) bullae, (3) bruising or necrosis of overlying skin, (4) gas in tissues

which can be felt or seen on images, (5) edema that extends beyond areas of

erythema, (6) local anesthesia, and (7) signs of systemic toxicity, such as

fever, leukocytosis, delirium, or renal failure.

Necrotizing infections must be treated with both antimicrobial therapy and

surgical procedures (excision and/or drainage).  Call surgery to see the patient

immediately in all cases.  Obtain tissue and blood cultures and begin empirical

antimicrobials.  For several necrotic diseases and/or pathogens, a combination

of two antimicrobials is recommended including a bactericidal antimicrobial

active at the cell wall or membrane (e.g., beta-lactam or glycopeptide) and an

antimicrobial that rapidly inhibits protein synthesis and thus inhibits toxin

production, typically clindamycin.

Repeat debridement should be performed daily until no further debridement is

necessary. Antibiotic therapy should be tailored as soon as culture results

become available.

Administer antibiotics until further debridement is no longer necessary, the

patient has improved clinically, and fever has been absent for 48-72 hours.

[Empirical therapy of necrotizing infections](orzid2-gmenu-necrot-infect-emp-therapy)

# Pathogen-directed treatment regimens

Determine efficacy of the initial regimen during the first 3 to 5 days.

disease has been diagnosed (e.g., pneumonia or cellulitis), (2) whether the

fever has resolved, and (3) the clinical course.

If a specific infectious disease and/or pathogen is identified, ensure that the

antimicrobial regimen is adequate to treat that pathogen or disease, and

continue broad-spectrum antimicrobial therapy.

TREATMENT

(The infectious disease associated with the fever has resolved, the pathogen has

been controlled or eradicated, and the patient seems well)

Stop antimicrobials after treatment for pathogen/disease is completed, often

after 7 days.

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

PATIENTS WITH NEUTROPENIC FEVER WHOSE FEVER PERSISTS THROUGHOUT THE FIRST 3 TO 5

DAYS OF TREATMENT

If no infectious disease has been diagnosed but the patient is clinically

stable, continue the current regimen.  If vancomycin was part of initial therapy

but culture results have not yielded a pathogen that must be treated with

vancomycin, discontinue it to minimize development of resistance.

Consider adding amphotericin B for empirical antifungal therapy.  Hematology-

oncology or Infectious Diseases may recommend another antifungal like

micafungin or voriconazole.  Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

If the patient is receiving prophylactic fluconazole, stop it when empirical

antifungals are started.

# Treatment

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# MASCC RISK INDEX FOR FEBRILE NEUTROPENIA

SCORING TOOL TO IDENTIFY LOW RISK FEBRILE NEUTROPENIC PATIENTS

Patients with minimal risk of severe or rapidly progressive infection can be

treated with oral antimicrobials safely.  Many can be treated as outpatients.

Use the scoring index to identify febrile neutropenic patients who at

sufficiently low risk for severe infections and can be treated with outpatient

oral antimicrobials.

# SCORING INDEX

# CharacteristicScore

Severity of symptoms of illness (choose one only)

No symptoms or mild symptoms5

Moderate symptoms  3

No hypotension  5

No chronic obstructive pulmonary disease4

Solid tumor or no previous fungal infection4

No dehydration  3

Outpatient status at onset of fever3

Age less than 60 years2

Sum total __

# Interpretation

The highest possible score is 26. A risk index score of 21 or greater indicates

that the patient is likely to be at LOW RISK for complications and morbidity.

This is a guide.  Always use clinical judgement.

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Klastersky, J Clin Oncol 2000, 18: 3038

# NOSOCOMIAL SINUSITIS

Nasogastric tubes increase the risk of bacterial sinus infection associated with

Staphylococcus aureus, streptococcus, and gram-negative bacilli, including

Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Aspirate sinuses for gram stain and culture to direct

antimicrobial therapy. Adequate sinus drainage is vital to treatment.

# Empirical antimicrobial treatment

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-3-375-gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q12h \($$\) R](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q12h)

# MRSA suggestive on gram-stain

[< ADD > Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# EMPIRICAL THERAPY FOR OSTEOMYELITIS

# Recommend Infectious Disease consultation.

Bone culture is essential and diagnostic. If patient is not clinically ill and a

diagnostic procedure is planned, antibiotics can be held until after the

procedure.

Therapy should be modified when culture results and patient response to therapy

are known.

Duration of treatment is 4 to 6 weeks.

# Empiric Therapy

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

History of Pseudomonas in wound:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h R](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

If MRSA history:

[<ADD> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Oral switch recommendations based on culture results

Treatment for MSSA and streptococci:

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h R](psjzid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-q12h)

Treatment for MRSA:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU OSTEOMYELITIS EVALUATION
menus.Text:
# Osteomyelitis Evaluation:

-Consider osteomyelitis in any infected, deep, or large foot ulcer, particularly

those that are chronic and over bony prominences.

-Plain films along with the probe-to-bone test are reasonable first steps

in evaluating for osteomyelitis.

-Patients where the diagnosis remains unclear should undergo MRI.

-Patients with findings suggesitve of osteomyelitis should undergo debridement

with bone culture BEFORE antibiotics are started, if possible

-Consult surgery (orthopedics or vascular) for potential surgical

intervention. (Vascular preferred for known PVD)

-Consult Infectious Diseases for evaluation and management of long-term

antibiotics.

[<Click here> Osteomyelitis](orzid2-gmenu-osteomyelitis)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# OTITIS EXTERNA

# Acute Localized Disease

Often due to furunculosis and usually associated with Staphylococcus aureus.

Treat mild cases with moist local heat. For cases with cellulitis or deep

invasion, incision and drainage as well as systemic antibiotics may be needed.

Refer to the Furuncles and Carbuncles page for antibiotic recommendations.

[Furuncles and Carbuncles](orzid2-gmenu-furuncles-and-carbuncles)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Acute diffuse and chronic otitis externa

Most commonly associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus and

Staphylococcus epidermidis. Irrigate to remove cerumen, desquamated skin and

purulent material which can improve effectiveness of topical antibiotics. Avoid

products that contain neomycin if the tympanic membrane is perforated.

# Preferred treatment if tympanic membrane is intact

[Neomycin-polymyxin-hydrocortisone ear drops 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) QID](psjzid-neomycin-polymixin-hc-otic-4-drps-qid)

for 7 days ($) [M]

# Alternative if tympanic membrane is perforated or allergy to preferred treatmen

[Ciprofloxacin-Dexamethasone otic 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) BID for 7 days \($\)](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-4-drps-bid)

[M]

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Complicated Cases

For cases resistant to topical therapy alone, patients with poorly controlled

diabetes mellitus, immunocompromised patients, cases where infection has spread

beyond ear canal and in those where topical therapy cannot be delivered

effectively. Culture secretions to guide therapy.

In addition to topical therapy above

[< ADD > ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) R,DI](psjzid-ciprofl-500mg-po-q12h)

Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenza, and Moraxella catarrhalis are

the most common bacteria to cause otitis media.

# Preferred treatment

Patient has NOT received antibiotics in the prior month

Patient has received antibiotics in the prior month

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

PARONYCHIA

Cutaneous infection of the hand, cuticle or fingers usually occurring near OR

around the nail.

Treatment depends on etiology.  Candida spp. are commonly involved when the

patient has extensive exposure to water (e.g. dishwashers).  Staphylococcus

aureus is more commonly after manicures or nail biting.  Herpes simplex

(whitlow) usually follows exposure to oral mucosa (e.g. wrestlers, dentists, or

anesthetists).

# ________________________________________________________

# Treatment for paronychia associated with Candida

# ________________________________________________________

Treat for 14 days

[Clotrimazole 1% apply to affected area once daily \($\) M](psjzid-clotrim-1-cream-topical-qday)

# Alternative

[Nystatin Cream to affected area BID \($\) M](psjzid-nystatin-cream-bid)

# ________________________________________________________

# Treatment for paronychia associated with Staphylococcus

# ________________________________________________________

Treat for 10 days

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID \($\) R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

# Alternative

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID \($\) DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment for paronychia associated with Herpes whitlow

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU PERIOCULAR INFECTIONS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PERIOCULAR INFECTIONS

# Eyelid infections

Patients with moderate or severe eyelid infections should be referred to

ophthalmology.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Blepharitis

Wash margins with baby shampoo daily and use warm compresses daily.

Antimicrobials have no benefit.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Hordeolum (stye)

For external disease (involving the gland of Zeis), daily hot pack massage

encourages drainage and relieves symptoms. For internal disease (involving

Meibomian glands) ophthalmology consult is encouraged, as the infection seldom

drains without intervention.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Lacrimal infections

Refer cases of lacrimal infection to ophthalmology, including infections of the

lacrimal gland (dacryoadenitis), lacrimal sac (dacrocystitis), or tear ducts

(canaliculitis).

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PERIODONTAL DISEASE

Periodontal disease, including gingivitis and periodontitis, may progress into

more severe disease or cause hematogenous spreading of bacteria if left

untreated. All patients with periodontal disease should be referred to the

dental service for assessment and direction of treatment. In the presence of

gingivitis, the most commonly isolated subgingival flora includes Prevotella

intermedia, Capnocytophaga spp, Finegoldia magna and Peptostreptococcus. In the

presence of periodontitis, flora increases in complexity to most commonly

include Porphyromonas gingivalis, P. intermedia, Aggregatibacter

actinomycetemcomitans, Tanneralla forsythensis and Treponema denticola.

# Consult Dental Service

# Non-severe periodontitis or acute simple gingivitis treatment

[Chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse swish for 30 seconds, then spit 15 ml twice](psjzid-chlorhexidine-0-12-oral-swish-bid)

daily for 7 days ($) [M]

# Severe periodontitis or acute complicated gingivitis (ulceration, rapidly

# advancing disease, severe pain, patients with immunocompromising conditions)

# treatment

Consult Dental Service

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU PNEUMOCYSTIS JIROVECII
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PNEUMOCYSTIS JIROVECII DISEASE

Diagnosis and treatment are complex, consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Pneumocystis jirovecii (formerly termed Pneumocystis carinii) in an ubiquitious

organism that causes disease in people with compromised cell-mediated immunity.

Disease is exceedingly rare in people with intact host defenses. Pneumonia is

the usual manifestation but P. jirovecii can infect extrapulmonary sites,

especially in patients who have been receiving prophylaxis with aerosolized

pentanmidine. P. jirovecii disease occurs most commonly in people with AIDS and

fewer than 200 CD4 T lymphocytes/microliter.

The abbreviation PCP is often used for Pneumocystis pneumonia. It was derived

from the old species name, Pneumocystis carinii.

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMZ) is the treatment of choice for P.

jirovecii disease, including disease that occurs despite TMP-SMZ prophylaxis.

Corticosteriods should be prescribed for patients with AIDS and P. jirovecii

pneumonia and an arterial oxygen tension <70 torr or an alveolar-arterial oxygen

gradient of >35 torr.

[LINK to Prophylaxis for Pneumocystis Jirovecii](orzid2-gmenu-abx-pneumocystis-jirovecii-prophylaxis)

# Preferred treatment for mild to moderate disease or step-down treatment once

# disease has stabilized

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS tablets PO q8h for 21 days \($\)R,DI](psozid2-tmp-smx-2ds-tablets-po-q8h-21days)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 5mg/kg PO q8h \($\)R,DI <AND> dapsone 100mg](orz-set-abx-trimethoprim-5-mg-kg-dapsone-100mg-po-qd)

PO QDay ($)[DI] for 21 days

Alternative

[Clindamycin 450mg PO q6h \($\)H,O <AND> Primaquine 26.3 mg PO QDay \($\)DI](orz-set-abx-clindamycin-450mg-q6h-primaquine-26-3mg-qd)

for 21 days

< OR >

[Atovaquone 750mg PO BID for 21 days \($\)M](psjzid-atovaquone-750mg-po-bid)

# Preferred treatment for severe disease

[Trimethoprim 5mg/kg - sulfamethoxazole 25MG/KG IV q8h for 21 days](psjizid-trimeth-sulfa-5-25-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

($$)[R,DI]

Alternative

[Clindamycin 600mg IV q6h \($$\)H,O <AND> primaquine 26.3mg PO QD \($\)DI](orz-set-abx-clindamycin-600-iv-q6h-primaquine-26-3mg-qd)

for 21 days

< OR >

Requires ID Approval: Pentamidine 4mg/kg IV q24h ($$$)[DI]

# Prednisone for patient WITH AIDS

[Prednisone 40mg PO twice daily for 5 days, then 40mg PO daily for 6 days,](psjzid-prednisone-40mg-po-bid-then-40-6days-then-20-10-days)

then 20 mg daily for 10 days.

Associated with Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# POSTSEPTAL CELLULITIS (ORBITAL CELLULITIS)

Postseptal cellulitis (orbital cellulitis) is often preceded by sinusitis and

requires immediate consultation with otolaryngology and ophthalmology. Urgent

surgical drainage may be necessary. The most common pathogenic organisms in

adults are streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus

aureus. Broad-spectrum empirical antimicrobials should be used until a pathogen

can be identified from the drainage fluid.

# Duration of treatment

Orbital cellulitis should be treated until all signs of infection have resolved.

Uncomplicated orbital cellulitis should be treated for minimum of 2 weeks and

complicated orbital cellulitis (severe ethmoid sinusitis and bony destruction of

sinus) should be treated for at least 4 weeks.

# Empiric treatment

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](orz-set-abx-pip-taz4-5gm-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro-vanco15mg-kg)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-q24h-metro-500gm-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-q12h)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

# Step-down treatment after initial intravenous therapy. Base selection on cultur

# results.  Adjust duration based on criteria above.

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID \($\) R < AND >](orz-set-abx-amox-clav-875-po-q12h-trimeth-sulfa-2ds-po-q12)

trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 7 days

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h \($\) R < AND > trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO](orz-set-abx-cefdinir-300mg-po-q12h-tmp-smx-2ds-po-q12h)

q12h ($) [R,DI] for 7 days

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU PRESEPTAL CELLULITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PRESEPTAL CELLULITIS

Preseptal cellulitis involves soft tissues in front of the orbital septum and

the eyelids and is often preceded by sinusitis. Infection does not involve the

orbital contents. The most common pathogenic organisms in adults are

streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus aureus.

Treat under the guidance of ophthalmology and/or otolaryngology. Intravenous

antimicrobials are indicated initially for treatment of moderate to severe

disease. Switch to oral antimicrobials when the patient's symptoms improve and

the patient can tolerate oral medications.

# Moderate to severe infection or failure of oral antibiotics

Transition to oral antibiotics can be considered if significant improvement

within 24-48 hours.

Preferred:

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](orz-set-abx-pip-taz4-5gm-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro-vanco15mg-kg)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R] for 5 days

# Treatment of mild disease or step-down treatment after initial intravenous

# therapy. Treat for a total duration of 5 days.

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID \($\) R < AND>](orz-set-abx-amox-clav-875-po-q12h-trimeth-sulfa-2ds-po-q12)

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days

Alternative:

PREVENTION OF BACTERIAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

Antimicrobial prophylaxis is often given to patients likely to have profound,

prolonged neutropenia.  Profound neutropenia is less than 100 neutrophils and

bands per microliter, and such neutropenia is considered prolonged when it is

expected to last more than 7 days.  Most patients who should receive prophylaxis

have received stem cell transplants or are undergoing induction chemotherapy for

acute leukemia.

# If antibacterial prophylaxis is indicated

Duration of therapy: During period of expected neutropenia

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h \($\) R,DI < OR >](psjzid-ciprofloxacin-500mg-po-q12h)

[Levofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h \($\) R](psjzid-levoflox-500mg-po-q24h)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h  \($\) R,DI < OR >](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

[Cefpodoxime 100 mg PO q12h \($$\) R](psjzid-cefpodoxime-100mg-po-q12h)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

PREVENTION OF FUNGAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

Antifungal chemoprophylaxis is often given to patients undergoing induction

chemotherapy for acute leukemia expected to have profound neutropenia (less than

100 neutrophils and bands per milliliter) for more than 10 days and for patients

receiving allogeneic stem cell transplantation.  For most other patients the

expected benefits do not outweigh the risks of adverse effects and selection of

resistant fungi.

Antifungal is usually given until the absolute neutrophil concentration

increases to more than 500 cells/microliter in patients undergoing induction

chemotherapy for leukemia.  Duration is 100 days for patients undergoing stem

cell transplantation.  Some physicians continue prevention after 100 days if

corticosteroids are part of the immunosuppressive regimen.

Recommend posaconazole prophylaxis for patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia.

Contact Hematology Oncology or Infectious Disease for more information.

Patients who have had invasive fungal infection in the recent past and who are

about to become neutropenic may require chemoprophylaxis.  Contact Hematology-

Oncology or Infectious Disease for more information.

# If antifungal prophylaxis is indicated:

Duration of therapy: during period of expected neutropenia

[Fluconazole 400 mg po q24h \($\) R,DI](psjzid-fluconazole-400mg-po-q24h)

# For patients being treated for AML:

Requires Infectious Disease approval:

Posaconazole 300mg Tablets twice daily on day 1, then 300mg once daily on

day 2 and thereafter. Continue for 7 days after the neutrophil count

rises above 500/mm3. ($$$$) [DI]

patients

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU PREV OF BACT ENDOCARDITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PREVENTION OF BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS

Bacteremia occurs several times a day during daily activities like eating and

brushing teeth and rarely results in endocarditis, even in people with abnormal

valves.  While bacteremia might occur following dental or other procedures, most

cases of endocarditis are from the millions more episodes of transient

bacteremia a person experiences per year from ordinary daily activities.  There

is no evidence that antimicrobial prophylaxis prevents endocarditis after

procedures.  The best available evidence suggests that prophylactic

antimicrobials confer more risks than benefits in most situations.  A decision

about whether to administer antimicrobial prophylaxis should be based on both

the risk of endocarditis conferred by the patient's cardiac defect and the risk

of bacteremia from a planned dental or surgical procedure.

# Minneapolis VAHCS SOP antimicrobial prophylaxis for dental surgery:

[SOP for dental surgery antimicrobial prophylaxis](orz-gtx-abx-url-dental-sop)

# Determine the need for prophylaxis through the 2-step process outlined

# below.

# Step 1.  Assess the risk of endocarditis for your patient

Prophylaxis is recommended if a patient has any of the following conditions:

o  Prosthetic cardiac valve or material including: Presence of cardiac

prosthetic valve, transcatheter implantation of prosthetic valves (e.g. TAVR

cardiac valve repair with devices (e.g. annuloplasty, rings, or clips), left

ventricular assist devices or implantable heart

o  A history of infective endocarditis

o  Certain specific congenital heart conditions - refer to the full SOP

(link above) or consult Cardiology for more detailed recommendations

o  Cardiac transplant that develops a problem in the heart valve

# Step 2.  Assess the risk of bacteremia from the planned procedure

Prophylaxis is indicated for these procedures:

o  All dental procedures that involve manipulation of gingival tissue or the

periapical region of teeth or perforation of the oral mucosa.

o  Procedures on the respiratory tract that involve incision or biopsy of the

respiratory mucosa, such as tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy. Prophylaxis is

recommended for bronchoscopy when procedure involves incision of the respir.

tract mucosa.

o  Procedures that involve incision through infected skin, skin structures, or

musculoskeletal tissue.

o  Dermatologic procedures that breach the oral mucosa.

# Prophylactic Antimicrobials select below:

[Patients undergoing dental or oral mucosa procedures](orzid2-gmenu-drug-pt-undergo-dental-proc)

[Patients undergoing procedures on the respiratory tract that involve incision or](orzid2-gmenu-surg-head-and-neck-surg)

biopsy of the respiratory mucosa

[Patients undergoing procedures for infected skin, skin structures, or infected](orzid2-gmenu-abx-proced-for-infected-skin-skin-structures)

musculoskeletal tissues

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Up-To-Date Article: Antimicrobial prophylaxis for the prevention of bacterial

endocarditis

Wilson et al., Circulation, 2021, 143(20)e963-e978

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU PREV OF PERTUSSIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PREVENTION OF PERTUSSIS

# Immunization

Give a single dose of tetanus-diphtheria acellular pertussis vaccine (Tdap) in

adults regardless of interval between most recent Td vaccine. One dose of Tdap

vaccine is given to pregnant women during each pregnancy.

# Postexposure prophylaxis in adults

Household contacts with symptomatic coughing should be treated as if they have

pertussis. Consult Infectious Diseases for all suspected cases of pertussis and

exposure to pertussis.

CDC recommends postexposure prophylaxis in household contacts within 21 days

after exposure to pertussis regardless of immunization history. Non-household

contacts who are at high risk of severe illness or who have close contact with

high-risk individuals should receive post exposure prophylaxis within 21 days of

exposure. Those at high risk of severe illness are infants less than one year of

age, women in third trimester of pregnancy and those with preexisting health

conditions that may be exacerbated by pertussis (e.g. immunosuppressed and

asthmatic individuals).

A single dose of Tdap should be administered in those who are not up to date.

Preferred:

[Azithromycin 500mg po day 1, then 250mg q24h for days 2-5 O](orz-set-abx-azithromycin-po-500-250-once-q24h-x4days)

Alternative for macrolide intolerant or allergic patients:

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h R,DI for 7 days](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

# PREVENTION OF PROSTHETIC JOINT INFECTION BEFORE DENTAL PROCEDURES

Dental procedures are not associated with an increased risk of prosthetic joint

infection. The routine use of antimicrobial prophylaxis before dental procedures

in patients with prosthetic joints is not recommended. Good dental health should

be maintained in patients with prosthetic joints and dental infections should be

treated promptly.

For more information contact Infectious Diseases.

menus.Text:

PUBIC LICE (PEDICULOSIS PUBIS)

Lice are parasitic insects. Human lice survive by feeding on human blood.

To make a diagnosis, use a nit comb, bright light, or lens to find a louse

living in pubic hair.

The presence of nits on a hair shaft, especially when they are located more

than 6 mm from the skin, does NOT indicate active infestation.  Nits may remain

present for months after successful treatment.

Household contacts and persons who may have come into contact with personal

belongings of an infested individual should be examined for evidence of lice

and discarded or cleaned if contaminated.

# Treatment

A repeat application may be used if live lice are seen 7-10 days after

treatment.

[Permethrin 1% lotion. Apply to affected area for 10 minutes then comb out](psjzid-permethrin-1-lotion-to-affect-area-10min)

nits ($) [M]

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU RETINITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# RETINITIS AND ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS

Retinitis is a subset of uveitis, is rare in immunocompetent people: in these

individuals it is usually caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) or herpes

simplex virus (HSV). Retinitis is more common in immunocompromised patients and

cytomegalovirus being the most common pathogen in these patients. Other

retinitis pathogens include Toxoplasma gondii, Bartonella henselae, Histoplasma

capsulatum, and Treponema pallidum. In most cases, patients have other

neurological symptoms or signs.  Patients with candidemia may present with 1-3

mm white punctate retinal lesions called cotton-wool spots. These may only be

visible on fundus examination. Treatment of candidal retinitis  is systemic

antifungal therapy. Consult Ophthalmology, Infectious Diseases, or Neurology for

help.

VZV and HSV cause nearly all cases of acute retinal necrosis (ARN), with a small

number being caused by cytomegalovirus. ARN is a rapidly progressing retinitis

that occurs primarily in immunocompetent people and can cause vision loss.

Treatment with intravenous acyclovir or valacyclovir is essential to halt

progression of ARN.

Ophthalmology and Infectious Diseases consultation is essential

# Treatment of Non-viral Retinitis or ARN

Refer to specific pathogen treatment recommendations of the CDSS to treat

underlying infection

# Treatment of Retinitis or ARN due to CMV:

[Link to Treatment of CMV Retinitis and ARN](orzid2-gmenu-abx-cmv-retinitis)

# Treatment of VZV Retinitis

[Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/d for 5-7 days \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-800mg-po-5x-d)

< OR >

[Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h for 7 days \($$\) R](psjizid-acyclovir-10-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

Alternative

[Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q8h for 5 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q8h)

# Treatment of HSV Retinitis

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 7-10 days \($\) R](psjzid-acyclovir-400mg-q8h)

< OR >

[Acyclovir 5 mg/kg IV q8h \($$\) R](psjizid-acyclovir-5-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

Alternative

[Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q12h for 7-10 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q12h)

# Treatment of VZV and HSV Acute Retinal Necrosis

Ophthalmologist involvement is essential for treatment including

corticosteroids, vitrectomy, or laser therapy. Intravitreal foscarnet in

addition to a systemic antiviral may provide added therapeutic efficacy.

Duration

Treat with intravenous therapy for a minimum of 7 days until disease has

stabilized then treat with or therapy for a minimum of 6 weeks

Treatment

[Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h for 7 days \($\) R](psjizid-acyclovir-10-mg-kg-iv-q8h)

[< Optional add-on therapy > Foscarnet 2.4mg/0.1 mL intravitreal injection STAT](psjzid-foscarnet-2-4mg-intravitreous-inject-once)

($$$$) [R,O]

< THEN >

[Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q8h for 42 days \($\) R](psjzid-valacyclovir-1gm-po-q8h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

SCABIES

Scabies is an infestation of the skin by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei.

It is transmitted by skin to skin contact. Outbreaks occur in nursing

homes, day care centers, and residential institutions.  Scabies is highly

contagious and meticulous infection control is needed.

Treatment is a single application of permethrin cream.  Some experts recommend a

second application 7-10 days after the first application if the patient is still

symptomatic or if live mites are found at that time.  Contact Dermatology or

Infectious Diseases for more information.

Treat family members and other close contacts to prevent spread and recurrence.

# Treatment

Repeat application 7-10 days after the first application if patient is still

experiencing symptoms, or if lives mites are found.

[Permethrin 5% cream apply from head to feet, leave on for 8-14 hours, then](psjzid-permethrin-5-cream-apply-from-head-to-feet)

wash cream off with soap and water ($) [M]

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

# SEPSIS AND SEPTIC SHOCK

Per the Sepsis-3 task force, sepsis is defined as life-threatening organ

dysfunction caused by dysregulated host response to infection.

Septic shock is a subset of sepsis in which profound circulatory, cellular, and

metabolic abnormalities occur. Septic shock requires vasopressor therapy and is

associated with in-hospital mortality greater than 40%.

Early intervention is crucial to prevention of death from sepsis. Antimicrobials

active against likely pathogens, based on source infection, and supportive

treatment to maintain vascular perfusion should be initiated immediately (within

the first hour of patient presentation). Reassess antimicrobial therapy daily to

narrow therapeutic spectrum when culture and susceptibility data are available.

# Sepsis/septic shock management bundles based on patient location (includes

# empiric antimicrobial treatment)

[Intensive Care Unit \(ICU\)](orz-gmenu-medicine-inpt-sepsis-orders-landing-page-2024)

[Hospital ward](orz-gmenu-medicine-inpt-sepsis-orders-landing-page-2024)

[Emergency department \(ED\)](orz-gmenu-uc-ed-sepsis-2)

Utilize management bundles above for treatment in patients. The link below is

provided to view antimicrobial recommendations as a reference.

[Sepsis antimicrobial treatment recommendations](orzid2-gmenu-sepsis-protocol-antimicrobials)

# SEPSIS WITH INTRAABDOMINAL INFECTION OR UNCLEAR INFECTIOUS SOURCE

# Consult Infectious Diseases

Empirical regimens listed below have broad coverage of likely pathogens based on

infectious site. Resistant gram-negative rods and MRSA coverage is not necessary

in most patients except those with recent isolates of these organisms. Strongly

consider rapid de-escalation of therapy in the first 24-48 hours based on MRSA

nares, isolated pathogen(s), and patient response to therapy. Refer to pathogen

specific sections of the Antimicrobial CDSS for additional treatment

recommendations.

# Empirical Treatment

Preferred:

[Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6H](psjizid-pip-taz-4-5gm-iv-q6h-sepsis-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

Penicillin allergy:

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q8h-sepsis)

Severe beta-lactam reaction:

[Treatment of Sepsis with Severe Beta-Lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-sepsis-severe-beta-lactam-reaction)

# Recent MRSA isolate

[<ADD> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h to one of the above regimens](orz-set-abx-vanco-sepsis-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Clinically unstable (ICU level care/hypotensive/tachycardic) AND recent multi-

# drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate

[<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV x 1 dose to one of the above regimens](psjizid-tobramycin-5-mg-kg-iv-sepsis)

*If CrCl less than 50 ml/min: 2 mg/kg x 1 dose (use order above and modify dose)

Pharmacy to follow

# treated with any of the above antibiotics.

# The following regimen(s) should only be used if the patient has a history of a

# severe reaction to a Beta-Lactam antimicrobial including but not limited to:

Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN)

Anaphylaxis

Drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS)

Generalized exanthematous pustulosis

Hemolytic anemia

Immune hepatitis

Interstitial nephritis

Mucosal, cardiovascular, or respiratory system involvement

Reaction needed medical intervention

Skin desquamation

Stevens-Johnson syndrome (SJS)

Toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN)

# SEPSIS WITH SUSPECTED INTRAABDOMINAL INFECTION

Site:  Unless the specific site or etiologic agent is known with a high

level of probability strong consideration should be given:  1) To

empiric broad spectrum antibiotics for empiric first dose therapy in the

first 24 hours following presentation (Empirical Therapy Site Unknown)

and 2) Strongly consider ID consult.

# Preferred treatment

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SEPSIS WITH SUSPECTED MENINGITIS OR OTHER CNS INFECTION

Consider consulting Infectious Diseases if CNS infection is not strongly

suspected as the main source of infection.

Empirical regimens listed below have broad coverage of likely pathogens based on

infectious site. Resistant gram-negative rods and MRSA coverage is not necessary

in most patients except those with recent isolates of these organisms. Strongly

consider rapid de-escalation of therapy in the first 24-48 hours based on MRSA

nares, isolated pathogen(s), and patient response to therapy. Refer to pathogen

specific sections of the Antimicrobial CDSS for additional treatment

recommendations.

# Listeria is NOT suspected

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h](orz-set-abx-sepsis-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Listeria IS a concern (Adults >= 50 Years or With Alcoholism, Debilitating

# Disease, or Impaired Cellular Immunity)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h <AND> ampicillin 2 gm](orz-set-abx-sepsis-ceftriax-2gm-vanco-15mg-kg-ampicillin-2gm-iv)

IV q4h

# Ceftriaxone or penicillin allergy (see below for severe reactions)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h](orz-set-abx-sepsis-mero-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-q12h)

# Severe Beta-lactam reaction

[Moxifloxacin 400 mg IV q24h <AND> trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 5mg/kg \(TMP](orz-set-abx-sepsis-moxi-400mg-iv-tmp-smx-5mg-kg-iv-vanco)

component) IV Q6H <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SEVERE SINUSITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SEVERE SINUSITIS

Community-acquired bacterial sinusitis is most often due to Streptococcus

pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenza or Moraxella catarrhalis. Group A

Streptococci, Staphylococcus aureus and anaerobes are isolated less frequently.

For patients who present with severe symptoms (high fever (>/= 102 degrees

Fahrenheit, >/= 39 degrees Celsius) and purulent nasal discharge for 3-4

consecutive days or facial pain lasting for at least 3-4 consecutive days at the

beginning of illness), initiate empiric antimicrobials and obtain CT of sinuses

to determine the extent of infection. If the CT shows extension of sinusitis

infection into surrounding structures (i.e. the cranium or orbit) consult ENT

immediately. Closely monitor all patients who present with severe signs and

symptoms to ensure that signs and symptoms improve within 72 hours.

# Outpatient Treatment

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 7 days](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

Alternatives:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 7 days](psjzid-cefdinir-300mg-po-q12h)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID  \($\) DI for 7 days](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Treatment of hospitalized patient

Preferred:

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3gm IV q6h \($\) R for 7 days](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h \($\) M for 7 days](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q24h)

# Treatment failure

If symptoms worsen or no improvement is seen after 3-5 days of treatment,

broaden coverage, switch to different antimicrobial class and treat 10 days. If

symptoms continue to worsen or there is no improvement after 3-5 more days of

treatment, obtain CT to investigate non-infectious or suppurative causes. ENT

consultation is recommended. If sinuses are aspirated, specimens should be

cultured.

Preferred

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-3-375-gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

for 7 days

< OR >

[Cefepime 2 gm IV q12h \($$\) R for 7 days](psjizid-cefepime-2-gm-iv-q12h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Chow et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2012, 54(8) e72-e112

Mandell chapter: Sinusitis

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SPINAL EPIDURAL ABSCESS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SPINAL EPIDURAL ABSCESS

Most cases are associated with Staphylococcus aureus. Others are associated with

Gram-negative bacilli and streptococci. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more

effective than vancomycin against susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus

is isolated, once methicillin-resistance is ruled out, switch to an anti-

staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen in

post-surgical patients or patients with known Pseudomonas colonization.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 4 to 8 weeks. Shorter durations may be used in patients who have

undergone surgical drainage and who have responded well to therapy.

# Empiric Treatment

Preferred if Pseudomonas is not suspected:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-2gm-q12h-and-vanco-15mg-kg-q12h)

Preferred if Pseudomonas is suspected:

[Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h \($$\) R  < AND > vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-cefepime-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Treatment if methicillin-sensitive S. aureus is isolated

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R,DI](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

< OR >

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

SPOROTRICHOSIS

Sporotrichosis occurs most often in people who have had significant outdoor

exposure to soil.  In immunocompetent people, disease is usually limited to the

skin.  In people with decreased host defenses (eg, HIV/AIDS, alcoholism,

diabetes mellitus, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) sporotrichosis

often disseminates to bones, joints, or lungs.  Consult Infectious Diseases or

Dermatology

# ____________________________________________________________________________

# Cutaneous infection in a patient without HIV infection

# ____________________________________________________________________________

resolved, usually for a total of 3-6 months ($) [DI]

# Alternative

Consult Dermatology or Infectious Diseases.

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SSTI PURULENT INFECTIONS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# PURULENT SKIN/SOFT TISSUE INFECTIONS

Includes furuncles/boils, carbuncles and cutaneous abscesses with or without

surrounding inflammation. The predominant pathogen is Staphylococcus aureus

(MSSA or MRSA).

Incision and drainage are recommended whenever feasible. Adjunctive antibiotics

are typically recommended. Incision and drainage alone are reasonable based on

patient preferences when abscess is smaller, limited surrounding inflammation,

no systemic signs of infections, and/or limited comorbidities.

# For recurrent skin abscesses in addition to culture and antibiotic therapy

# recommend considering a decolonization regimen.

[Click Here for Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization](orzid2-gmenu-abx-staphylococcus-aureus-decolonization)

# Preferred oral therapy:

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet BID for 5 days R,DI](psjzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tab-bid)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 5 days DI](psjzid-doxycycline-100mg-po-q12h)

# Preferred IV therapy:

[Vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q 12 hours R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Alternative:

Reserve for contraindication, precaution, failure to preferred options, or for

patient where parenteral antibiotics would be otherwise be selected.

[Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 5 days DI,O](psjzid-linezolid-600mg-po-q12h)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU STAPH SCALDED SYNDROME
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

STAPHYLOCOCCAL SCALDED SKIN SYNDROME (RITTER'S DISEASE)

Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) presents with severe skin

blistering and exfoliation resulting from toxins produced by Staphylococcus

aureus.  SSSS is usually found in children and rarely in older adults.  Obtain

a skin biopsy to differentiate between SSSS and toxic epidermal necrolysis.

Initiate anti-staphylococcal therapy and obtain cultures and susceptibilities.

Empiric therapy active against both MRSA and MSSA until results available.

If cultures reveal methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), change

to nafcillin or cefazolin for better antimicrobial activity.

# Empirical treatment

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Treatment if MSSA is isolated

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) DI](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

< OR >

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Up-to-date website

Sanford keyword: Staph. Scalded skin syndrome

Mandell chapter: The acutely ill patient with fever and rash

Stevens DL Clin Infect Dis 2014, 59: 147

Patel GK Am J Clin Dermatol 2003, 4:165

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU STAPH TOXIC SHOCK SYNDROME
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

CDC CRITERIA FOR DIAGNOSIS OF STAPHYLOCOCCAL TOXIC SHOCK SYNDROME

These criteria were developed for epidemiological purposes.  Treat cases when

fewer criteria are met if staphylococcal TSS seems likely.

Definite:  All 6 of the following criteria are met.

Probable:  Five of the 6 criteria are met.

# Fever

T >38.9 degree Celsius (102.0 degree Fahrenheit)

# Hypotension

Systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg, orthostatic drop in diastolic 15 mmHg,

orthostatic syncope or dizziness

# Rash

Diffuse macular erythroderma

# Desquamation

Occurs 1 to 2 weeks after onset of illness and usually involving palms and

soles

# Multisystem involvement (3 or more of the following organ systems)

# GI

Vomiting or diarrhea at onset of illness

# Muscular

Severe myalgia or CPK elevation >2 times the normal upper limit

# Mucous membranes

Vaginal, oropharyngeal, or conjunctival hyperemia

# Renal

BUN or serum creatinine >2 times the normal upper limit, or pyuria (>5

WBC/hpf)

# Hepatic

Bilirubin or transaminases >2 times the normal upper limit

# Hematologic

Platelets <100,000/microLiter

# Central nervous system

Disorientation or alterations in consciousness without focal neurologic

signs in the absence of fever and hypotension

# Negative results on the following tests, if obtained

Blood, throat, or cerebrospinal fluid cultures for another pathogen (blood

cultures may be positive for S. aureus).

Serologic tests for Rocky Mountain spotted fever, leptospirosis, or measles

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

MMWR 1990, 39(RR-13):1

DeVries AS PLoS One 2011, 6(8):e22997

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU STREP TOXIC SHOCK SYNDROME
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

CRITERIA FOR DIAGNOSIS OF STREPTOCOCCAL TOXIC SHOCK SYNDROME

These criteria were developed for epidemiological purposes.  Treat cases when

fewer criteria are met if streptococcal TSS seems likely.

1.)  Isolation of Group A Streptococcus from a normally sterile site (eg, blood

cerebrospinal, pleural, or peritoneal fluid, tissue biopsy, or surgical wound)

< AND >

2.)  Hypotension (systolic blood pressure 90 mm Hg in adults

< AND >

# 3.)  Two or more of the following:

# Renal impairment

(creatinine in adults, 2 mg/dL, in children, two-times upper limit of normal

for age, in patients with pre-existing renal disease two-fold elevation over

baseline)

# Coagulopathy

(eg, thrombocytopenia, disseminated intravascular coagulation)

# Liver involvement

(eg, two-times upper limit of normal for age of transaminases or bilirubin, in

patients with pre-existing liver disease two-fold elevation over baseline)

# Adult respiratory distress syndrome

# Erythematous macular rash

may desquamate

Soft tissue necrosis (eg, necrotizing fasciitis, myositis, or gangrene)

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Working Group on Severe Streptococcal Infections JAMA 1993, 269:390

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SUBDURAL EMPYEMA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SUBDURAL EMPYEMA

Most cases (60-90%) result from extension of sinusitis or otitis media

(contiguous sources). Surgical drainage is necessary. Obtain material for

culture. For patients with severe penicillin allergy consult Infectious

Diseases.

# Consult Neurosurgery, Neurology, and Infectious Disease

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 4-6 weeks

# Empiric Treatment for Infection from Contiguous Source

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-ceftriax-2gm-iv-q12h-metro-500mg-iv-q8h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O](psjizid-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h)

# Empiric Treatment for Unknown Source, History of MRSA Infection or Colonization

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-metro-500mg-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O  <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SUPP INTRACRANIAL THROMBOPH
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# SUPPURATIVE INTRACRANIAL THROMBOPHLEBITIS

Adjust therapy from empirical regimens listed below after consultation with

Infectious Disease or Neurosurgery services. Beta-lactam antibiotics are more

effective than vancomycin against susceptible Staphylococci. If Staphylococcus

is isolated, once methicillin-resistance is ruled out, switch to an anti-

staphylococcal beta-lactam antibiotic. Pseudomonas is a potential pathogen in

post-surgical patients or patients with known pseudomonas colonization.

Consult Infectious Disease and Neurosurgery.

# Duration of Therapy

Treat for 3 to 6 weeks.

# Empiric Treatment

Preferred if Pseudomonas is not suspected:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h](orz-set-abx-ceftr-2gm-metro-500mg-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

($) [DI] <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Preferred if Pseudomonas is suspected:

[Cefepime 2gm IV Q8h \($$\) R <AND> metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h \($\) DI](orz-set-abx-cefe2gmivq8h-metro500mgivq8h-vanco15mg-kgivq12hstat)

<AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h ($) [R]

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O  <AND> vancomycin 15mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

# Treatment if Methicillin-Sensitive S. Aureus is Isolated

[Nafcillin 2 gm IV q4h \($$\) R,DI](psjizid-nafcillin-2gm-iv-q4h)

< OR >

[Cefazolin 2 gm IV q8h \($\) R](psjizid-cefazolin-2gm-ivpb-q8h)

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SUPP ODONTOGENIC INFECT
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

# DENTAL INFECTIONS

Surgical drainage, scaling and antimicrobial treatment are essential. All

patients should be referred to the dental service for assessment and direction

of treatment. Empirical coverage for likely pathogens (streptococci,

Peptostreptococcus, Finegoldia, Bacteriodes and other oral anaerobes) is

required.

# Consult Dental Service

# Preferred:

[Amoxicillin 500 mg PO q8h for 5 days \($\) R](psjzid-amoxicillin-500mg-po-q8h)

< OR >

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO q12h for 5 days \($\) R](psjzid-amox-clav-875-125mg-po-q12h)

# Primary alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h \($\) R for 5 days](psjzid-cefdinir-300mg-po-q12h)

# Secondary alternative, after assessment of beta-lactam reaction above:

[Azithromycin 500mg po day 1, then 250mg q24h for days 2-5 \($\)O](orz-set-abx-azithromycin-po-500-250-once-q24h-x4days)

_______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SURG 48HRS AFTER PROC
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

PATIENTS WITH SIGNS OF INFECTION MORE THAN 48 HOURS AFTER PROCEDURE

Most post-operative infections appear at least 4 days after the operation.  If

the wound appears normal to examination surgical site infection is unlikely.

Seek other source of fever.  Consider opening wounds that show induration or

erythema.  Obtain material for gram stain and culture whenever possible.

Determine whether the patient has signs of invasive or systemic infection like

erythema (diameter greater than 5 centimeters), temperature greater than 38.5

degrees Celsius (101.3 degrees Fahrenheit) or heart rate higher than 100 beats

per minute.

If there are no signs of invasive or systemic infection systemic antimicrobials

are unnecessary.  Dressing changes alone are indicated.

# For wounds that require complicated care

[Wound care \(ET\) nurse consult](gmrctz-wocn-ostomy-inpt)

If there are signs of invasive or systemic infection obtain blood cultures and

wound Gram stain and cultures.  Whenever possible select antimicrobial therapy

based on the Gram stain.  When the Gram stain cannot provide guidance give

empirical therapy as indicated:

# Empirical treatment of INFECTED WOUNDS AFTER CLEAN SURGERY or wounds on the

# trunk, head, neck, arms or legs

Vancomycin should be included in the initial regimen due to the prevalence of

methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.  However beta-lactam antibiotics

are more effective for susceptible bacteria than is vancomycin.  If methicillin-

susceptible S. aureus is identified switch to an anti-staphylococcal beta-lactam

antibiotic.

[Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h \($\) R](orz-set-abx-vanco-new-start-15mg-kg-q12h-mrsa-nares-screening)

# Preferred empirical treatment for INFECTED WOUNDS AFTER CLEAN-CONTAMINATED or

# CONTAMINATED SURGERY

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h \($$\) R < OR >](psjizid-ampicillin-sulbactam-3gm-iv-q6h)

[Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h \($\) R,DI <AND> Clindamycin 600 mg IV](orz-set-abx-ciprofl-400-mg-iv-q12h-clinda-600mg-iv-q8h)

q8h ($$) [H]

[Piperacillin-tazobactam 3.375 gm IV q6h \($$\) R](psjizid-pip-taz-3-375-gm-iv-q6h-ne-extinf-ci-cefep-metro)

# Alternative if methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus is suspected

[Ampicillin-sulbactam 3 gm IV q6h \($$\) R <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg](orz-set-abx-ampi-sulb-3gm-iv-q6h-vanco-15mg-kg-iv-q12h)

IV q12h ($) [R] < OR >

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

BILIARY SURGERY

Surgical prophylaxis is indicated for open procedures and high risk

laparoscopic procedures.  Additional doses should not be given after

incisions are closed. Surgical prophylaxis is not indicated in elective

low risk laparoscopic procedures.

The risk of infectious complications after laparoscopic cholecystectomy is

increased after emergent procedures, procedures lasting more than 120 minutes,

intraoperative gall bladder rupture or bile spillage, conversion from

laparoscopic to open cholecystectomy, and insertion of a prosthetic device.

The risk is increased in patients who have had an episode of colic or a

biliary procedure within 30 days before the procedure, patients with acute

cholecystitis or jaundice, patients with a nonfunctional gallbladder, patients

with immunosuppression, pregnancy, diabetes, age greater than 70 years, or

American Society of Anesthesiologists classification of 3 or greater.

If one of these risk factors exists, prophylaxis is indicated for laparoscopic

cholecystectomy.  If there is a substantial likelihood that one of these risk

factors will develop during a procedure, the surgeon may elect to order

prophylaxis.

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

CARDIAC SURGERY

[Click here to go to CIED Surgery Prophylaxis](orzid2-gmenu-surg-cied-preop)

[Click here to go to CV \(open heart\) Surgery Prophylaxis](orzid2-gmenu-abx-meds-delayed-pre-op-antibiotics-cv-surgery2)

Antimicrobial prophylaxis is not indicated before cardiac catheterization

with or without stent placement or for transesophageal echocardiogram.

For patients undergoing cardiac procedures the recommended regimen is a

single pre-incision dose of antibiotic with additional doses

while incisions are open for long procedures.

Prophylaxis should not be continued beyond 24 hours

even if drains or intravenous catheters remain in place.

Cefazolin is preferred for prophylaxis, as it is more active than vancomycin

against methicillin-susceptible staphylococci.  Vancomycin should

be used when methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus infection is likely.

Consult Cardiothoracic Surgery or Infectious Diseases for more information.

Place post-op IV antimicrobial prophylaxis orders after admission to ward.

Duration of antimicrobial prophylaxis should not exceed 24 hours. Durations

longer than 24 hours have not been shown effective in preventing cardiothoracic

surgical site infections. There is no benefit to continuing antimicrobial

prophylaxis until all indwelling drains and intravascular catheters are removed.

[CIED Surgery Postoperative Prophylaxis](orzid2-gmenu-surg-vascular-surg-postop)

Antimicrobials are not indicated in the absence of obstruction or intervention.

If obstruction is present or intervention is likely antimicrobial prophylaxis

menus.Name: ORZID2 GMENU SURG NEUROSURGERY
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

NEUROSURGERY

Risk factors for postoperative infections following neurologic procedures

include diabetes, procedure duration longer than two to four hours, placement

of a foreign body, repeat surgery, emergency surgery, cerebrospinal fluid

(CSF) leak, postoperative intracranial pressure monitoring or presence of a

ventricular drain for more than five days postoperatively, and concurrent or

prior infection of an incision or shunt.

In spinal surgery, the infection rate after conventional lumbar discectomy is

low, but due to the severe consequences of postoperative infection at this site

antimicrobial prophylaxis is recommended. Infection rates are higher after

prolonged spinal surgery or spinal procedures involving fusion or insertion of

foreign material, and antimicrobial prophylaxis is also recommended.

Antimicrobial prophylaxis is warranted for patients undergoing clean craniotomy

CSF shunt procedures, or intrathecal pump placement.

For all other neurosurgical procedures, antimicrobial prophylaxis is not

indicated.

Cefazolin is preferred for most patients as it penetrates into the cerebrospinal

fluid and is more active than vancomycin against susceptible staphylococci.

Vancomycin should be used when the patient is colonized or has been recently

infected with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus.  Consult Neurosurgery

or Infectious Diseases for more information.

# If no antimicrobial prophylaxis recommended, select below:

[Click here No antimicrobial prophylaxis recommended for procedure](orz-gtx-abx-pre-op-url-nurse-generic-order)

[Cefazolin Weight Based Dosing Preop R](orzid2-gmenu-surg-cefazolin-weight-based-dosing)

[Click here Beta-lactam allergy assessment](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Vancomycin 15mg/kg Weight Based Dosing Preop R](orzid2-gmenu-surg-vancomycin-weight-based-dosing)

References

Bratzler DW, et al.  Clinical practice guidelines for antimicrobial prophy

in surgery, Am J Health-Syst Pharm. 2013 Vol 70 page 195-283

Letter 2012 Vol 10 pages 73-77

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Inpt\)](orzid2-gmenu-abx-general-information-inpatient)

OPHTHALMIC SURGERY

When indicated, ophthalmology will order antimicrobial prophylaxis before

procedures.

# Cataract Surgery

Intracameral moxifloxacin is recommended for use to reduce the risk of

post-operative endophthalmitis after cataract surgery only in those patients

at highest risk of infection, including the following:

* Patients with prior intravitreal injections

* Immunosuppressed patients

* Patients with significant ocular surface eyelid disease

* Complication occurs during surgery (i.e. capusle rupture, vitreous loss)

* Other possible high risk situations as they arise but not listed above

# Preferred:

[Moxifloxacin 500mcg/0.5ml Eye Inj Intracameral Cataract \(Conc.=100mcg/0.1ml\)](psjizid-moxifloxacin-vigamox-eye-drops-cataract-surgery)

# References:

Arshinoff S., J Cataract Refract Surg, (2016) 42:1730-1741
