menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU MASTOIDITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# MASTOIDITIS

# Acute Mastoiditis

Acute mastoiditis most commonly occurs as a suppurative complication of acute

otitis media. Diagnosis is supported by CT or MRI imaging and culture of

drainage. Antibiotics and drainage of middle ear are sufficient treatment in

most cases. Mastoidectomy is necessary if abscess has formed in the mastoid

bone. If complication of first episode of acute otitis media, etiologies

typically include Streptococcus pneumonia (most common), Streptococcus pyogenes,

or Staphylococcus aureus. If secondary to chronic otitis media, etiologies

typically include Staphylococcus aureus or Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Patients

usually too ill for outpatient therapy. ENT consultation recommended. Obtain

cultures of auditory canal or middle ear fluid (preferred).

# Empirical treatment of uncomplicated disease

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

# Empirical Treatment of complicated disease

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

# Step down treatment after initial intravenous antibiotic treatment in patients

# who can tolerate oral therapy. Base selection on culture results. Adjust for a

# total duration of 3 weeks of antimicrobial therapy.

[Amoxicillin/clavulanate 875-125 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) R](psozid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-amox-clav-875-125mg-7ds-po-bid)

< OR >

[Cefuroxime 500 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) R](psozid2-cefuroxime-500mg-po-bid-7ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefuroxime-500mg-po-bid-7ds)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) DI](psozid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-7ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-7ds)

# __________________________________________________________________

# Chronic Mastoiditis

Chronic mastoiditis is usually the result of chronic otitis media with

perforation of the tympanic membrane. There is often associated formation of a

cholesteatoma (keratoma). Diagnosis is supported by CT or MRI imaging and

culture of drainage. Long term treatment with topical antimicrobials is first

line therapy. Infection is often polymicrobial, including Staphylococcus aureus,

Pseudomonas aeruginosa and anaerobes. Treatment should be managed in

collaboration with otolaryngology and includes topical antimicrobials, care of

external auditory canal, and is some cases mastoidectomy. If possible, withhold

therapy until a pathogen is identified by culture of drainage to direct therapy.

Specific drug choice dictated by culture results.

Empirical Treatment

Preferred:

[Ciprofloxacin-Dexamethasone otic 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) BID for 4 weeks \($\)](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-bid-28-days)

[M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-bid-28-days)

Alternative:

[Neomycin-polymyxin-hydrocortisone ear drops 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) QID for 4](psozid2-neomycin-polymyxin-hydroc-ear-4-drps-qid-28-days)

weeks ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-neomycin-polymyxin-hydroc-ear-4-drps-qid-28-days)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Mandell chapter: Otitis Externa, Otitis Media, and Mastoiditis

Loh et. al., The Journal of Laryngology & Otology. 2018, 132(2)96-104.

Sanford keyword: Mastoiditis

Up-to-Date article: Chronic otitis media, cholesteatoma, and mastoiditis in

adults

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU MORE ABOUT PHARYNGITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# MORE ABOUT PHARYNGITIS/ TONSILLITIS AND THE MODIFIED CENTOR SCORE

As most cases are of viral origin, antimicrobials are not indicated in these

cases. Warm saltwater gargle rinses and throat lozenges provide temporary relief

of throat pain. Five to 10% of cases are caused by group A Streptococcus.

Antimicrobial treatment reduces symptoms by one day, prevents suppurative

complications and prevents acute rheumatic fever, an uncommon disease in US

adults.

Streptococcal pharyngitis or tonsillitis should be suspected when patients have

fever and exudate on the pharyngeal wall or tonsils without symptoms like cough,

nasal congestion, or runny nose that suggest viral infection or common cold. If

streptococcal pharyngitis is suspected in adults, perform PCR testing for group

A streptococci and treat only if positive.

Neisseria gonorrhoeae is a rare cause of pharyngitis. N. gonorrhoeae should be

considered for patients with risk factors for sexually transmitted diseases. N.

gonorrhoeae infections must be reported to the state health department and this

will be done by Infection Control if the culture is positive.

# The Modified Centor score

Used to estimate the likelihood that a patient with sore throat has

streptococcal pharyngitis and whether rapid PCR testing should be performed.

1) Absence of cough = 1 point

2) Swollen and tender anterior cervical nodes = 1 point

3) Temperature greater than 100.4 degrees Fahrenheit (38 degrees Centigrade) = 1

point

4) Tonsillar exudates or swelling = 1 point

5) Age: 3-14 years = 1 point

15-44 years = 0 points

45 years and older = -1 point

Patients with a score of 0 or 1 are at very low risk. PCR testing and antibiotic

treatment are not indicated. Patients with a score of 2 to 4 are at moderate to

high risk. PCR testing should be obtained in these patients to determine if GAS

is present. In patients with a score of 4 or greater, consider empiric

antibiotic treatment.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

CDC STD 2015 Guidelines MMWR. 2015, 64(3)1-7

Choby, Am Fam Physician. 2009 79(5) 383-390

Mandell chapter: Pharyngitis

Sanford keyword: Streptococcal Pharyngitis

Stanford et al, Clinical Infectious Diseases. 2012, cis629

# PREVENTION OF INFECTION IN PATIENTS WITH NASAL PACKING

Antimicrobial prophylaxis to prevent infection and toxic shock syndrome in

patients with nasal packing is not recommended. Antibiotics increase the risk of

adverse events in patients with nasal packing with no proven effectiveness in

preventing infection.

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU NEUTROPENIC FEVER
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

NEUTROPENIC FEVER

The risk of severe, rapidly progressive infections increases when the absolute

neutrophil count (ANC, segmented neutrophils plus bands) is less than 500

cells/microliter.  The risk increases dramatically when the ANC is <100

cells/microliter.  Because of these risks, patients with fever and neutropenia

to this degree should receive empirical antimicrobial therapy immediately.

Empirical therapy should also be given to patients with fever and ANC 500-1000

cells/microliter when the concentration is expected to be <500 cells/microliter

within the next 48 hours.  For this purpose, fever is defined as a single

temperature greater than 38.3 degrees Celsius.

# Initial therapy

Since infection can be rapidly progressive and severe, broad-spectrum

antimicrobials are given urgently to patients with neutropenic fever as defined

above.  Vancomycin should only be given when there are clear indications for its

use.

Candidates for empirical treatment with oral antimicrobials include those who

are febrile but who have no evidence of focal infection or signs or symptoms of

severe disease, like hypotension.  Outpatient antimicrobials for neutropenic

fever must be ordered only in consultation with Hematology-Oncology or

Infectious Diseases.

# Treatment

[If patient IS a candidate for oral therapy](orzid3-gmenu-neut-cand-oral-therapy)

[If patient is NOT a candidate for oral therapy](orzid3-gmenu-neut-not-cand-oral-therapy)

[Link to a scoring tool that identifies low risk patients for oral therapy](orzid2-gmenu-neut-fever-scoring-tool)

# Modifcation to therapy

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

[References](orzid2-gmenu-abx-references)

Hughes WT Clin Infect Dis 2002, 34: 730

Rolston KVI Clin Infect Dis 2004, 39: S44

Sipsas NV Cancer 2005, 103: 1103

# NOSOCOMIAL SINUSITIS

Nasogastric tubes increase the risk of bacterial sinus infection associated with

Staphylococcus aureus, streptococcus, and gram-negative bacilli, including

Pseudomonas aeruginosa. Aspirate sinuses for gram stain and culture to direct

antimicrobial therapy. Adequate sinus drainage is vital to treatment.

# Empirical antimicrobial treatment

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# OROLABIAL HERPES

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompetent patients

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Antiviral therapy is not beneficial after formation of vesicles. However, when

started as soon as prodromal symptoms of burning or tingling occur, antivirals

reduce duration of pain and lesions.

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO TID for 5 days \($\) R](psozid2-acyclovir-5ds-400mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-acyclovir-400mg-po-5x-d-5ds)

Alternative

[Valacyclovir 2 gm BID for 1 day \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-1day-2gm-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-1day-2gm-po-bid)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Immunocompromised patients

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Immunocompromised patients in whom herpes simplex infections can be more severe

include: patients with HIV infection, organ transplant recipients, patients

undergoing chemotherapy, malnourished patients, and those with compromised skin

integrity.

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO TID for 7-14 days\($\) R](psozid2-acyclovir-7days-400mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-acyclovir-400mg-po-5x-day-7ds)

< OR >

[Valacyclovir 1 gm BID for 7-14 days \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1gm-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1gm-po-bid)

# Treatment for severe disease

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Chronic suppressive therapy

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Indicated for patients with greater than 6 recurrences or severe recurrences,

immunocompromised patients or as adjunct to prevent transmission. Suppressive

therapy is optional, and some patients may find episodic treatment more

convenient. Patients should be reassessed every few years to evaluate if chronic

suppressive therapy is still necessary.

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO BID \($\) R](psozid2-acyclovir-1yr-400mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-acyclovir-1yr-400mg-po-bid)

< OR >

[Valacyclovir 500 mg PO QDay \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-1yr-500mg-po-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-1yr-500mg-po-qday)

# EMPIRICAL THERAPY FOR OSTEOMYELITIS

# Recommend Infectious Disease consultation.

Bone culture is essential and diagnostic. If patient is not clinically ill and a

diagnostic procedure is planned, antibiotics can be held until after the

procedure.

Therapy should be modified when culture results and patient response to therapy

are known.

Duration of treatment is 4 to 6 weeks.

# Empiric Therapy

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

# Oral switch recommendations based on culture results

Treatment for MSSA and streptococci:

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO q12h R](psozid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-28ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid-28days)

Treatment for MRSA:

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h DI](psozid2-doxycycline-28ds-100mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-28ds-100mg-po-bid)

# OSTEOMYELITIS

Obtain material for gram-stain and culture before initiating antimicrobials.

Blood and bone cultures are ideal.

Antibiotics should be held if patient does not have adjacent skin/soft tissue

infection

Duration of treatment and route will vary with differences in location of

infection, infecting organism, and host comorbidities.

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU OSTEOMYELITIS EVALUATION
menus.Text:
# Osteomyelitis Evaluation:

-Consider osteomyelitis in any infected, deep, or large foot ulcer, particularly

those that are chronic and over bony prominences.

-Plain films along with the probe-to-bone test are reasonable first steps

in evaluating for osteomyelitis.

-Patients where the diagnosis remains unclear should undergo MRI.

-Patients with findings suggesitve of osteomyelitis should undergo debridement

with bone culture BEFORE antibiotics are started, if possible

-Consult surgery (orthopedics or vascular) for potential surgical

intervention. (Vascular preferred for known PVD)

-Consult Infectious Diseases for evaluation and management of long-term

antibiotics.

[<Click here> Osteomyelitis](orzid3-gmenu-osteomyelitis)

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU OTITIS EXTERNA
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# OTITIS EXTERNA

# Acute Localized Disease

Often due to furunculosis and usually associated with Staphylococcus aureus.

Treat mild cases with moist local heat. For cases with cellulitis or deep

invasion, incision and drainage as well as systemic antibiotics may be needed.

Refer to the Furuncles and Carbuncles page for antibiotic recommendations.

[Furuncles and Carbuncles](orzid3-gmenu-furuncles-and-carbuncles)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Acute diffuse and chronic otitis externa

Most commonly associated with Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Staphylococcus aureus and

Staphylococcus epidermidis. Irrigate to remove cerumen, desquamated skin and

purulent material which can improve effectiveness of topical antibiotics. Avoid

products that contain neomycin if the tympanic membrane is perforated.

# Preferred treatment if tympanic membrane is intact

[Neomycin-polymyxin-hydrocortisone ear drops 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) QID](psozid2-neomycin-polymyxin-hydroc-ear-4-drps-qid-7days)

for 7 days ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-neomycin-polymyxin-hydroc-ear-4-drps-qid-7days)

# Alternative if tympanic membrane is perforated or allergy to preferred treatmen

[Ciprofloxacin-Dexamethasone otic 4 drops in affected ear\(s\) BID for 7 days \($\)](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-bid-7days)

[M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-dexamethasone-otic-bid-7days)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Complicated Cases

For cases resistant to topical therapy alone, patients with poorly controlled

diabetes mellitus, immunocompromised patients, cases where infection has spread

beyond ear canal and in those where topical therapy cannot be delivered

effectively. Culture secretions to guide therapy.

In addition to topical therapy above

[< ADD > ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h for 7 days \($\) R,DI](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-bid)

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PANCREATITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PANCREATITIS

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid3-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Antimicrobials are not indicated for uncomplicated pancreatitis.

In cases of necrotizing pancreatitis without infection, antimicrobial

prophylaxis does not improve patient outcomes. Antimicrobials increase the risk

of fungal superinfection and should not be used.

Antimicrobials are indicated for cases with pancreatic abscess, infected

pancreatic pseudocyst, or infected necrotic pancreas (phlegmon). The diagnosis

of infection can be difficult and may require aspiration. Consultation with

Gastroenterology and/or Infectious Diseases is encouraged.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Uncomplicated pancreatitis

No antimicrobials are indicated.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Pancreatic abscess, infected pancreatic pseudocyst, or infected necrotic

# pancreas (phlegmon)

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Total duration of antimicrobial therapy is typically 2 to 4 weeks

# Treatment

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Mandell chapter: Pancreatic Infection

Sanford Guide article: Pancreatitis

Solomkin et al, Clin Infect Dis, 2010, 50:133-64

Up-to-Date article: Management of acute pancreatitis

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# BABESIA SPECIES

Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat for 7-10 days. If patient has persistent relapsing disease, treat for 6

weeks including 2 weeks after babesia are no longer detected in blood smear.

# Treatment of mild to moderate disease

[Azithromycin 500 mg PO once \($\) on day 1, then 250 mg PO QDay \($\) M for 6](orz-set-abx-op-azith-500-then-250-x6ds-atova-750mg-q12h-7ds)

days <AND> atovaquone 750 mg PO BID ($) [M] for 7 days

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-azith-500-then-250-x6ds-atova-750mg-q12h-7ds)

Alternative

*Consult Infectious Diseases, requires NF consult for quinine.

Clindamycin 600 mg PO TID <AND> quinine 650mg PO TID

# Treatment of severe disease

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

References:

Mandell chapter: Babesia Species

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PARASITE TOXOPLASMA SPP.
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# TOXOPLASMA SPP.

If patient is immunocompetent and not pregnant, treatment is usually not needed

as disease is usually self-limited. Patients who are immunocompromised, pregnant

or have severe disease should be treated. Consult Infectious Diseases in all

cases.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Non-pregnant patients

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treat immunocompetent patients for 2-4 weeks. Treat immunocompromised patients

for 6 weeks or longer if radiologic disease is extensive or response is

incomplete at 6 weeks.

# Preferred treatment

Patients weighing <60 kg

[Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once \($$$\), then 50 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND>](orz-set-abx-op-pyrimeth-200-then-50-sulfadia-1gm-leucorv-10mg)

sulfadiazine 1 gm PO QID ($$) [DI,O] <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO QDay($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrimeth-200-then-50-sulfadia-1gm-leucorv-10mg)

Patients weighing >60kg

[Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once \($$$\), then 75 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND>](orz-set-abx-op-pyrim-200mg-then-75mg-sulfadia-1-5gm-leuc-25mg)

sulfadiazine 1.5 gm PO QID ($$) [DI,O] <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO QDay($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrim-200mg-then-75mg-sulfadia-1-5gm-leuc-25mg)

# Preferred alternative for sulfa allergy

Patients weighing <60 kg

[Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once \($$$\), then 50 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND>](orz-set-abx-op-pyrimeth-200-then-50-clinda-600-leucov-10mg)

clindamycin 600 mg PO QID ($) [H,O] <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO QDay ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrimeth-200-then-50-clinda-600-leucov-10mg)

Patients weighing >60 kg

[Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO once \($$$\), then 75 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND>](orz-set-abx-op-pyrim-200mg-then-75mg-clinda-600mg-leuc-25mg)

clindamycin 600 mg PO QID ($) [H,O] <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO QDay ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrim-200mg-then-75mg-clinda-600mg-leuc-25mg)

# Secondary alternatives

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for IV options

< OR >

[Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg-sulfamethoxazole 25 mg/kg PO BID \($\) R,DI](psozid-trimeth-5mg-kg-sulfa-25mg-kg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-trimeth-5mg-kg-sulfa-25mg-kg-po-bid)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Chronic Maintenance therapy for immunocompromised patients

# _______________________________________________________________________________

Discontinue maintenance therapy if patient has remained asymptomatic and CD4 >

200 cells per microliter.

# Maintenance therapy

[Pyrimethamine 50 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND> sulfadiazine 0.5-1 gm PO QID](orz-set-abx-op-pyrim-50mg-sulfadiaz-500mg-leuco-10mg)

($$) <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO QDay ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrim-50mg-sulfadiaz-500mg-leuco-10mg)

# Preferred alternative for sulfa allergy

[Pyrimethamine 50 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND> clindamycin 600 mg PO TID \($\)](orz-set-abx-op-pyrim-50mg-clinda-600mg-leuco-10mg)

[H,O] <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO QDay ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrim-50mg-clinda-600mg-leuco-10mg)

# Secondary alternatives

[Pyrimethamine 25 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND> atovaquone 750-1500 mg PO](orz-set-abx-op-pyrim-25mg-atova-750mg-leuco-10mg)

BID ($) [M] <AND> leucovorin 10-25 mg PO QDay ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrim-25mg-atova-750mg-leuco-10mg)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim sulfamethoxazole 1DS tablet PO QDay \($\) R,DI](psozid-triemth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-triemth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-qday)

< OR >

[Atovaquone 750-1500 mg PO BID \($\) M](psozid-atovaquone-susp-750mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-atovaquone-susp-750mg-po-bid)

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Pregnant patients

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Patient diagnosed <16-18 weeks of gestation

*Contact Infectious Diseases, non-formulary consult is required for spiramycin

Spiramycin 1 gm po TID until week 18 of gestation

# Patient diagnosed >16-18 weeks of gestation

[Pyrimethamine 50 mg BID for 2 days, then 50 mg PO QDay \($$\) DI,O <AND>](orz-set-abx-op-pyrimethamine-sulfadiazine-leucovorin-pregnancy)

sulfadiazine 75mg/kg once, then 50mg/kg BID ($$) [DI,O] <AND> leucovorin 10-25

mg PO QDay ($) [M] for 4 weeks or duration of pregnancy if ultrasound evidence

of fetal distress

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-pyrimethamine-sulfadiazine-leucovorin-pregnancy)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

PARONYCHIA

Cutaneous infection of the hand, cuticle or fingers usually occurring near

around the nail.

Treatment depends on etiology.  Candida spp. are commonly involved when the

patient has extensive exposure to water (e.g. dishwashers).  Staphylococcus

aureus is more commonly after manicures or nail biting.  Herpes simplex

(whitlow) usually follows exposure to oral mucosa (e.g. wrestlers, dentists, or

anesthetists).

# ________________________________________________________

# Treatment for paronychia associated with Candida

# ________________________________________________________

Treat for 14 days

[Clotrimazole 1% apply to affected area once daily \($\) M](psozid2-clotrim-1-crm-top-qday-14days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-clotrim-1-crm-top-qday-14days)

# Alternative

[Nystatin Cream to affected area BID \($\) M](psozid-nystatin-cream-apply-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-nystatin-cream-apply-bid)

# ________________________________________________________

# Treatment for paronychia associated with Staphylococcus

# ________________________________________________________

Treat for 10 days.

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID \($\) R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-10days-1ds-tab-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-10days-1ds-tab-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-10ds-100mg-po-bid)

# DISSEMINATED MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM DISEASE TREATMENT

Many of these patients have HIV/AIDS. Management is complex. Consult

Infectious Diseases.

Rifabutin is optional for disseminated disease. Rifabutin can improve cure

rates, but may decrease blood concentrations of many drugs. Consult Infectious

Diseases or Pharmacy for more information.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treatment is continued for 12 months and until CD4 count is >100 cells per

microliter for at least 6 months.

# Two-drug treatment

Preferred treatment

[Clarithromycin 500 mg PO BID \($\) R,DI <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO QDay](orz-set-abx-op-clarithro-500mg-ethambu-15-mg-kg)

($$) [R]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-clarithro-500mg-ethambu-15-mg-kg)

Alternative

[Azithromycin 250 mg PO QDay \($\) M <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO QDay R](orz-set-abx-op-azithro-250-mg-ethambutol-15-mg-kg)

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-azithro-250-mg-ethambutol-15-mg-kg)

# Three-drug treatment

Preferred treatment

[Clarithromycin 500 mg PO BID\($\) R,DI <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO QDay](orz-set-abx-op-clarith-500-ethamb-15-rifabutin-300)

($$) [R] <AND> rifabutin 300 mg PO QDay ($$) [R,DI]

<AND> rifabutin 300 mg QDay ($$) [R,DI]

# MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM INTRACELLULARE (MAI OR MAC)

MAI colonization in patients with chronic lung disease is common. These

patients should not be treated with antimicrobials.

Occasionally, MAI causes pulmonary disease in patients who are not

immunosuppressed. Diagnosis and management are complex. Consult Infectious

Diseases and/or Pulmonary.

MAI causes systemic disease commonly in patients with HIV/AIDS. Most of these

cases do not involve the lungs. After treatment, long-term prophylaxis is

usually given. Consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

# MYCOBACTERIUM AVIUM PNEUMONIA

Diagnosis and treatment are complex. Regimens containing 3 or 4 drugs are

usually recommended, but two drug regimens may be sufficient in some cases.

Consult Infectious Diseases and/or Pulmonary in all cases.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Treatment is continued until sputum cultures are consecutively negative for 12

months.

# Three-drug regimens

Preferred treatment

[Clarithromycin 500 mg PO BID \($\) R,DI <AND> ethambutol 15 mg/kg PO QDay](orz-set-abx-op-clarith-500-ethamb-15-rifabutin-300)

<AND> rifabutin 300 mg QDay ($$) [R,DI]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-azith-250-ethamb-15-rifabutin-300)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PELVIC INFLAMMATORY DISEASE (PID)

Pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) refers to bacterial infection of the upper

female reproductive tract. Likely bacterial pathogens include Neisseria

gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, anaerobes, enteric Gram-negative rods, and

Streptococcus agalactiae. PID should be considered in sexually active women

with pelvic tenderness and signs of lower genital tract inflammation. Signs and

symptoms may be mild or non-specific, and providers should have a low threshold

to initiate treatment. All women who are diagnosed with acute PID should be

tested for N. gonorrohoeae, C. trachomatis, and HIV. Male sex partners of

patients with PID should be examined and treated (see below) if they had sexual

contact within the 60 days before onset of the patient's symptoms.

Judge severity of infection based on clinical signs and symptoms, including

blood pressure, pulse, mental status, and degree of fever.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

Treat for 14 days.

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM x 1 dose \($\) M < AND > doxycycline 100 mg BID for 14](orz-set-abx-op-ceft-im-doxy-14ds-100mg-metro-14ds-500mg)

days ($) [DI] < OPTIONAL > metronidazole 500 mg PO BID ($) [DI]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-ceft-im-doxy-14ds-100mg-metro-14ds-500mg)

# For patients who cannot take ceftriaxone and doxycycline, call ID

# Treatment of sex partner who is a veteran

Treat for both Chlamydia and Gonorrhea

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM x 1 dose \($\) M < AND > doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for](orz-set-abx-op-ceftr-500mg-im-x1-doxyc-7ds-100-po-bid)

7 days ($) [DI]

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-ceftr-500mg-im-x1-doxyc-7ds-100-po-bid)

< OR >

[Ceftriaxone 500 mg IM x 1 dose \($\) M < AND > azithromycin 1 gm PO x 1 dose](orz-set-abx-op-ceft-500mg-im-once-azith-1gm-po-once)

($) [M]

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Treatment for severe disease

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PERI ASSOC CAPD
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PERITONITIS ASSOCIATED WITH PERITONEAL DIALYSIS

Peritonitis associated with peritoneal dialysis usually presents with abdominal

pain, fever, nausea or vomiting, and cloudy effluent. The leukocyte

concentration is greater than 100 cells/microliter of dialysate, with more than

50% neutrophils.

Obtain Gram stain, culture, and cell count with differential of dialysate before

antimicrobials are given. Nephrology consultation is essential. If cultures

show Gram-negative or mixed bacterial infection, a gastrointestinal tract

infectious source is more likely. Gram-positive organisms like staphylococci

usually result from external contamination. Fungal peritonitis is rare and

requires immediate catheter removal.

**Antimicrobial recommendations are for empirical therapy only. Regimens should

be tailored according to patient response and microbiology results in

consultation with Nephrology and/or Infectious Diseases for more information.

To prevent catheter occlusion by turbid dialysate, add 1,000 units of heparin

per dialysis bag each day until one day after the dialysate is clear.

If vancomycin is used, trough serum concentrations should be kept above 15

mcg/ml to ensure adequate intraperitoneal levels. Usually vancomycin must be

given every 3 to 7 days. Contact Nephrology and/or Pharmacy for more

information.

# Consult Nephrology in a all cases.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Antimicrobial therapy

# Duration

Duration of therapy depends on the pathogen identified. Treat staphylococcal and

streptococcal infections for 2 weeks and all other gram-positive infections for

3 weeks. In patients who have Staphylococcus isolated and had a previous

staphylococcal infection, treat for 3 weeks.

# All antimicrobials below are administered via peritoneal dialysate bag over 6

# hours

# Empirical treatment while waiting for results of gram stain

[Cefepime 1 gm PD q24h \($$\) R](orz-set-abx-op-pd-cefep-1gm-q24h-snpw)

<OR>

[Cefazolin 15 mg/kg \($\) R <AND> gentamicin 0.6 mg/kg \($\) R,O PD q24h](orzid3-gmenu-pd-cefazolin-15mg-kg-q24h-gentamicin-0-6mg-kg-q24h)

MRSA risk factors

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PERIOCULAR INFECTIONS

# Eyelid infections

Patients with moderate or severe eyelid infections should be referred to

ophthalmology.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Blepharitis

Wash margins with baby shampoo daily and use warm compresses daily.

Antimicrobials have no benefit.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Hordeolum (stye)

For external disease (involving the gland of Zeis), daily hot pack massage

encourages drainage and relieves symptoms. For internal disease (involving

Meibomian glands) ophthalmology consult is encouraged, as the infection seldom

drains without intervention.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Lacrimal infections

Refer cases of lacrimal infection to ophthalmology, including infections of the

lacrimal gland (dacryoadenitis), lacrimal sac (dacrocystitis), or tear ducts

(canaliculitis).

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# PERIODONTAL DISEASE

Periodontal disease, including gingivitis and periodontitis, may progress into

more severe disease or cause hematogenous spreading of bacteria if left

untreated. All patients with periodontal disease should be referred to the

dental service for assessment and direction of treatment. In the presence of

gingivitis, the most commonly isolated subgingival flora includes Prevotella

intermedia, Capnocytophaga spp, Finegoldia magna and Peptostreptococcus. In the

presence of periodontitis, flora increases in complexity to most commonly

include Porphyromonas gingivalis, P. intermedia, Aggregatibacter

actinomycetemcomitans, Tanneralla forsythensis and Treponema denticola.

# Consult Dental Service

# Non-severe periodontitis or acute simple gingivitis treatment

[Chlorhexidine 0.12% oral rinse swish for 30 seconds, then spit 15 ml twice](psozid2-chlorhexidine-0-12-oral-swish-bid-7days)

daily for 7 days ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-chlorhexidine-0-12-oral-swish-bid-7days)

# Severe periodontitis or acute complicated gingivitis (ulceration, rapidly

# advancing disease, severe pain, patients with immunocompromising conditions)

# treatment

Consult Dental Service

# PERTUSSIS

Pertussis also known as "whooping cough" is caused by Bordetella pertussis. CDC

recommends antibiotic therapy for those presenting within three weeks of

symptoms (cough). After three weeks, patients may  not be infectious, and thus

antibiotic administration is not routinely recommended.

[Prevention of pertussis](orzid3-gmenu-prevention-pertussis)

# PHARYNGITIS AND TONSILLITIS

Most cases are viral, primarily due to adenovirus. Aside from streptococcal and

gonococcal pharyngitis, antimicrobials are not indicated. For gonococcal

pharyngitis, use link below for recommendations.

[Treatment of Gonorrheal Infections](orzid3-gmenu-gonococcal)

Consider HIV screening for patients with pharyngitis

[HIV AG/AB Lab](lrtz-hiv-ag-ab)

# Streptococcal Pharyngitis and Tonsillitis

Diagnosis of group A streptococcal (GAS) infection is made through detection by

rapid PCR and should be reserved for patients who have a moderate to high risk

of GAS infection according to the Modified Centor Score. Use link below for

Modified Centor score criteria and for more details.

[More About Pharyngitis/Tonsillitis and Modified Centor score](orzid3-gmenu-more-about-pharyngitis)

[Rapid Strep A throat PCR testing lab order](lrtz-strep-a-pcr)

Antimicrobials are not indicated

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PNEUMOCYSTIS JIROVECII DISEASE

Diagnosis and treatment are complex, consult Infectious Diseases in all cases.

Pneumocystis jirovecii (formerly termed Pneumocystis carinii) in an ubiquitious

organism that causes disease in people with compromised cell-mediated immunity.

Disease is exceedingly rare in people with intact host defenses. Pneumonia is

the usual manifestation but P. jirovecii can infect extrapulmonary sites,

especially in patients who have been receiving prophylaxis with aerosolized

pentanmidine. P. jirovecii disease occurs most commonly in people with AIDS and

fewer than 200 CD4 T lymphocytes/microliter.

The abbreviation PCP is often used for Pneumocystis pneumonia. It was derived

from the old species name, Pneumocystis carinii.

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TMP-SMZ) is the treatment of choice for P.

jirovecii disease, including disease that occurs despite TMP-SMZ prophylaxis.

Corticosteriods should be prescribed for patients with AIDS and P. jirovecii

pneumonia and an arterial oxygen tension <70 torr or an alveolar-arterial oxygen

gradient of >35 torr.

# Prophylaxis for Pneumocystis jirovecii

[CLICK HERE](orzid3-gmenu-pneumocystis-jirovecii-prophylaxis)

# Preferred treatment for mild to moderate disease or step-down treatment once

# disease has stabilized

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 2 DS tablets PO TID for 21 days \($\)R,DI](psozid2-tmp-smx-2ds-tablets-po-q8h-21days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-smx-2ds-tablets-po-q8h-21days)

PO QDay ($)[DI] for 21 days

for 21 days

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-clindam-450mg-q6h-primaquine-26-3mg-qd)

< OR >

[Atovaquone 750mg PO BID for 21 days \($\)M](psozid2-atovaquone-750mg-po-bid-21days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-atovaquone-750mg-po-bid-21days)

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PNEUMOCYSTIS JIROVECII PROPHYLAXIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PNEUMOCYSTIS JIROVECII PROPHYLAXIS

Indications for primary prophylaxis of P. jirovecii include:

1) HIV/AIDS patients with CD4 count <200 cells/microliter

2) Hematopoietic or organ transplantation patients during immunosuppression

3) Patients receiving Alemtuzumab, temozolomide or fludarabine

4) Patients receiving >/= 20mg equivalent of prednisone per day for over 1 month

5) Patients with acute lymphocytic leukemia, rheumatologic disease receiving

immunosuppressive therapy and certain primary immunodeficiencies (e.g. severe

combined immunodeficiency, idiopathic CD4 T-lymphocytopenia, hyper-IgM syndrome)

Dose and duration of prophylaxis varies with the indication. Please contact

Infectious Diseases or Hematology/Oncology for more information.

Prophylaxis should be discontinued when host defenses are restored. In persons

with AIDS on highly active antiretroviral therapy, Prophylaxis should be

discontinued when the CD4 cell concentrations remain over 200 cells/microliter

for 3-6 months in patients, except that prophylaxis should be continued for

life in those who have had P. jirovecii disease.

# Recommended FIRST-LINE prophylaxis:

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q day \($\) R,DI](psozid-tmp-smx-1-ds-tablet-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-tmp-smx-1-ds-tablet-qday)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 SS tablet q day \($\) R,DI](psozid-tmp-smx-1-ss-tablet-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-tmp-smx-1-ss-tablet-qday)

# Alternative when trimethoprim/sulfa is poorly tolerated or contraindicated:

**Patient should be tested for glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6-PD)

deficiency before starting dapsone. Individuals deficient in G6-PD

show about a 2-fold increase in sensitivity toward dapsone-induced hemolytic

anemia.

G6-PD lab test are resulted the same day or next day. May be add on lab.

G6-PD lab result should be "normal" to start dapsone therapy.

[Click here G6-PD Screen Lab Order](lrtz-g6-pd-screen)

[Dapsone 100mg PO q day \($\) O](psozid-dapsone-100mg-po-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-dapsone-100mg-po-qday)

# Alternative to the above preferred regimens:

# Atovaquone is alternative for patient for clinical reason:

(e.g. patients with SLE, hematologic concerns, G6PD deficiency)

[Atovaquone 1500mg qday for PCP prophylaxis \($$\) DI](psozidatovaquone-1500mg-qday-pcp-prophylaxis)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-atovaquone-1500mg-susp-qday-pcp-prophylaxis)

# POSTSEPTAL CELLULITIS (ORBITAL CELLULITIS)

Postseptal cellulitis (orbital cellulitis) is often preceded by sinusitis and

requires immediate consultation with otolaryngology and ophthalmology. Urgent

surgical drainage may be necessary. The most common pathogenic organisms in

adults are streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus

aureus.

Contact otolaryngology or ophthalmology immediately for urgent surgical

drainage. Broad-spectrum empirical antimicrobials should be used until a

pathogen can be identified from the drainage fluid.

# Duration of treatment

Orbital cellulitis should be treated until all signs of infection have resolved.

Uncomplicated orbital cellulitis should be treated for minimum of 2 weeks and

complicated orbital cellulitis (severe ethmoid sinusitis and bony destruction of

sinus) should be treated for at least 4 weeks.

# Empiric treatment

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

# results.  Adjust duration based on criteria above.

# The FDA amended its rules in 2015 concerning the Pregnancy, Labor and delivery,

# and Nursing mothers subsections of the Use in Specific Populations section of

# product labeling. Pregnancy categories A, B, C, D, and X have been removed.

# Drugs approved after June 30 will use the new format immediately, while drugs

# approved after June 30, 2001 will be phased in gradually.

See Sanford Guide for comprehensive antimicrobial pregnancy risk and lactation

safety information

[Sanford Guide Pregnancy Risk & Lactation Safety Table](orz-gtx-abx-sanford-pregnancy)

Risk Factors (A,B,C,D,X) were assigned to all drugs, based on the

level of risk the drug poses to the fetus. Risk Factors were designed to

help the clinician quickly classify a drug for use during pregnancy. They

do not refer to breastfeeding risk. The definitions of the Risk Factors

are those used by the FDA.

# Category Description

# A Controlled studies show no risk

Adequate, well-controlled studies in pregnant women

have failed to demonstrate risk to the fetus.

# B No evidence of risk in humans

Either animal findings show risk (but human

findings do not) or, if no adequate human studies

have been done, animal findings are negative.

# C Risk cannot be ruled out

Human studies are lacking and animal studies

are either positive for fetal risk or lacking

as well. However, potential benefits may

justify the potential risk.

# D Positive evidence of risk

Investigational or postmarketing data show risk

to fetus. Nevertheless, potential benefits may

outweigh the risk.

# X Contraindicated in pregnancy

Studies in animals or humans, or investigational

or postmarketing reports have shown fetal risk

which clearly outweighs any possible benefit to

the patient.

# IMMUNIZATION OF PREGNANT PATIENTS

Pregnant women should receive the tetanus, diphtheria, and acellular pertussis

vaccine (Tdap) during pregnancy and the influenza vaccine during or before

pregnancy. Live vaccines are contraindicated (e.g. MMR and Varicella). See

immunization information pages located at the bottom of this page for other

indications, contraindications, and one-time dose orders to listed vaccines.

[Patient vaccine history](orz-gtx-abx-joint-legacy-viewer)

[CDC Recommended Adult Immunization Schedule](orz-gtx-abx-cdc-adult-immunization-schedule)

for patients with these indications or refer to the Haemophilus influenza type b

vaccine information menu below.

[Meningococcal A, C, W and Y: indicated in asplenia, HIV, complement deficiency](orzid3-gmenu-abx-menacwy-vaccine-information-page)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PRESEPTAL CELLULITIS

Preseptal cellulitis involves soft tissues in front of the orbital septum and

the eyelids and is often preceded by sinusitis. Infection does not involve the

orbital contents. The most common pathogenic organisms in adults are

streptococci, Haemophilus influenzae, anaerobes, and Staphylococcus aureus.

Treat  under the guidance of ophthalmology and/or otolaryngology. Intravenous

antimicrobials are indicated initially for treatment of moderate to severe

disease. Switch to oral antimicrobials when the patient's symptoms improve and

the patient can tolerate oral medications.

# Treatment of mild to moderate disease

Preferred:

[Amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg PO BID \($\) R < AND>](orz-set-abx-op-amox-clav-875-bid-tmp-sulfa-2ds-5days)

Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS PO BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-amox-clav-875-bid-tmp-sulfa-2ds-5days)

Alternative:

[Assessment of Beta-lactam Reaction](orzid2-gmenu-abx-beta-lactam-allergy-assesment)

[Cefdinir 300 mg PO q12h \($\) R <AND> trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS PO](orz-set-abx-op-cefdinir-300mg-bid-tmp-smx-2ds-bid-5days)

BID ($) [R,DI] for 5 days

[Non-VA order for above](orz-set-abx-nv-cefdinir-300mg-bid-tmp-smx-2ds-bid-5days)

# Treatment of severe disease

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

PREVENTION OF BACTERIAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

Antimicrobial prophylaxis is often given to patients likely to have profound,

prolonged neutropenia.  Profound neutropenia is less than 100 neutrophils and

bands per microliter, and such neutropenia is considered prolonged when it is

expected to last more than 7 days.  Most patients who should receive prophylaxis

have received stem cell transplants or are undergoing induction chemotherapy for

acute leukemia.

# If antibacterial prophylaxis is indicated

Duration of therapy: During period of expected neutropenia

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 7 days \($\) R,DI](psozid2-ciprofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-ciprofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-bid)

< OR >

[Levofloxacin 500 mg PO QDAY for 7days \($\) R,DI](psozid2-levofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-qday)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-levofloxacin-7ds-500mg-po-qday)

< OR >

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID for 7 days \($\) R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

< OR >

[Cefpodoxime 100 mg PO BID x7days \($$\) R](psozid-cefpodoxime-100mg-po-bid-x7days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-cefpodoxime-100mg-po-bid-x7days)

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PREV INFECT FUNGAL PROPHYL
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

PREVENTION OF FUNGAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY

Antifungal chemoprophylaxis is often given to patients undergoing induction

chemotherapy for acute leukemia expected to have profound neutropenia (less than

100 neutrophils and bands per milliliter) for more than 10 days and for patients

receiving allogeneic stem cell transplantation.  For most other patients the

expected benefits do not outweigh the risks of adverse effects and selection of

resistant fungi.

Antifungal is usually given until the absolute neutrophil concentration

increases to more than 500 cells/microliter in patients undergoing induction

chemotherapy for leukemia.  Duration is 100 days for patients undergoing stem

cell transplantation.  Some physicians continue prevention after 100 days if

corticosteroids are part of the immunosuppressive regimen.

Recommend posaconazole prophylaxis for patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia.

Contact Hematology Oncology or Infectious Disease for more information.

Patients who have had invasive fungal infection in the recent past and who are

about to become neutropenic may require chemoprophylaxis.  Contact Hematology-

Oncology or Infectious Diseases for more information.

# If antifungal prophylaxis is indicated

Duration of therapy: during period of expected neutropenia

[Fluconazole 400 mg po qday for 10 days \($\) R,DI](psozid-fluconazole-400mg-po-qday-x10days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-fluconazole-400mg-po-qday-x10days)

# For patients being treated for AML:

Requires Infectious Disease approval:

Posaconazole 300mg Tablets twice daily on day 1, then 300mg once daily on

day 2 and thereafter. Continue for 7 days after the neutrophil count

rises above 500/mm3. ($$$$) [DI]

NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines, Prevention and Treatment of Cancer-

Related Infections. Version 1.2019. nccn.org

patients

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PREV OF BACT ENDOCARDITIS OUTPATIENT
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PREVENTION OF BACTERIAL ENDOCARDITIS

Bacteremia occurs several times a day during daily activities like eating and

brushing teeth and rarely results in endocarditis, even in people with abnormal

valves.  While bacteremia might occur following dental or other procedures, most

cases of endocarditis are from the millions more episodes of transient

bacteremia a person experiences per year from ordinary daily activities.  There

is no evidence that antimicrobial prophylaxis prevents endocarditis after

procedures.  The best available evidence suggests that prophylactic

antimicrobials confer more risks than benefits in most situations.  A decision

about whether to administer antimicrobial prophylaxis should be based on both

the risk of endocarditis conferred by the patient's cardiac defect and the risk

of bacteremia from a planned dental or surgical procedure.

# Minneapolis VAHCS SOP antimicrobial prophylaxis for dental surgery:

[SOP for dental surgery antimicrobial prophylaxis](orz-gtx-abx-url-dental-sop)

# Determine the need for prophylaxis through the 2-step process outlined

# below.

# Step 1.  Assess the risk of endocarditis for your patient

Prophylaxis is recommended if a patient has any of the following conditions:

o  Prosthetic cardiac valve or material including: Presence of cardiac

prosthetic valve, transcatheter implantation of prosthetic valves (e.g. TAVR

cardiac valve repair with devices (e.g. annuloplasty, rings, or clips), left

ventricular assist devices or implantable heart

o  A history of infective endocarditis

o  Certain specific congenital heart conditions - refer to the full SOP

(link above) or consult Cardiology for more detailed recommendations

o  Cardiac transplant that develops a problem in the heart valve

# Step 2.  Assess the risk of bacteremia from the planned procedure

Prophylaxis is indicated for these procedures:

o  All dental procedures that involve manipulation of gingival tissue or the

periapical region of teeth or perforation of the oral mucosa.

o  Procedures on the respiratory tract that involve incision or biopsy of the

respiratory mucosa, such as tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy. Prophylaxis is

recommended for bronchoscopy when it involves incision of the respiratory

tract mucosa.

o  Procedures that involve incision through infected skin, skin structures, or

musculoskeletal tissue.

o  Dermatologic procedures that breach the oral mucosa.

# Prophylactic Antimicrobials select below:

[Patients undergoing dental or oral mucosa procedures](orzid3-gmenu-pbe-dental-oral-resp-proc)

[Patients undergoing procedures on the respiratory tract that involve incision or](orzid2-gmenu-surg-head-and-neck-surg)

biopsy of the respiratory mucosa

[Patients undergoing procedures for infected skin, skin structures, or infected](orzid3-gmenu-abx-proced-for-infected-skin-outpatient)

musculoskeletal tissues

# _______________________________________________________________________________

References:

Up-To-Date Article: Antimicrobial prophylaxis for the prevention of bacterial

endocarditis

Wilson et al., Circulation, 2021, 143(20)e963-e978

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PREVENTION PERTUSSIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PREVENTION OF PERTUSSIS

# Immunization

Give a single dose of tetanus-diphtheria acellular pertussis vaccine (Tdap) in

adults regardless of interval between most recent Td vaccine. One dose of Tdap

vaccine is given to pregnant women during each pregnancy.

# Postexposure prophylaxis in adults

Household contacts with symptomatic coughing should be treated as if they have

pertussis. Consult Infectious Diseases for all suspected cases of pertussis and

exposure to pertussis.

CDC recommends postexposure prophylaxis in household contacts within 21 days

after exposure to pertussis regardless of immunization history. Non-household

contacts who are at high risk of severe illness or who have close contact with

high-risk individuals should receive post exposure prophylaxis within 21 days of

exposure. Those at high risk of severe illness are infants less than one year of

age, women in third trimester of pregnancy and those with preexisting health

conditions that may be exacerbated by pertussis (e.g. immunosuppressed and

asthmatic individuals).

A single dose of Tdap should be administered in those who are not up to date.

Preferred:

[Azithromycin 500mg po day 1, then 250mg q24h for days 2-5 O](psozid2-azith-500mg-po-once-then-250mg-po-qday-x4ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-azith-500mg-po-once-then-250mg-po-qday-x4ds)

Alternative for macrolide intolerant or allergic patients:

[Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID for 7 days R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-7days-1ds-tab-bid)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# PRIMARY INFECTION (CHICKENPOX)

# ________________________________

# Immunocompetent patients

# ________________________________

# Prevention

Vaccinate all adults without evidence of immunity except for pregnant women.

Test antibody first in adults who have uncertain history of chickenpox or

vaccination.

Give Varicella vaccine x 2, 2nd dose 4-8 weeks after 1st dose

# Treatment

Therapy must be started within 24 hrs onset of rash.

[Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/day for 5-7 days \($\) R](psozid2-acyclovir-5ds-800mg-po-5x-d)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-acyclovir-5ds-800mg-po-5x-d)

# Alternative

Therapy must be started within 24 hrs onset of rash.

[Valacyclovir 1 gm PO TID for 5 days \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-5ds-1gm-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-5ds-1gm-po-tid)

# ________________________________

# Immunocompromised patients

# ________________________________

# Prevention

Immunocompromised patients without prior immunity to varicella who are at risk

for disease include: patients with malignancy, current immunosuppressive

therapy, or HIV infection. Vaccination is not recommended while patients are

immunocompromised.

Contact Infectious Diseases for more information.

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

[Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/day for 7 days \($\) R](psozid2-acyclovir-800mg-po-5x-day-7ds)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-acyclovir-800mg-po-5x-day-7ds)

< OR >

[Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO TID for 7 days \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1000mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1000mg-po-tid)

# Treatment for severe disease, or if mild to moderate disease doesn't improve on

# above therapy

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

# ENTEROCOCCAL INFECTIONS IN BONE OR JOINT PROSTHESES

For acute, moderate or severe infections, treat with intravenous antibiotics

followed by oral antibiotics. For severe infections, add an aminoglycoside for

synergy during the first weeks of therapy. Mild infections can be treated with

oral antibiotics only.

Consult Infectious Diseases for specific management advice.

# Duration of Treatement

Treat for a total duration of 4-6 weeks. Chronic oral antimicrobial suppression

may follow treatment based on individual patient circumstances.

# Intravenous Treatment

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

# Oral Treatment For Mild Infections, Continuation of Therapy and Chronic

# Suppression

[Amoxicillin 500 mg PO TID \($\) R](psozid-amoxicillin-500-mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-amoxicillin-500-mg-po-tid)

< OR >

[Penicillin VK 500 mg PO QID \($\) R](psozid-penicillin-500mg-po-qid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-penicillin-500mg-po-qid)

Allergy to penicillin

[Minocycline 100mg PO BID \($\) DI](psozid-minocycline-100mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-minocycline-100mg-po-bid)

For resistant isolates only

[Linezolid 600 mg PO BID \($\) DI,O](zzpsozid-linezolid-600mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-linezolid-600mg-po-bid)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# STAPHYLOCOCCUS AUREUS INFECTIONS IN BONE OR JOINT PROSTHESES

Consult Infectious Diseases for specific management advice.

# Treatment Following Debridement and Retention of Prosthesis

Treat with intravenous antibiotic for 2 to 6 weeks followed by 3 to 6 months of

an oral antibiotic combined with rifampin (3 months in total hip, elbow,

shoulder and ankle arthroplasty and 6 months in total knee arthroplasty).

# Treatment Following 2-stage Exchange or Resection Arthroplasty Without Planned

# Staged Reimplantation of Prosthesis

Treat with intravenous antibiotic for 6 weeks for all joint types.

# Treatment Following 1-Stage Exchange of Prosthesis

Treat with intravenous antibiotic for 2 to 6 weeks followed by 3 months of an

oral antibiotic combined with rifampin for all joint types.

# Rifampin Synergy

Rifampin is recommended for treatment with debridement and retention or one

stage exchange. When rifampin is combined with a beta-lactam or vancomycin in

vitro, bacterial killing is enhanced. Do not use rifampin alone, as bacterial

resistance develops rapidly. If patient does not tolerate rifampin it may be

omitted from treatment regimen. Contact Infectious Diseases for more

information.

# Chronic Suppression

Chronic suppression with oral antimicrobials may follow treatment based on

individual patient circumstances.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Intravenous Treatment

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

# _______________________________________________________________________________

# Oral Treatment for Continuation of Therapy or Chronic Suppression

[Cefadroxil 1000 mg PO BID \($\) R](psozid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-cefadroxil-1000mg-po-bid)

MRSA or allergy to penicillin or cephalosporin

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO BID \($\) R,DI](psozid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-trimeth-sulfa-1-ds-tablet-po-bid)

< OR >

[Minocycline 100mg PO BID \($\) DI](psozid-minocycline-100mg-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-minocycline-100mg-po-bid)

# Rifampin Synergy for Debridement and Retention or One Stage Exchange (Not For

# Chronic Suppression)

In addition to PO treatment above < ADD >

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-rifampin-600mg-po-qday)

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# Antibiotic Prophylaxis Transrectal Ultrasound Prostate Biopsy Procedures (TRUSP)

The recommendations for prophylaxis for TRUSP procedures have been updated based

based on emergence of resistant E-coli bacteria strains.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Preferred:

# Outpatient Prescriptions for Mailing:

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once \($\) R,DI < AND >](orz-set-abx-cipro-cefuroxime-mail-po)

Cefuroxime 1000 mg po once ($) [M], BOTH 2 to 3 hours before

scheduled prostate biopsy.

# Outpatient Prescriptions for Window Pick-up:

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once \($\) R,DI < AND >](orz-set-abx-cipro-cefuroxime-po-window)

Cefuroxime 1000 mg po once ($) [M], BOTH 2 to 3 hours before

scheduled prostate biopsy.

# __________________________________________________________________

# Alternative for patients who have not taken the oral medications:

# Administer in clinic on the day of procedure.

# Patients weighing less than 300lbs:

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once \($\) R,DI < AND > Ceftriaxone 500 mg](orz-set-abx-op-ceftriaxone-500-im-and-cipro-500-po-x1)

Intramuscularly once ($) [M] BOTH given 1 hour before the procedure.

# Patients weighing 300lbs or greater:

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once \($\) R,DI < AND > Ceftriaxone 1 gram](orz-set-abx-op-ceftriaxone-1gm-im-and-cipro-500po-trusp)

Intramuscularly once ($) [M] BOTH given 1 hour before the procedure.

# _________________________________________________________________

# Alternative for patients with anaphylactic or other serious beta-lactam allergy

# Administer in clinic on the day of procedure.

[Ciprofloxacin 500 mg po once \($\) R,DI < AND > Aztreonam 1 gm intramuscularly](orz-set-abx-op-aztreonam-1gm-cipro-500-once-prophylaxis-trusp)

once ($$$$) [R] BOTH given 1 hour before the procedure.

# __________________________________________________________________

Becopoulos T et al  J Chemother 1990 2:244-246

# INFECTIONS IN BONE OR JOINT PROSTHESES

# Empirical therapy before a pathogen is identified is not recommended unless

options depending on patient's condition. Consult Infectious Diseases

results are obtained may be justified.

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU PUBIC LICE (PEDICULOSIS PUBIS)
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

PUBIC LICE (PEDICULOSIS PUBIS)

Lice are parasitic insects. Human lice survive by feeding on human blood.

To make a diagnosis, use a nit comb, bright light, or lens to find a louse

living in pubic hair.

The presence of nits on a hair shaft, especially when they are located more

than 6 mm from the skin, does NOT indicate active infestation.  Nits may remain

present for months after successful treatment.

Household contacts and persons who may have come into contact with personal

belongings of an infested individual should be examined for evidence of lice

and discarded or cleaned if contaminated.

# Treatment

A repeat application may be used if live lice are seen 7-10 days after

treatment.

[Permethrin 1% lotion. Apply to affected area for 10 minutes then comb out](psozid2-permethrin-1-lot-10min-7days)

nits ($) [M]

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-permethrin-1-lot-10min-7days)

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU REACT PRIM INFECT ZOSTER
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# REACTIVATION OF PRIMARY INFECTION (ZOSTER OR SHINGLES)

Zoster represents reactivation of varicella-zoster virus. After primary

infection, virus remains latent in the sensory dorsal root ganglia.

Reactivation syndrome is characterized by painful, unilateral, vesicular,

dermatomal rash.

# Prevention

Vaccinate all adults greater than or equal to 50 years of age with the

recombinant zoster vaccine regardless of past episode or receipt of the live

zoster vaccine.

Give recombinant zoster vaccine x2, 2nd dose 2-6 months after the first

# ________________________________

# Immunocompetent patients

# ________________________________

# Treatment in persons <50 years

Treatment is not beneficial, none is recommended.

# Treatment in persons >=50 years

Treatment with antivirals can shorten duration of pain and rash in patients over

50 years old. Treatment must be started within 72 hours of onset.

[Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO TID for 7 days \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1000mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1000mg-po-tid)

There is evidence that addition of corticosteroids to antiviral

therapy decreases pain and duration of rash and improves quality of life

modestly during the acute shingles episode. Corticosteroids do not decrease the

incidence of post-herpetic neuralgia. Some authorities recommend addition of

corticosteroid therapy to antiviral therapy for patients over age 50 years.

Corticosteroids are not recommended for patients at greater risk for steroid

toxicities (e.g., insulin-dependent diabetes mellitus, hypertension, peptic

ulcer disease) or for immunocompromised patients.

Optional Recommendation:

[Prednisone 60 mg daily for 7 days then 30 mg daily for 7 days, then 15 mg](psozid-prednisone-taper-for-herpes-zoster)

daily for 7 days. ($)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid-prednisone-taper-for-herpes-zoster)

# ________________________________

# Immunocompromised patients

# ________________________________

# Treatment

Immunocompromised patients at increased risk for complications of VZV disease

include: patients with malignancy, current immunosuppressive therapy, or HIV

infection. Treatment with antivirals shortens duration of symptoms and reduces

incidence of complications. In immunocompromised patients, treatment is

recommended to be started at any point during an active infection.

# Treatment for mild to moderate disease

[Valacyclovir 1000 mg PO TID for 7 days \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1000mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1000mg-po-tid)

# Treatment for severe disease or progression from mild to moderate disease in

# patients <=65 years

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

# Treatment for severe disease or progression from mild to moderate disease in

# patients >65 years

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.

References:

Kim et al. Annals Intern Med. 2018, 168(3):210-220

menus.Text:

# PERSISTENT OR RECURRENT URETHRITIS OR CERVICITIS

Retreat with initial treatment regimen if patient was non-compliant with initial

treatment regimen or re-exposed to an untreated sex partner. If infection is not

due to non-compliance with treatment regimen or re-exposure to an untreated sex

partner, infection is most commonly caused by M. genitalium and less commonly T.

vaginalis.

# Treatment for persistent or recurrent urethritis and failure of initial

# doxycycline treatment

[Metronidazole 2 gm PO x 1 dose \($\) DI Azithromycin 1 gm PO x 1 dose \($\)](orz-set-abx-op-metro-2gm-po-x1-azithro-1gm-po-x1)

[M]

# Failure of above treatment

Consult Infectious Diseases (outpatient)

# RELIEF RX =  SYMPTOMATIC CARE PACK FOR VIRAL RESPIRATORY INFECTION

Acute Respiratory Tract Infections typically do not require an antimicrobial

prescription, however, patient's may be left unsatisfied. Relief Rx,

a symptom care pack including educational material, to ease veterans' symptoms

and help limit inappropriate antimicrobial prescriptions for viral infections.

Note: The Relief RX package does not contain medications (other than throat

lozenges). Provider may order additional symptomatic medications.

Select clinics are participating in the Relief RX program with the Antimicrobial

Stewardship Team. Please use link below to contact the team with questions

or to obtain more Relief RX packages for your site.

[<Select Here> Contact ASP/CDSS Team](orz-gtx-abx-cdss-email)

menus.Name: ORZID3 GMENU RETINITIS
menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

# RETINITIS AND ACUTE RETINAL NECROSIS

Retinitis is a subset of uveitis, is rare in immunocompetent people: in these

individuals it is usually caused by varicella-zoster virus (VZV) or herpes

simplex virus (HSV). Retinitis is more common in immunocompromised patients and

cytomegalovirus being the most common pathogen in these patients. Other

retinitis pathogens include Toxoplasma gondii, Bartonella henselae, Histoplasma

capsulatum, and Treponema pallidum. In most cases, patients have other

neurological symptoms or signs.  Patients with candidemia may present with 1-3

mm white punctate retinal lesions called cotton-wool spots. These may only be

visible on fundus examination. Treatment of candidal retinitis  is systemic

antifungal therapy. Consult Ophthalmology, Infectious Diseases, or Neurology for

help.

VZV and HSV cause nearly all cases of acute retinal necrosis (ARN), with a small

number being caused by cytomegalovirus. ARN is a rapidly progressing retinitis

that occurs primarily in immunocompetent people and can cause vision loss.

Treatment with intravenous acyclovir or valacyclovir is essential to halt

progression of ARN.

Ophthalmology and Infectious Diseases consultation is essential

# Treatment of Non-viral Retinitis or ARN

Refer to specific pathogen treatment recommendations of the CDSS to treat

underlying infection

# Treatment of Retinitis or ARN due to CMV:

[Link to Treatment of CMV Retinitis and ARN](orzid3-gmenu-cmv-retinitis)

# Treatment of VZV Retinitis

[Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x/d for 5-7 days \($\) R](psozid2-acyclovir-5ds-800mg-po-5x-d)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-acyclovir-5ds-800mg-po-5x-d)

< OR >

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

Alternative

[Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q8h for 5 days \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-5ds-1gm-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-5ds-1gm-po-tid)

# Treatment of HSV Retinitis

[Acyclovir 400 mg PO q8h for 7-10 days \($\) R](psozid2-acyclovir-7days-400mg-po-tid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-acyclovir-7days-400mg-po-tid)

< OR >

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

Alternative

[Valacyclovir 1 gm PO q12h for 7-10 days \($\) R](psozid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1gm-po-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-valacyclovir-7ds-1gm-po-bid)

# Treatment of VZV and HSV Acute Retinal Necrosis

Ophthalmologist involvement is essential for treatment including

corticosteroids, vitrectomy, or laser therapy. Intravitreal foscarnet in

addition to a systemic antiviral may provide added therapeutic efficacy.

Duration

Treat with intravenous therapy for a minimum of 7 days until disease has

stabilized then treat with or therapy for a minimum of 6 weeks

Treatment

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS for parenteral therapy

# _______________________________________________________________________________

menus.Text:
[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

SCABIES

Scabies is an infestation of the skin by the mite Sarcoptes scabiei.

It is transmitted by skin to skin contact. Outbreaks occur in nursing

homes, day care centers, and residential institutions.  Scabies is highly

contagious and meticulous infection control is needed.

Treatment is a single application of permethrin cream.  Some experts recommend

a second application 7-10 days after the first application if the patient is

still symptomatic or if live mites are found at that time.  Contact Dermatology

or Infectious Diseases for more information.

Treat family members and other close contacts to prevent spread and recurrence.

# Treatment

Repeat application 7-10 days after the first application if patient is still

experiencing symptoms, or if lives mites are found.

[Permethrin 5% cream apply from head to feet, leave on for 8-14 hours, then](psozid2-permethrin-5-crm-top-appl-from-head-to-feet)

wash cream off with soap and water ($) [M]

# SECOND RECURRENCE OF CLOSTRIDIOIDES DIFFICILE INFECTION (CDI)

Discontinue implicated antibiotic(s). Narrow antibiotic spectrum if antibiotic

therapy is still needed. Avoid antiperistaltic agents (narcotics, loperamide,

etc.). Avoid antacid therapy without clear indication. If diarrhea has improved

or resolved prior to starting C. difficile treatment, consider re-assessing the

diagnosis before initiating therapy. C. difficile infection usually responds to

antimicrobial therapy. If symptoms do not respond to appropriate antimicrobial

therapy, re-consider the diagnosis.

# Second Recurrence CDI:

[Vancomycin Extended Pulse-Taper Regimen M](psozid2-vancomycin-taper-and-pulse-dosing)

(Vancomycin 125 mg PO q6h for 10 days, then taper and pulse with 125 mg po q12h

for 7 days, then 125mg po qday for 7 days, then 125mg every other day for 6

weeks)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-vancomycin-taper-and-pulse-dosing)

< OR >

If fidaxomicin not previously used:

[Fidaxomicin 200 mg po q12h for 10 days M](psozid2-fidaxomicin-200mg-po-q12h-10days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-fidaxomicin-200mg-po-bid-10ds)

< OR>

If fidaxomicin not previously used:

[Fidaxomicin Extended-Pulse Regimen M](psozid2-fidaxomicin-200-mg-extended-pulse-regimen)

(Fidaxomicin 200mg po bid x5days,then 200mg every other day x20days)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-fidaxomicin-200mg-extended-pulse-regimen)

# Third or more recurrence: Consult Gastroenterology or Infectious Disease

# COMPLICATED INTRA-ABDOMINAL INFECTIONS: SECONDARY PERITONITIS, INTRAABDOMINAL

# ABSCESS, INTRAPERITONEAL ABSCESS

[Oral step-down treatment](orzid3-gmenu-abx-step-down-treatment)

Complicated Intra-abdominal infections (cIAI) include any infectious process

that extends from an intra-abdominal organ into a sterile space and is

associated with peritonitis with or without abscess.

Community-acquired cIAI: patients without recent procedure related to site of

perforation or abscess

Healthcare-associated cIAI: patients developing a new infection > 48 hours after

an incident intra-abdominal procedure

# Primary therapy: abscess drainage

CT or US-guided percutaneous or surgical drainage should be considered in all

cases for diagnostic confirmation, microbiologic evaluation, and therapy.

# Duration of antimicrobial therapy

Adequate source control: 4 days after source control

Incomplete source control and no abscess: 5-7 days tailored to improvement.

Re-evaluate need for source control if ongoing signs/symptoms of infection

beyond 7 days

Abscess: 2-6 weeks depending on resolution on repeat imaging. ID Consult

recommended.

# Community-acquired infection without severe illness or immunosuppression

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

# Healthcare-associated infection, severe illness, or immunosuppression

Refer to the Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS

menus.Text:

# Daily Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Asplenia

The need for daily antibiotic prophylaxis and its duration is typically

determined individually based on patient age, immune status, history of

infection, potential for adverse drug reactions and other factors.

# Consider Prophylaxis:

1) Approximately 1 year prophylaxis for all patients following splenectomy.

2) Lifelong prophylaxis for patients with history of sepsis or other severe

infections caused by encapsulated organisms.

3) Prophylaxis for as long as the patient is immunocompromised or for life

for patients with concurrent immunocompromising conditions (e.g. hematologic

malignancy, hypogammaglobulinemia, solid-organ transplant, advanced liver

disease, or HIV infection).

# Daily antibiotic prophylaxis is in addition to the emergency supply.

# Recommended:

[Amoxicillin 500MG PO bid for daily prophylaxis for asplenic patient \($\) R](psozid-amoxicillin-500mg-po-bid-for-asplenia-daily-prophylaxis)

< OR >

[Cephalexin 250MG PO bid for daily propylaxis for asplenic patient \($\) R](psozid-cephalexin-250mg-po-bid-daily-prophylaxis-asplenia)

# Functional or Anatomical Asplenia Vaccine & Antibiotic Prophylaxis Guideline

Following a splenectomy there is considerably increased risk of developing

septicemia from invasive encapsulated organisms, namely Streptococcus pneumonia,

Haemophilus inluenza type b and meningococcus. Key measures to prevent

such infections include education, vaccination, prophylactic antimicrobial

therapy in selected patients, and early empirical therapy for febrile

epsisodes. It is critically important to educate patients regarding the

lifelong risk of postsplenectomy sepsis, the importance of vaccinations,

and the need for urgent action in response to a febrile episode.

# Management of an Episode of Fever in an Asplenic Patient

*See Inpatient CDSS*

# Initiation of vaccine regimen:

Routine vaccines should be up to date.

See CDSS Immunization section to order, if needed.

[click here Vaccinations for Adults without a Spleen](orz-gtx-abx-url-asplenia-vaccination-recommendations)

Ideally splenectomy vaccinations should be given 10 to 12 weeks before

elective splenectomy.  Where this is not possible they can be given up to

two weeks before or at least two weeks post-splenectomy.

[click here Place order for specific vaccines for asplenia](orzid3-gmenu-splenectomy-opt-chart)

# Use of Antibiotic Prophylaxis for Asplenia:

Use of antibiotic prophylaxis, in addition to vaccination, further reduces

the risk of infection and poor outcomes.

# Daily Antibiotic Prophylaxis: (in addition to emergency supply)

[Daily Antibiotic Prophylaxis](orzid3-gmenu-splenectomy-daily-antibiotic)

# Emergency Supply Empiric Abx for Fever or Other Signs of Systemic Infection:

[Self-medicate Empiric Antibiotics](orzid3-gmenu-splenectomy-empiric-abx)

SPOROTRICHOSIS

Sporotrichosis occurs most often in people who have had significant outdoor

exposure to soil.  In immunocompetent people, disease is usually limited to the

skin.  In people with decreased host defenses (eg, HIV/AIDS, alcoholism,

diabetes mellitus, or chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) sporotrichosis

often disseminates to bones, joints, or lungs.  Consult Infectious Diseases or

Dermatology

# PURULENT SKIN/SOFT TISSUE INFECTIONS

Includes furuncles/boils, carbuncles and cutaneous abscesses with or without

surrounding inflammation. The predominant pathogen is Staphylococcus aureus

(MSSA or MRSA).

Incision and drainage are recommended whenever feasible. Adjunctive antibiotics

are typically recommended. Incision and drainage alone are reasonable based on

patient preferences when abscess is smaller, limited surrounding inflammation,

no systemic signs of infections, and/or limited comorbidities.

# For recurrent skin abscesses in addition to culture and antibiotic therapy

# recommend considering a decolonization regimen.

[Click Here for Staphylococcus aureus Decolonization](orzid3-gmenu-abx-sa-decolonization)

# Preferred outpatient treatment:

[Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet BID for 5 days R,DI](psozid2-tmp-sulfa-5days-1ds-tab-bid)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-tmp-sulfa-5days-1ds-tab-bid)

< OR >

[Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 5 days DI](psozid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-5d)

[Non-VA order for above](pshzid2-doxycycline-100mg-po-bid-5d)

# Alternative:

Reserve for contraindication, precaution, failure to preferred options, or for

patient where parenteral antibiotics would be otherwise be selected.

[Linezolid 600 mg PO BID for 5 days DI,O](psozid2-linezolid-600mg-po-bid-5days)

[Help, legend, allergy info, consults, alternative antimicrobials and more \(Opt\)](orzid3-gmenu-abx-general-information-outpatient)

STAPHYLOCOCCAL SCALDED SKIN SYNDROME (RITTER'S DISEASE)

Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) presents with severe skin

blistering and exfoliation resulting from toxins produced by Staphylococcus

aureus.  SSSS is usually found in children and rarely in older adults.  Obtain

a skin biopsy to differentiate between SSSS and toxic epidermal necrolysis.

Initiate anti-staphylococcal therapy and obtain cultures and susceptibilities.

If cultures reveal methicillin-susceptible Staphylococcus aureus (MSSA), change

to nafcillin or cefazolin for better antimicrobial activity.

# Treatment

Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS.
